author: Fozzie
title: Chapter 24: The Transformation of Surplus-value into Capital
content:
Harry Cleaver's study guide to Marx's Capital volume one, chapter 24.

The employment of surplus-value as capital = accumulation of capital.

Although net revenue (sales minus costs) = surplus-value, it takes the form of money. It only becomes capital when invested in more means of production and in the hiring of more labor.

For this to happen annual production must include: whatever new means of production that are needed to replace worn-out means of production (depreciation), new means of production that can be bought by the net revenue or surplus-value, new labor power (workers) that can be hired and new means of subsistence to sustain them.

The availability of new labor-power implies wages that "suffice, not only to maintain [the existing working class], but also to increase its numbers."

"The cycle of simple reproduction alters its form and, to use Sismondi's expression, changes into a spiral."

Thus laws of private property that assume equal exchange [and indeed often prosecute unequal exchange or cheating] thus hide the real relationship. Equal exchange (assuming wages = value of labor-power) is a mere semblance - a form that mystifies the real content of the relationship, i.e., money/surplus-value (=unpaid labor) is stolen from workers.

"Originally the rights of property seemed to us to be grounded in a man's own labor." [e.g., John Locke's theory of property](1)) But in capitalism property - of the means of production - "turns out to be the right . . . to appropriate the unpaid labor of others".

"General law of commodity production" = "law of exchange" = exchange of equal values. Marx assumes this to always hold, yet exploitation exists because workers produce more value than the value of their wages.

Generalization of commodity production only occurs when labor-power becomes a commodity - which happens only with the development of capitalism - thus capitalism includes this generalization.

There are two basic points in this section. The first is that for capitalism to expand beyond simple reproduction the surpus-value earned through the exploitation of workers, and accruing to the capitalists as money realized through the sale of the commodities produced by those workers, must be invested rather than consumed. The second point is that such investment, wherein surplus-value is used to purchase new means of production and to hire new workers to expand production, doesn't violate the "laws of exchange", i.e., we can continue to assume equality in exchange. But, because the extraction of surplus-value constitutes the very unequal exploitation of workers, the "laws of exchange" hide the reality of the situation.

Investment: by corporations, by philanthropies and by the state.

In simple reproduction - where the existing situation is merely reproduced - all surplus-value is consumed, either by the capitalist class to whom it belongs or, perhaps, by the beneficiaries of any charity the capitalists might distribute to the poor. Marx doesn't discuss charity but others of his time were well aware of this use of a little bit of surplus-value. Some, such as the Reverand Thomas Malthus whom Marx both draws upon and frequently mocks, argued against it. (2) Others, such as Emile Zola, the French novelist, drew biting portraits of such condescention on the part of capitalists. (see the description in Germinal (1885)(3) of the annual charity bestowed on coal miners by the wives of the mine owners.) Beyond charity, a few extremely wealthy capitalists have employed some of the surplus-value they have extraced from workers for "philanthropy." (see below)

In expanded reproduction, or accumulation, surplus-value is used to buy more means of production and to hire more workers in order to expand both the scale of production and to expand the amount of surpus-value/money realized from enlarged sales. Such expanded reproduction in industry, however, requires that both the new means of production and the new workers be available. Therefore, current production must produce not only the means of production necessary to replace worn-out or used up means of production but also new means of production available in exchange for surplus-value that can be used to expand production. At the same time, current production must produce sufficient means of subsistence to support the expanded reproduction of the working class, i.e., the procreation and rearing of children. author: Unknown
title: Fransa: Öğrenciler alanlara egemen oluyor; sokaklar 13 Ekim'de yeni dalgaya hazırlanıyor
content:
Fransa'da öğretmen eksikliğine, kalabalık sınıflara ve yetersiz eğitim koşullarına karşı başlayan liseliler hareketi, perşembe günü Paris'in Bastille Meydanı'nda düzenlenen büyük bir gösteriyle üçüncü haftasını tamamladı. Hükümetin önlemlerini yetersiz bulan liseliler, üniversiteliler ve sendikalar,13 Ekim Salı'yı ülke çapında yeni bir eylem ve grev günü ilan ettiler.  


"Bastille'in zaptı"


Perşembe günü Paris'te Cumhuriyet Meydanı'ndan (Place de la République) yürüyüşe geçen öğrenciler Bastille'e ulaştı. Çevre banliyölerden gelen lise gruplarına üniversiteliler, öğretmenler, sendikacılar ve siyasi örgütler katıldı.


Meydandaki kalabalığın fotoğraflarını paylaşan Boyun Eğmeyen Fransa (La France insoumise – LFI) lideri Jean-Luc Mélenchon, 1789 Fransız Devrimi'ne gönderme yaparak “Bastille yeniden zaptedildi" ("La Bastille est reprise") dedi.


Öğrenciler Bastille'de yeni eylem kararını, hükümetin eğitim sistemindeki sorunlara yönelik ilk somut önlemleri açıkladığı gün ilan ettiler. Öğrenci temsilcileri, geçici öğretmen görevlendirmelerinin krizin nedenlerini ortadan kaldırmayacağını açıkladı.

Lise Öğrencileri Sendikalar Birliği (Union syndicale lycéenne) Eş Genel Sekreteri Marius Mesnil, Eğitim Bakanı'yla görüşmelerin ardından taleplerinin yalnızca küçük bir bölümünün karşılandığını belirterek mücadelenin süreceğini söyledi.


71 bin 500 gösterici, 504 gözaltı


İçişleri Bakanlığına göre Fransa genelindeki yürüyüşlere 71 bin 500, Paris'teki gösterilere ise 24 bin 500 kişi katıldı. Bakanlık, okul önlerindeki protestolara katılanların sayısını ayrıca 55 bin olarak açıkladı. 


Gün boyunca 504 kişi gözaltına alındı. Bakanlık 48 polisin ve jandarma personelinin yaralandığını bildirdi. Göstericilerin yaralı toplamı açıklanmadı.


6 Ekim'deki eylemlere hükümete göre 266 bin, organizatörlere göre ise 450 bin kişi katılmıştı. Perşembe günkü katılım daha düşük olsa da lise işgalleri, okul girişlerinin kapatılması ve yerel gösteriler sürdü.


Eğitim Bakanı 3 bin öğretmen görevlendirecek


Eğitim Bakanı Édouard Geffray, perşembe akşamı TF1 televizyonunda, öğretmen eksikliğinin en ağır yaşandığı okullara 9-13 Ekim arasında 3 bin yedek öğretmen gönderileceğini duyurdu.


Geffray, 114 lisede durumun çok ciddi, yaklaşık 400 okulda ise önemli sorunların bulunduğunu belirtti. Yüzlerce yeni personel alınabileceğini de söyledi.


Ancak 3 bin kişilik görevlendirme, yeni kadrolar açılmasından çok mevcut yedek öğretmenlerin ihtiyaç duyulan okullara dağıtılmasını öngörüyor.


Başbakan Sébastien Lecornu, ekim sonuna kadar öğrenci taleplerine mali kaynakları belirlenmiş yanıtlar vereceklerini açıkladı. Öğrenci örgütleri ise bu takvimi yeterli bulmadı.


Öğrenciler ne istiyor?


Hareketin talepleri boş geçen derslerin doldurulmasıyla sınırlı değil. Liseliler öğretmen ve yardımcı personel sayısının artırılmasını, sınıfların küçültülmesini, bakımsız okul binalarının yenilenmesini ve uzun okul günlerinin kısaltılmasını istiyor.


▶︎

 Öğrenci sendikaları eğitime 10 milyar avro ek kaynak ayrılmasını talep ediyor.


▶︎

 Üniversitelilerin katılımıyla Parcoursup yerleştirme sisteminin kaldırılması ve yükseköğrenime erişimin genişletilmesi de talepler arasına girdi.


▶︎

 Örgütler, üniversite yemekhanelerindeki bir avroluk öğün uygulamasının bütün öğrencilere yayılmasını istiyor.


LFI, 8 Ekim açıklamasında talepleri desteklediğini ve 13 Ekim'de öğrencilerin yanında olacağını duyurdu. Hükümetin polis müdahalelerini eleştirdi.


Banliyö öğrencileri ön saflarda


Paris yürüyüşünde çevre ilçelerle kent merkezindeki liselerin ortak hareket etmesi dikkat çekti.


Le Monde muhabirlerinin izlediği yürüyüşte Paris ilçeleri lise koordinasyonunun pankartları, Genel İş Konfederasyonu'nun (CGT) ve sol örgütlerin bayraklarıyla birlikte taşındı.


Charlemagne Lisesinden 16 yaşındaki Eliana, gazeteye özellikle dezavantajlı ilçelerdeki öğrencileri desteklemek için gösteriye katıldığını söyledi. Başbakan Lecornu'nün vaatlerini ikna edici bulmadığını belirtti.


Mediapart da Bastille'deki öğrencilerin artık yeni vaatler beklemediklerini aktardı. Gazetenin görüştüğü gençler mücadeleyi en az 17 Ekim'e kadar sürdürmek istediklerini söyledi. Bu tarih, 13 Ekim'deki sendikal eylemden farklı bir hedefi işaret ediyor. Harekette yer alanların bir bölümü eylemleri gelecek hafta boyunca sürdürme eğiliminde. 


Bastille'de polis müdahalesi


Bastille Meydanı'ndaki gösteri akşam saatlerinde polis müdahalesiyle sona erdi.


AFP'ye göre bazı göstericilerin polise kaldırım …

author: Sharon Zhang
title: JD Vance Defines Socialism in US as Replacing Americans “With Foreign Workers”
content:
When asked to define the term, the vice president stuttered, saying, “it’s a hard term to define these days.”

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

When asked to define socialism on Thursday, Vice President JD Vance said that the rising left-wing ideology means a desire to “replace American workers with foreign workers” — a bizarre response coming from an administration that has made anti-socialist policies one of its central priorities.

Vance spoke to the press about the Trump administration’s announcement on Thursday that it is suspending Microsoft, Adobe, and other firms from a program that grants green cards to workers who work in the U.S. under H-1B visas.

Following his press conference, Vance was asked to give his definition of socialism in response to the growing number of socialist candidates running for office across the U.S. this election cycle.

Vance stuttered, saying “it’s a hard term to define these days” and that “I don’t know what the term means anymore.”

“Classically, you would think socialism is about prioritizing workers, and yet in reality I guarantee that most of the self-described socialists running across the United States of America are going to howl about this announcement today, which is prioritizing American workers over foreign workers,” he said, using a racist definition of “Americans” that excludes people who move from other countries.

H-1B visas are issued for highly skilled jobs, typically in science, technology, engineering, and math (STEM) fields, that people already in the U.S. aren’t likely to fill. Because of that, H1-B visas are already highly limited, though research has found that such workers are a boon to the U.S. economy and can even help raise other U.S. workers’ salaries.

“I think in reality, what it actually means in the American context is that you want to replace American workers with foreign workers and you want boys to play in girls’ sports. That’s what unites the socialists I see running across the United States of America today,” Vance said.

“They love the idea of replacing American workers with foreign workers, which suggests to me it’s not really about the working class, it’s about their hatred of native-born citizens,” he went on.

It’s unclear what socialist proposals Vance is referring to.

Many left-wing candidates are opposed to the Trump administration’s mass deportation policies, which, along with being horrific and abusive, harm the economy. Time and again, research has found that immigration contributes to the growth of the economy, contributing to tax revenue and helping to bolster welfare programs and the labor market in the U.S.

As Vance suggests, labor is indeed a central tenet of socialism. Democratic socialist candidates and socialist organizations and activists in the U.S. have a strong focus on worker rights and the labor movement, which is a major source of power and unity on the left. Recent polls have found that democratic socialist candidates outpoll those who back Trump.

Additionally, there isn’t evidence of left-wing candidates for office saying that they have a “hatred of native-born citizens.” In fact, it is the Trump administration that has been endangering U.S. citizens with its fascist anti-immigration policies. President Donald Trump has famously sought to drastically upend birthright citizenship, and his Department of Homeland Security has detained at least 500 U.S. citizens in its mass deportation campaign across the U.S.

As Trump cracks down on political speech, independent media is increasingly necessary.

author: rezgar2
title: From Hierarchical Organization to Networked Democratic Organization, Organizational Renewal of the Left in the Digital Age
content:
Rezgar Akrawi: It is no secret that the left in many countries of the world has seen a decline in recent years. There are many reasons for this decline, objective and subjective, yet organizational structure and the forms of work and leadership have played a large part in it. I therefore believe that this stage requires a gradual shift from a hierarchical structure to a horizontal one, in which the base, the new generations and women have the greatest role in shaping policies and choosing leaders, and in which the leadership supports the base, backs it and coordinates its work.


Author


Rezgar Akrawi


رزكار عقراوي


    Submitted by

rezgar2

 on October 8, 2026


Organizational Renewal of the Left in the Digital Age


From Hierarchical Organization to Networked Democratic Organization


Rezgar Akrawi


”Freedom is always and exclusively the freedom of those who think differently.” Rosa Luxemburg


How We Run the Party Today Reflects How We Will Run Society Tomorrow


This text starts from the conviction that a left party is a miniature of the society it seeks to build and to run, and that its bylaws give an early picture of the kind of administration it would offer if it came to lead the state.

 The way decisions are made inside the party, the place of the rank and file in making them, the limits on the powers of the leadership and the way it is elected, and the degree of respect for dissenting opinion all give the masses a practical answer to an essential question. Will power in the society we aspire to rest in the hands of the masses themselves and under their continuous oversight, or will it be concentrated in the hands of limited bodies, however good their intentions?


To take one example, a party whose rank and file elect its leadership and hold it to account, in which positions rotate and the right of the minority to express itself openly is protected, offers a working picture of a state in which the people elect those who govern them and hold them to account, in which power changes hands and the rights of the opposition are protected.

Hence the importance of bylaws that embody, starting today, the values of democracy, participation, transparency and rotation that we promise society for tomorrow.


The idea for this text came from a debate now under way in the Iraqi left, after the Iraqi Communist Party put its draft bylaws up for public discussion ahead of its Twelfth National Congress.


What I put forward, however, is a view of left organization in general, and it concerns all parties and organizations of the left, in the Global South and in the West alike. I write from personal experience in the ranks of the left movement since the 1980s, in which I knew clandestine work and the strict centralism it imposed, a centralism that was at the time a condition of survival and whose historical necessity I fully recognize.


The question carries particular weight in the Middle East and the countries of the Global South, where many organizations of the left still reproduce organizational mechanisms that were shaped under conditions of clandestine work and persecution by dictatorial regimes. Those mechanisms served the forces of the left in their time, and some of their elements may remain necessary wherever repression persists, yet many of them have become outdated and unable to keep pace with the times. Left parties in Europe and North America face similar questions of their own, from declining membership to the drift of the new generation away from traditional party forms.

Capitalism, meanwhile, renews its mechanisms of work and its forms of organization by the minute, and it may prove hard to confront it with organizational structures that have not developed adequately for decades.


The renewal I am calling for rests on four pillars.


First:

 The various socialist ideas and experiences, past and present, approached through an open and critical reading that benefits from their strengths and achievements and learns from their shortcomings and failures, at the intellectual and the organizational level alike.


Second:

 Knowledge, which is now open and widely accessible and no longer the preserve of a particular group that monopolizes the interpretation of reality.


Third:

 Rights consciousness, which has advanced greatly on questions of freedom of expression, full equality for women, human rights, the rights of minorities, the environment and personal freedoms.


Fourth:

 The digital revolution, which …

author: Charlotte Reck
title: Labour’s Byelection Candidate Stayed Quiet on Israel’s Genocide in Gaza
content:
The Labour candidate seeking to win former prime minister Keir Starmer’s seat has failed to condemn Israel’s genocide in Gaza but has criticised the recent Green party

‘Zionism is Racism’ motion

 as “divisive”. 


Sagal Abdi-Wali, a Starmer ally and leader of Camden council, is running against Green leader Zack Polanski in the Holborn and St Pancras byelection, which is widely considered to be a two-horse race between Labour and the Greens.


Abdi-Wali has not publicly spoken about Israel’s devastation of Gaza at any point between October 2023 and her selection as Labour’s byelection candidate, according to a detailed

feature in Tribune magazine.

 


Abdi-Wali also drawn criticism for

dodging questions

 about Israel’s genocide on the campaign trail. 


Camden council, led by Abdi-Wali since May after four years serving as a councillor, has seen its investments in US spytech firm Palantir, which supplies military tech to Israel, soar by over 1,200% since October 2023, according to FOI disclosures

first shared with Declassified UK

.  


The council’s overall holdings in companies complicit in Israel’s apartheid, occupation and genocide of the Palestinian people, including weapons manufacturer Elbit Systems, have increased in value by nearly 30% – worth £28m – since June 2024. 


The council has repeatedly ignored calls for divestment. 


Abdi-Wali also failed to sign the

Palestine Solidarity Campaign’s pledge

 calling on local government candidates to commit to working to end complicity in genocide. It was signed by more than 1,600 councillors from various parties – including 30 Labour party councillors in the neighbouring borough of Islington – ahead of the May local elections. 


At a Board of Deputies-organised hustings in late September, she acknowledged the “strength of feeling that the conflict in Palestine and Israel has brought to communities here” and said she wanted to “bring a sense of hope to parliament”.


When candidates were asked

“are you a Zionist, yes or no?”

, Polanski declared himself an “anti-Zionist”, while Abdi-Wali did not deliver a straight answer, instead saying: “I believe in a two-state solution.”

 


Labour’s candidate has been more vocal on the Greens’ ‘Zionism is Racism’ motion, passed just days ago with 1,022 member votes to 813 at the party’s conference.


“It has been brought up to me by people literally at the school gates this morning, of how, 


like, divisive they found that motion and how worried they are by it,” Abdi-Wali

told The Standard

. “I think it’s worrying for anyone who believes in a two-state solution,” she added.

author: cnt.es
title: El sindicato de inquilinas consigue una confluencia sindical histórica
content:
«

Ha sido una reunión histórica

». Así ha calificado Nieves Román, secretaria general de la CNT, la asamblea celebrada este miércoles, 7 de octubre, entre los sindicatos de toda la geografía nacional. Sindicatos como CNT, CGT, Solidaridad Obrera, LAB, CCOO, UGT, Co.bas, Confederación Intersindical, Intersindical Alternativa de Catalunya, Intersindical Valenciana, o la Unión de actores y actrices han confluido ante el llamamiento del Sindicato de Inquilinas para la organización de «una huelga general de verdad, en la que se detenga la producción y lo paremos todo».


Las reivindicaciones de la huelga general pasan por «

obtener reformas avanzadas en favor de la clase trabajadora con respecto al problema de la vivienda

» y «

abrir un nuevo período de luchas de cara a los próximos meses y años, con el sindicalismo en el centro y con capacidad de frenar a la reacción

». La decisión de la fecha para la huelga, 11 de noviembre como proponían Inquilinas, fue celebrada con aplausos por las personas asistentes. Lamentablemente, momentos después contrastó con la triste noticia del fallecimiento de Mari Carmen, apoyada por el Sindicato de Inquilinas y personalmente por algunas de las personas asistentes al acto.


«

Podríamos decir que nunca se celebró una cumbre como ésta

»- nos confirma el historiador Juan Pablo Calero. «

Podemos congratularnos de estar más cerca de conseguir una unidad más amplia del movimiento obrero. Queremos que el sindicalismo llegue a todos los sectores, incluyendo juventud, población migrante y otros que tradicionalmente han estado oprimidos.

» – ha señalado Román.


El sindicato CNT se encuentra actualmente manteniendo reuniones, tanto a nivel interno como externo, para la preparación de la huelga, y, previsiblemente, la anunciará en unos días. «

Tenemos que medir muy bien el encaje legal, contactar con otras organizaciones y, lo más importante, consultar a nuestras bases y tomar una decisión democrática, como mandan nuestros principios anarcosindicalistas

» – concluyó Román.


La entrada

El sindicato de inquilinas consigue una confluencia sindical histórica

 se publicó primero en

Confederación Nacional del Trabajo

author: infolibre
title: “ΟΥΤΕ ΣΤΗΝ ΕΛΕΥΣΙΝΑ, ΟΥΤΕ ΠΟΥΘΕΝΑ”, φασιστική επίθεση σε 32χρονο, μέλος του αντιφασιστικού κινήματος στην Ελευσίνα την Πέμπτη 8/10
content:
Την Πέμπτη 8/10, το βράδυ, ένας 32χρονος, μέλος του αντιφασιστικού κινήματος δέχθηκε δολοφονική επίθεση από ομάδα φασιστών στην Ελευσίνα. Ο 32χρονος δέχθηκε μαχαιριές στο πόδι και διακομίστηκε στο Τζάνειο Νοσοκομείο Πειραιά όπου νοσηλεύεται. Χθες, μετά το γεγονός, πραγματοποιήθηκε αντανακλαστική αντιφασιστική πορεία στην Ελευσίνα με κεντρικό σύνθημα “Ούτε στην Ελευσίνα, ούτε πουθενά, τσακίστε τους φασίστες σε κάθε γειτονιά”.  Παρακάτω οι ανακοινώσεις και απαντήσεις αντιφασιστικών πρωτοβουλιών και οργανώσεων σχετικά με την χθεσινή φασιστική επίθεση καθώς και η ανταπόκριση από την πορεία.


 


Ανακοινώσεις:


Σύλλογος Πολιτισμού «Παύλος Killah P Φύσσας»


ΑΝΑΚΟΙΝΩΣΗ – ΔΕΛΤΙΟ ΤΥΠΟΥ


Η δολοφονική επίθεση γνωστών οργανωμένων νεοναζί εναντίον ακτιβιστή του αντιφασιστικού κινήματος στην Ελευσίνα είναι κομβικής σημασίας για την πορεία του φασισμού στην Ελλάδα.


Αν οι φασίστες αφεθούν ξανά ελεύθεροι να επιτίθονται σε όποιον δεν τους αρέσει, σε αντιφασίστες, συνδικαλιστές και μετανάστες, με μαθηματική ακρίβεια θα φτάσουν ξανά στις δολοφονίες.


Είναι άκρως ανησυχητική η αρχική στάση της αστυνομίας που διέρρευσε (και μέρους των ΜΜΕ που αναπαρήγαγαν) το σενάριο της υποτιθέμενης “ληστείας” ενώ ήταν εξ αρχής γνωστά και επιβεβαιωμένα τα κίνητρα των νεοναζί.


Καλούμε όλους τους φορείς, τις οργανώσεις και τις συλλογικότητες από κάθε κοινωνικό και πολιτικό χώρο, σε άμεση κινητοποίηση πριν να είναι ξανά αργά.


Καλούμε κάθε αρμόδιο θεσμικό φορέα να αναλάβει τις ευθύνες του.


Δε θα επιτρέψουμε ξανά τη θεσμική ανοχή ή και συγκάλυψη των ναζιστικών εγκλημάτων.


Να δράσουμε τώρα!


Σύλλογος Πολιτισμού


«Παύλος Killah P Φύσσας»


9.10.2026


Προλεταριακό Αντιφασιστικό Μέτωπο Δυτικών Προαστίων


ΦΑΣΙΣΤΕΣ ΤΟ ΜΕΛΛΟΝ ΣΑΣ ΕΙΝΑΙ ΠΡΟΔΙΑΓΕΓΡΑΜΜΕΝΟ


Η Δολοφονική επίθεση με μαχαίρι στον αντιφασίστα στην Ελευσίνα θα απαντηθεί κοινωνικά και μαχητικά.


Καλούμε όλο το αντιφασιστικό κίνημα σε πλήρη συσπείρωση και μαχητική θέση ενάντια στους μαχαιροβγαλτές νοσταλγούς των ναζί.


Ο φασισμός δεν πέφτει από τον ουρανό. Γεννιέται μέσα στις αντιθέσεις της καπιταλιστικής κοινωνίας και αποτελεί την πιο ακραία και αντιδραστική μορφή υπεράσπισης της εξουσίας του κεφαλαίου. Όταν η κοινωνική οργή μεγαλώνει, ο φασισμός επιχειρεί να της δώσει άλλον στόχο. Να στρέψει τον εργαζόμενο ενάντια στον μετανάστη, τον φτωχό ενάντια στον φτωχότερο, τον έναν καταπιεσμένο ενάντια στον άλλο. Ο ρατσισμός και ο εθνικισμός είναι τα όπλα του για να διασπά την εργατική τάξη και να κρύβει τον πραγματικό ταξικό αντίπαλο.


Γι’ αυτό η αποφυλάκιση του Ηλία Κασιδιάρη και η δηλωμένη πρόθεσή του να επιστρέψει στην πολιτική δράση δεν μπορούν να αντιμετωπίζονται με αδιαφορία. Η Χρυσή Αυγή δεν ήταν απλώς ένα ακροδεξιό κόμμα. Ήταν μια ναζιστική οργάνωση με τάγματα εφόδου, ξυλοδαρμούς και δολοφονικές επιθέσεις. Δεν ξεχνάμε τους Αιγύπτιους αλιεργάτες, τους συνδικαλιστές του ΠΑΜΕ, τον Σαχζάτ Λουκμάν. Δεν ξεχνάμε τον Παύλο Φύσσα. Και δεν πρόκειται να αφήσουμε τη μνήμη αυτών των εγκλημάτων να ξεθωριάσει για να παρουσιαστούν ξανά οι ίδιοι άνθρωποι και οι ίδιες ιδέες ως κάτι «καινούργιο» ή «αντισυστημικό».


Σε μια εποχή πολέμων, ακρίβειας, φτώχειας και ανασφάλειας, η ακροδεξιά προσπαθεί ξανά να δηλητηριάσει την κοινωνική οργή με ρατσισμό, εθνικισμό και μίσος. Προσπαθεί να πείσει τον εργαζόμενο ότι για τη ζωή που του στερούν φταίει ο πρόσφυγας, ο μετανάστης, ο διαφορετικός. Να μετατρέψει την αγανάκτηση σε τυφλό μίσος και να αφήσει στο απυρόβλητο τις πραγματικές σχέσεις εκμετάλλευσης και εξουσίας.


Απέναντι σε αυτή την απειλή δεν χωρά εφησυχασμός. Ο φασισμός δεν αντιμετωπίζεται με σιωπή και αναμονή. Αντιμετωπίζεται πολιτικά και μαζικά, στους χώρους δουλειάς, στις σχολές και στις γειτονιές, με οργάνωση, ταξική αλληλεγγύη και συλλογική δράση. Η αντιφασιστική πάλη δεν είναι τελετουργία μιας επετείου. Είναι καθημερινό μέτωπο απέναντι στον φασισμό, στον ρατσισμό και στις κοινωνικές συνθήκες που τους επιτρέπουν να σηκώνουν ξανά κεφάλι.


ΦΑΣΙΣΤΕΣ ΘΑ ΠΕΡΑΣΟΥΜΕ ΑΠΟ ΠΑΝΩ ΣΑΣ

title: AfD im Bundestag fordert Verbot von „Antifa“, indymedia.de und Roter Hilfe
content:
Die rechtsextreme AfD versucht in Deutschland auf Bundes- wie auf Länderebene Antifaschismus zu kriminalisieren, anzugreifen und zu verbieten. Wie läuft das im Bundestag und wie auf Ländereben?


In einem aktuellen Entschließungsantrag für den Deutschen Bundestag fordert die AfD im Rahmen ihrer „24 Maßnahmen gegen linksextremistische Gewalt und Terror“ unter anderem ein Verbot der „Antifa“ sowie der Roten Hilfe. Hinsichtlich der Antifa, richtet sich der AfD-Antrag exemplarisch gegen die„Antifa Süd“. Ferner wird ein Verbot und Abschaltung der Website de.indymedia.org gefordert.


Der AfD-Antrag- ein Sammelsurium an Forderungen


Erst am 06.10.2026 legte die AfD-Fraktion im Bundestag, darunter so berüchtigte Rechtsextremisten wie

Martin Hess

,

Gottfried Curio

,

Bernd Baumann

,

Maximilian Krah

, einen achtseitigen Entschließungsantrag (

als PDF

) vor, in welchem sie 24 Forderungen aufstellt.


Das Sammelsurium der Forderungen reicht von einer „erheblichen personellen Verstärkung der für die Aufklärung und Ermittlung im Bereich des Linksextremismus zuständigen Abteilungen der Sicherheitsbehörden“, über „regelmäßige Erstellung von internen Lagebildern durch das BKA zur aktuellen Gefährdungslage durch gewaltorientierte Linksextremisten mit Serien- und Musteranalyse“ bis hin zur Forderung der „dauerhafte(n) Räumungen aller besetzten Szeneobjekte, (…) wie beispielsweise der „Rigaer Straße 94“ in Berlin oder der „Roten Flora“ in Hamburg, die rechtswidrig von Linksextremisten in Besitz genommen wurden und von denen aus wiederholt Straftaten verübt worden sind oder die als Unterschlupf für linksextremistische Gewalttäter dienen“.


Aber auch ein „Verbot und Abschaltung der Website de.indymedia.org als Nachfolgeplattform von linksunten.indymedia.org“, wird gefordert, ferner die „konsequente Prüfung von Verboten nach dem Vereinsgesetz in Bezug auf linksextremistische Gruppierungen, die sich unter der Bezeichnung „Antifa“oder „Antifaschistische Aktion“ zusammengeschlossen haben“ sowie ein „Verbot der Roten Hilfe e.V. (RH), da diese bundesweit „linksextremistische und mithin verfassungsfeindliche Ziele von unterschiedlicher Intensität“ verfolgt“.


Begründung der AfD


Der Einstieg des Antrages der AfD bildet ein Verweis auf „die Vorgänge rund um die Berliner Wahlsiegerin DIE LINKE, an deren Wahlparty Vertreter aus dem Clanmilieu und Islamisten teilgenommen haben“, diese würden „dabei nur die Spitze eines Eisbergs dar(stellen), auf den Deutschland sicherheitspolitisch ungebremst zusteuert“. Anschließend geht es in einem wilden Parforceritt von einem „gezielten Brandanschlag auf das Stromnetz im Raum Berlin Steglitz-Zehlendorf zu Beginn des Jahres“, welchen der „Vulkangruppe“ zugerechnet wird, über einen weiteren „Anschlag (…) im Juni dieses Jahres in Reutlingen“ über welchen auf „der linksextremistischen Internetseite „Switch Off““ umfassend berichtet worden sei. Nicht fehlen dürfen „die konspirativ vorbereiteten Überfälle der sogenannten „Antifa-Ost“ oder auch „Hammerbande“ genannt, denn diese würden „das ganze Ausmaß der Eskalation (zeigen): Gezielte Angriffe auf Menschen, bei denen Opfer schwerste Verletzungen erlitten haben.“


Die RAF wird auch noch erwähnt, denn „bei den Hammerbandenprozessen handelt es sich (…) um die umfangreichsten Verfahren gegen Linksextremisten seit den RAF-Prozessen vor knapp 50 Jahren“, so die AfD.


Weitere Schlagworte „Missbrauch der Versammlungsfreiheit durch Linksextremisten“, Bekämpfung der „Gefahren durch linke Militanz“ vermittels der oben genannten Verbote, denn, so die AfD-Abgeordneten, „um diese Fehlentwicklungen aufzuhalten, müssen auch linksextremistische Strukturen zerschlagen werden. Vereinsrechtliche Verbotsverfahren gegen gewaltlegitimierende Strukturen der Antifa müssen vorrangig geprüft und konsequent umgesetzt werden“.


Die Rote Hilfe ist der AfD besonders ein Dorn im Auge, denn, so die Begründung des Antrags, die Rote Hilfe sei „mit rund 14.400 Mitgliedern und bundesweit rund 50 Ortsgruppen die größte und eine der wichtigsten Gruppierungen im deutschen Linksextremismus. Sie bietet nicht nur einen Legitimationsrahmen für die Begehung von Straf- und Gewalttaten“. Insbesondere befürworte und unterstütze sie „die Anwendung von Gewalt als Mittel der politischen Auseinandersetzung“.


Fazit und Ausblick


Der Bundestag hat am 08.10.2026 rund eine Stunde lang über den Antrag der AfD im Plenum

öffentlich beraten

. Vermutlich wird er im Anschluss daran an die Ausschüsse …

title: Sparkasse und GLS kündigen (z.B.) ABC Dresden und Rote Hilfe: Debanking gegen linke, solidarische Strukturen durch langen Arm der US-Regierung?
content:
Dossier


„

Im November und Dezember 2025 wurden solidarischen Organisationen und Einzelpersonen Bankkonten gekündigt – ohne Begründung, teils fristlos. Diese Praxis heißt Debanking und bedeutet den Ausschluss aus grundlegenden Bankdienstleistungen. Betroffen sind Initiativen, die sich gegen Krieg, Repression und soziale Ausgrenzung einsetzen. Spenden werden blockiert, Strukturen handlungsunfähig gemacht, Existenzen unter Druck gesetzt. Dagegen hat sich ein Netzwerk aus Betroffenen und solidarischen Unterstützer:innen gegründet. Wir machen Debanking sichtbar, vernetzen uns und bauen politischen Druck auf!…“

Meldung von „Debanking stoppen“ vom Dezember 2025


 („Debanking stoppen“) des Bündnisses gegen Debanking („Debanking trifft solidarische Strukturen“) – siehe mehr Informationen zur Roten Hilfe, ABC Dresden, Folgen und Widerstand:


Konto bleibt: Rote Hilfe gewinnt auch das Hauptsacheverfahren gegen Sparkasse Göttingen beim Landgericht Göttingen


„

Rote Hilfe gewinnt auch Hauptsacheverfahren gegen Sparkasse Göttingen. Das Landgericht Göttingen hat die Kündigung des Kontos für unwirksam erklärt. Ein wichtiger Erfolg gegen politisch motiviertes Debanking und für die Solidaritätsarbeit der Roten Hilfe. (…) Ein zusätzliches Risiko durch die US-Listung der sogenannten „Antifa Ost“ als Terrororganisation  konnte die Sparkasse nicht plausibel machen. Das OLG stellte zudem klar, dass die Rote Hilfe nicht eine Organisation „Antifa Ost“ finanziert, sondern gemäß ihrer Satzung Beschuldigte und Angeklagte in den entsprechenden Verfahren unterstützt. Die US-Einstufung selbst entfaltet keine unmittelbare rechtliche Wirkung in Deutschland. Dieser Beurteilung des OLG schloss sich das Landgericht heute »vollumfänglich« an.


Damit hat die Rote Hilfe nach den Erfolgen im Eilverfahren nun auch in der Hauptsache Recht bekommen. Für die Rote Hilfe geht es über den eigenen Fall hinaus auch um die Frage, wie weit politische Entscheidungen und Sanktionslisten aus Drittstaaten auf zivilgesellschaftliche Strukturen in Deutschland durchschlagen können

…“

Pressemitteilung vom 08.10.2026


 („Konto bleibt: Rote Hilfe gewinnt Hauptsacheverfahren“)


OLG Braunschweig hat die Berufung der Sparkasse Göttingen zum Konto von Rote Hilfe (und damit willkürliche Kontenkündigungen) zurückgewiesen


OLG: Sparkasse Göttingen muss Konto der Roten Hilfe fortführen

„

Das OLG Braunschweig hat die Berufung der Sparkasse Göttingen zurückgewiesen: Das Konto der Rote Hilfe e.V. muss vorerst weitergeführt werden. Für die angeführten Verdachtsmomente sah das Gericht keine ausreichende Tatsachengrundlage. Für die Rote Hilfe e.V. ist das ein wichtiges Signal gegen Debanking und gegen politischen Druck auf zivilgesellschaftliche Strukturen

.

(…)


Die Sparkasse hatte das Konto am 9. Dezember 2025 gekündigt und stützte sich dabei unter anderem auf Spendenaufrufe des Vereins mit den Verwendungszwecken „unverzagt“ und „Budapest“. Daraus leitete sie gesteigerte Prüfpflichten nach dem Geldwäschegesetz ab, die das Konto für sie unwirtschaftlich gemacht hätten.


Das Gericht hat den Verdacht als unbegründet bewertet. Er habe einer Tatsachengrundlage entbehrt. Die Sparkasse habe die Spendenaufrufe inhaltlich falsch wiedergegeben. Der Verein habe nicht zur „Unterstützung der Antifa-Ost“ aufgerufen, sondern zur „Unterstützung im Antifa-Ost-Verfahren“ und „gegen die Auslieferung und Unterstützung verfolgter Antifas in Ungarn“. Das entspreche dem satzungsgemäßen Zweck des Vereins, Beschuldigten und Angeklagten faire Verfahren zu ermöglichen. Auch eine Verschleierung sah das Gericht nicht. Kurze, prägnante Verwendungszwecke seien bei rund 2.300 Zahlungseingängen nachvollziehbar, um Spenden einzelnen Kampagnen zuordnen zu können, und der Verein habe diese Zuordnung offen vorgenommen. Dass andere Banken dem Verein nach der Kündigung kein Konto eröffnet haben, belege den Verdacht ebenfalls nicht, zumal die Gründe dafür nicht bekannt seien.


Auch die Eilbedürftigkeit hat das Gericht bestätigt. Der Anspruch des Vereins auf Fortführung des Kontos sei weitgehend eindeutig. Würde man den Verein auf das Hauptsacheverfahren verweisen, müsste er zunächst das Konto wechseln und im Erfolgsfall wieder zurückwechseln. Dieser doppelte Aufwand wäre angesichts der Vielzahl von Zahlungseingängen und Mitgliedern so erheblich, dass er faktisch einer Verweigerung von Rechtsschutz gleichkäme. Die Interessen der Sparkasse müssten demgegenüber zurücktreten

…“

author: labor4pal
title: Eyewitness report: Strikers and students rock France, Anti-fascism and Palestinian liberation mixed with anger at president Emmanuel Macron and the establishment (Socialist Worker-UK)
content:
Anti-fascism and Palestinian liberation mixed with anger at president Emmanuel Macron and the establishment

On the streets of Paris (Picture: Guy Smallman)

There were protests in 40 cities across France on Tuesday as workers and parents joined the movement of secondary school students demanding a future.

In Paris, organisers said 100,000 packed the streets. They were overwhelmingly young school and university students.

Young people chanted anti-fascist slogans. They included, “La jeunesse emmerde le Front National”—“The youth tell the Front National to fuck off” in a reference to the previous name of the fascist RN. And, “Siamo tutti antifascisti”—“We are all anti-fascist”.

They sang the Internationale and the French national anthem La Marseillaise. And there were Palestinian flags and chants of “free Palestine”. Other home made placards referenced the student and worker uprising of 1968.

When the presidential candidate for the left wing LFI party, Jean-Luc Mélenchon, arrived at the start of the march, he was mobbed by crowds of people. Both young and older protesters greeted him with chants of “president Mélenchon”.

Mélenchon called on his supporters, including many members of parliament, to join the protests. He wore a white armband on Tuesday to symbolise his support for the high school students.

As the march arrived in Place de la Nation, hundreds of riot police attacked with huge clouds of tear gas and charged at the crowd with batons. Protesters threw fireworks and set bins on fire.

Nora, Sarah and Sonia, three university students, spoke to Socialist Worker about their reasons for joining the protest.

“We protest for the rights of high school students,” they said. “All the media talks about is violence. But there are real reasons behind their protests.

“The RN is fascist. It’s homophobic and Islamophobic”.

Another student, Alice, said that young people are worried about their futures, “We are all worried about fascism, every student is worried about that. And about finding a job, everything is kind of scary.

“High school students are very stressed. We went through that so we want to be here with them.”

Trade unionists linked arms and faced up to cops with tear gas.

Pierre works in the tax office and is part of the Solidaires union federation. He told Socialist Worker, “I am on strike today, in solidarity with the students against repression and because we have the same problems with austerity.”

Clement, from the CFDT union federation, told Socialist Worker, “The demands of the school students are totally legitimate. The buildings are crumbling, there are rats in the classrooms, there are 30, 35 or even 40 people in a classroom.

“It’s a terrible period with the far right rising across Europe. We could see fascism in France for the second time in its history.”

Clement added that the current president Emmanuel Macron has “rolled out the red carpet for the RN’s Marine Le Pen”.

Another protester mentioned that there are already fascists joining the police force and that Le Pen would use them to smash the movement on the streets if she was in office.

Meet the pupils’ blockade: ‘We are young, determined and revolutionary’

Macron’s austerity measures and repression, combined with the normalisation of racism against migrants has created the conditions for the far right to rise.

Le Pen is currently leading in the polls, while Mélenchon is currently in second place.

The best hope of beating Le Pen will be if the movement stays on the streets and links the anger of the students with the power of the organised working class.

Key opportunities to deepen the movement are coming this month. Total Energy workers are set to strike Thursday—and there is a day of action on 17 October.

Anti-fascists are planning to demonstrate against the far right RN party’s conference on 24 October.

If the movement of school students and strikes deepens, it has the power to transform the political situation in France.

title: Bring Maja back: Antifaschist*in muss sofort aus Ungarn hierher überstellt werden!
content:
Bring Maja back: Antifaschist*in muss sofort aus Ungarn hierher überstellt werden!


Der Fall gehört zum sog. Budapest-Komplex: Maja und weiteren Antifaschist*innen wird vorgeworfen, sich im Februar 2023 an körperlichen Auseinandersetzungen mit Nazis am Rand des

NS

-verherrlichenden Großevents „Tag der Ehre“ in Budapest beteiligt zu haben. Seither läuft eine internationale Verfolgungsjagd gegen Antifaschist*innen, die vor allem von Ungarn und Deutschland vorangetrieben wird. Ende 2023 wurde Maja in Berlin von deutschen Ermittlungsorganen verhaftet und im Juni 2024 in einer rechtswidrigen Nacht-und-Nebel-Aktion an Ungarn ausgeliefert – nur Stunden, bevor das Bundesverfassungsgericht diesen Schritt explizit untersagte: Insbesondere für eine non-binäre antifaschistische Person ist die Situation im weiterhin rechtsautoritären und offen queerfeindlichen Ungarn lebensgefährlich. Das Gericht hatte dabei am 24. Januar 2025 nicht nur die Rechtswidrigkeit von Majas Auslieferung festgestellt, sondern auch die deutschen Behörden verpflichtet, sich für eine schnellstmögliche Rückführung einzusetzen.

Seit diesem Rechtsbruch der deutschen Behörden war Maja unter katastrophalen Haftbedingungen in Budapest eingekerkert: Schimmliges Essen, Ungeziefer in der Zelle, defizitäre Duschmöglichkeiten, ständige nächtliche Kontrollen und demütigende Nacktdurchsuchungen, Trennscheibe bei allen Besuchen – und vor allem anhaltende Isolationshaft, die nach internationalen Standards als Folter gilt. Mit einem mehrwöchigen Hungerstreik protestierte Maja im Sommer 2025 gegen diese unmenschliche Behandlung. Am 17. Juli 2026 kam es sogar zu brutaler körperlicher Gewalt durch vermummtes Wachpersonal, das Maja in der Zelle zusammenschlug, zwangsweise entkleidete, um Maja zum Tragen von nach ihrer Ansicht geschlechtsentsprechender Kleidung zu zwingen, und dann auch noch disziplinarisch verfolgte. Es war genau diese Situation, vor der im Auslieferungsverfahren immer wieder gewarnt worden war.

Für die Farce des offenkundig politischen Schauprozesses in Ungarn war keine angemessene Vorbereitung möglich: Anwaltsgespräche konnten nur beeinträchtigt stattfinden, die meisten Unterlagen lagen nur auf ungarisch vor, und Maja konnte die digitale Akte kaum sichten. Im Gerichtssaal wurde die non-binäre Person in Ketten und an einer Hundeleine vorgeführt, begleitet von medialer Stimmungsmache. Obwohl der Prozess keinerlei Hinweise erbrachte, dass Maja aktiv an den vorgeworfenen Handlungen beteiligt war, belief sich das erstinstanzliche Urteil am 4. Februar 2026 auf acht Jahre Haft unter schwersten Bedingungen. Die Berufung reduzierte dieses absurde Strafmaß am 30. September 2026 nur geringfügig auf sieben Jahre sowie eine Geldstrafe und machte damit erneut deutlich, dass in erster Linie die antifaschistische Haltung bestraft werden sollte.

Dass Maja spätestens nach dem Urteil umgehend zurück nach Deutschland überstellt wird, war ohnehin die bindende Grundvoraussetzung für die rechtswidrige Auslieferung gewesen.

„Der Fall von Maja ist ein politischer und juristischer Skandal, der von den deutschen Behörden durch die nächtliche Auslieferung offen rechtswidrig produziert und seit nunmehr weit über zwei Jahren durch Tatenlosigkeit fortgesetzt wird“, empörte sich Hartmut Brückner vom Bundesvorstand der Roten Hilfe e. V. „Wir fordern insbesondere das Bundesjustizministerium auf, endlich das Urteil des Bundesverfassungsgerichts umzusetzen und sofort die Rücküberstellung in die Wege zu leiten.“ Zudem appellierte Brückner: „Wir rufen die Öffentlichkeit dazu auf, gemeinsam politischen Druck auf die zuständigen Behörden auszuüben – durch Petitionen, öffentliche Proteste und Kampagnen. Schluss mit der Folter in Ungarn: Bring Maja back!“

Damit endete ein politischer Schauprozess, der auf rechtsstaatliche Mindeststandards verzichtete, doch die unmenschlichen Haftbedingungen im ungarischen Kerker dauern an und haben sich in der Strafhaft teilweise noch verschärft. title: Historic Trees Demolished, Land Defenders Arrested and New Treesit at US-Mexico Border
content:
Lochiel, AZ – In the early hours of October 5, Border Patrol agents raided the anti-border camp called “Tierra Libre” on the U.S.-Mexico Border near Lochiel, Arizona. An estimated 200 Border Patrol Agents invaded camp — entering the tracts of private property along the border that had long-shielded land defenders from the authority of the federal agents — and cut down the ancient Grandmother tree that campers had attempted to protect. Less than 24 hours later, land defenders established a new treesit in the immediate path of construction, this time on the Mexican side of the border. 


Although Border Patrol agents were parked along the easement throughout the night, a masked land defender snuck past them and scrambled up into the 50-foot-tall Grandmother tree and into the platform already built there. “This brave warrior climbed right up there,” said Pablo, a land defender who was at camp Tuesday morning. “The new treesit is very much blocking construction, as long as someone is in that tree they will not be able to build their wall.”


Past Coverage:

Treesit Blocks US-Mexico Border Wall Construction for Six Weeks in Arizona


According to multiple sources on the ground who spoke with Unicorn Riot, Border Patrol agents entered private property Monday morning, refusing to show evidence of a warrant allowing them to do so, and refusing to explain what authority granted them that right.


Agents shoved and tackled campers, pointed guns at them, stomped on their necks, and pushed several campers into the barbed wire fence that marks the private property line. One land defender who goes by the name Hoops showed wounds on her hands and wrist to members of the media that she said resulted from agents twice her size tackling her into the barbed wire fence. 


“Border Patrol has been coming onto private property since yesterday morning,” said Rachel, a land defender who spoke with Unicorn Riot about the raids. “No warrants are shown, as far as we can tell there’s no legal ground for them to come onto private property. It seems like they’re pushing through the construction process quickly and will deal with the law later.” 


Construction workers protected by Border Patrol agents used a cherrypicker to cut branches off of the 200-year-old cottonwood Grandmother tree, in which a treesit had been sustained for 71 days. Agents then removed a treesitter stationed to protect the tree from border wall construction.


Within minutes, the Grandmother tree was felled and the treesit destroyed. Ten land defenders were arrested, including the treesitter. Ten more were cited and released.

title: Far Right Gleeful Over Firing Squad Death Sentence for Muslim Fort Hood Shooter
content:
Trump has approved the killing of Muslim US soldier Nidal Malik Hasan — the first Army execution in over 60 years.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Conservative figures have reacted with glee to the Trump administration’s approval of a firing squad death sentence for Muslim Army member Nidal Malik Hasan, in what would be the first execution carried out by the U.S. military in over six decades.

Hasan was convicted of committing a mass shooting at Texas’s Fort Hood in 2009, killing 13 people, with jurors recommending a maximum sentence of death. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth said in September 2025 that he was seeking President Donald Trump’s final approval for the military to execute Hasan, and the Pentagon has since laid out a plan to carry out three more executions for those who remain on the military’s death row.

Sean Parnell, the Pentagon’s spokesperson, announced on Monday that Trump has given his approval for the execution, characterizing Hasan as a “jihadist” and highlighting that he shouted “Allahu Akbar,” meaning “God is great,” during the attack.

“The Secretary of the Army will set the time and place of the execution. Judgement day for Hasan has finally come,” Parnell said in a post on X.

Hasan is a U.S.-born Muslim of Palestinian descent. At the time, he admitted to committing the killings, saying that he was against his upcoming deployment to Afghanistan and opposed to the U.S. military’s biases against Muslims. His family said that he was discriminated against for being Muslim while in the military.

If Hasan’s execution is carried out, this would be the first execution done by the military since 1961, when Army private John Bennett was executed by hanging. Bennett, who was Black, was accused of raping and attempting to kill an Austrian girl, who was white, and retrospective reports said that his case was not tried properly; in the six years leading up to his execution, eight other Black soldiers on the military’s death row were executed, while six others who were white lived.

Execution by firing squad is also relatively rare in the U.S. According to the Death Penalty Information Center, only 34 out of over 8,700 executions in the U.S. between 1890 and 2010 were carried out through firing squads. This method is only legal in a handful of states, but Trump has moved to bring it back in order to ramp up the use of the death penalty.

Typically, in an execution by firing squad, the prisoner is hooded and bound to a chair. A doctor pinpoints the prisoner’s heart and puts a target on it. Between three and five shooters are in an enclosure nearby and aim at the target through a slot; in some protocols, one shooter’s gun is randomly loaded with blanks. The shooters all fire at once, and the prisoner dies via gunshot to the heart, or bleeds out.

Conservatives online were exuberant following Parnell’s announcement, which Hegseth described as “[j]ustice.”

“More of this please. This is what I voted for. More dead jihadists!” said conservative influencer and Trump confidante Laura Loomer.

Some right-wing accounts on X called for the administration to televise the execution for Americans to watch.

“I volunteer to pull the trigger,” said Carl Higbie, a former Navy SEAL and current daily host on far right outlet Newsmax.

“This is the way,” said NewsNation host Katie Pavlich.

The Trump administration’s announcement came just days after the botched execution of Christa Pike in Tennessee. Pike, who was convicted of murdering a classmate in 1995, was hospitalized after Tennessee prison officials administered two doses of pentobarbital that were supposed to kill her, against medical recommendations. Pike’s attorney said on Sunday that she is on a ventilator and in critical condition.

title: Yıldırım: Sentence reductions have become a defence for femicide perpetrators
content:
In Kurdistan, where femicides are widespread alongside special warfare policies, the perpetrators may change, but the methods and defences used after the murders remain the same. Taking their cue from unjust provocation and good conduct sentence reductions granted by the judiciary, perpetrators research defences used in previous cases and make similar statements in court.


Recent femicide cases in Diyarbakır (Amed) have also revealed examples of this pattern. Arselan Akdemir, who murdered Sultan Kara, resorted to the defence, “I am mentally ill. I have a medical report,” while Cemal Alparaslan, who murdered İlayda Alkaş, appeared at his first hearing wearing a tie.


 


Derya Yıldırım, a member of the Board of Directors of the Diyarbakır Bar Association, drew attention to the impact of perpetrators' defences on judicial proceedings in femicide cases. She said sentence reductions granted on grounds such as unjust provocation, good conduct and mental health obscure the history of violence behind femicides.


Yıldırım said the defences used by perpetrators during judicial proceedings are increasingly becoming an established method. She added: “We follow social media and press reports to see which defences have led to sentence reductions in femicide cases and on what grounds the state and judicial authorities grant such reductions. Because reductions for unjust provocation, claims of mental illness and grounds for impunity are accepted without sufficiently detailed investigation, they are becoming a significant defence mechanism for perpetrators.”


Yıldırım pointed out that in most femicide cases, judicial proceedings focus solely on the moment the killing took place, while the woman's life and the violence she experienced before the murder are not adequately examined.


Yıldırım said: “When we look at these cases as a whole, we see that perpetrators are effectively tried only for the moment of the murder, the act of killing itself, while the judicial authorities disregard everything that came before it. We see that the woman had previously been subjected to extensive violence, had sought help from numerous institutions, that no measures were taken, or that merely symbolic restraining orders were issued but never enforced. Unfortunately, none of this is examined during the trial. The focus is placed directly on the act committed at the moment of the killing.”


‘The perpetrator’s actions are not questioned’


Derya Yıldırım said the perpetrator’s actions are not sufficiently scrutinised when courts consider unjust provocation, and continued: “The actions of the male perpetrator are not even discussed. The trial focuses solely on a sentence allegedly uttered by the woman, without any concrete evidence to support it. The statements male perpetrators use to obtain reductions for unjust provocation resonate with certain sections of society. When explaining why an unjust provocation reduction should apply or why he committed the murder at that moment, the perpetrator is also playing to society. He is trying to gain sympathy in the eyes of the public.


When the perpetrator says, ‘She did something like this, so I killed her,’ some sections of society think, ‘He is a man. How could he tolerate that?’ At a certain point, he gains the support of society as well, and unfortunately, this approach is rapidly becoming established in judicial practice.”


‘The perpetrator’s defence is considered, not the history of violence’


Yıldırım stressed that judicial practices must change to prevent femicides and that the violence women experience before being murdered must be taken into account during trials. She said regulations were particularly needed regarding sentence reductions for unjust provocation.


Yıldırım added: “Particularly in femicide cases, no justification for killing a woman should qualify for a reduction on the grounds of unjust provocation. We know very well that the events leading to the murder did not develop suddenly. There is actually a history behind them: the woman being subjected to violence, constantly humiliated, seeking help and being left without a solution. It is absolutely clear, including from a judicial perspective, that the woman's life is in danger. Above all, a serious monitoring mechanism must be established to ensure her protection.”

author: Victoria Law
title: Mississippi Is in Danger of Executing Woman on Death Row, Despite Key Evidence
content:
Lisa Jo Chamberlin’s co-defendant confessed to coercing her into their crime. Will that be enough to stop her execution?

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Lisa Jo Chamberlin’s life has always been a tangle of drug use, abuse, and extreme violence. Her mother drank and used Sudafed heavily during her pregnancy. As a result, Chamberlin was born with Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder (FASD), a group of medical conditions, including poor reasoning and judgment skills, learning disabilities, and intellectual disability, that occur when a fetus is exposed to alcohol.People with FASD are more vulnerable to manipulation by others. For Chamberlin, that vulnerability led to a death sentence.

The 45 women on death row across the country make up 2 percent of the total number of Americans sentenced to death. The vast majority of women behind bars have experienced abuse before arrest. Ninety-six percent of women on death row had experienced gender-based violence before arrest, 80 percenthave intellectual or psychosocial disabilities, and 90 percent have no prior conviction for a violent felony. Chamberlin checked all of these boxes.

As a child, she suffered constant physical and sexual abuse from her father, her mother, her stepfather, her brother, and even her fourth-grade teacher. Her mother beat her with whatever was on hand, sometimes whipping her with a wooden spoon until it broke. When she was six, her 11-year-old brother put her into a closet with three neighborhood children, instructing them to touch her sexually. He also sexually abused her for years. Chamberlin told her mother, who dismissed her complaints.

When she was 12, Chamberlin began using drugs to numb the constant violence and abuse.

As an adult, her boyfriends used her substance dependency to exert control. They also physically and sexually abused her. Roger Gillett, who would become her co-defendant, strangled her, attempted to drown her, and raped her. He ordered her to move with him from Oregon, where her family lived, first to Kansas and then Mississippi in 2004. That was where Gillett killed two people.

Now 53, Chamberlin is the sole woman on Mississippi’s death row. If her appeals fail, she will be the first woman the state executes since 1944.

“In capital cases, women who have experienced some of the most extreme forms of gender-based violence and oppression are also among those who have received the least support from the legal system, from their communities, from their families, and from society,” Sandra Babcock, founder and director of the Cornell Center on the Death Penalty Worldwide, told Truthout. “There are two dynamics: One is that these women are among the most damaged and vulnerable survivors to become involved in the criminal legal system. But their experiences of violence and trauma go unrecognized by the legal system when they are charged with a capital crime.”

In Mississippi, Chamberlin and Gillett stayed with Gillett’s cousin, Vernon Hulett, and his cousin’s girlfriend, Linda Heintzelman. At first, they all got along. Then, after an auto accident between the two couples, they hatched a plan for Heintzelman to report the accident, collect insurance, and split it with Gillett and Chamberlin.

Heintzelman never filed the insurance claim, leading to tension between the two couples. When their hosts suggested that they move out, Gillett tortured and killed them. He and Chamberlin then placed their bodies into a freezer, loaded it into Heintzelman’s truck, and drove to an abandoned Kansas farm owned by Gillett’s grandfather.

There, police conducted a drug raid, arresting both. They later found the freezer and charged the couple with the deaths of Hulett and Heintzelman.

The pair were tried separately. Both were convicted and sentenced to death.

Chamberlin’s trial was marked by demonizing gender stereotypes. The prosecutor painted her as the mastermind behind the murders. He introduced testimony about Chamberlin’s sex life, including testimony from two jailhouse informants. Jailhouse informants’ testimonies, commonly motivated by law enforcement, are inherently unreliable and have been the leading cause in 46 percent of death row exonerations. Le jeu vidéo — comme le cinéma, la

? Des jeux vidéo anarchistes 

 

?


Le sexisme dans le milieu du jeu vidéo


Les femmes travaillant dans l'industrie vidéoludique constatent une différence de salaire (25,3 % d'écart au bénéfice des hommes). Certains rejettent les designs de personnages féminins non hyper‐sexualisés. Dans les studios de développement français, les femmes représentent 24 % des effectifs alors qu'elles n'en constituaient que 10,6 % il y a 10 ans. Depuis 2018, nous constatons toujours la même disparité selon les catégories de métier, avec une sous‐représentation des femmes dans les métiers techniques (programmation, data). La question du harcèlement au bureau est également régulièrement soulevée. D'autres formes de sexisme évoquées sont le manque de volonté d'inclure des personnages féminins bien représentés dans les jeux vidéo.


Les jeux qui cherchent à mettre en avant des personnes non hommes peuvent entraîner un harcèlement de leurs scénaristes et développeurs : c'est le cas de Amber Scott, scénariste du jeu Baldur's Gate : Siege of Dragonspear, harcelée en 2016. Elle a en effet inclus un personnage principal féminin et un personnage secondaire transgenre dans le jeu, en plus de se moquer du Gamergate

 [

]

 dans une réplique. En réponse à ces actions, elle est la cible d'une campagne de harcèlement et le jeu reçoit des retours négatifs en masse.


En juillet 2021, suite à son harcèlement par un manager, une employée du studio américain de jeux vidéo Activision Blizzard se suicide. Deux mille de ses collègues signent alors une pétition protestant contre des méthodes de management, et organisent un mouvement de grève. De manière plus générale, c'est la «

 

 culture Bro 

 

», culture sexiste répandue dans les milieux de la tech, qui est mise en accusation.


Sur les 152 major games publiés en 2022, 61 % des personnages sont des hommes, 39 % des femmes, et 31,7 % des jeux vidéo mettent en scène des personnages exclusivement masculins. Dans les 50 RPGs les plus joués ces 30 dernières années, les hommes parlent en moyenne 2 fois plus que les femmes.


67 % des françaises jouent aux jeux vidéo, elles ont 39 ans en moyenne et représentent 48 % des personnes qui jouent au moins une fois par semaine. Mais 40 % d'entre elles affirment avoir déjà dû se résoudre à cacher leur genre dans des parties en ligne, 46 % des gameuses jugent les contenus qu'elles voient en ligne trop sexistes ou misogynes, et elles sont aussi 40 % à avoir déjà vécu des situations de harcèlement en ligne.


Il n'y a sans doute pas plus de sexistes dans le jeu vidéo que dans le reste de la société : ce triste constat n'est que le reflet de l'état des lieux en général. Mais, comme dans la littérature ou le cinéma, changer le contenu ne devrait‐il pas participer à changer les mentalités

author: Sanya Osha
title: Art by Rock Hard African Women
content:
Oftentimes, mass acts of violent rebellion primarily driven by youths are viewed as counterproductive and nihilistic. But it is important to note that this isn’t always the case, as three major examples in African contemporary history demonstrate notably: the anti-colonial theory of violence proffered by Frantz Fanon that galvanised Algeria into civil disobedience and warfare during the colonial era; the Arab Spring that gripped North Africa and parts of the Middle East in 2011; and the #RhodesMustFall movement that rattled South Africa in 2015.  Each of these instances of mass rebellion were largely youth-driven and shook the political status quo in their respective countries, leading to sociopolitical reform and fervent collective contemplation.


In this sense, rebellion in and of itself becomes a thoroughly creative act, a measure to shake up jaded and monolithic political edifices in urgent need of transformation as atrophy and retrogression set in within the body politic. Youths often excluded or marginalised in key decision-making bodies and processes are left with no option but to revolt. And in the act of rebellion, they are not only offering their voice but also their signature as an essential component of the body politic. When dominant political structures become unresponsive to the needs and aspirations of the majority, when they become complacent and incapable of growth and innovation, then the rebellion of youth and other segments of the populace becomes not only unavoidable but also desirable. Indeed, the desirability of revolt as a creative act is the line of thinking behind this discussion. Revolt as a massive glitch in the polity can also be viewed as a rite of purification, a collective cleansing of the communal being before renewed energies are unleashed for social reconstruction.


Having established that the physical act of actual revolt could sometimes have therapeutic and reconstructive properties, it is important to note that Africa has produced many contemporary female artists whose works stand as testaments to powerful creative agency within the continent and defiant feminist sensibilities.


“Strike a woman, strike a rock” (

imbokodo

) is a Zulu proverb that became popular after the 1956 women’s march to Union Buildings in Pretoria to protest the apartheid pass laws. It is possible to explore other equally productive meanings of rock art by rock hard people and, in this instance, the San communities of Southern Africa come to mind. The San, also known as “the First People”, can be found principally in Angola, Namibia, Botswana and, of course, South Africa. Centuries ago, they mastered the art of making paintings and engravings on rock surfaces. These works of art were not merely decorative. They tell stories, communicate healing and enact rituals for communal wellness and cohesion. In spite of colonisation and various forms of oppression, these works of art have endured and this attests to the strength and resilience of the people who created them. Indeed, San communities are littered across the Southern African region despite mounting challenges, and their survival represents a broader African narrative of durability and adaptability. Their story forms the essential backdrop to this article on women who struggle against all kinds of dispossession: political, cultural, economic, and sexist, among other types of oppression.


The work of two black South African photographers, Zanele Muholi

and Ingrid Masondo, can be construed as efforts to debunk the misrepresentations of the black African woman by centuries-long colonial imagery, on the one hand, and — in spite of the constitutional recognition of gay rights — within the matrix of a largely homophobic, patriarchal, post-apartheid South Africa, on the other. Within colonial consciousness, the black female body was preposterously exoticised, anaestheticised, and hypersexualised. By being thrust into a vortex of unruly instincts, the black African female was grossly violated in more ways than one.


Sarah Bartmann was an unfortunate indigene of what eventually became South Africa who was enslaved to be paraded in the freak shows of London and Paris during the nineteenth century on account of her well-endowed posterior ( a contemporary equivalent would be the Brazilian Butt Lift – BBL). author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: Leyte farmer files harassment complaint vs military
content:
By Veronika Barbosa TACLOBAN CITY – A farmer filed a complaint on September 22 with the Commission on Human Rights Regional Office 8 against the Philippine Army’s 93rd Infantry Battalion (IB) due to intimidation against her and her family.

Accompanied by the National Union of People’s Lawyers Eastern Visayas and Katungod Sinirangan Bisayas, Brenda Lagado said that the first incident happened on July 28 in their house in Jaro, Leyte. “We were visited by elements of the Armed Forces of the Philippines. At first, they were just checking in on us but they eventually pressured us to confess that we have connections with the New People’s Army even if we have none.”

In the same month, Lagado said that her 16-year-old cousin was also interrogated by soldiers and alleged military assets.

“He [my cousin] was tending to farm animal when he was approached by seven soldiers and seven other individuals. At first, he was told to wait for a certain Basas who was supposed to talk to him but the latter did not arrive. He was instead confronted by a certain Simon who later grabbed him by the collar, hit him with a piece of chopped wood, and threatened that he will be hanged or electrocuted if he does not cooperate with them.”

Lagado said that his cousin was coerced by at least 14 men to divulge information about certain individuals that the victim does not know about.

She said that in August, a certain Sgt. Andres visited their house and compelled her to go to the barangay hall to purportedly “clear her name” which she refused to do. “We already went to the barangay before but the harassment still continued.”

In the same month, Lagado said that a child development worker of the Daycare Center where her child 3-year-old child was enrolled in, also experienced interrogation. “The teacher told us that a certain Cris Edison Rivera, who we later found out was from the 93rd IB, asked for the name and even live birth of my child. He also interrogated the teacher and asked information about our family.”

On September 11, Lagado received a letter from an unknown sender via express delivery. The letter included an unknown number and contained statements maligning Brenda and her family. “The letter pressured me to cooperate and call the number written on the letter within 24 hours or else they would let my entire family and my husband know that I have a relationship with an NPA rebel.”

“I am scared for my family and worried about my children’s safety. I am scared because the military have pictures of my family and even my children,” Lagado said. In a statement, Katungod SB condemned the 93rd IB’s series of harassment targeted against the Lagado family and their intimidation tactics involving innocent children.

“Children are not the tools of war…they should never be used, threatened, or assaulted to serve the military’s agenda. The 93rd IB, the entire AFP, and the NTF-ELCAC should all be held accountable for using a child and physically assaulting a minor to force the family to surrender or report to the 93rd IB.” Katungod SB called on the Commission on Human Rights to swiftly investigate and to protect the Lagado family against further intimidation and harassment. (DAA)
