title: KHRN reports enforced disappearances of five Kurdish opposition figures in Iran
content:
The security agencies of the Islamic Republic of Iran, specifically the Ministry of Intelligence and the Intelligence Organization of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), have increasingly deployed enforced disappearance against members of Kurdish opposition groups since June 2025, following the outbreak of the 12-day Israel-Iran conflict, which also involved US military strikes.


At least five Kurdish political activists have since been subjected to enforced disappearance: Mohsen Ghaderi, Sara Rashidi Kachlanlou, Zahra Pirdehghan, Parvin (Akhtar) Rasegh Qizilbash and Sirwan Habibi. They were arrested in Baneh, Paveh, Orumiyeh, and Kamyaran, and subsequently subjected to enforced disappearance.


Despite credible eyewitness testimonies and evidence confirming their detention by Iranian government security forces, Iran’s judicial authorities have not formally registered their detention. Security agencies also continue to deny their families information about their whereabouts or custody status.


This situation places the detainees outside the protection of the law, depriving them of access to legal counsel, communication with their families and necessary medical care.


These enforced disappearances have emerged amid a shift in detention practices following the recent regional hostilities and the bombardment of several security facilities.


The emerging pattern involves the relocation of detainees to unofficial detention facilities, denial of due process and restrictions on communication with legal representatives and family members.


Previously, individuals arrested in the Kurdish region were generally transferred to designated intelligence detention centres in provincial capitals. Security agencies are now increasingly holding detainees in secret facilities or relocating them to detention facilities in neighbouring provinces, including Hamadan and East Azerbaijan.


In all five documented cases, state agencies have refused to acknowledge responsibility for the arrests. Relevant local courts have consistently refused to provide information, effectively blocking families from pursuing legal avenues to establish the fate and whereabouts of their relatives.


As a result, all five detainees have been completely cut off from the outside world, with their current whereabouts and conditions remaining unknown.


The following section documents the circumstances surrounding the arrests and subsequent enforced disappearances of the five Kurdish political activists.


Mohsen Ghaderi


Political affiliation: Free Life Party of Kurdistan (PJAK)


Date of arrest: 22 June 2025


Location: Hangeh-Zhal border area, Baneh


Detaining agency: IRGC Intelligence Organization


Mohsen Ghaderi was arrested alongside a local border worker (kolbar) in the Hangeh-Zhal border area of Baneh on 22 June 2025.


Following their arrest, both men were taken to an IRGC facility in Baneh before being transferred to the IRGC Intelligence Organization’s Shahramfar detention centre in Sanandaj.


The kolbar, who was released on bail after three months, confirmed that no military engagement had taken place at the time of their arrest.


However, the IRGC Intelligence Organization twice summoned Ghaderi’s family in mid-2025, claiming that he had been killed during a military confrontation and prohibiting the family from holding a funeral service.


Local inquiries and accounts from residents contradict the Iranian authorities’ narrative, indicating that both individuals were taken into custody without any armed confrontation.


Ghaderi was last seen at the Shahramfar detention facility in September 2025. Unconfirmed reports indicate that he may subsequently have been transferred to an IRGC intelligence detention facility in Orumiyeh.


The Iranian authorities had previously made false claims regarding Ghaderi’s death following a July 2021 ambush in Bukan. Ghaderi later publicly rejected those claims in a video message.


Despite evidence of his detention, the authorities have not acknowledged his current custody status or disclosed his whereabouts.


Sara Rashidi Kachlanlou


Political affiliation: A Kurdish opposition party


Date of arrest: 11 January 2026


Location: Kermanshah–Paveh Road, near Paveh


Detaining agency: IRGC Intelligence Organization


Sara Rashidi Kachlanlou was arrested without a court warrant while travelling in a civilian vehicle on the Kermanshah–Paveh road during the January 2026 protests.

title: Μικροφωνική συγκέντρωση για τον νέο αντιμεταναστευτικό νόμο, Πέμπτη 8/10, στις 19.00, στη στάση Μετρό Αγίας Σοφίας
content:
Καλούν οι:

Οριζόντια Κίνηση και Ανάρες, ομάδα δράσης και αλληλεγγύης


Αφίσες/Καλέσματα:


Οριζόντια Κίνηση – για την Αναρχία και τον Ελευθεριακό Κομμουνισμό


Μικροφωνική – Συγκέντρωση σχετικά με τον νέο αντι-μεταναστευτικό νόμο


Πέμπτη 8/10, 19:00, Στάση Μετρό Αγίας Σοφίας


Οριζόντια Κίνηση – Για την Αναρχία και τον Ελευθεριακό Κομμουνισμό


Σχετικά με τον νέο αντι-μεταναστευτικό νόμο


«Το μεταναστευτικό κατά την άποψή μου μπορεί να λυθεί με δύο τρόπους, οι οποίοι σιγά σιγά πρέπει να λέγονται ξεκάθαρα. Ο πρώτος τρόπος είναι η φύλαξη των συνόρων, να καταλάβουμε τι εννοούμε, φύλαξη των συνόρων δεν μπορεί να υφίσταται αν δεν υπάρχουν απώλειες, και για να γίνω κατανοητός, αν δεν υπάρχουν νεκροί…Πρέπει να περνάνε χειρότερα. Η ζωή τους, η κόλαση, να φαντάζει παράδεισος σ’ αυτά που θα ζουν εδώ πέρα»


Τα παραπάνω αποτελούν δηλώσεις του φασίστα υπουργού μετανάστευσης και ασύλου Θάνου Πλεύρη το 2011, όντας τότε μέλος του ακροδεξιού κόμματος ΛΑΟΣ, μαζί με άλλα στελέχη της ΝΔ. Στην εποχή μας, το μεταναστευτικό παρουσιάζεται ως μία από τις μεγαλύτερες «απειλές» για την Ευρώπη. Κυβερνήσεις και μέσα ενημέρωσης καλλιεργούν συστηματικά τον φόβο, το μίσος και τον ρατσισμό, μετατρέποντας τους ανθρώπους που αναγκάστηκαν να εγκαταλείψουν τα σπίτια τους σε αποδιοπομπαίους τράγους για κάθε κοινωνικό πρόβλημα, καλώντας ανοιχτά ακόμα και σε δολοφονίες εναντίον τους. Στην Ελλάδα βλέπουμε συστηματικά να καλλιεργούνται τέτοιες αφηγήσεις σχεδόν από ολόκληρο το πολιτικό φάσμα της βουλής, που αποτελείται κατά βάση από φιλελεύθερους, ακροδεξιούς και φανατικούς χριστιανούς.


Την ίδια στιγμή, τα πραγματικά αίτια της μετανάστευσης μένουν κρυμμένα πίσω από τις ακροδεξιές ρητορικές. Οι περισσότεροι άνθρωποι δεν εγκαταλείπουν τον τόπο τους από επιλογή. Φεύγουν εξαιτίας πολέμων, δικτατοριών, φτώχειας, περιβαλλοντικών καταστροφών. Αυτές οι άθλιες συνθήκες προκαλούνται διαχρονικά από τα δυτικά καπιταλιστικά κράτη και τις πολεμικές και οικονομικές διακρατικές συμμαχίες (ΝΑΤΟ, ΕΕ). Σε Αφρική, Δυτική Ασία, Νότια Αμερική, η αποικιοκρατία και αργότερα οι ιμπεριαλιστικές επεμβάσεις διαλύουν υποδομές και οικονομίες και αποσυνθέτουν κοινωνίες εδώ και αιώνες, ώστε το δυτικό Κεφάλαιο να μπορεί να εκμεταλλευτεί τον τοπικό πλούτο, τις αγορές και τους εμπορικούς δρόμους. Σπέρνουν την διχόνοια, τους εμφυλίους πολέμους, οπλίζουν δικτατορικά καθεστώτα, υποβοηθούν τις γενοκτονίες.


Στην πρόσφατη περίπτωση των μεταναστ(ρι)ών στην Θέουτα, που προσπάθησαν να “εισέλθουν παράνομα στην Ισπανία και την Ε.Ε.” παρακινούμενοι/ες από αγνώστου προελεύσεως fake news σε σχέση με την δυνατότητα “νομιμοποίησής” τους, έχουμε την περίπτωση μιας εκ των τελευταίων ευρωπαϊκών αποικιών, έναν “Ισπανικό” θύλακα σε Αφρικανικό έδαφος, που σε μια αντιστροφή της ιστορικής πραγματικότητας, δέχθηκε δήθεν “οργανωμένη εισβολή”. Οι περισσότεροι/ες από τους/τις χιλιάδες μετανάστ(ρι)ες που πέρασαν τα “Ευρωπαϊκά” σύνορα, στο έδαφος βέβαια της δικής τους ηπείρου, επέστρεψαν σύντομα οικειοθελώς, αλλά και μετά την βίαιη απάντηση του δήθεν προοδευτικού Ισπανικού Κράτους. Οι λιγοστοί που έμειναν, υφίστανται την ρατσιστική βία από “ντόπιους”, δηλαδή Ισπανούς πολίτες, υποκινούμενη από οργανωμένους φασίστες, με επιθέσεις στους καταυλισμούς τους και παρεμπόδιση της διανομής τροφίμων από ανθρωπιστικές οργανώσεις.


Η αντιμετώπιση, λοιπόν, αυτών των ανθρώπων από την λεγόμενη «πολιτισμένη Δύση» αποτελεί ένα δείγμα της απανθρωπιάς και του μίσους που καλλιεργείται απέναντι στους μετανάστες. Τα τελευταία χρόνια έχουν καταγραφεί αμέτρητα περιστατικά από διεθνείς οργανισμούς και οργανώσεις ανθρωπίνων δικαιωμάτων σχετικά με παράνομες επαναπροωθήσεις, αυθαίρετες κρατήσεις, βίαιες συμπεριφορές και δολοφονίες στα σύνορα.


Στην Ελλάδα όλα αυτά συμβαίνουν σχεδόν σε καθημερινή βάση, τόσο στα θαλάσσια σύνορα, όσο και στον Έβρο και το μεγαλύτερο ποσοστό των περιστατικών αυτών δεν φτάνουν ποτέ στα αυτιά μας. Το λιμενικό, οι συνοριοφύλακες, πολλές φορές μάλιστα μαζί με παραστρατιωτικές μονάδες, χτυπούν, ληστεύουν, βιάζουν και πνίγουν μετανάστες και μετανάστριες στα σύνορα. Τρανό παράδειγμα αποτελεί το ναυάγιο της Πύλου με τους τουλάχιστον 600 δολοφονημένους μετανάστες και μετανάστριες (ανάμεσά τους και πολλά παιδιά).


Ταυτόχρονα, η πραγματικότητα για όσους και όσες επιβιώνουν το πέρασμα των συνόρων, αλλά εντοπίζονται από τις ελληνικές αρχές, είναι εξίσου βασανιστική. Ο εγκλεισμός σε καμπ κολαστήρια, που στερούνται ακόμη και των πιο υποτυπωδών υποδομών, ιδίως σε σχέση με την υγεία και την περίθαλψη, δημιουργεί μια ανυπόφορη …

author: EDRi
title: Your data, their decision: the hidden surveillance infrastructure behind Europe’s digital borders
content:
A new report by ARTICLE 19 examines how the European Union is presiding over the most significant expansion of border surveillance in its history. Much of this development is being outsourced to private companies – with profound consequences for privacy and freedom of expression.

By ARTICLE 19 (guest author) · October 8, 2026

In October 2025, the EU began systematically collecting and storing fingerprints and facial images of every third-country national crossing its external border, under the Entry/Exit System (EES). By late 2026, the European Travel Information and Authorisation System (ETIAS) will expand this approach by pre-screening visa-exempt travellers before they arrive at EU borders.

Together, the two systems are capable of processing more than 1.4 billion travellers, integrating biometric, migration, visa, and law-enforcement data into searchable profiles.

The new report by ARTICLE 19, examining how the EU is significantly expanding border surveillance, focuses on the agency at the heart of the system: EU-LISA (EU Agency for the Operational Management of Large-Scale IT Systems in the Area of Freedom, Security and Justice). This little-scrutinised entity plays a key role in building and maintaining the large-scale digital infrastructure projects that underpin EU migration and border management.

ARTICLE 19 analysed EUR 1.99 billion in contracts awarded by EU-LISA between 2019-2025. The analysis shows how private companies, including IDEMIA, Sopra Steria, IBM, and Leonardo SpA, have gained unprecedented power to shape how the systems operate.

Because of the way EU-LISA procurement works, private companies are gaining real influence over what the systems can do and recommend, through large building blocks of biometrics, engineering, and operations. In practice, this means that surveillance capacities within EES and ETIAS could be expanded through ‘technical adjustments’ decided by companies rather than accountable political decisions.

Those same companies are part of a growing industry that spans global digital IDs, defence and security projects worldwide. IDEMIA, for instance, develops and implements national biometric identification systems in countries including Morocco, Chile, and Colombia, as well as election management technologies in Kenya.

How these technologies travel across contexts deserves further scrutiny.

This scale of digitalisation at the border has real-life consequences for the people subjected to it.

For migrants and people on the move, participation in these systems is not optional: biometric registration and automated risk-scoring are conditions for mobility or legal status, not choices people can opt out of.

This is deeply concerning because interconnected systems mean a single database error can cascade across the entire network, leading to delayed or denied entry or visa refusals – often with little transparency about how a decision was made or how to challenge it. Many migrants lack the linguistic, legal, and financial resources needed to exercise rights they formally have.

The long-term picture remains uncertain: how exactly will these systems classify people, what further changes might be introduced, and what mechanisms can people use to question decisions or access their own data.

One thing is clear: accountability mechanisms are lagging further behind the pace of deployment of these surveillance tools.

Individuals’ rights and freedoms should not be subordinated to commercial interests. Strengthening rights mechanisms and transparency for migrant populations requires protective frameworks designed for the conditions they face.

Existing legal frameworks cannot simply apply to EES and ETIAS on paper. They need to be enforced without the broad exceptions for migration and law enforcement that currently undermine both the GDPR and the AI Act. EDRi and its members have already documented how the AI Act fails migrants and people on the move.

We need binding transparency obligations around EU-LISA’s procurement processes and its relationships with private contractors. Decisions that expand surveillance capacities should require the same level of public scrutiny and political accountability as any other major policy change. They cannot be left to commercial and engineering considerations alone.

More broadly, the design, development, and deployment of digital border infrastructure must not be allowed to proceed without open public debate and meaningful participation of …

author: anonerror
title: Crónica de Naada en Ceuta
content:
Van a cumplirse un par de semanas desde que volví de Ceuta, y el panorama está cada vez más calentito en nuestro país. Es difícil hablar de cualquier tema político o social sin que surja enemistad… Primero la crisis de Ceuta. Manifestaciones en defensa de España. Mari Carmen. La acampada en Sol y en otras ciudades. Más manifestaciones. El rechazo de los dos decretos. Las elecciones anticipadas…

Me demoré en escribir estas líneas porque me parecía que en este momento podría juzgarse de frivolidad. Que hablar de Ceuta en la actualidad, con otros muchos problemas, sería tachado de inoportuno. Pero me doy cuenta de que ha sido, sigue siendo y será imprescindible no silenciar su voz. Especialmente tras mi visita a la ciudad autónoma, donde pude despertar y ser consciente de que vivimos una gran desinformación desde fuera. Como si a las noticias; las publicaciones en redes sociales y los reportajes les costara cruzar el estrecho sin deformarse, tergiversarse o manipularse en el intento.

Un pueblo mal informado es un pueblo manipulable. Y un pueblo además dividido es un pueblo controlable. Ya lo decía Julio César.

Por eso no es de extrañar que haya una buena campaña de desinformación en marcha desde la entrada masiva de migrantes el 30 y 31 de julio en Ceuta. Existen unos creadores de contenido en redes sociales que buscan, precisamente, la polarización de la sociedad en pensamientos realmente radicales. Hay bulos por todas partes que siembran y alimentan los pensamientos retorcidos llenos de racismo, odio y, a fin de cuentas, miedo. Mientras organizaciones humanitarias, vecinos y vecinas ceutíes y grupos autogestionados se organizan en terreno para responder a contrarreloj y sin medios a todas las necesidades humanitarias de los migrantes que el Gobierno no cubre, otros seres a los que no quiero poner nombre, pero defensores de pensamientos fascistas, se dedican patrullar las calles para “cazarlos a todos”, como un diputado de Vox animaba a hacer. Organizados por redes sociales, se dividen los barrios marginales para dar ueltas en sus coches, amenazar, violentar y perturbar tanto a los dadores de ayuda como a sus receptores.

Es real el descontento de los ceutíes. Hay críticas sobre la situación de la ciudad; sobre la intervención- o su ausencia-, su alcance, su demora, y el modo de ejecutarla del Gobierno y las instituciones. Hay quejas y más quejas. Sin embargo se ven pocas manos tendidas a ayudar. Lo fácil es colgar la bandera del balcón, sacarla al escaparate de tu negocio, o ponérsela en la muñeca, solicitando que tu ciudad vuelva a ser la misma. Más difícil y valiente es jugársela a ser apartado e ir contracorriente de tus vecinos odiadores por acoger en tu casa a unas cuantas personas. Esos casos también los hay y me llenan de emoción, dándome todavía algo de esperanza en la humanidad. Hay estos vecinos y vecinas, que son los que están levantando Ceuta a pasitos pequeños pero constantes.

Sin embargo, lamentablemente, hay un discurso que nos venden como el predominante, porque es lo que interesa que España vea. El de odio y de racismo que están calando en estratos de la sociedad que no deberían hacer manitas con dichas ideologías. Básicamente por puros principios.

Pero creo que ya no sabemos ni qué quiere decir esa palabra. Porque antes que crisis política o social estratégicamente buscada por los hilos invisibles de los poderes fácticos americanos y sionistas, esto es una grandísima crisis humanitaria. Y lo que más está escaseando es la humanidad. Lo que estamos viviendo en Ceuta no es casual y, como vemos, tampoco será inocuo. Pero en este texto no me quiero extender en el análisis de sus orígenes y consecuencias geopolíticas. Eso se lo dejo a los expertos.

Yo tan solo soy una enfermera que ha estado en terreno y que necesita sacar de las entrañas toda la frustración acumulada en mi paso por Ceuta. Así que hablemos de lo que pude experimentar allí, de todo aquello que fui testigo y que contrasta fuertemente con lo que se difunde en redes. Hablemos de lo que realmente está sucediendo a los migrantes y a las vecinas ceutíes.

El día 20 de septiembre celebraron en Ceuta una manifestación en la frontera, a la que acudieron según los reportes 200 personas, con nuestra bandera de España ondeando al grito de “¡invasores fuera! Expulsión”. Bandera que siguen haciendo suya y con la que defienden lo indefendible; la segregación, el maltrato, la violencia. Hablan de defender España y a los Españoles, a los ceutíes …

author: Unknown
title: Daxwaza ji bo wergêrê kurdî qebûl nekirin: Penaberê îraqî yê Kurd wekî hemwelatiyê Efxanistanê tomarkirin
content:
Salih Omer Celalê iraqî ji sala 2018an ve li Afyonkarahisarê dijî. Salih Omer Celal xwediyê serlêdana parastina navneteweyî ye ku di 20ê Gulana 2026an de ji bo serlêdana wî ya mafê rûniştinê bê qebûlkirin ket mulaqatê.


Celal diyar kir ku ew nikare di mulaqata parastina navneteweyî de bi asteke ku xwe bi zelalî îfade bike bi tirkî biaxive û ji Rêveberiya Îdareya Koçê ya Bajar daxwaza wergêrê kurdî kir. Lêbelê daxwaza Celal nehat qebûlkirin. Di belgeya serlêdanê ya Celal de jî ew weke “hemwelatiyê Efxanistanê” hate nivîsandin.


Celal weha behsa tiştên ku di hevdîtinê de jiyaye kir: “Ji min re gotin ku wergêrê kurdî tune ye. Piştre ji min re gotin ‘an tu yê bikevî mûlaqatê an jî em ê neçar bimînin ku te bişînin bajarekî din.’ Ji ber vê yekê min nekarî sedemên serlêdana parastina navneteweyî û bûyerên ku rûbirû bû me di mûlaqatê de bi tevahî bînim ziman. Ez wekî hemwelatiyê Efxanistanê tomar kirim. Ji ber vê statûya min ket xetereyê.”


Li gorî Xala 70emîn ya Qanûna Parastina Navneteweyî û Biyaniyan ya Bi Hejmar 6458an, heke serlêderê parastina navneteweyî, di hevdîtinên kesane yên qonaxên serlêdan, tomar û mûlaqatê de daxwaza wergêr bike, divê bê peydakirin. Rêxistina Penaberan a Neteweyên Yekbûyî (UNHCR) diyar dike ku di çarçoveya kiryarên parastina navneteweyî yên li Tirkiyeyê de piştevaniya wergêriyê dê bi rêya rayedarên Rêveberiya Îdareya Koçê ya Bajar bê dabînkirin. Di xeta şêwirmendiyê ya UNHCRê de hatiye diyarkirin ku li ser daxwazê piştevaniya şêwirmendiya kurdî jî dikare bê dayîn.


Ji bo piştevaniya hiqûqî çûye SGDD-ASAMê


Celal di 17ê Tîrmeha 2026an de ji bo ku li ser pirsgirêka wergêriyê ya di mûlaqatê de jiyaye piştevaniya hiqûqî wergire, çûye ofîsa Komeleya Piştgiriya bi Penaber û Koçberan re (SGDD-ASAM). Celal da zanîn ku wî ji xebatkaran re ragihandiye ku zimanê wî ê dayikê kurdî ye û pêdiviya wî bi piştevaniya hiqûqî ya derbarê dosyaya wî ya parastina navneteweyî de heye. Lêbelê hat îdîakirin ku ji wî re weha gotine: “Heke tu ji vir neçî em ê li polîsan bigerin.”


“Armanca min ne derxistina pirsgirêkan bû”


Celal destnîşan kir û weha got: 


“Armanca min tenê ew bû ku ez kêşeya xwe ya wergêriyê ya di dema mulaqata parastina navneteweyî de rûbirû bûme bînim ziman û piştevaniya hiqûqî wergirim,” û axaftina xwe wiha berdewam kir: “Bi taybetî serlêder divê bikaribin behsa xwe û kêşeyên xwe bikin. Pêdiviya me bi gihîştina xizmeta wergêriyê û wergirtina piştevaniya hiqûqî heye. Ji bo min wergêr peyda nekirin. Ji ber vê yekê Rêveberiya Îdareya Koçê ya Bajar tevî ku ez hemwelatiyê Iraqê me jî, ez wekî hemwelatiyê Efxanistanê tomar kirim. Divê ev tişt bê sererastkirin. Serlêdanên min ketin ber xetereyê. Ked û xebata min a heşt salan dê vala biçe.”


(FY/AY)

author: Mag
title: Die europäische Mauer in der spanischen Exklave Ceuta: Wieder einmal erfolgreich gestürmt
content:
Dossier


Etwa 500 Flüchtlingen aus dem subsaharischen Afrika gelang es in der letzten Woche, die europäische Mauer in der spanischen Exklave (sprich: Kolonialbesitzung in Afrika) Ceuta zu überwinden. Der kurze

Videofilm „Cientos de subsaharianos entran en Ceuta“, am 16. Februar 2017 von Faro TV auf You Tube

 


 gepostet, zeigt ihre Ankuft, und – nicht zuletzt – die Freude über die gelungene Überwindung und über das Wiedersehen mit Freunden oder Familienangehörigen. Das ist der Unterschied zwischen EU und Trump. Der will an der Grenze eine Mauer bauen, die EU baut Festungsmauern gleich „im Feindesland“… Siehe Hintergründe und weitere „Stürmungen“:


Spanien räumt Flüchtlingslager und spricht von freiwilliger Rückkehr


„

Betroffene von Druck durch die Polizei. Menschenrechtler protestieren: Konnten Schutzsuchende überhaupt Asyl beantragen?


Nach der Räumung eines großen improvisierten Lagers in der spanischen Nordafrika-Exklave Ceuta wachsen Zweifel am Vorgehen der Behörden. Rund 1.100 Menschen sind spanischen Medien zufolge innerhalb von zwei Tagen nach Marokko zurückgekehrt, ohne zuvor registriert worden zu sein. Die spanische Regierung bezeichnet das Verfahren als freiwillige Rückkehr. Hilfsorganisationen und Betroffene stellen diese Freiwilligkeit infrage. Die Polizei hatte am Sonntag mit mehr als 350 Beamten begonnen, das Lager am Strand El Trampolín zu räumen. Unterstützt wurden die Einsatzkräfte von zahlreichen Fahrzeugen, darunter auch gepanzerte Wagen. Etwa 1.100 Menschen wurden am ersten Tag mit Bussen zum Grenzübergang Tarajal gebracht. Rund 900 von ihnen gingen anschließend nach Marokko zurück. Am Montag folgten weitere Rückreisen. (…) Am Grenzübergang standen die Betroffenen nach Angaben spanischer Medien vor zwei Möglichkeiten: Sie konnten sich registrieren lassen, oder ohne Registrierung nach Marokko zurückkehren. Die Behörden werten die zweite Möglichkeit als freiwillige Ausreise. Nach Recherchen spanischer Medien wurden die Menschen vor ihrer Entscheidung jedoch darüber informiert, dass eine Registrierung ebenfalls sehr wahrscheinlich ein Rückführungsverfahren nach sich ziehen wird. Betroffene berichteten zudem von Druck durch Polizeibeamte. Das spanische Innenministerium weist den Vorwurf zurück, Menschen zur Ausreise zu zwingen. Die deutsche Hilfsorganisation Mission Lifeline, die mit einem Team in Ceuta tätig ist, spricht von einer unzulässigen Massenabschiebung. „Unter Druck und umringt von rabiat vorgehender Polizei mit Panzerwagen kann von Freiwilligkeit und einem rechtsstaatlichen Verfahren keine Rede sein“, erklärte der Vorsitzende Nolte Bauer. Die Organisation fordert individuelle Prüfungen sowie Zugang zu Dolmetschern, medizinischer Versorgung und rechtlicher Beratung. Unter den Bewohnern des Lagers hätten sich auch Frauen und Minderjährige befunden. (…) Die Räumung erfolgte gut eine Woche vor dem geplanten Besuch des spanischen Königspaares in Ceuta. Einen offiziellen Zusammenhang zwischen dem Besuch und dem Zeitpunkt der Aktion gibt es nicht.“


Meldung vom 6. Oktober 2026 im MiGAZIN

 


Für Spaniens Regierung wird der Umgang mit den Minderjährigen in Ceuta zum Lackmustest als letzte Bastion einer humanen Migrationspolitik“ 


„… Während in Spanien dabei zunächst ein möglicherweise beabsichtigtes Versagen der marokkanischen Grenzkontrollen im Fokus stand, konzentrierte man sich im Rest Europas auf Madrids Rolle in der gemeinsamen Migrationspolitik. Aus der Grenzkrise wurde in wenigen Tagen ein europäischer Richtungsstreit.


Den Aufschlag machte dabei Italiens rechte Premierministerin Giorgia Meloni. Bereits am 31. Juli führte Rom Kontrollen für Drittstaatsangehörige ein, die aus Spanien einreisten, und begründete diesen Schritt mit Risiken für Italiens nationale Sicherheit. Spaniens Premier Pedro Sánchez reagierte mit einem scharfen Brief an EU-Kommissionspräsidentin Ursula von der Leyen, in dem er neben der »solidaritätsbasierten Einwanderungspolitik« auch den effektiven Grenzschutz seines Landes betonte und eine Dringlichkeitssitzung der EU-Innenminister forderte. Fast zeitgleich kritisierten 22 EU-Staaten, angeführt von Italien und Dänemark, die spanische Migrationspolitik als möglichen »Pullfaktor«. In ihrem Schreiben bezog sich die Gruppe vor allem auf eine Regelung, die international als Dreh- und Angelpunkt des spanischen Sonderwegs in Sachen Migration wahrgenommen worden war. Im Frühjahr hatte die Linkskoalition eine außerordentliche Legalisierung für Menschen beschlossen …

author: Wildcat #116
title: 1976 – 1991: Das Albartus-Papier der Revolutionären Zellen
content:
Die Jahre 1976 und 1991 markieren zwei deutliche Abstürze in der Geschichte der radikalen Linken in der BRD. Bezeichnenderweise kam Ende 1991 das Albartus-Papier der Revolutionären Zellen auf 1976 zu sprechen: die Flugzeugentführung von Entebbe. Anlässlich des 50. Jahrestags haben wir in der aktuellen Wildcat einen langen Artikel, der diese Verbindungen aufzudröseln versucht: »Entebbe und die Folgen«. Hier eine Kürzestfassung plus update:


Im Juni und Juli 1976 herrschte in Europa eine Hitzewelle. Die Temperaturen in Deutschland stiegen wochenlang regelmäßig über 30 Grad auf Spitzenwerte bis 36 und 37 Grad.


Politisch endete vor 50 Jahren das »rote Jahrzehnt«: 24. März 1976 Militärputsch in Argentinien. Am 9. Mai 1976 starb Ulrike Meinhof. Anfang Juni brach auf dem »Pfingstkongress« ein breiter Teil der radikalen Linken mit der Militanz und machte sich auf in die Institutionen. Am 10. Juli begann die Chemiekatastrophe in Seveso. Im August das Massaker von Tel al-Zaatar. Am 6. Oktober der Militärputsch in Thailand.


Auch kulturell war 1976 schlimm: ABBA »Dancing Queen«, Jürgen Drews »Ein Bett im Kornfeld«, Boney M. »Daddy Cool«. Kurz danach kamen dann die BeeGees »Stayin’ Alive« – der Sound zum Deutschen Herbst!


Für die deutschen Maoisten der diversen K-Gruppen lag 1976 zwischen dem Besuch von Franz Josef Strauß bei Mao (Januar 1975) einerseits, dem Krieg Vietnams gegen Kambodscha und den »Reformen« von Deng Xiao Ping (beides im Dezember 1978) andererseits. Die meisten fielen vom Glauben ab, viele von ihnen gründeten die Grüne Partei, andere später die Antideutschen. Diese eroberten nach 1991 die Hegemonie in der radikalen Linken.


Die Flugzeugentführung nach Entebbe…


Seit Anfang 1976 eskalierte der libanesische Bürgerkrieg. Nach monatelanger Belagerung stürmten Falangisten am 12. August das Lager von Tel al-Zaatar und töteten Tausende palästinensische Flüchtlinge.


Im Zusammenhang damit entführte ein deutsch-palästinensisches Kommando aus RZ und PFLP-EO am 27. Juni 1976 ein Flugzeug nach Entebbe und forderte die Freilassung von politischen Gefangenen. In der Nacht zum 4. Juli befreiten israelische Spezialkräfte die meisten der Geiseln. Das wird von gewissen Kreisen bis heute als das beste Kommandounternehmen aller Zeiten bejubelt (etwa: »Mit der Geiselbefreiung von Entebbe zeigte Israel vor 50 Jahren, wie man den Terror bekämpft« Nius 2. Juli 2026). Benjamin Netanjahu, dessen älterer Bruder bei der Befreiungsaktion starb, hat seine gesamte politische Karriere auf »Entebbe« und den »Kampf gegen den Terrorismus« aufgebaut.


»Die Aktion von Entebbe wurde rasch zu einem Vorwand für verschiedene Akteure, die bislang mit dem Milieu der radikalen Linken verbunden waren, sich von Internationalismus und Antiimperialismus ganz zu lösen.« (Gerhard Hanloser: »Desaster mit Nachspiel«)


Wegweisend war der Anti-Repressionskongress des Sozialistischen Büros Anfang Juni (»Pfingstkongress«). Am Abschlusstag hatte der spätere Außenminister Joschka Fischer vor 20.000 Besuchern in der berühmten Römerberg-Rede mit seiner militanten Vergangenheit gebrochen. Später hat er – die Dinge chronologisch auf den Kopf stellend – auf seinem Weg ins Außenministerium immer mal wieder betont, »Entebbe« sei das Ereignis gewesen, das ihn vom Saulus zum Paulus gemacht habe. Dabei lieferte es nur nachträglich den Vorwand.


»Entebbe« ist bis heute wirkmächtig. Das sah man an den Dutzenden von Artikeln und mehreren Büchern, die zum 50. Jahrestag erschienen. Das sah man aber auch daran, dass im März 2023 Mitglieder der Entebbe-Spezialeinheit eine der schärfsten Kritiken an Benjamin Netanjahu in einem offenen Brief formulierten. Netanjahu opfere den Staat Israel und das israelische Volk für seine eigenen Interessen, diffamiere Demonstranten gegen die Justizreform als Anarchisten und alle, die ihn nicht unterstützen, als Terroristen; er hetze Israelis gegeneinander auf.


… und die beginnende Institutionalisierung der radikalen Linken


1976 hätte auch anders ausgehen können. Im Juli hatten Chemiearbeiter in Seveso gestreikt, um die Katastrophe überhaupt öffentlich zu machen – aber sie hatten nicht mehr die Macht wie Jahre zuvor, die Wirtschaftspolitik des Landes neu zu orientieren. Die massenhaften Schüler- und Studentenproteste in Soweto seit Juni waren größtenteils selbst organisiert und schienen politisch endlich eine Alternative zum ANC zu eröffnen. Aber die Bullen schlugen die Bewegung brutal nieder; sie töteten mehr als 500 der …

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: "Incredible Moment for the Borderlands": Judge Blocks Border Wall Expansion in Big Bend & West Texas
content:
In a victory for environmentalists and immigration rights’ advocates, a federal judge in El Paso, Texas, has blocked further border wall construction inside Big Bend National Park. “We slammed the brakes on $7 billion worth of corrupt construction contracts,” says Laiken Jordahl, a national public lands advocate with the Center for Biological Diversity, which sued to block the expansion. “We have effectively stopped construction across West Texas, and it’s incredible.”


Jordahl also responds to the Trump administration’s excavation of a 200-year-old cottonwood tree on the Arizona-Mexico border that had been protected by activists for months. “Watching those videos of them toppling this ancient tree that was very likely older than the border itself is symbolic of how

DHS

 has treated the border region. They see our communities, our wildlife, our nature as a sacrifice zone,” says Jordahl.

author: Unknown
title: Cagnard prend fin, la lutte continue
content:
En cette rentrée, Cagnard a décidé de clôturer ses activités politiques. Dans ce texte, nous nous retrouvons à quelques-un·e·s pour tirer le bilan de l'existence du collectif et situons sa trajectoire dans la séquence politique que nous traversons. Nous exprimons là notre avis sur la tenue et fermeture de cet espace d'organisation alors que le groupe voit la fin de ses activités comme un constat qui s'impose à lui-même. Diverses lectures découlent de la situation parmi les membres restants.


Il est ainsi à noter que, pour certain·es d'entre nous, ce sont le manque d'effectifs et de motivation qui bloquent aujourd'hui le groupe.


Cette ligne identifie l'impossibilité de l'action future du groupe dans les tensions inter-personnelles qui ont pu apparaître au fil de notre activité et dans un manque de renouvellement de nos effectifs. L'accueil de nouveaux membres aurait alors pu permettre de diluer les divergences politiques, de mettre une distance entre les susceptibilités inter-personnelles ou de voir partir des camarades tout en laissant de nouvelles forces assumer les tâches organisationnelles laissées vacantes.


D'autres camarades voient poindre des problématiques liées à notre fonctionnement, notre ouverture et notre composition. C'est afin de préciser cette lecture que nous écrivons ce texte.


En premier lieu, nous détaillons les enjeux qui ont motivé la création du collectif. Puis, nous revenons sur l'actualité politique du groupe et livrons des éléments d'analyse du contexte. De nouveaux impératifs se dessinent constamment dans la lutte : notre réflexivité doit servir à ajuster nos perspectives politiques à l'aune des obstacles que nous traversons et des tâches qui émergent.


Cagnard, sa création et ses objectifs


Cagnard a été créé en mars 2025 avec pour ambition de former un groupe autonome et ouvert sur Marseille. À rebours des logiques affinitaires et de cooptation, des camarades ont souhaité initier un projet de rupture avec les institutions traditionnelles du mouvement – partis et syndicats – qui assume dans le même temps la nécessité et l'accessibilité de l'organisation politique. Dans un cadre de composition, des personnes de sensibilités politiques diverses se sont organisées sur la base de perspectives communes, à commencer par l'intensification des mouvements sociaux et leur défense face à la répression.


Nous avons œuvré à la diffusion de pratiques de défense, soutenu les inculpé·es face à la Justice et animé des ateliers de formation politique. Il est crucial de battre en brèche les dynamiques de spécialisation lorsqu'elles entravent la participation effective des camarades à l'organisation politique. L'action de rue se doit d'être massive et ne doit pas être l'apanage d'une élite éclairée. Quant à la défense juridique, elle ne doit pas être abandonnée à des spécialistes du droit. Ces deux pendants du renforcement d'un mouvement doivent se trouver aux mains du plus grand nombre de camarades.


Nous entendions défendre ces lignes, ce qui entraînait parfois de porter la rupture au sein du mouvement social, dans la rue et au sein des espaces d'organisation. Plus largement, nous cherchions à soutenir le débordement face à la répression, le dépassement des mots d'ordre défensifs, sectoriels et des cadres de lutte institués, et à exacerber les contradictions en leur sein.


La théorie n'étant qu'un moment de la pratique, la tenue d'ateliers de formation politique et culturelle devait servir à affûter nos perspectives d'intervention dans les mobilisations naissantes et celles à venir. La composition devait nourrir l'intelligence collective : loin de penser que la contradiction affaiblit le mouvement révolutionnaire, nous sommes convaincu·es qu'elle le renforce et qu'elle doit être entretenue. Au-delà du dogmatisme et du sectarisme, l'ouverture de nos espaces visait un objectif clair : défendre et construire l'autonomie politique, dans le prolongement de ce que ce champ a su porter d'anti-capitalisme, d'anti-étatisme et d'indépendance vis-à-vis des partis et organisations syndicales. Il s'agissait aussi d'accroître nos forces de lutte, de propager l'auto-organisation pour gagner en puissance collective.


Tout au long de son existence, le collectif a fait preuve d'une activité politique constante. Toutefois, ces derniers mois, ses membres ont éprouvé des contradictions dans la mise en œuvre de ces objectifs. Notre modèle politique éprouve des limites certaines.

author: Fozzie
title: Chapter 25: The General Law of Capitalist Accumulation
content:
Harry Cleaver's study guide to Marx's Capital volume one, chapter 25.

Marx’s opening remarks on the “composition of capital” harken back to the analysis in Chapter 15 on relative surplus value. There we saw how efforts to offset reductions in the working day by raising productivity involved capitalists replacing troublesome workers with compliant machinery. He suggests that the introduction of more machinery per worker can be formulated as a rise in the technical composition of capital, something we can represent symbolically by MP/LP, the material configuration of means of production and labor-power.(1) Looked at from the point of view of of value invested, increased expenditure on machinery raises the value composition of capital, or c/v, a ratio of the value invested in constant capital, c, to that invested in variable capital, v. However, because the value composition can change independently of any change in the technical composition,(2) Marx calls the value composition—when changes are only due to changes in the technical composition—the organic composition of capital. To differentiate, we can represent the organic composition of capital as co/vo. So, c/v can change, even if co/vo does not; but any change in co/vo is also a change in c/v. Therefore, whenever he refers to changes in the organic composition he is talking about a change in the technical composition, but in value terms. Eventually—especially in Volume III of Capital—we find that Marx’s analysis of some tendencies to crisis are formulated in terms of the organic composition of capital.(3)

Although we can analyze these various “compositions of capital” at every level of the economy, from individual enterprises through branches of industry to the total social capital, it is “with this [last] alone that we are concerned here”.(4) In other words, the subject is the expansion of the total social capital. It is therefore vital to be clear about what Marx means by accumulation.

Had he defined accumulation merely as an expansion of the total social capital, it would be easy to confuse accumulation with economists’ concepts of “growth”, or, taking qualitative changes into account, with concepts of “economic development”. But he doesn’t leave it at that; he carefully defines accumulation in social terms as the reproduction “of the capital-relation on an expanded scale, with more capitalists, or bigger capitalists, at one pole, and more wage-laborers at the other pole.”(5) In other words, what is being accumulated are the antagonistic class relationships of capitalism. Unlike economists who recognize neither classes nor class antagonism, and think of growth in terms of production functions such as Q = f(K, L), where factors of production K (capital) and L (labor) produce output (Q) that grows as the economy expands, Marx re-emphasizes here that his interest is precisely those antagonistic relationships within which K (MP or c), L (LP in action or v) and Q (C’ and M’) are only elements or moments.

He then proceeds to discuss the dynamics of accumulation in terms of the relationships between the classes. In this first section he assumes that the composition of capital (by each definition) remains the same, so that when capitalists invest, their money buys both more means of production (MP) and more labor-power (LP). (He relaxes this assumption in the next section.) Under this assumption, capitalist investment increases the demand for labor-power and puts upward pressure on wages as capitalists compete for available workers.(6)

Marx then brings this association between investment and the demand for labor to bear on the analysis of the fluctuations in business activity. He recognizes how downturns and upturns were recurring periodically, but his real interest lay not their periodicity but how major downturns constituted crises for capitalism. That is to say, large-scale layoffs, rising unemployment and increased poverty can lead to worker-led uprisings and a crisis for capitalist control. Unlike economists who prefer the term business cycle, optimiostically presuming that downturns will always be followed by upturns, for Marx each major crisis opened the possibility of the revolutionary overthrow of capitalism.

Assuming a constant composition of capital, as he does in this section, rapid accumulation was achieved by capitalists hiring more labor, sometimes buying new machines and processing more raw materials to produce more output, whether in agriculture …

title: Karasu: South Kurdistan needs a democratic unity government based on local democracy
content:
KCK Executive Council member Mustafa Karasu discussed developments in Kurdistan, Turkey, and the Middle East during a special program broadcast on

Medya Haber

.


The first part of this interview can be read

here

, and the second

here

. 


You’ve often noted that the war against the Kurds has corrupted many things in Turkey. Recently, corruption – particularly involving the AKP government – has been exposed in the economic sphere. It is becoming increasingly clear that the people’s money is being stolen by circles close to the ruling party. This decay is being discussed. How do you evaluate this?


The capitalist system is, by its very nature, about stealing from society. It means stealing society’s labor. It means stealing society’s values. Nothing else can be expected from the capitalist system. The capitalist system is corrupt. When it is cornered or under pressure, it seizes society’s values. As we recall, during the Özal era, a wave of bankers emerged. These bankers collected the people’s money, and then all of them went bankrupt. Where did the money go? It was diverted to the bourgeoisie and to the state’s war expenditures. The people’s savings were seized. That’s how capitalism works; that’s how these states operate. When they’re under pressure or in a bind, they find a way, a method to seize the people’s savings; they steal it. Capitalism is a system of theft. Governments are also a system of theft. So where did all the money go? It didn’t just vanish into thin air. It both went into the pockets of the rich, and it was absorbed by certain government institutions. They took that money and spent it.


The state senses everyone’s every move and tries to control them. Is it really blind to such massive corruption – to the seizure of the people’s values? Doesn’t it get any information? Doesn’t it know what’s going on at the stock market and elsewhere? That’s how this system works. And there’s more – many more things will come to light. During the time of war, they covered it all up. They set the motto “Homeland, Nation, Sakarya.” They only talked about the war, and they talked about separatism. It wasn’t allowed to open up any other debate. Everything was done under their control. Now the war has slowed down a bit. They can no longer cover everything up by invoking “Homeland, Nation, Sakarya” or “national survival.” That’s why these things are coming to light now. The people need to take ownership of this. The people need to see this. It is capitalism’s plunder. It is the capitalists’ plunder. Whenever they’re in a bind, whenever they need capital, they set their sights on the people’s savings. What about the gold stashed under the pillows? They’re channeling capital into the system.


Another issue on the public agenda was the US withdrawal from Southern Kurdistan. There are serious concerns, and to a certain extent, this is understandable. The question is how the gains of Southern Kurdistan can be defended.


There’s this debate: The US withdrew from here, the US withdrew from there, and the US is withdrawing from everywhere in the region. The world has changed; the methods and styles of warfare have changed. It’s costly for the US to maintain troops in certain areas. At the same time, technology has advanced to the point where they no longer fight against ground forces. Instead, they coordinate a handful of technical personnel – whether 50 or 100 – from a central location and conduct operations through them. This isn’t a withdrawal. Could we think of it this way: Does war conform to the logic of politics? They’re going to wage such a fierce war against Iran. Right now, Iran is the US’s main problem, but they’ll remove their bases right next to Iran. This isn’t just about that missile Iran launched. The style and methods of warfare have changed. War has become highly technical. I don’t know – maybe they’re using artificial intelligence, or maybe they’re using this or that method. It’s not quite accurate to assess the withdrawal as a positive move.


Now the debate is about what will happen to the situation in Southern Kurdistan. Southern Kurdistan’s relationships are continuing as usual. But the government in Southern Kurdistan is weak. Undemocratic governments are always weak. They cannot gain support from the people. They cannot create unity. And without unity, the Southern Kurdistan government is weak. author: Unknown
title: Jeff Shantz - Speed Kills
content:
Author

: Jeff Shantz

Title

: Speed Kills

Subtitle

: Snuff Capitalist Acceleration

Date

: 1996, Fall

Source

: Scanned from Anarcho-Syndicalist Review #95, Fall 2026


 Whether we like it or not, capital is accelerationist. Speed-up is built right into the very engine of capitalism. Capital’s drive for accumulation, in competition with other capital for profit, means that it must always go faster, must always accelerate exploitation and value extraction. This is the drive behind the ceaseless, permanent, push for technological advance, from motors to assembly lines to robots to computers, to AI, and beyond.


 Speed is the means by which capital beats its competitors in extracting value. More surplus value in an ever-shorter period of time. Any worker knows the tyranny of the clock in the capitalist workplace. Marx suggests that this surplus value extraction is either absolute, the lengthening of the working say, so we work longer beyond the point that we produce the value equivalent to our wages or relative, narrowing the time it takes us to produce the equivalent of our wages. Relative surplus value is the logic of the speed up—using technology to get us producing more and faster. Both forms of extraction, though, dominate the worker’s lifetime. Denying us rest, breaks, mealtimes, or even bathroom breaks. Stealing our life times— time away from family, from loved ones, from ourselves.


 Speed also, significantly, overcomes obstacles—first and foremost among them the slowness built into human labor by the physical and mental limits and frailties of our bodies. Technological acceleration is therefore about overcoming the human element in labor. It is about controlling us too, taking initiative away from us.


 Reducing and then replacing our numbers, and our capacities to resist or control the labor process. Fundamentally it is about rendering our human labor irrelevant, while doing the same to the embodiment of that labor itself—us.


 Capital has used speed to overcome the limitations posed by workers on value extraction and accumulation. But under current and emerging conditions of accelerating electronicization (AI and its ilk are exemplars), capital is accelerating, not with workers, but without us. The working class becomes an obstacle to be overcome, not only at work but increasingly outside of work. The living bodies of the working class slow down the circuits of capital in distribution (consumption) as well as in production. Capital moves quickly from stealing our life times to stealing our life itself.


 The elimination of jobs at the workplace now coincides with the elimination of former workers outside the workplace under snuff capitalism. And this elimination too must be done at accelerating rates. Time, as always, is money from capital’s perspective.


From Social Services to Snuff Services


 Those expelled from production and (simultaneously) from consumption are too costly for capital, too much of an obstacle to accumulation. As capital becomes more desperate it increasingly sees any supports that might sustain the unemployed, such as welfare, unemployment insurance, social housing, health care, as a transfer of wealth by the state away from capital and to the unproductive and unnecessary. They are, from capital’s perspective, expendable. They must be eliminated. This is the impetus, and organizing principle, of snuff capitalism.


 Like production and consumption themselves, this elimination must be done quickly, at accelerating speeds. Every day the unneeded are kept around is an impediment to accumulation, a drain on capital.


 This elimination must at least keep pace with the elimination of jobs, of workers from work, of consumers from consumption. Time, as always for capital, is money. First and foremost.


 This is driving expansion of and innovation in snuff industries, innovation and expansion of murder infrastructures, innovation and transformation of capital’s states from neoliberal tools (of crisis) to democidal weapons (of extermination).


 This is made to happen through the dual spheres of the state as usual, through law (legality) and force (police). Increasingly it will happen through what were once called social services—health care as assisted suicide and coercive detention, social assistance as death camp labor and medical experimentation.


 One focus of democidal states has been the removal of laws and regulations that would impede capital or slow its circulation, such …

author: anred
title: El podcast de Manuela Santucho: entrega, amor y revolución
content:
El podcast “Manuela Santucho. La vida. Los nombres. El lugar”, realizado por Diego Genoud, publicó su primer episodio el último 7 de septiembre y viene a traernos una historia cargada de emocionalidad y militancia, características que suelen ser disociadas en los vericuetos fetichistas de las lecturas históricas, y más cuando se trata de los setenta.

 Por Nicolás Salas, para ANRed.


“Nenita”, como la reconocen sus familiares y amigos, fue la segunda mujer entre diez hermanos. Nació en la Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires aunque sus raíces y mudanzas siempre orbitaron en dirección a Santiago del Estero.


Esta producción, que puede seguirse en el canal de youtube “Otro periodista”, nos muestra la historia de una militante del Partido Revolucionario de los Trabajadores (PRT) que, como muchos de su generación, se propuso realizar una revolución socialista en la Argentina.


En ningún momento se disimula tamaña ambición. Tampoco se niegan las características de quienes encarnan ese proyecto colectivo. Esta historia nos muestra, a través de “nenita”, que se puede dar la vida por la transformación social y venir de un profundo catolicismo. Que se puede integrar una organización guerrillera sin dejar de lado los gustos por los vestidos y la elegancia. Que sin amor nada importante puede hacerse en la vida.


Su paso por Gramillia, Corrientes, el viaje a Cuba, el diario El Mundo, la defensa de los presos políticos, su amor, el casamiento, el partido, Roby, Perón, Tucumán y los ingenios, el FAS, mil reuniones, “chicho”, Francisco René, Adelita, las primeras caídas, las primeras desapariciones, la disciplina y varios momentos de la vida de Manuela dotan de dinámica a estos primeros cinco capítulos de un podcast que promete mucho más.


Foto: Página 12


El rol de quien asume la narración y la reconstrucción de la historia no es menor. Genoud además de periodista es hijo de Manuela, lo cual imprime una visión humana necesaria y particular. El recorrido por la vida personal de la protagonista no implica en ningún momento el abandono de una lectura política precisa, sino todo lo contrario. Ambas caras de la misma moneda son conjugadas dialécticamente para mostrarnos, a través de una historia individual, un momento trascendental en la lucha de clases contemporánea de la Argentina. Tamaña búsqueda se lleva a cabo sin hacer concesiones a las defecciones que suele generar el paso del tiempo y que, en la actualidad, tiene su expresión en visiones revisionistas tanto por derecha como por “centro”. 


Cabe destacar que es un trabajo sostenido sobre fuentes documentales que incluyen decenas de cintas y grabaciones de entrevistas realizadas durante las últimas décadas. Cada capítulo ronda los 25 minutos, tiempo suficiente para experimentar emociones que van desde la empatía que nos genera una situación familiar particular hasta la bronca por algún acontecimiento político.


Esta producción aparece a 50 años de la desaparición forzada de Manuela Santucho (y gran parte de su familia) a manos de las fuerzas represivas de la última dictadura. El 13 de julio de 1976 la secuestraron en Villa Crespo junto a Cristina Navajas y a Alicia D’Ambra. Se supo que pasó por varios campos de concentración como Orletti, Campo de Mayo, El Vesubio, Coordinación Federal y el Pozo de Banfield. Quienes sobrevivieron a esos lugares y conocieron a Manuela aseguraban que, pese a las torturas y los tormentos, “nenita” se mantuvo fiel a sus principios, dando ánimo al resto de sus compañeros y compañeras, y levantando redes de resistencia en las peores condiciones posibles. Su vida, como lo refleja el podcast, reafirman que las revoluciones las hacen personas de carne y hueso, con sus aciertos y errores, pero ante todo con una entrega sin parangón en el pensamiento enajenado de la sociedad capitalista.

Ringrazio vivamente i compagni dell’Esercito Zapatista di Liberazione Nazionale, le basi d’appoggio dell’organizzazione, chi ci sta seguendo attraverso le trasmissioni in diretta dai 

puyes

 [NdT: i puyes – in lingua maya tseltal chiocciola o conchiglia di fiume – sono le nuove  zone di organizzazione politica e comunitaria delle comunità indigene zapatiste, che sostituiscono i vecchi “caracol”] e anche chi ci accompagna da altri paesi attraverso internet. Un ringraziamento al Capitano Marcos e al Subcomandante Moisés; oggi per me è un onore essere qui con voi.


Sono molto emozionato, e confesso di essere anche molto nervoso. Dopo tutto quello che si è detto in questo seminario, come anche questa mattina, pensavo di intervenire affermando di essere d’accordo con quasi tutto e chiudere così il mio intervento. Ma nonostante questo vi condividerò alcune questioni che spero possano essere di vostro interesse.


Appartengo ad una generazione che ha visto il Messico sommergersi nella barbarie e il mondo entrare in una profonda e grave crisi. Non fraintendetemi, non penso che il Messico o il mondo in precedenza fossero luoghi migliori, ma è necessario accettare che la guerra del capitalismo nei confronti dell’Umanità e dei Territori ci ha condotto verso un punto di non ritorno. Il 2006 è un anno che ha rappresentato per molti di noi un bivio: è l’anno in cui Felipe Calderón Hinojosa ha diffuso e intensificato la guerra in tutto il Messico. Col senno di poi, possiamo renderci conto che in verità quell’anno rappresenta solamente un tassello di una lunga guerra di sfruttamento e espropriazione. Ciò nonostante, è stato anche l’anno in cui diverse geografie del paese hanno cominciato a vivere la brutalità della guerra. Quella guerra che si viveva, con modi e intensità differenti nei vari territori del Messico, si è diffusa in tutti i boschi, foreste, mari, deserti, strade, scuole e posti di lavoro del paese. 


Dal 2011 in poi ho avuto l’opportunità di visitare diversi stati del paese. Durante questi viaggi ho conversato con membri di organizzazioni sociali, con famiglie in cerca di 

desaparecidos

, con famiglie che hanno sofferto femminicidi, con famiglie di persone assassinate. Durante questi colloqui ho conosciuto la morte nelle sue forme più atroci, nelle modalità in cui è possibile arrivare ad assassinare la memoria stessa. Quei discorsi mi hanno fatto capire che in Messico si puo moriré piu volte: esiste la morte fisica, la morte per oblio e la morte di chi, non più in vita, viene perseguitato e colpevolizzato del proprio assassinio.


La maggior parte delle persone con cui ho conversato denuncia ripetutamente la complicità della polizia, dei governi locali e federali con il crimine organizzato. In alcuni casi hanno segnalato l’esistenza di legami diretti tra presidenti municipali, deputati, membri dei partiti politici e i gruppi criminali. Uno dei casi che ho potuto conoscere da vicino è quello di Melchor Flores Hernández, un giovane di 26 anni che lavorava in strada facendo la statua umana. Il

, il personaggio interpretato da Melchor, è stato arrestato dalla polizia di Monterrey, Nuevo León, e poi consegnato ad un gruppo criminale. E da quel momento non si sa più nulla di lui.


Il caso di Melchor non è l’unico, esistono centinaia di casi simili. È grazie alle ricerche dei familiari delle stesse persone

author: Fozzie
title: Chapter 21: Piece Wages
content:
Harry Cleaver's study guide to Karl Marx's Capital volume 1, chapter 21.

Piece wages seem as if workers sell their embodied labor in each piece. Piece wages seem as if the wage is not determined by the value of labor power.

Piece wages and time wages often exist side-by-side:

Marx gives us an example as a point of departure:

1) Setting of piece rates is a source of struggle between workers and capitalists

2) With piece work the need for direct "superindendence" is reduced or even eliminated; workers are forced to work fast and well to meet the going standard of production under the threat of not being fully paid, or losing their job.

3) Piece wages tend to produce hierarchies of wages

4)Piece wages result in workers being willing, or even desirous, of longer working hours.

5) Technological change that increases the productivity of a given time and intensity of labor will:

To illustrate this dynamic, Marx modifies the example previously given on the basis of a doubling of productivity, i.e., total output goes from 24 to 48. As a result:

"Piece-work", to the experienced worker whether in home, factory or field always carries the flavor of exploitation. The subtlety that Marx insists upon - how the form of payment leads workers to drive themselves to high intensity and long hours - is not always immediately apparent to new and naive workers. To them piece-work may seem to provide an opportunity for great achievement: the more you work, the more you get paid. They don't realize at first that the piece rates have been set so that even with their greatest efforts they will earn little in relation to what they produce. They don't realize, because they haven't had the experience, that if they outperform past standards, the piece-rates will be adjusted downward so that their income rises but little, even with increased effort.

In the passage below, from his story "The Apostate", Jack London describes some of this psychological dynamic as well as the physical costs workers may bear under such conditions of exploitation.

After he recovered, he got work in a glass factory. The pay was better, and the work demanded skill. It was piece-work, and the more skilful he was, the bigger wages he earned. Here was incentive. And under this incentive he developed into a remarkable worker.

It was simple work, the tying of glass stoppers into small bottles. At his waist he carried a bundle of twine. He held the bottles between his knees so that he might work with both hands. Thus, in a sitting position and bending over his own knees, his narrow shoulders grew humped and his chest was contracted for ten hours each day. This was not good for the lungs, but he tied three hundred dozen bottles a day.

The superindendent was very proud of him, and brought visitors to look at him. In ten hours three hundred dozen bottles passed through his hands. This meant that he had attained machine-like perfection. All waste movements were eliminated. Every motion of his thin arms, every movement of a muscle in the thin fingers, was swift and accurate. He worked at high tension, and the result was that he grew nervous. At night his muscles twitched in his sleep, and in the daytime he could not relax and rest. He remained keyed up and his muscles continued to twitch. Also he grew sallow and his lint-cough grew worse. Then pneumonia laid hold of the feeble lungs within the contracted chest, and he lost his job in the glass-works.

(Jack London, "The Apostate', in Jack London, Novels & Stories, New York: The Library of America, 1982.

One of the great attractions of piece work and piece wages to capitalists is that with piece rates set low enough, very little supervision is required. In order to earn a living wage workers must work hard, fast and well to produce enough pieces - quite irrespective of whether anyone is looking over their shoulder. The costs of supervision are essentially passed from the capitalist to the workers as they internalize the discipline of piece work and impose work on themselves. This self-imposition of work, of course, goes against workers' instinctive ressentment and resistance to suffering the indignities of alienating work - doing what some one else says to do, they way they say to do it, for their profit and enrichment, and so on. The piece workers, therefore, pay the psychological costs not only of alienation but of the hour-to-hour experience of imposing that alienation on themselves.

author: Erica Malatesta
title: New Stormy Petrel Now Out!
content:
This is the 8th edition of our theoretical magazine in which we discuss issues in more depth. Articles include:


Dossier on AI, Work in the Future Society, Age Verification, the General Strike, Mujeres Libres, and a letter from a reader on veganism.


Editorial


Now and tomorrow


Now: Hope in Every Heart or Business as Usual?


Andy Burnham’s accession to power doesn’t mark any radical change in the direction of the Labour Party. He backs the Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood’s immigration reforms, increasing the wait for indefinite leave to remain from five years to between 10 and 20 years. He supports expanding the use of detention centres. He wrote recently in

The Times

 that “Increasing our national security, in every sense, will be my first priority,” and that arms manufacture would be central in “regenerating and reindustrialising the country.” He threatened that he would “not be squeamish about cutting welfare” to invest more in the arms industry.


He intends to proceed with the £31bn Dreadnought-class boats and with the building of Trident nuclear submarines. He urged EU countries to supply Ukraine with Patriot missiles. He signed a military AI deal with Ukraine, accessing Ukraine’s Avengers AI Labs database. This huge AI database holds data collected by thousands of daylight cameras and infrared sensors across the war zone in Ukraine. They capture footage of millions of objects and the data is then fed back to the Avengers Lab to train new AI models. This will be used to protect military bases from “protesters and hostile actors trying to gain intelligence.” The Burnham administration also will work with Ukraine to explore the development of next-generation low-power AI chips to power drones and robotics.


Burnham appointed Kanishka Narayan as the first AI minister, signalling Labour support for AI, whilst coming out with rhetoric about independence from US Big Tech.


He continues to back Israel and its genocidal policies. Whilst we have experienced the hottest summer on record, Burnham talks about new drilling for oil and gas in the North Sea, exhibiting a complete unconcern about the connection between fossil fuel and climate change. He talks about a “business-friendly socialism”, as if such an obscene coupling was either possible or desirable.


The Future Society


“A map of the world that does not include Utopia, is not even worth glancing at, for it leaves out the one country at which Humanity is always landing… Progress is the realisation of utopias.”


Oscar Wilde


The theme of this issue is ‘The Future Society’. This came about because of our experience of people asking questions about what an anarchist communist society will be like, such as ‘How will it be possible?’, ‘What about crime?’, ‘What about jobs that no one wants to do?’ When many Marxists, and others, envisage a future society it usually involves automation and advanced technology, including AI. While we reject ‘anarcho-primitivism’ (see Issue 7 of Stormy Petrel), we take a critical approach to technology, especially AI. We need to ensure that it will actually enhance our lives as well as be compatible with environmental and resource concerns.


In order to address some of the questions about an anarchist communist society, in each topic we first address the reasons why the status quo is a disaster, both for the working class and the planet. We then also look at the struggles going on today. The attacks on workers’ organisation, surveillance, the insidious insertion of AI into all areas of life, the environmental effects of resource plundering, war, and the drive for growth at any cost, not only have tragic consequences today, but will make it harder for us to create the future we want. We will only be able to collectively create an anarchist communist future if we overthrow capitalism and begin to establish a vision and the foundations for this society.


We have to envision a different future. There has been an ideological onslaught over the past few decades with the capitalist slogan of ‘There Is No Alternative’ advanced over and over again. Any idea of an alternative future is mocked and laughed at. The 19

th

 century vision of a stateless, classless and free society shared by socialists and anarchists is rarely addressed, and dull grey reformism is the order of the day. This was apparent at this year’s Tolpuddle event, where an array of trade union speakers on AI failed to voice any real opposition to it, but just talked …

title: Gary Dean Jaworski - Pitirim A. Sorokin’s Sociological Anarchism
content:
Author

: Gary Dean Jaworski

Title

: Pitirim A. Sorokin’s Sociological Anarchism

Date

: 1993

Notes

: Paper presented at the 62

nd

 Annual Meeting of the Eastern Sociological Society, Arlington, Virginia, April 1992. The author gratefully acknowledges the advice of Robert K. Merton, Lewis A. Coser and two anonymous reviewers for this journal.

Source

:

journals.sagepub.com

.

History of the Human Sciences

, 1993, Vol. 6 No. 3 © 1993 SAGE (London, Newbury Park and New Delhi) pp. 61–77.

doi: 095269519300600304


Introduction


 Pitirim A. Sorokin (1889–1968) was a Russian emigre, an internationally renowned sociologist, the first chairman of the Department of Sociology at Harvard University, a president of the American Sociological Association, among many other honors, and a gadfly to the discipline of sociology (Sorokin, 1950a, 1963a, 1963b). Robin M. Williams, Jr (1980 : 103), a former student of Sorokin’s at Harvard, called his teacher a sui generis thinker and a man who thinks otherwise. He was a thinker who, as Nietzsche might have said, was ‘out of season’ with the discipline with which he identified.


 Sorokin was a lone scholar during the ascendancy of team research (cf. Merton, 1959), a pessimist during a period of postwar optimism, an antipositivist during the reign of positivism, an internationalist during the rise of American sociological hegemony, an advocate of cyclical theories of change while the contrasting view of liberal progressivism prevailed, and a grand theorist during a period of skepticism and hostility toward such theories.


 But times change. At present, when there is a renewed appreciation for grand theory (e.g. Skinner, 1985), when there is a return to cyclical theories of change (e.g. Kennedy, 1987), when there is a renewed interest in altruism (Piliavin and Chamg, 1990), and when, with the evident conclusion of the cold war and collapse of state communism, there is a revived interest in global harmony (see Goldfarb, 1989), the time is ripe for a re-examination of Sorokin’s work. The challenge of this undertaking has been accepted by scholars both here and abroad. Not only is a Russian scholar writing Sorokin’s comprehensive intellectual biography,

[1]

 but in the United States Barry Johnston (1986, 1987, 1991) continues his efforts to elucidate Sorokin’s life and work.


 The present essay contributes in a modest way to this re-examination. It does not provide an analysis of Sorokin’s work in its entirety, which, given the extensiveness of his output, would be a monumental task (e.g. Cowell, 1952). Rather, the present study investigates an important but neglected strain in Sorokin’s oeuvre, the anarchistic dimension of his work. With few exceptions, such as Tiryakian’s (1968) encyclopedia article on Sorokin, most studies fail to mention Sorokin’s links to the anarchist tradition. Yet, my recent survey of Sorokin’s published writings and unpublished correspondence demonstrates the centrality of this tradition to his works.

[2]

 A re-examination of his writings along these lines is long overdue.


 In what follows I first establish the pertinence of this line of thought to an understanding of Sorokin’s work and, second, explore the ethical project of Sorokin’s writings and reveal its roots in ethical anarchism. In the conclusion, I draw implications for future Sorokin studies and for contemporary theorizing.


Sorokin as ‘Conservative, Christian Anarchist’


 Pitirim Alexandrovich Sorokin was born in a rural village in the north of Russia in 1889. The beauty of the terrain, its pristine rivers and lakes, vast forests and flowery meadows, provided an aesthetic counterpoint to the simple but harsh conditions of life. Sorokin’s mother died when he was about 3 years old, and his father, an itinerant artisan, and a loving man when he was sober, became depressed and violent during his occasional alcoholic binges. Leaving home to escape their father’s domination and wrath, Pitirim Alexandrovich and his older brother moved from village to village while earning their living in their father’s trade, as gilders of religious icons and other cult objects (Sorokin, 1963b: 4–7).


 Sorokin’s background in the village communities of northern Russia at the turn of the century provided fertile ground for developing sensibilities favorable to the anarchist tradition in at least two respects. First, the Russian anarchist literature, such as the writings of Peter Kropotkin, was consistent …

author: heinhtetkyaw
title: An Anarchist Perspective on Israel, Palestine, and the Endless Cycle of Violence
content:
From October 7 to the Present: States at War with Human Beings The Israeli–Palestinian conflict cannot be said to have begun on October 7, 2023, just as it cannot simply be reduced to a war between “two nations.”

The roots of this catastrophe go back decades: to the end of the British Mandate, the 1948 war, the establishment of the State of Israel, the displacement and expulsion of more than 700,000 Palestinians, and the emergence of what Palestinians call the Nakba — the catastrophe. Following the 1967 war, the occupation of the West Bank, East Jerusalem, and Gaza, the expansion of Israeli settlements, and extensive restrictions on Palestinians’ lives and freedom of movement further entrenched structures of inequality and domination. Today, nearly 5.9 million Palestinian refugees are eligible for services provided by UNRWA.From an anarchist perspective, the question is not simply: “Which state has the right to govern which territory?” The more fundamental question is: Why should human beings have to submit to states, armies, borders, and military institutions in order to live, enjoy freedom, and secure their safety? October 7: A Crime That Cannot Be Justified On October 7, 2023, Hamas forces and several other Palestinian armed groups attacked southern Israel. Approximately 1,200 people were killed, and 251 were abducted and taken to Gaza. Civilians were among those targeted in the assault. According to the findings of the United Nations Independent International Commission of Inquiry, hostage-taking, murder, torture, and other acts against civilians constituted war crimes. From an anarchist standpoint, no occupation, repression, or historical injustice can justify the deliberate killing of civilians or the taking of hostages. But this principle must be applied consistently, without exception. If killing an Israeli child is a crime, killing a Palestinian child is equally a crime. If taking an Israeli civilian hostage is a crime, depriving an entire civilian population of water, food, medicine, and security cannot be justified as a “right to self-defence” either. From “Revenge” to Collective Punishment Following October 7, the Israeli government launched a large-scale war in Gaza. The scale of killing, destruction, displacement, and deprivation of basic necessities went far beyond a limited military operation against armed groups.In 2024, the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry reported that Israeli operations in Gaza involved war crimes and crimes against humanity, including murder, extermination, forcible transfer, torture, and the use of starvation as a method of warfare. The same Commission also identified Hamas and other Palestinian armed groups as responsible for war crimes committed during the October 7 attack. In September 2025, the same Commission went a step further, concluding that, based on its investigation, Israel had committed genocide in Gaza. This is a finding by a UN Commission of Inquiry; it is not the same as a final ruling by the International Court of Justice in the genocide case, and the two should not be conflated. South Africa's case against Israel remains before the International Court of Justice. In November 2024, the International Criminal Court also issued arrest warrants for Benjamin Netanyahu and Yoav Gallant on charges of war crimes and crimes against humanity. These decisions, however, do not constitute final convictions; they are part of an ongoing international judicial process. An Anarchist Is Neither a Supporter of the Israeli State nor of a Palestinian State This is where the difference between an anarchist perspective and many prevailing narratives becomes clear. Anarchism fundamentally opposes turning human beings into soldiers serving a state. From this perspective:

The State of Israel, even if it regards the protection of its citizens as its responsibility, has no right to pursue security through mass killing and military domination over another people.

Hamas, even if it describes itself as a resistance movement, has no right to kill civilians or take hostages in the name of the Palestinian people. No state, army, or armed organization owns human lives.

“National security” cannot be used to justify depriving millions of people of their freedom and dignity.

The suffering of one community must never become an excuse for repressing another.

Victims must not be turned into soldiers serving state ideologies.From this perspective, the binary choice between …

title: «Construir colectivamente donde dicen que no se puede»: presentan experiencia de los barrios comunitarios Crisol Popular y Norita Cortiñas
content:
¿Cómo se construye un barrio cuando todo parece indicar que no se puede? Este jueves 8 de octubre, a las 17, se presentará en la Facultad de Ciencias Exactas y Naturales de la UBA el cuadernillo “Barrios comunitarios: construir colectivamente donde dicen que no se puede”, que sistematiza la experiencia de los barrios comunitarios Crisol Popular, en Cuartel V, Moreno, y Norita Cortiñas, en Guernica. La actividad se desarrollará en el Aula 1115 del Edificio Cero + Infinito y contará con un conversatorio sobre el rol de la universidad y la academia en los procesos de organización territorial.


La publicación reconstruye una experiencia nacida después de la recuperación de tierras de Guernica en 2020 y desarrollada a partir de la organización comunitaria, el acceso a la vivienda, el trabajo autogestionado y la articulación con equipos técnicos, universidades y organismos públicos. Ambos proyectos comparten “acceso a la vivienda con perspectiva comunitaria”, “asamblea como método de organización”, “defensa de los derechos humanos” y “generación de trabajo autogestionado comunitario”.

Por ANRed.

El cuadernillo reconstruye una experiencia que busca enfrentar una problemática estructural.

El barrio comunitario

Crisol Popular

Cuartel V

, adquirido luego de que uno de los proyectos impulsados por las asambleas fuera aprobado por la Secretaría de Integración Socio Urbana. En el caso del barrio

Norita Cortiñas

, la propia organización logró concretar la compra comunitaria de un terreno de dos hectáreas en Guernica, después de que el segundo proyecto no obtuviera financiamiento estatal.

”, la “

” y la “

generación de trabajo autogestionado comunitario

La publicación también sistematiza el trabajo realizado para resolver necesidades básicas que el acceso formal a una vivienda no garantiza por sí solo. Entre los objetivos aparecen “lograr condiciones dignas de habitabilidad para las familias de ambos barrios”, garantizar agua potable, mejorar el acceso a la energía y desarrollar sistemas de drenaje y tratamiento de efluentes.
