title: Elecciones Brasil 2026, una batalla contra el imperialismo
content:
Las amplias elecciones que el próximo 4 de octubre tendrán lugar en Brasil, en las que se elegirán presidente, gobernadores y legisladores, son de importancia estratégica para nuestra Abya Yala y para todo el globo terráqueo. Brasil es el 5to país más extenso, está entre las 10 economías más grandes y demográficamente ocupa el séptimo lugar en el mundo.


Por otra parte, el Brasil de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, del Partido de los Trabajadores (PT), forma parte de los BRICS, quienes vienen abogando por un orden mundial más justo y equilibrado; su principal socio comercial es China, con una tendencia al crecimiento en su intercambio comercial; ha hecho fuertes críticas al ente sionista que, con la ayuda de los EE. UU., está ejecutando un genocidio contra el pueblo palestino. Todo lo anterior lo convierte en el principal objetivo del presidente Trump en el hemisferio. Ya le ha impuesto a las importaciones de EE. UU. desde Brasil, entre el 12.5 % y el 50 % de aranceles, lo que ha hecho descender las exportaciones brasileñas hacia los EE. UU. a sus niveles más bajos desde 1997, lo que ha afectado negativamente su economía, expresado esto, en el bajo crecimiento de su PIB durante 2026.


Trump y su secretario de Estado, Marco Rubio, se han estado pronunciando a favor de la candidatura de Flavio Bolsonaro y criticado ferozmente el juicio que se le siguió a Jair Bolsonaro, por el intento del golpe de Estado, llegando al extremo de tomar medidas coercitivas unilaterales contra el juez que llevó la causa.


La intromisión de los EE. UU. en los asuntos internos de otros países es bien conocida. En Nuestra América han derrocado decenas de gobiernos e instalado dictaduras militares, han desestabilizado gobiernos legítimos, han bloqueado e impuesto medidas ilegales e inhumanas contra pueblos enteros y han llegado a violar la soberanía de varios países con agresiones militares directas: México, Cuba, Haití, Nicaragua, República Dominicana, Panamá, Granada y Venezuela son ejemplo de ello. Han manipulado elecciones abiertamente, teniendo los últimos 18 meses los ejemplos de Honduras, Ecuador, Colombia y Perú, donde, de manera grotesca y descarada, han impulsado candidatos, amenazado a la población con bloquear el envío de remesas, amedrentado a los gobiernos y empresarios con elevar aranceles y han utilizado sus mecanismos de manipulación y desinformación contra amplios sectores de la población, utilizando técnicas como la Big Data, los algoritmos de las redes sociales y buscadores y la última tendencia que es el uso de la inteligencia artificial como una más de estas nefastas herramientas.


La injerencia de EE. UU. en los asuntos internos de decenas de países, ha quedado registrado en diversos libros, como los de William Blum (2005) y (2006), Guenther Roppel (2005) y Luis Suárez Salazar (2006) entre otros. En el caso brasileño ya en 1960 los militares, por presión de la embajada yanqui, exigieron y lograron la salida del presidente Quadros, quien pocos meses antes de ser destituido había otorgado la máxima condecoración, para autoridades extranjeras, al Che Guevara. En 1964 le darían un golpe de Estado al presidente Joao Goulart, poco después de anunciar la expropiación y redistribución de tierras privadas y la nacionalización de refinerías de petróleo y lograrían la destitución de la presidente Dilma Rousseffa del PT, a través de un impeachment, en 2016.


Por otra parte, el candidato con mayores posibilidades de disputar la presidencia a Lula, es el actual senador del Partido Liberal (PL), Flávio Bolsonaro. Como digno hijo de su padre, el ex presidente Jair Bolsonaro, viajó a Washington a reunirse con el secretario de Estado, para planear la campaña en contra de Lula, lo que resultó en la aplicación de aranceles del 50 % a importantes productos provenientes de Brasil, pretendiendo afectar a todo el pueblo de Brasil, con la intención de robarle apoyo al gobierno de Lula. Pocos días después de esta visita, llegó Rubio a declarar que, “Brasil no es amigo de Estados Unidos”, lo cual fue dirigido a genera malestar y angustia en las clases medias y altas del país.


Flavio Bolsonaro también visitó Tel Aviv, buscando el apoyo de Netanyahu y ofreció cambiar la embajada de Brasil a Jerusalem, en caso de ganar las elecciones. El apoyo sionista es muy importante, ya que tienen relaciones muy importantes con los grandes grupos económico-financieros que manejan la economía brasileña y mundial. author: Helmut Weiss
title: „Was wir nicht verdienen, zahlen wir nicht“ – eine landesweite Initiative in Spanien organisiert Mietstreik
content:
Dossier


„…

Es ist wahrlich kein Aprilscherz. Am 1. April 2020 treten nun viele Familien, Selbstständige sowie kleine und mittlere Firmen im ganzen spanischen Staat in den Mietenstreik. Mietergewerkschaften, wie sie ausgehend von Katalonien ab 2017 wie das „Sindicat de Llogaters i Llogateres“ gegründet haben, und soziale Organisation rufen zum Streik gegen fehlende Notmaßnahmen der sozialdemokratischen Regierung für die einfache Bevölkerung auf. Die 200 Initiativen schlagen vor, ab April die Miete nicht mehr zu bezahlen. (…) Eigentlich hatten sich die Mietergewerkschaften wegen explodierender Mieten gegründet. Sie forderten bisher vor allem stärkere Mieterrechte und eine Regulierung der explodierenden Mieten, vor denen spanische Gesetze praktisch nicht schützen. Einige der Aktivisten hatten Hoffnungen in die neue Regierung gesetzt, doch sie wurden massiv enttäuscht

…“ – aus dem

Beitrag „Mietenstreik wegen Coronavirus in Spanien“ von Ralf Streck am 01. April 2020 bei telepolis


 über die landesweite Initiative. Siehe dazu die weitere Entwicklung und Hintergründe:


„Ni una Maricarmen más“: Zwangsräumung der 87-jährigen Maricarmen Abascal treibt massive Proteste gegen Wohnungsnot und Mietwucher über Madrid hinaus an 


Die 87-jährige Maricarmen, deren Zwangsräumung die Bewegung in Spanien radikalisiert hat, ist vor der erkämpften Rückkehr in ihre Wohnung erschöpft gestorben 


„

Die 87-Jährige ist am Mittwoch im Krankenhaus Gregorio Marañón in Madrid verstorben, wie die Mietervereinigung in einer Erklärung bestätigte (…) In dieser Erklärung, die auch von ihrer Familie und ihrer Anwältin unterzeichnet wurde, erinnern sie daran, dass sie seit der Zwangsräumung im Krankenhaus lag. „Zwar wurde eine historische Einigung erzielt, die ihr die Rückkehr in ihre Wohnung ermöglicht hätte, doch diese Lösung kam viel zu spät“, bedauern sie. Die Unterzeichner sind der Ansicht, dass die Ereignisse nach ihrer Zwangsräumung – Massendemonstrationen, Zeltlager auf den Plätzen, vorgezogene Wahlen und der Aufruf zu einem Generalstreik – „einen Wendepunkt in der Geschichte dieses Landes“ darstellen, warnen jedoch, dass „der Preis, den wir dafür gezahlt haben, zu hoch war“. Und sie verabschieden sich mit der Bitte, die sie ihnen immer wieder gesagt hat: „Kämpft, kämpft weiter für das, was euch gehört.“


Dank des gesellschaftlichen Drucks stand zum ersten Mal in Spanien eine zwangsgeräumte Person kurz davor, in ihr Zuhause zurückzukehren, nachdem der Eigentümer bereit war, einen neuen Mietvertrag abzuschließen. Dennoch hatten die Zwangsräumung und die vorangegangenen Versuche Maricarmen körperlich stark mitgenommen, sodass sie sich in ihren letzten Lebensjahren nur noch im Rollstuhl fortbewegen konnte und bei den alltäglichen Verrichtungen auf Hilfe angewiesen war. Hinter ihr lagen fast sieben Jahre gerichtlicher Auseinandersetzungen, um in ihrem Zuhause bleiben zu können. In den letzten Monaten hatte sich ihr körperlicher Zustand verschlechtert. Sie hatte an Muskelmasse verloren, hatte Schwierigkeiten beim Essen und sagte, dass sich sogar ihre Stimme verändert habe. „Es hat mich in jeder Hinsicht beeinträchtigt. Ich bin jetzt nicht mehr ich selbst“, erzählte sie zwei Tage, bevor sie ihr Haus verließ

…“ span.

Artikel von Lucía Franco und Beatriz Olaizola vom 7.10.2026 in El Pais online


 (maschinenübersetzt) und auch:


Der Verband der Mieterinnengewerkschaften ruft zu einer Schweigeminute und einem Generalstreik für Maricarmen auf


„

Heute, Freitag, um 12 Uhr mittags an allen Arbeits- und Bildungseinrichtungen im ganzen Land. Der Aufruf des Verbandes der Mieterinnengewerkschaften erfolgt, nachdem sich die PP und Vox am Donnerstag geweigert hatten, in der Madrider Regionalversammlung eine Schweigeminute für Maricarmen einzulegen, mit der Begründung, sie wollten „nicht zu ihrer politischen Instrumentalisierung“ in einer „interessengeführten Kampagne“ beitragen, obwohl gerade die Verstorbene selbst dazu aufgerufen hatte, für die politische Sache gegen Zwangsräumungen und für menschenwürdigen Wohnraum zu kämpfen und sich zu mobilisieren. (…) Deshalb bitten wir dich, alle Arbeitnehmerinnen und Arbeitnehmer sowie die gesamte Gesellschaft, morgen, Freitag, um 12 Uhr mittags an allen Arbeits- und Bildungseinrichtungen des Staates eine Schweigeminute einzulegen. Außerdem bitten wir dich, dich darauf vorzubereiten, dass wir am 11. November einen historischen Generalstreik durchführen. Wir werden nicht aufhören, bis wir alles verändert …

author: Harriet Williamson
title: The Greens Are Still Relevant. They Just Need a Strategy
content:
Labour has held on in former prime minister Keir Starmer’s vacated seat of Holborn and St Pancras – a constituency the party has never lost since its creation in 1983 – with Green leader Zack Polanski coming in second. Camden council leader and Starmer ally Sagal Abdi-Wali won 45% of the vote, down 3.75% on Labour’s 2024 general election result, while the Greens more than tripled their vote share, taking 33%.


There are certainly some reasons for optimism among Green supporters this morning, while Polanski is asked on the mainstream media round if he’ll now be standing down as party leader until all our ears bleed. (Answer, no he won’t.)


The Cortado


          Get your shot of political analysis from

Ash Sarkar

 and

Steven Methven

, every Monday and Friday morning.

Email:

Privacy Policy

. Try again later.

The Greens took more of the vote last night than their combined 2024 vote share with Starmer’s nearest challenger, the independent and former South African MP Andrew Feinstein. The local campaign group born out of Feinstein’s challenge to Starmer on his record on Gaza, the Camden People’s Alliance, endorsed Polanski this time around.


While turnout was down on the last election – 2024’s “loveless landslide” – at 39% compared to 54%, we saw a 13% Labour to Green swing.


Ultimately, around 3,000 votes separated the victorious Abdi-Wali (12,292) and Polanski (8,928), and prime minister Andy Burnham can breathe a sigh of relief that the first major electoral test to his premiership is won.


There’s no doubt that Abdi-Wali benefitted from the ‘Burnham bounce’. She might be smiley and local, but her council carries

an appalling record on housing

 in the borough – a brief she was directly responsible for as Camden’s former housing lead – and she was tainted by her association with Starmer and the Starmite project that,

according to a valuable

 two-part

Tribune deep-dive

, birthed her candidacy.


There was something vaguely nauseating about Abdi-Wali campaigning on a message of “hope” for the people of Holborn and St Pancras when

on top of being council leader

 from May of this year, her party has always held the seat – including with a sitting prime minister. If Labour was going to bring hope to this constituency, it would’ve done it already.


But Abdi-Wali,

‘ming-vased’ by her party

, received remarkably little mainstream press scrutiny throughout the campaign (

remind you of anyone?

), as the – allow me a moment to adjust my chic tinfoil hat – political-media class closed ranks against the Greens.


The drop in last night’s

Lib Dem vote share

 alone can be taken as a suggestion of negative mobilisation against the Green party, who’ve weathered months of bad faith attacks after the political and media establishment swung back into action following

a Polanski tweet

 around the Golders Green stabbing.


Polanski’s personal approval ratings continue to show the strain, with the Green leader dipping four points below Nigel Farage on -28 in a

More in Common poll

 on Wednesday. The same pollster also has Westminster voting intention for the Greens

on 8%

, while

YouGov shows 11%

 – down from a March high of 21%. It’s unlikely that a deluge of

negative attention

 and the resurgence of an antisemitism narrative over the Greens’ recently-passed ‘Zionism is Racism’ conference motion will have helped matters, either.


While the result of this hotly-contested byelection was ultimately closer than the bookies’ odds (16/1 on Polanski yesterday) made out, Gorton and Denton this was not. The terrain has changed, and the Greens have not yet adapted quickly or robustly enough with it. Burnham in Number 10 requires a different approach for the party to

the one that worked

 under Starmer’s toxic premiership.


But

in her acceptance speech

 this morning, Abdi-Wali accepted key parts of the Greens’ electoral programme – public ownership of water and addressing the housing crisis. Polanski’s party is reshaping Labour in the face of everything the political and media elite can throw at it.


There’s no question of Green irrelevance, only of Green strategy. In my book, that’s a reason to be hopeful.

title: Río Negro: la Cámara de Bariloche confirmó el desalojo de la Lof Inalef y la comunidad anuncia que seguirá resistiendo
content:
La Cámara de Apelaciones en lo Civil de Bariloche confirmó la sentencia que ordena el desalojo de la Lof Inalef, en la Rinconada de Inalef, paraje Mallín Ahogado, Río Negro. «Informamos que la Cámara de Apelaciones en lo Civil de Bariloche ha dictado un fallo desfavorable para nuestro Lof. Se confirmó la sentencia anterior y sigue en pie el pedido de desalojo sobre nuestro territorio», informó la comunidad este miércoles 7 de octubre. La comunidad denunció, además, falencias en su primera defensa técnica y anunció que continuarán apelando y sosteniendo la permanencia territorial: «esto no termina acá. Seguiremos con los recursos y acciones que correspondan, defendiendo nuestra permanencia en el territorio». El nuevo fallo se produce en un escenario de creciente conflictividad territorial en la Patagonia y días después de que la Corte Suprema reactivara la derogación de la Ley de Tierras Rurales impulsada por el gobierno de Javier Milei.

Por ANRed.


La

Lof Inalef vuelve a quedar frente a una orden de desalojo

 sobre un territorio que reivindica como ancestral, luego de que la

Cámara de Apelaciones en lo Civil de Bariloche confirmó la sentencia que ordena el desalojo del territorio mapuche ubicado


en la Rinconada de Inalef, paraje Mallín Ahogado, El Bolsón, Río Negro.


La comunidad informó este miércoles 7 de octubre que recibió un nuevo revés judicial y cuestionó tanto la decisión como el desempeño de la primera defensa técnica: «informamos que la Cámara de Apelaciones en lo Civil de Bariloche ha dictado un fallo desfavorable para nuestro Lof.

Se confirmó la sentencia anterior y sigue en pie el pedido de desalojo sobre nuestro territorio»

, comunicaron desde la Lof Inalef, que anticipó que continuará recurriendo la resolución: «esto no termina acá.

Seguiremos con los recursos y acciones que correspondan, defendiendo nuestra permanencia en el territorio

«.


El conflicto tiene antecedentes de larga data. En mayo de este año, la jueza

Paola Bernardini

 había dictado una

sentencia de desalojo en favor de Juan Lux Auroux

, mientras en otra causa

el exintendente de El Bolsón Félix Argentino Merino había obtenido una resolución similar sobre tierras de la familia Inalef

. La comunidad sostiene que se trata de un territorio ancestral y que distintos procesos judiciales desconocen esa historia.


Foto del aniversario de el Bolsón del 28 de enero del 2026. Se lo ve al gobernador Alberto Weretilneck, al intendente Bruno Pogliano y el hijo de Félix Argentino Merino, el abanderado.


La propia documentación judicial incorpora antecedentes sobre esa ocupación: en la causa vinculada a Auroux consta que

el Consejo de Desarrollo de Comunidades Indígenas (CODECI) reconoció en 2018 la conformación de la Lof Inalef y tuvo por acreditada “la posesión ancestral, tradicional, actual y pública” sobre tierras de sus abuelos José Antonio Inalef y María Antonia Leviu, registradas por el Estado desde 1907

. El expediente también señala que la tramitación del relevamiento territorial de la Comunidad Newenche, de la que forma parte la Lof Inalef, se inició en 2012.


El comunicado de este miércoles cuestiona además la actuación de quienes ejercieron inicialmente la representación legal de la comunidad: «sabemos cómo está jugando la política hoy en día. Además,

la primera defensa técnica presentó graves falencias no incluyó nuestros testigos ni nuestras pruebas y no ejerció la defensa en etapas clave

«, denunciaron. En este marco,

la Lof anunció que continuará utilizando las herramientas judiciales disponibles y convocó a las comunidades y organizaciones que históricamente acompañaron su lucha

.


El antecedente reciente muestra que esa red de solidaridad ya tuvo una expresión concreta en junio de este año, cuando la Lof Inalef convocó a un trawn frente a la amenaza de desalojo y recibió el

acompañamiento de comunidades mapuche, organizaciones de derechos humanos, sindicatos, movimientos sociales y organizaciones ambientales de la Comarca Andina

. Entre otras, acompañaron Lof Coronado-Inalef, Lof Pu Huayteka, Lof Che Buenuleo, Lof Quemquemtrew, la APDH, la CTA, organizaciones docentes y asambleas ambientales.


La disputa territorial se encuentra además atravesada por una historia de violencia:

en agosto de 2024, Juan Carlos Villa fue asesinado a tiros por un efectivo de la Policía de Río Negro durante un operativo en la zona de Rinconada de Inalef y su hijo Emanuel resultó gravemente herido

. La Coordinadora del …

title: "She Put Her Body on the Line": Maricarmen, 87, Dies; Her Eviction Sparked Spain Housing Protests
content:
The 87-year-old pensioner in Spain whose eviction from her lifelong home sparked nationwide protests has died. María del Carmen Abascal, better known as Maricarmen, died on Wednesday just hours before she was set to sign a new rental agreement. She was forcibly removed from her Madrid apartment last month on a stretcher after the private investment company that owns the building hiked her rent. After massive public outcry, the landlord had agreed to allow her back into her apartment.


Independent Spanish journalist María Carrión says that although Maricarmen’s story galvanized much of the country, evictions like hers are “a daily occurrence” in Spain.


“Rents have gone up 80% in the last 10 years, while salaries have not kept up,” Carrión says. “Young people cannot leave their homes. They cannot become independent or start families. And this is what people are trying to change from the street.”

title: Çeşme Belediye Başkan Yardımcısı 16 aydır tutukluydu: Tahliye edildiği gün yine gözaltına alındı
content:
İstanbul Büyükşehir Belediyesine (İBB) yönelik yürütülen soruşturma kapsamında yaklaşık 16 aydır Silivri Cezaevi’nde iddianamesiz tutuklu bulunan Çeşme Belediye Başkan Yardımcısı Onur Gülin, hakim karşısına çıktığı ilk duruşmada tahliye edildi. Ancak Gülin, aynı gün Çeşme Belediyesine düzenlenen eş zamanlı operasyonda hakkında verilen yeni gözaltı kararı nedeniyle özgürlüğüne kavuşamadan İzmir İl Jandarma Komutanlığı’na sevk edilecek.

Onur Gülin, 20 Mayıs 2025 tarihinde eşi Yelda Gülin’in ameliyatı için bulunduğu hastaneden gözaltına alınarak tutuklanmıştı. Kasım 2025’te hazırlanan yaklaşık 4 bin sayfalık ana İBB iddianamesinde yer almayan Gülin, süreç içerisinde kısa süreli bir tahliye kararı alsa da savcılığın itirazı üzerine Silivri Cezaevi’nde kalmaya devam etti. İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı’nın ana dosyadan ayırarak 21 Temmuz 2026’da hazırladığı ek iddianamede, Gülin ve beraberindeki sanıklara İBB Basın Yayın ve Halkla İlişkiler Daire Başkanlığı ihalelerine ilişkin "ihaleye fesat karıştırma", "rüşvet" ve "kamu zararından dolandırıcılık" suçlamaları yöneltildi.

İstanbul 7. Ağır Ceza Mahkesi’nde dün görülen davanın ilk duruşmasında mahkeme heyeti, aralarında Onur Gülin’in de bulunduğu 5 sanığın tahliyesine karar verirken bir sanığın tutukluluğunun devamına hükmetti.

İzmir Büyükşehir Belediye Başkanı Cemil Tugay'ın AKP'ye geçtiği günün sabahında dün Çeşme Belediyesine yönelik 12 kişi hakkında "suç örgütü kurma", "rüşvet", "irtikap" ve "resmi belgede sahtecilik" suçlamalarıyla başlatılan soruşturmanın ihbarla başladığı öğrenildi.

Onur Gülin'in yarım kalan tahliye sevinci ise ilk değil. 4 Aralık’taki aylık tutukluluk incelemesinde aralarında Ekrem İmamoğlu’nun şoförlerinin de bulunduğu 21 kişilik gruptan Gülin dahil 19 kişi hakkında tahliye kararı verildi.

İzmir’den gelen ailesi ve iki küçük kızıyla cezaevi kapısında buluşmayı bekleyen Gülin, savcılığın jet hızıyla yaptığı itiraz üzerine cezaevinden çıkamadan, gece yarısı jandarma karakoluna götürülerek 9 saat içinde yeniden tutuklandı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

Das Projet-Evasions ist ein mehrsprachiges Netzwerk anarchistischer Freundschaften, das seit 2019 besteht. Nach sieben fröhlichen Jahren, in denen wir unsere kleinen Aktivitäten* durchgeführt haben, ist es nun an der Zeit, euch um Unterstützung zu bitten.

author: ACG
title: When history accelerates: Maricarmen’s eviction
content:
We publish below the statement from the Spanish group Liza on the Maricarmen mobilisation and the need for revolutionary organisation.


Context: On Saturday, September 26, thousands of people marched through the streets of Madrid to protest the eviction of 87-year-old disabled  Maricarmen Abascal from her home. Her door was broken down by local riot police, and she was evicted on a stretcher despite the resistance of a cordon of protesters. Maricarmen, who had lived in her apartment for 70 years, instantly became a symbol of the housing crisis plaguing Spain, particularly in major cities. Whose fault is it? Rampant gentrification, in which real estate developers systematically buy up buildings in city centres, taking the opportunity to “revise” rents. Maricarmen’s rent, which was around 500 euros per month, was increased by 275% to 2,750 euros! Anger swept across Spain, withtens of thousands mobilised and fifty demonstrations,, particularly in Madrid, where the demonstrations, claimed as involving as high as 500,000, culminated in an impromptu encampment at Puerta del Sol, reminiscent of the 2011 protests that sparked the Indignados movement. This time, a few nights of occupation were enough for the real estate company that had evicted Maricarmen to reverse its decision, release her from the hospital, and reinstate her in her apartment, cancelling the rent increase it had planned to impose. While applauding this outcome, the Puerta del Sol “campers” are maintaining the pressure, as numerous other evictions are taking place daily across Spain. They are demanding that the “socialist” government enact a new, more protective law to curb rising purchase and rental prices.

Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez promised once more to introduce a new bill to regulate rent levels.  However, this was blocked by the conservative People’s Party (PP) and far-right Vox and the centre-right, pro-independence Together for Catalonia (JxCat). Sánchez has now called a snap election.


On the political climate and the need for revolutionary organisation


“Revolutions have their own rhythm, punctuated by accelerations and decelerations. They also have their own geometry, in which the straight line breaks at the bifurcations and sharp turns of history.” Daniel Bensaid,

Politics as a Strategic Art


There is a fundamental difference between chronological time and political time. The former unfolds in a seemingly uniform manner: days follow days, and development is linear. The latter, however, under the dialectical logic of a contradictory reality, is very different: There are historical periods in which months or even years seem to contain very few substantial transformations, while there are moments in which, in a matter of days, political reality can be radically transformed.


This means that political time cannot be understood simply as the succession of events on the calendar. It is, above all, the pace at which the relationships between social forces, institutions, organisations, and the possibilities for political action change. There are specific events that, based on the accumulation of internal contradictions, appear as turning points, making possible, in qualitative terms, what until recently was unthinkable.


A society can remain seemingly stable for years and yet be accumulating contradictions. These contradictions don’t necessarily manifest themselves immediately. They can remain separate, partially invisible, or even appear unconnected. An economic crisis, a labour dispute, a housing crisis, a particular police action, a popular mobilisation, or an institutional crisis may seem, individually, like isolated phenomena. However, they can establish connections between them: each event modifies the conditions under which the next ones occur, and each new conflict can amplify, accelerate, or transform the previous ones. It is at this point that the acceleration of political time appears, the concrete expression of latent contradictions.


It is not that an isolated event creates a revolutionary situation out of thin air. Rather, it happens that a prior accumulation of contradictions finds certain events capable of condensing them and making them politically visible. The event then acts as a catalyst for processes that were already developing in society.


“Men make their own history, but they do not make it as they please; they do not make it under self-chosen circumstances, but under circumstances directly encountered, given and …

author: Judy Mundey
title: Judy Mundey: ‘Public housing needed as housing crisis deepens’
content:
This is a slightly abridged version of a speech by Judy Mundey, housing campaigner and women's rights activist, to a meeting focused on NSW Labor’s development plan in the Bays West precinct, organised by Better Futures Coalition on September 29.

The Sydney Morning Herald, in May, referred to twin babies born to a mother who lived and gave birth to them in a tent on the banks of the Murrumbidgee River at Wagga Wagga in NSW. One died; the other had to be hospitalised.

A local councillor said the tragedy was a predictable result of systemic failures to address homelessness. He put the problem down to a lack of public housing.

The SMH editorial referred to the surge in people living in cars, tents and caravan parks, describing it as having echoes of the Depression era.

In Sydney, people are sleeping in the St James railway station tunnel, parks and other forms of less than salubrious accommodation.

Then there is the scourge of domestic violence and the desperate need for safe housing for the victim-survivors. For many women it is a choice between living with domestic violence or homelessness. The refuge system is unable to cope and thousands are on the waiting list for public housing.

Renting in the private property market also presents problems.

A recent estimate said that, nationwide, more than 1.25 million low-income households are in financial stress. Even where people can find rental accommodation, it is often less than stable.

A new report from Adelaide University said children who grow up in rental housing move every 2.3 years, on average, and that by the age of 14 a child in private rental had moved an average of six times, with some as often as 10 times.

Such frequent moves can incur or inflict other disadvantages, such as changing schools and the loss of friendship, sporting and social relationships.

We are not only in the midst of a housing crisis, we are experiencing a systemic failure to address it.

There is no shortage of promises meant to rectify the problem. Recently, NSW Labor announced some 9,400 homes would be built in the Woolahra/Edgecliff area, with towers of 32 and 34 stories. Almost all such proposals involve the private sector and that has not always gone well.

People will recall the examples of developer-built projects with serious defects, such as Opal Towers in 2018 and Mascot Towers in 2019, with some homes remaining uninhabitable.

Peoples’ lives have been ruined. They save and borrow, only to find they cannot not live in their new home but there is no financial recovery. At that time, developers were able to employ private certifiers.

The explosion of defect-riddled apartment project failures with their multi-million dollar repair bills prompted the NSW government to appoint NSW’s first Building Commissioner in 2019.

But then came the collapse of Dyldam disaster in 2020, one of NSW’s biggest apartment builders, with debts of half a billion dollars. The NSW building regulator identified serious defects in a 230 apartment development in Baulkham Hills, including defects so serious as to be labelled a threat to human life. That development is still undergoing repair work.

There are almost daily reports about the impact of these dodgy developers.

The latest dodgy developer in the spotlight is Bathla. It has collapsed, owing debts of $3.3 billion. Many buyers have been left in the lurch, losing large sums paid as deposits.

Bathla’s work was not only riddled with defects, it also engaged in unsafe work practices. It was fined $135,000 in 2018 over a serious injury on a project at Doonside and was slapped with more than 300 notices by Safe Work NSW relating to safety issues.

Thousands of partially-built properties have been left unfinished.

These collapses has inevitably had a devastating effect on those further down the supply chain — suppliers, sub contractors and employees are owed, as are those who paid deposits.

Bathla’s collapse is also a disaster for the national housing supply, as there are 14,000 apartments stalled.

The NSW target for new housing is already running well behind target.

The Chris Minns Labor government pledged to build 378,000 homes by mid 2029. This requires 22,000 homes to be delivered each year until mid 2029. There appears to be a massive disparity between the government’s promises and its actual delivery.

Notwithstanding these dodgy developer disasters, Labor seems wedded to private development.

But there is an alternative — public housing …

content:

Bertolt Brecht


2004 verkaufte der Berliner Senat in einer SPD-PDS Regierung 65.000 Wohnungen der städtischen Wohnungsgesellschaft GSW zum Schnäppchenpreis von 400 Mio Euro an private Spekulanten, der Wohnungsbestand ging 2011 schließlich an die Deutsche Wohnen über, die mittlerweile in einer Fusion mit Vonovia zum größten börsenorientierte Wohnungsunternehmen in Deutschland wurde. 2019 werden 6000 Wohnungen, also rund 10 Prozent der 2004 verkauften Wohnungen, für 920 Mio Euro vom ‘rot-rot-grünen’ Senat unter Federführung der PdL Stadtentwicklungssenatorin zurückgekauft. 2021 werden dann für knapp 2,5 Milliarden Euro an die 15.000 weitere Wohnungen mit Schwerpunkt Kreuzberg von Deutsche Wohnen/Vonovia zurückgekauft. Seitdem dürfen sich die Mieter in den Hochhäusern rund um das Kottbusser Tor über steigende Mieten und explodierende Nebenkosten freuen, die alles weit in den Schatten stellen, was die Profitmaximierungsexperten der Deutsche Wohnen zu verantworten hatten.


Sämtliche im Zuge der Kahlschlagsanierung Ende der 70er entstandenen ‘Neubausiedlungen’ rund um das Kottbusser Tor weisen einen extremen Sanierungsstau auf, ständig fallen wichtige Infrastruktur wie Fahrstühle aus, behinderte Mieter, die auf Rollstühle angewiesen sind, sitzen teilweise monatelang in ihren Wohnungen fest. Wie sich die städtische Wohnungsbaugesellschaft HOWOGE, die jetzt auch in Kreuzberg besitzt, eine “Mieterfreudliche Sanierung” vorstellt, exekutierte sie jüngst in Reinickendorf, wo 170 Mieter mit einer Vorlauffrist von nur 6 Monaten darüber informiert wurden, dass ihre Wohnanlage komplett saniert werde und sie Umsetzwohnungen verteilt über das gesamte Stadtgebiet erhalten sollen, was gegen jede Rechtsprechung auf eine ‘Wohnortnahe Umsetzung’ verstößt.


Während börsenorientierte Unternehmen wie die ‘Deutsche Wohnen’ aufgrund von medialen Meltdowns gezwungen waren, besonders skandalöse Zustände in ihren Wohnungsanlagen abzustellen, glänzt die HOWOGE seit Jahren mit der weitgehenden Verweigerung der direkten Kommunikation mit ihren Mietern und dem Aussitzen von Problemen. Bezeichnenderweise wechselte der operative Leiter des Vorstandes der HOWOGE im Frühjahr dieses Jahres zu genau dem technischen Dienstleister, der in den letzten Jahren zahlreiche Aufträge der diversen ausgegliederten HOWOGE-Tochtergesellschaften erhalten hatte. Eigentlich können die betroffenen Berliner Mieter im Nachhinein wahrscheinlich froh darüber sein, dass sich der “Sieg” des ‚Volksentscheids Deutsche Wohnen und Co enteignen’ bisher im typischen Berliner Wohnungssumpf verloren hat. Denn nun kommt ja der “Vergesellschaftungshammer” der PdL.

title: Mass protest against solar power plant projects in Bingöl
content:
A protest was held in the Solhan district of Bingöl against Solar Power Plant (GES) projects planned for grazing areas used by more than 60,000 animals, as well as pastures and forested areas where beekeeping is carried out.


Representatives of political parties and civil society organisations, along with residents from the Karlıova (Kanîreş) and Yedisu (Çêrme) districts, attended a press statement organized by the Bongilan Ecology Platform. The statement emphasised the need to protect pastures and highland meadows.


Canfidal Boldaş, the Bingöl (Çewlîg) Provincial Secretary of the Union of Chambers of Turkish Engineers and Architects (TMMOB), stated that implementing renewable energy projects in unsuitable locations causes environmental destruction. He opposed the destruction of pastures and forested areas for the sake of companies’ economic interests.


Turan Hişan, president of the Bingöl Bar Association, said the projects must be assessed in terms of environmental protection and the right to life. Hişan added that they would launch legal action before irreparable damage occurs and would continue to monitor the process.


Ömer Faruk Hülakü, DEM Party MP for Bingöl, also said the projects were turning the region’s land into areas for profit-making, stressing that the living spaces of people who depend on livestock farming and agriculture for their livelihoods must be protected.


The protest ended with participants chanting slogans calling for the protection of nature and livelihoods.

author: Gwynne Hogan
title: Protests Erupt in New York City After ICE Agent Shoots Father in the Bronx
content:
The man, who is still being detained, had his 5-year-old child in his car at the time of the shooting.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

A federal immigration officer shot a man Thursday afternoon in New York’s Marble Hill neighborhood, according to police, eyewitnesses and the Department of Homeland Security, in an incident that drew swift rebuke from elected officials and a crowd of spontaneous protesters late Thursday night.

The man was treated at a nearby hospital for a gunshot wound to the neck, officials said.

Eyewitnesses described a chaotic scene unfurling on a busy street in Marble Hill — a neighborhood that is legally in Manhattan but connected to The Bronx — around 4 p.m., as a slew of New Yorkers were getting home from work and school. As shots rang out, bystanders sheltered in neighboring businesses, the eyewitnesses said.

New York City officials said the ICE agents were in plainclothes wearing masks and construction vests at the time of the shooting, and video and photos of the moments after showed one agent brandishing an assault rifle, as passersby ducked for cover.

Crowds of protesters and elected officials arrived at the scene in the hours after the shooting and outside the nearby NewYork—Presbyterian Allen Hospital, where the wounded man was taken.

“What happened today was an outrage,” Mayor Zohran Mamdani said at a press conference at the scene late Thursday night. Mamdani confirmed the man’s 5-year-old son was in the car at the time of the shooting.

“When ICE agents opened fire, a 5-year-old child — a 5-year-old child — was in the back seat of that car,” he said. “Thank god that child is physically unharmed.”

The mayor said he spent two hours on the phone with President Donald Trump and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin in a failed attempt to get the shooting victim — identified as 28-year-old Oscar Belgal — released. Instead, Mamdani said, ICE agents “whisked him away” from the hospital in Upper Manhattan. “During the incident, an ICE officer discharged his weapon and the criminal illegal alien was injured,” the statement read. “ICE officers immediately rendered aid. The individual is alive and at a local hospital. The FBI and HSI are on the scene. The incident remains under investigation.”

Belgal was identified by Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch late Thursday. Court records showed he pleaded guilty in 2025 to grand larceny in the fourth degree and had an open charge for criminal possession of a controlled substance stemming from an arrest in 2025.

Eyewitnesses to the shooting spoke to The City Reporter and Documented in the hours after the shooting, recalling the commotion as gunfire erupted in the middle of a residential neighborhood. Iris Rosa, a school therapist, said after she emerged from a nearby shop, she saw a man bleeding on the ground in front of a car, while agents milled around, one holding a small child.

“He was all full of blood,” she said, while the child an agent held was quiet. “How could you do this? What is going on? And then I’m looking at the baby.”

Stephanie Ferrer, 30, who lives in Marble Hill, said she heard multiple shots and called 911. She watched the scene from one of her bedroom windows until agents carried the man away by his arms and legs.

“He was disoriented, I think because one of the guys that was holding him next to him was trying to keep him aware, trying to keep him awake by just doing some taps on the cheek,” she said. “You know, like, ‘hey buddy,’ like ‘stay awake, don’t fall asleep.’”

A video posted to social media appeared to show the chaotic aftermath, with a crowd gathered as NYPD officers rushed to a car and carried a man, seemingly unconscious, out of it and into the back of a law enforcement vehicle.

“Put pressure,” one officer is heard to say as they load the man into the back seat.

In a statement posted to X, the NYPD confirmed federal agents were behind the shooting and took the victim to the hospital. “The NYPD was not involved in the incident and was not on scene at the time of the shooting,” they said.

By Thursday evening a crowd of protesters had gathered at the scene, while NYPD officers and caution tape blocked off the street. The dented car Belgal was driving could still be seen blocking West 225th Street at Marble Hill Avenue. Two agents in plainclothes from the Department of Homeland Security were canvassing the area for video …

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: "Abolish ICE": Protests Erupt in NYC After ICE Agents Shoot Father with 5-Year-Old Son in Car
content:
Protests have erupted in New York City after a federal immigration agent shot and wounded a man in the Bronx on Thursday afternoon. As masked agents reportedly posing as construction workers attempted to arrest 28-year-old Oscar Belgal, they opened fire on his car. Belgal was shot in the neck. His 5-year-old child, who was in the back seat, was physically unharmed. Belgal was taken to a local hospital, where hundreds, including our guests, Democratic congressional candidate Darializa Avila Chevalier and New York City Councilmember Carmen De La Rosa, gathered to demand his release.


“What we saw yesterday was a prime example of why [

ICE

] is a terror to our communities, why it should not exist,” says Avila Chevalier. She was among multiple people assaulted by officers with the

NYPD

 unit that specializes in protest policing, known as the Strategic Response Group (

SRG

). Four others were arrested at Thursday evening’s protest. Avila Chevalier, who was knocked down to the ground by officers, says, “This is why we also must demand that we get rid of and disband the

SRG

, because this type of response should have never happened for folks who were just simply trying to protect their neighbor.”


“I personally witnessed the

NYPD

 escalating aggressively towards our community, barricading the community in … I also witnessed

NYPD

 helping the

ICE

 vehicles whisk away our neighbors and come in and out of the hospital,” adds De La Rosa.


“We have become less safe with the presence of

ICE

, and we need to make sure that we are actually upholding the sanctuary policies of the city. There is no reason why

NYPD

 should be collaborating this way,” says Avila Chevalier.

author: Groupe Révolutionnaire Charlatan
title: Wird es am 17. Oktober stattfinden?
content:
Spontane Kommentare zur aktuellen Schülerrevolte


1.


Die Schülerrevolte ist die Speerspitze der für den 17. Oktober angekündigten Bewegung.


2.


Die „Gruppen“ von Schülern aus Arbeitervierteln bilden die eigentliche treibende Kraft innerhalb und gegen die aktuelle Jugendbewegung. In gewisser Weise ist diese Kraft weniger Teil der Schülerbewegung als vielmehr die Fortsetzung der Revolte für Nahel. Sie hat weder Forderungen noch Vertreter, sie findet sich nicht in den Codes der Linken wieder und lehnt bürgerliche Höflichkeit ab. Sie will ihre Rache.


3.


Die Universitäten sind den Oberschulen gefolgt und haben sich der Dynamik der Blockaden angeschlossen. Sie könnten ihrerseits einen qualitativen Sprung bewirken, indem sie beispielsweise eine Besetzungsaktion starten, die von anderen Bereichen der Gesellschaft – ob Schüler oder nicht – aufgegriffen und weiterverbreitet werden könnte. Diese Hypothese wird jedoch durch die erdrückende Dominanz der studentischen Gewerkschaftsorganisationen vereitelt, die der Spontaneität der Gruppen, dem kollektiven Erfindungsreichtum und der auto-subversiven Praxis wenig Raum lassen.


4.


Wenn man von „Blockaden“ an den Oberschulen spricht, befindet man sich bereits in einer Form der Reduktion und Vereinfachung der Praktiken der Schülerrevolte. Es gibt Sabotageakte (angezündete Türen, umgestürzte Tore, „E-Blockaden“ gegen Fernunterricht) und Racheakte (gegen die Hierarchie in der Schule und die Polizei draußen), städtische Guerillataktiken (Barrikaden) und wilde Streiks (Arbeitsniederlegungen in den Pausen und zeitversetzte Blockaden), und schließlich etwas in der Art eines Spiels, das darauf abzielt, die Macht lächerlich zu machen (Slogans über Macron und seine Lehrerin, Superhelden-Verkleidungen im Gegensatz zu den Uniformen der Unterdrücker).


5.


Die Gewerkschaften können sich mit der Idee des 17. Oktober nicht anfreunden, da sie sie zu sehr an die Gelbwesten erinnert. Sie müssen vorgeben, sich der Bewegung anzuschließen, um besser die Kontrolle darüber zu erlangen – sowohl durch das Verhandlungsmonopol als auch durch die Entscheidung über den Zeitplan. Wenn l’intersyndicale zum 6. Oktober gemeinsam mit den Schülern aufgerufen hat, dann nur, um den Aufruf zum 17. Oktober besser zu entschärfen, den sie auf einen Zwischentermin vor ihrer Mobilisierung am 5. November reduzieren möchte.


6.


An den Oberschulen unterscheidet sich die Linke von den anderen politischen Kräften in der Form, nicht aber im Inhalt. In der Form drängt die Linke die Schüler in eine Opferrolle, wodurch sie sich als die „verantwortungsbewussten Erwachsenen“ präsentieren kann. Man denke an die Menschenketten aus Eltern und Lehrern oder auch an gewählte Vertreter, die den Einsatz von LBD-Waffen durch die Polizei anprangern. Dabei fällt auf, dass Schlagstöcke, Schutzschilde, Helme und andere übliche Bestandteile des Arsenals der Demokratie weitaus seltener in Frage gestellt werden.


7.


Inhaltlich schließt sich die Linke den anderen politischen Kräften in ihren Bemühungen um eine Befriedung an. Genau das geschieht, wenn sie Forderungen herausstellt, die mit ihrem Programm vereinbar sind, und damit gleichzeitig dazu beiträgt, die „guten“ Schüler (die als legitim erachtete Forderungen haben) von den „schlechten“ Schülern (diesen „Randalierern“ ohne Ideen oder echte politische Motive) zu separieren.


8.


Im Gegensatz zur Linken haben wir weder Fahnen, die wir schwenken könnten, noch ein Tempo, das wir vorgeben müssten, noch Lektionen, die wir erteilen müssten.


9.


Wie soll man mit der Begeisterung für den „17. Oktober“ umgehen und mit der Art und Weise, wie bestimmte Teile der Jugend ihn als Echo der Gelbwesten-Bewegung präsentieren? Auch wenn eine neue Generation seine symbolische Kraft voller Hoffnung zu beschwören scheint, ist es keineswegs sicher, dass das Wiederverwenden des Objekts uns helfen wird, seinen Geist wiederzufinden. Dennoch ist es vielleicht genau das, was von uns erwartet wird: es sich überzustreifen und zu sehen, ob es – wenn auch nur vorübergehend – ein Gefühl der Zugehörigkeit verkörpert, mit dem sich andere identifizieren und dem sie sich anschließen können, ohne es sich dabei anzueignen. Auf die Gefahr hin, lächerlich und anachronistisch zu wirken und es sofort wieder beiseitezulegen.


10.

title: Veranstaltungen und Mobilisierung zum Basel18 Prozess
content:
Nach über zehn Jahren geht im November der Prozess gegen die Basel18 weiter – in zweiter Instanz am Basler Appellationsgericht.


Veranstaltungen: Am 29. Oktober in Basel und am 30. Oktober in Zürich (siehe unten)


Mobilisierung zum Gericht: Am 2. November und am 13. November vor dem Appellationsgericht Basel (siehe unten).


Auf Repression antworten wir mit Solidarität


Was bisher geschah: Am Abend des 24. Juni 2016 fand in Basel eine kleine, militante Demonstration gegen Rassismus, Repression und Stadtaufwertung statt. Dabei wurden unter anderem grosse Versicherungskonzerne, ein SVP-Büro und das Strafgericht angegriffen, die Polizei wurde mehrmals vertrieben, ein paar Einsatzfahrzeuge lädiert.


Im Anschluss wurden vierzehn Personen verhaftet, einige waren mehrere Monate in Untersuchungshaft. Es gab zahlreiche Hausdurchsuchungen, weitere Verfahren und schliesslich wurden 18 Menschen angeklagt. Daher der Name: Basel18.


Kollektivstrafen und Knast


Weil die Beweise fehlen, um einzelnen Personen konkrete Straftaten nachzuweisen, konstruierte die Staatsanwaltschaft eine Mittäter:innenschaft: Alle Angeklagten sollen nicht «nur» für Landfriendsbruch, sondern für alles, was bei dieser Demonstration passiert ist, verantwortlich gemacht werden – für jede Sachbeschädigung, für Angriff und Körperverletzung. Das ist ein Präzedenzfall. Ein Novum in der Schweizer Justiz.


So verurteilte beim ersten Prozess 2018 eben jenes Gericht, das bei der Demo angegriffen worden war, 15 der 18 Angeklagten zu im Schnitt zwei Jahren Gefängnis – teils auf Bewährung, teils nicht. Hinzu kommen immense Verfahrenskosten und Schadenersatzforderungen.


Der Fall der Basel18 steht damit für ein neues Mass an Repression. Gerade in Basel: Die Staatsanwaltschaft führte seither auch bei den Basel-Nazifrei-Prozessen Kollektivstrafen ins Feld; die Polizei verhindert, wie jüngst bei der palästina-solidarischen Demo im August, Proteste oft von Beginn weg.


Den «langen Sommer der Repression» nannte 2016 eine Broschüre die damalige Zeit. Ein Sommer der Solidarität war es aber ebenso – wie auch die darauffolgenden Jahre: Neue Freund:innenschaften entstanden, 2021 erschien das Buch «Abendessen 16:30», das


die U-Haft-Erfahrungen der Festgenommenen thematisiert.


Repression zielt darauf ab einzuschüchtern, zu zermürben und den Basel18 drohen seit nun über einer Dekade mehrere Jahre Knast. Und dennoch sind sie und ihr Umfeld kämpferisch geblieben. Umso entscheidender also, auch beim aktuellen Prozess deutlich zu machen: Solidarität hat viele Formen und sie überdauert die Mühlen der Justiz.


Lassen wir die Angeklagten mit den Prozesskosten nicht allein. Lassen wir uns nicht einschüchtern, stehen wir weiter für revolutionäre Ideen ein – kämpfen wir zusammen für ein gutes Leben für alle!


Veranstaltungen: Zehn Jahre her - reflektieren, diskutieren und weiter denken


Basel: 29.10.26 18:30 Einlass, 19:00 Uhr Beginn / Über dem Neuen Kino, Klybeckstrasse 247


Zürich: 30.10.26 18:30 Uhr Essen, 19:30 Uhr Beginn Veranstaltung, ab 22 Uhr Konzert und Party! Im Postsquat, Wipkingerplatz 7


Wir laden ein zur Reflexion von 2016 bis heute - was hat uns damals bewegt und was heute? Welche Rolle spielt Militanz in unserem Kampf um Freiheit und Gerechtigkeit? Was macht Repression mit uns als Einzelne und als Bewegung? Wie können wir Repression kollektiv gegenüberstehen?


Auf einen Input folgt eine Diskussion, in welcher das Publikum herzlich eingeladen ist, mitzudiskutieren.

author: Kullathida Krajangkul & Elliot Lodge
title: Thailand’s Anti-Israeli Protest Wave Isn’t About Palestine
content:
On a hot and humid morning in early September, hundreds of people gathered outside the Israeli embassy in Bangkok. While a few carried familiar symbols of Palestinian solidarity – a flash of red, black, white and green here, a watermelon there – a far greater number came carrying Thai flags. For every placard demanding an end to the genocide, or a boycott of Israel, many more bore nationalist statements, from “Thailand is not for sale” to the openly antisemitic “You Jewish folks don’t understand Thai culture, so get out”.


Thailand has been awash with anti-Israeli sentiment over the past few weeks, resulting in unprecedented mobilisations in the capital and on the country’s largest and most touristic island, Phuket. While Palestine solidarity has played a small part in these protests, they have mostly been organised by prominent rightwing agitators calling on supporters to “take Thailand back”.


Unlike in other parts of the world, where protests condemning Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza and occupation of the West Bank have become a mainstay of progressive politics, until recently, few Thais seemed interested. Palestine solidarity was the quiet work of Muslim communities, a handful of student and left activists, and a small number of campaigning organisations. 


In one fortnight, the right mobilised more Thais against Israel than years of solidarity campaigning had managed.


‘My money builds your country.’


Israeli tourists, many of them recently discharged soldiers seeking a dose of tropical hedonism and escape, have long been a cause of consternation for Thai locals. In the past few years, as Israeli tourists have arrived in ever greater numbers,

reaching a record 405,000 in 2025

, hotspots such as the backpacker village of Pai in the north and the island of Koh Phangan have been visibly transformed by the influx, with entire parts of town now catering almost exclusively to the Israeli market. 


Labour, meanwhile, runs the other way.

Some 65,000 Thais are currently working in Israel

, most of them on farms,

in jobs once done by Palestinians.

 Since October 2023, when Israel suspended the permits of more than 100,000 West Bank workers, it has leaned on Thai labour harder still. “They’re trying to prevent Palestinians from getting jobs in Israel,” said Saowaluck Phothingam of Socialist Worker Thailand. “The way they do that is by importing foreign labour instead.” It’s “a problem of inequality” Saowaluck added. Thais go to Israel to do the work Palestinians are no longer permitted to do; Israelis come to Thailand to be served.


Reports of Israeli tourists behaving badly regularly surface in Thai media, with almost the entire country now seeming to have watched a video that went viral last year, of an

incensed Israeli tourist telling a worker that “my money builds your country”

, after she was asked to take her shoes off in a restaurant. 


It isn’t just Israelis upsetting the locals. Despite Thailand’s significant reliance on tourism revenue, anti-foreigner sentiment is on the rise more generally. In one of a spate of recent incidents, a group of Italian students were

forced into a public apology in late July

. Their crime? Being loud and inconsiderate on public transport. Yet Israelis have become a particularly problematic category of foreigner in the public imagination, with attention shifting from individual misbehaviour to Israeli-owned businesses.


And it’s true that something more organised than backpacking has grown alongside the Israeli influx. On Koh Phangan, for instance,

one in seven registered companies now has Israeli shareholders

. One of these businesses is a centre called David’s Circle, which had taken in more than 900 Israelis by last May, about half of them discharged soldiers. Its founder, the trauma specialist Yael Shoshani-Rom,

told the Times of Israel

 she wanted “something like a Chabad house, but therapeutic”, a reference to the Orthodox Jewish outreach centres that follow Israeli backpackers around the world. David’s Circle runs in partnership with Let’s Do Something, a nonprofit founded by friends of a young Israeli murdered at the Supernova festival, which also produces pro-Israel content and invests in what it calls “next-generation defence

s

olutions”.


For most Thais, concern about whether Israeli businesses actively support genocide is secondary to a more generalised anxiety about foreign investment and “grey” capital – the Chinese and Russian money linked …

author: Brian Hioe
title: Indigenous Groups Protest Typhoon Ragasa Response Last Month
content:
INDIGENOUS COMMUNITY members protested last month outside of the Executive Yuan, marking the one-year anniversary of deadly flooding in Matai’an, also known as Guangfu Township. The deadly flooding occurred after Typhoon Ragasa in September 2025.

Such community members have called on the Executive Yuan to ensure that reconstruction is carried out in coordination with the wishes of the local community, while working with the local government to do so. On the other hand, community members have criticized when reconstruction takes place in such a manner that leads to mass land expropriation, depriving local residents of their land.

In this sense, Matai’an community members have criticized broken promises from the government, which has promised to fund reconstruction and provide resources. The protest also raises how Matai’an has become highly dependent on donations from the outside world after the deadly flooding.

As part of the demonstration, participants threw plastic bottles filled with sand and water from Matai’an at photos of KMT caucus leader Fu Kun-chi, Hualien county magistrate Hsu Cheng-wei, Ljaucu Zingrur, head of the Council of Indigenous Peoples, and minister without portfolio Chen Chin-te.

One notes that anger, then, is directed both at the central and local governments. In particular, Fu Kun-chi and his wife, Hsu Cheng-wei, are often understood as members of a political dynasty that rules over Hualien. Fu and Hsu have been criticized as not doing enough for Hualien in the aftermath of Typhoon Ragasa, as well as after successive earthquakes have damaged infrastructure there. At the same time, the central government and the Council of Indigenous Peoples have also been criticized for failing to take sufficient action in the aftermath of the disaster–as well as to avoid such disasters occurring in the future.

Indeed, one notes that in the aftermath of the deadly flooding, Fu attempted to put the blame for the disaster on the central government. Fu alleged that the central government did not warn local authorities in time, and suggested that the central government was mostly at fault for delays in reconstruction.

Either way, one notes that though there was a wave of volunteers who traveled to Hualien to assist in the aftermath of Typhoon Ragasa, attention has now shifted elsewhere. Likewise, if external aid in the wake of the disaster is simply followed by how the disaster is used as a pretext for land seizures, this continues colonialism directed at Indigenous communities. It proves deeply colonial, of course, if a disaster simply serves as a pretext to conduct land seizures and further displace Indigenous people from their land.

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: Festival-themed protest underscores teachers’ economic demands
content:
MANILA – On World Teachers’ Day, members of the Alliance of Concerned Teachers (ACT) held a protest near Malacañang Palace billed as “Pistang Protesta: Dagdag Sweldo, Hindi Dagdag Trabaho.”

Teachers from different public and private schools all over Metro Manila, as well as students and supporters marched Padre Noval Street corner España Boulevard toward Mendiola, October 5, 2026.

Carrying bunting flags and surrounded by ice cream carts, protesters called for a reduced and humane workload, allocation of six percent of GDP to education, P5,000 (approximately US$79.68) economic relief allowance and P50,000 (approximately US$796.81) entry-level salary for all teachers.

The current starting basic pay of a Teacher is pegged at P31,705 (approximately US$505.26) while the economic relief allowance is only P2,000 (approximately US$31.87)

Hogier Villarias, secretary general of Alliance of Concerned Teachers NCR, said that their call for salary hike is timely considering the increase in the country’s Gross Domestic Product.

“Our primary call remains a salary increase since our GDP grew by four percent, so we are expecting that wages should also be increased,” said Villarias, who joined the protest along with his fellow teachers from Andres Bonifacio Elementary School.

According to the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA), the GDP of the country grew by 4.4 percent in 2025. However, progressive groups argued that economic growth is meaningless if it does not translate to higher wages and better working conditions.

Katrina Ortega, president of All UP Academic Employees Union Diliman, meanwhile, pointed out wrong priorities of the Marcos Jr. administration.

“We cannot accept that funds are diverted to confidential funds and flood control projects while we lack teachers and classrooms. The children suffer — they have no learning materials, and even basic school needs like water and comfort rooms are lacking. All of these affect the children,” Ortega stated.

In the proposed P7.2-trillion (approximately US$114.74 billion) national budget for 2027, P1.326 trillion (approximately US$21.13 billion) is allotted for the education sector — P975.96 billion (approximately US$15.56 billion) for the Department of Education and P176.5 billion (approximately US$2.81 billion) for higher education. This is around 1.41 percent lower than the P1.345 trillion (approximately US$21.43 billion) allocated in 2026.

The proposed P1.467 trillion (approximately US$23.38 billion) fund for the government-wide infrastructure program is still 10.6 percent higher than the budget proposed for education. Moreover, there is also a roughly 13.8 percent increase in infrastructure budget from the P1.29 trillion (approximately US$20.56 billion) allocated in 2026.

Infrastructure projects are vulnerable to political patronage, according to the People’s Budget Coalition (PBC). In fact, the coalition identified P970 billion (approximately US$15.46 billion) worth of potential ‘pork’ from the proposed 2027 budget as they observed patterns of alleged political influence particularly in flood-control projects.

Concerns over potential misuse and abuse of these funds fueled protesters’ calls for a different direction in government spending. Progressive groups are urging the administration to stop feeding political interests and instead pour more funds toward public welfare programs.

During the protest, former ACT Teachers Party-list Representative France Castro amplified her condemnation of corruption and demand for greater funding for social services, including education.

“From the passage of the budget to its signing into law, the budget is full of corruption — this is what we are opposing. What we are demanding is funding for social services, education, housing, and others,” Castro said.

Protesters said their fight doesn’t end with the dispersal, pledging to carry the fight beyond the streets and continue pushing for urgent education reforms. (RVO)

author: David Swanson
title: Nobel Peace Prize Turns Toward Peace in 2026
content:
By David Swanson, World BEYOND War, October 9, 2026


The Nobel Peace Prize has just been awarded to Navi Pillay who is not, like

last year’s laureate

, pleading for the world’s largest military to attack her country. Nor is she, in the manner of various past laureates, waging war. Nor is she, like various past recipients, an admirable humanitarian working in a field unrelated to war. In fact, Navi Pillay has long been recognized as advancing the cause of peace. In 2025 she was awarded the

Sydney Peace Prize

 in Australia. The foundation awarding that prize said:


“Judge Pillay has played a critical role in holding the tide against the global rise in impunity for war crimes and crimes against humanity, advocating for accountability, the rule of law, and the protection of human dignity – from South Africa to Sri Lanka, Rwanda to Myanmar, and the Occupied Palestinian Territory. She has worked for justice at the centre point of some of humanity’s most brutal conflicts. Upon accepting the 2025 Sydney Peace Prize nomination, Navi Pillay stated: ‘This award is not mine alone. It belongs to all those who, across decades and continents, have stood up against injustice – often at great personal cost. It belongs to every survivor who found the courage to testify, to every human rights defender who remains steadfast in the face of threats and hostility, and to every young person who dares to believe in a better, more just world.'”


Pillay has been a prominent advocate for the rule of law in place of the rule of mass killing, and her work has been cited by advocates for peace in

Palestine

 and for the elimination of

weaponized drones

. To have finally acknowledged someone whose work in any way addressed the horrors of Zionism is an encouraging sign from the Nobel Committee. Is Pillay “the person who shall have done the most or the best work for fraternity between nations, for the abolition or reduction of standing armies and for the holding and promotion of peace congresses,” as required by the will of Alfred Nobel? The idea is not, as in most years, ridiculous. In this year’s leadup, there were even non-satirical commentators

pushing

 for Donald Trump to get the prize for his war on Iran.


This is the second time in three years that the prize has gone to someone worthy. In 2024 as well, the prize was

actually related to peace

. The Nobel Committee has frequently given the peace prize to major war makers, and frequently to do-gooders whose work in a variety of fields has been unrelated to abolishing war. It has also often given the prize to opponents and victims of the targets of Western empire. But it has never given the prize to open advocates of war and fascistic government. Trump was never going to be given the prize directly. Last years’ awarding of a peace prize to someone asking Trump to attack her country was clearly

an attempt

 to do the closest thing possible to giving Trump the prize himself.


Most winners in recent years have either been people who did nice things that had nothing whatsoever to do with the relevant work (

Kailash Satyarthi

 and

Malala Yousafzai

 for promoting education,

Liu Xiaobo

 for protesting in China,

Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC)

and

Albert Arnold (Al) Gore Jr.

 for opposing climate change,

Muhammad Yunus

 and

Grameen Bank

for economic development, etc.) or people who actually engaged in militarism and would have opposed the abolition or reduction of standing armies if asked, and one of whom said so in his acceptance speech (the European Union, Barack Obama, etc.). Of course, Henry Kissinger is remembered as a Nobel Peace laureate, while Gandhi never measured up.


The Nobel Committee outraged Trump because it gave the prize to U.S. President Barack Obama who, after delivering the only pro-war Nobel Peace Prize acceptance speech ever, went to Hiroshima and

told everyone there

, including the survivors of the nuclear bombs who would later get the prize, that nuclear weapons would not be eliminated in his lifetime. He then proceeded to peddle familiar

pro-war myths

.


Three years ago the Nobel Committee awarded

a peace prize

 that had Iran in the role of Venezuela. Since then, we have seen Iran bombed and threatened by the upholders of Western civilization. It would not have been surprising for this year’s award to have gone to some victim of the government of Cuba or Russia, China or North Korea, Greenland or perhaps the moon — some new …

title: ACHTUNG: Berliner Kundgebung gegen die Todesstrafe am 10.10. HINTER die US Botschaft verlegt
content:
Der Berliner Versammlungsbehörde scheint nach mehrmonatiger vorheriger Anmeldung aufgefallen zu sein, daß das „Festival of Lights“ ebenfalls am kommenden Samstag rund um das Brandenburger Tor stattfindet. Nun haben sich die Veranstalter*innen bereit erklärt, den Protest HINTER die US Botschaft zu verlagern:


Behrensstr. / Eberstr. gegenüber US Botschaft


(mit dem Stelenfeld im Rücken)


Sa. 10. Oktober 2026 – 19 – 20:00 Uhr

Abschaffung der Todesstrafe überall!

Kommt am 10. Oktober 2026, dem internationalen Tag gegen die Todesstrafe, von 19 – 20:00 Uhr hinter die US Botschaft, Behrensstr. Ecke Ebertstr. – U5-Brandenburger Tor


Noch immer wird die Todesstrafe, also das staatliche Ermorden von Gefangenen in vielen Teilen der Welt durchgeführt. Ein Gefangener im US Bundesstaat Ohio kämpft derzeit gegen seine drohende Hinrichtung und den Rassismus und Klassismus, die seinem Urteil zu Grunde liegen: Keith LaMar. Er wurde nach dem Lucasville Gefängnisaufstand von 1993 zum Tode verurteilt. Er wurde für den Tod mehrerer Schließer verantwortlich gemacht. Dabei ist unstrittig, dass er gar nicht an dem Aufstand teilgenommen hat. Der Afroamerikaner Keith LaMar wurde von einer ausschließlich weißen Jury für schuldig befunden. Er hatte zuvor sich und andere Gefangene als Jailhouse Lawyer (Gefangenenanwalt) juristisch gegen die willkürliche Gewalt im Knast verteidigt und war den Behörden ein Dorn im Auge. Zuerst wurde ihm ein Deal angeboten: er solle sich schuldig bekennen, um die nach dem Aufstand über die Zustände im bundesstaatlichen Gefängnis empörte Öffentlichkeit zu beruhigen und Kritik verstummen zu lassen. author: FMF Staff
title: ICC Arrest Warrants Challenge the Normalization of Taliban Rule and Gender Persecution
content:
On October 5, the International Criminal Court (ICC) unsealed arrest warrants for four senior Taliban officials. They include Taliban Supreme Leader Haibatullah Akhundzada, Chief Justice Abdul Hakim Haqqani, Education Minister Habibullah Agha, and Higher Education Minister Neda Mohammad Nadim. The warrants were issued in July 2025 but had remained sealed.

The ICC says there are reasonable grounds to believe the four are criminally responsible for the “crime against humanity of persecution on gender grounds against girls, women, and others who do not conform to the Taliban’s policies on gender, gender identity, or expression.” The crimes include conduct involving murder, imprisonment, torture, rape, and enforced disappearance.

The Court also found that Taliban decrees and edicts have severely deprived women and girls of fundamental rights, including education, privacy and family life, as well as freedoms of movement, expression, thought, conscience, and religion. Importantly, the Court recognized that gender persecution can encompass not only direct acts of violence, but also systemic and institutionalized forms of harm.

What does the arrest warrant mean for the four Taliban officials?

The warrants do not mean that the four Taliban leaders will suddenly be arrested. The ICC has no police force of its own and relies on states to execute its arrest warrants. The 125 countries that are parties to the Rome Statute have obligations to cooperate with the Court, including complying with requests for arrest and surrender.

That puts a significant question before those countries: What does it mean to engage with or recognize a regime whose senior leaders are subject to ICC arrest warrants for alleged crimes against humanity?

As governments continue to weigh whether to recognize the Taliban, the warrants create an unavoidable diplomatic and legal question, especially for countries that are members of the ICC: Will you recognize and legitimize a regime whose senior leaders are wanted by the International Criminal Court?

The question is particularly significant in a region where several countries maintain relationships with the Taliban but are not parties to the Rome Statute. Pakistan, India, Iran, Qatar, China, Uzbekistan, Turkiye, and Russia are not ICC States Parties.

That distinction matters. Non-States Parties generally have no obligation under the Rome Statute to arrest and surrender ICC suspects, although the ICC can request their cooperation and countries can choose to assist.

And these are precisely the kinds of countries where Taliban officials have been able to travel and engage diplomatically. Russia, for example, recognized the Taliban government in 2025 and hosted a high-level Afghanistan meeting in Moscow this week attended by Taliban officials and representatives from countries including Iran and Pakistan.

A warrant can be difficult to enforce and still matter

The lack of an immediate mechanism to arrest the Taliban leaders does not make the warrants meaningless.

They establish an important record of international accountability and put governments on notice about the allegations against senior Taliban officials. They also make it harder to treat the Taliban’s systematic restrictions on women and girls as merely an internal matter, a cultural difference, or a set of domestic policies.

The ICC has identified the persecution of women and girls under the Taliban as a crime against humanity.

For governments considering recognition, diplomatic engagement, or deeper ties with the Taliban, the warrants leave a clear question:

How do you recognize a regime while its senior leaders face ICC arrest warrants for alleged crimes against humanity?

For Afghan women and girls, the warrants represent something more fundamental: a recognition that what has happened to them is not simply policy. It is not cultural and it is not religious. Their persecution is a matter of international criminal accountability.

The warrants may not immediately bring the Taliban leaders to The Hague, but they put accountability on the table and leave every government deciding how to engage with the Taliban with a choice to make.

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: RCMP arrest suspect in Pangnirtung shooting
content:
The RCMP has arrested a 21-year-old man in relation to a shooting in Pangnirtung on Tuesday afternoon.


Police received reports of gunshots at around 4:03 p.m. Tuesday. Ten minutes later, they arrested Jonah Kuniliusie, according to a news release issued by Sgt. George Henrie on Thursday.


Kuniliusie faces two counts of endangering life, two counts of pointing a firearm, two counts of aggravated assault, and the unlawful possession of a weapon in public. He also faces three counts for breach of probation.


The RCMP was not immediately available to answer questions about the incident.


Deputy mayor Markus Wilcke said the event harmed everyone in the community, either directly or indirectly, including children who were nearby

when the shooting happened

.


Kuniliusie remains in custody and will have his next court appearance on Oct. 20 in Iqaluit.

author: Harriet Williamson
title: UK Terrorism Arrests up 1,553% Since Palestine Action Ban
content:
Terror arrests in the UK have increased by 1,553% and hit a record high, with the overwhelming majority linked to support for Palestine Action, new Home Office statistics show. 


3,867 arrests were made for terrorism-related activity in the year ending June 2026, compared to 234 arrests in the year ending June 2025, according to

data released by the Home Office

 on Thursday. 


Of those arrests, a whopping 3,630 – 94% – were linked to support for Palestine Action following the group’s proscription. 


The Labour government under Keir Starmer proscribed Palestine Action as a terrorist group in July 2025, making it the first direct action group to be banned under the Terrorism Act in British history.


Protests against Palestine Action’s proscription, organised by campaign group Defend Our Juries (DOJ), have seen elderly and disabled people arrested and carried away by police after holding up paper signs with the words “I oppose genocide. I support Palestine Action.” 


Since the ban, terrorism-related arrests are up 1,525% on the historical ten-year median of 238 arrests.


The Home Office’s report also confirmed that 704 arrests had so far resulted in a charge, with 634 of those charges made under Section 12 or Section 13 of the Terrorism Act 2000 and linked to supporting Palestine Action. 


A spokesperson for DOJ told Novara Media: “History shows that unjust laws become unenforceable when they are met with mass opposition, until governments are eventually forced to abandon them. The statistics released today are a clear indication of just how unpopular and unenforceable the government’s ban on Palestine Action is.


“Over a year on, and hundreds of regular people are still prepared to be arrested as ‘terrorists’ to demand that the new Labour leadership to do the only sensible thing and lift the ban on Palestine Action.”


In a statement, Amnesty International UK’s law and human rights director Tom Southernden said: “The vast majority of the enormous increase in terrorism arrests are of grandparents, teenagers and everyone in between for peacefully holding placards. 


“We are seeing a shameful attack on our right to protest. It’s past time to end the proscription of Palestine Action and with it the use of counter terrorism power to punish direct action protests.”


Dozens of peaceful protesters

opposing Israel’s genocide and the ban on Palestine Action – including

a 94-year-old Jewish human rights lawyer

 – were arrested outside the Labour party conference in Liverpool at the end of September. 


The next day, foreign secretary Ed Miliband replied to a question about the proscription

from Andrew Marr on LBC

about “all those elderly people and vicars and grannies and so on” by saying: “I don’t think anyone’s intent was to have those people criminalised.” 


Palestine Action co-founder Huda Ammori has been granted permission to challenge the ban in the Supreme Court.

author: EDRi
title: EDRi-gram, 8 October 2026
content:
What has the EDRi network been up to over the past few weeks? Find out the latest digital rights news in our regular newsletter. In this edition: Turning up the heat – Commission backs social media bans, Apple held accountable, summer to-dos, & more!

This EDRi-gram edition includes a real snapshot of the disconnect between the kind of technology and protections people and communities around the world need, and the kind that are being pushed at us by lawmakers and companies either for the sake of profits, as easy fixes to structural societal issues or more sinister reasons.

Take the EU’s recently announced KIDS ACT. We unpack the many shortcomings of the proposal which is a missed opportunity to address the root cause of why online platforms are harmful to children – and everyone else. We also look at the Cloud and AI Development (CADA) Act, a part of the EU’s Tech Sovereignty Package announced earlier this year. What was sold as a way to jumpstart the EU’s “sovereign AI” ambitions seems to be set to hurt digital rights and environmental protections instead, while also imposing an unreliable technology onto us.

Elsewhere, Austria will soon get to find out what happens when AI systems are allowed to issue legally binding government decisions without any human oversight. EDRi-member epicenter.works detail the draft proposal and all the ways it could backfire.

None of the above is without resistance from those of us working to protect your rights. Dutch EDRi-member Bits of Freedom have launched a new campaign demanding a ban on Meta’s “pervert glasses”, aka, AI glasses which can be used to film people without them knowing. Meta was clearly paying attention – their viral satirical video on these glasses was removed from Instagram.

From critical campaigns, and urging EU countries to not treat data protection and “competitiveness” as opposing goals as they discuss the Digital Omnibus, to legal action against Big Tech corporations preying on our minds – we’re fighting back.

Next week, at our flagship annual event #PrivacyCamp26, we’ll be asking the real questions – where does technology come from? Who shapes it? And what would self-determination look like if it were defined by the people, not dictated by profits or a state’s agenda? We hope to see some of you attending!

title: Yıldız Teknik Üniversitesi'nde siber saldırı duyurusu: 140 bin öğrencinin verisi çalınmış olabilir
content:
Yıldız Teknik Üniversitesi'nde (YTÜ) 1 Ekim'den bu yana yaşanan sistem aksaklıklarının arkasından siber saldırı çıktı. Kişisel Verileri Koruma Kurulu'nun (KVKK) 7 Ekim tarihli kararıyla üniversitedeki veri ihlali resmi olarak kamuoyuna duyuruldu. Yaşanan siber saldırı ve veri ihlalinden yaklaşık 140 bin öğrenci ile 4 bin 500 personelin etkilendiği belirtildi.

Yıldız Teknik Üniversitesi'nde altyapı sorunu: Öğrenciler çevrimiçi derslere erişemiyor

Üniversitenin resmi internet sitesi, Öğrenci Bilgi Sistemi (OBS), Online Yıldız ve çeşitli başvuru sistemlerine günlerce erişim sağlanamazken, üniversite yönetiminin yaşanan aksaklıklara ilişkin ilk etapta kapsamlı bir açıklama yapmadığı görüldü. Yönetim, 3 Ekim'de yaptığı ilk duyuruda süreci yalnızca "teknik çalışma" olarak nitelendirmişti. Ancak KVKK'nın devreye girmesiyle birlikte sistem kesintilerinin arkasında bir fidye yazılımı saldırısının olduğu netlik kazandı.

Kişisel Verileri Koruma Kurulu’nun yayımladığı duyuruda "Veri sorumlusu sıfatını haiz Yıldız Teknik Üniversitesi tarafından Kurula iletilen veri ihlal bildiriminde özetle; ihlalin 01.10.2026 tarihinde başladığı ve aynı gün tespit edildiği, veri sorumlusunun sanallaştırma altyapısı ve üzerinde çalışan sunucuların fidye yazılımı saldırısından etkilendiği, ihlalden etkilenen ilgili kişi grubunun öğrenci, personel ve ziyaretçiler olduğu, mevcut kayıtlara göre ihlalden etkilenmiş olabilecek ilgili kişi sayısının yaklaşık 140.000 öğrenci ve 4.500 personel olduğu, ziyaretçilere ilişkin sayının henüz belirlenemediği, ihlalden etkilenen kişisel veri kategorilerinin belirlenemediği bilgilerine yer verilmiştir" ifadeleri kullanıldı.

Öğrencilerin hangi kişisel verilerinin siber saldırıdan etkilendiği ve dışarı sızdırıldığı konusundaki belirsizlikler ise hâlâ devam ediyor.
