Women’s rights around the world +

We join women, girls, and human rights defenders across Africa and the globe on this 28th day of September to commemorate the 2026 International Safe Abortion Day, reaffirming a simple truth: safe abortion is essential healthcare.

We are reminded of the transformative power of the Protocol to the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights on the Rights of Women in Africa (the Maputo Protocol), which is lauded as one of the most progressive and comprehensive legal instruments for the promotion and protection of women’s rights globally, particularly in the area of sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR). Adopted in 2003 by the African Union, the Protocol goes beyond existing international human rights standards by explicitly articulating a wide array of SRHR protections that are often left ambiguous or unstated in other international and regional human rights instruments.

Article 14 of the Maputo Protocol guarantees women’s rights to health and reproductive autonomy, including the right to control their fertility, decide on family size and spacing, and to choose their method of contraception. Most critically, Article 14 makes the Maputo Protocol the first and only binding international human rights treaty to explicitly guarantee access to safe medical abortion in specific circumstances—namely, where the continued pregnancy endangers the mental or physical health of the mother or the life of the mother or the fetus, or in cases of sexual assault, rape, or incest. This Article also mandates access to comprehensive reproductive health services, including antenatal care, safe delivery, family planning, and sexual and reproductive health education. In doing so, the Protocol moves abortion access from a matter left to state discretion to one of binding treaty obligation — a distinction that remains central to the advocacy for its full domestication across the continent.

Currently, 46 of the 55 African states have ratified the Maputo Protocol, while nine – Burundi, Chad, Egypt, Eritrea, Madagascar, Morocco, Niger, Somalia, and Sudan – are yet to ratify it. Bringing these final states on board is vital because over 150 million African women and girls currently live outside the protective legal framework of the Maputo Protocol.

Despite its progressiveness, 9 out of the 46 member states have placed reservations to various provisions of the Maputo Protocol, with Article 14 being the most reserved provision. A reservation lowers the minimum human rights standards contained in a particular treaty for the reserving states and enables the reserving states to escape accountability for human rights violations.

Currently, Africa accounts for 70% of global maternal deaths. These preventable deaths are compounded by persistent gaps in access to sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) services, which are essential to safeguarding the lives and dignity of women, children and adolescents. Unsafe abortions continue to claim the lives of thousands of African women and girls, while millions more are left with severe injuries and long-term health complications. According to the World Health Organization, nearly half of all abortions worldwide are unsafe, with Sub-Saharan Africa carrying the highest burden. The Guttmacher Institute further estimates that three-quarters of all abortions in the region are unsafe, making unsafe abortion one of the …

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: Quebec Liberal Sandrine Rioux prioritizes health care, housing, cost of living
content:
Nunatsiaq News reached out to each candidate running in the Ungava riding ahead of Quebec’s Oct. 5 provincial election. Here’s what Quebec Liberal Party candidate Sandrine Rioux had to share with us.


Quebec Liberal Party candidate Sandrine Rioux said the reason she decided to run for office is simple: she wants to help people.


“My main goal is to help people, to be there, to be present, and to write good legislation at the National Assembly of Quebec,” said Rioux, speaking to Nunatsiaq News Tuesday from Chibougimou, where she was born and raised.


She’s among five candidates running in Ungava, the largest riding in the province geographically.


Her main priorities are improving access to health care, constructing more homes, addressing the cost of living and ensuring profits generated from resource development benefit communities.


Her party has a goal of building 100,000 homes per year in Quebec, she said, and wants to implement deadlines for housing authorities to encourage quicker development.


Each community, no matter how remote, should have a baseline 24-7 access to front-line health care services like doctors, nurses and pharmacists, she said. Telemedicine can fill gaps when specialists aren’t available.


At least five per cent of Quebec’s health budget should be dedicated to prevention, she said, and if elected, she wants to reduce Nunavik’s reliance on fly-in-fly-out health-care professionals.


Rioux has been involved with the Liberal party since 2019 and was president of its Ungava association.


She has a degree in business technology management from Université de Sherbrooke and a professional background in business analysis and marketing.


But she always held an interest in politics, she said, working for Élections Québec during the 2018 provincial election as an administrative assistant. It was one of her first jobs out of university and one that allowed her to visit each of Nunavik’s villages.


So far during the campaign, Rioux has visited Chapais, Chisasibi, Oujé-Bougoumou, Matagami, Mistissini, Radison, Waskaganish and Waswanipi. Travelling to Nunavik isn’t in the budget, but she said Kuujjuaq is first on her list if she gets elected.


“I really genuinely hope, if the people trust me, and invest in me, to be able to represent them at the National Assembly,” she said. “I want to make sure the lines of communication are always open.”

author: Izzy Knowles
title: Don’t Let Barbie Out of the Glovebox – An OCD Account
content:
W

hen I was in fifth grade, I convinced myself I was pregnant. I had never even kissed a boy. A slight stomachache after guzzling down my morning glass of milk became the beginning of early-onset morning sickness. A fleeting urge for bacon at a time that wasn’t breakfast suddenly meant that I was experiencing a full-fledged pregnancy craving. I would look around the band room and stare at the other girls in my class, wishing so deeply I was them so I wouldn’t have to deal with this phantom baby.


The following summer, I was certain I had developed a powerful addiction to making my little sister’s Barbie doll, a foxy brunette called Nancy, do back walkovers. During a sixteen-hour road trip from Chicago to Vermont, I picked up Nancy and mindlessly began kicking her leg back over her head and onto my thigh. As I flipped her in circles over and over, I started to worry I would never be able to stop. I pictured a future bound to this motion alone, where the only escape would be a bedridden life with my hands permanently restrained to my sides. Terrified of the fate ahead of me, I cried and pleaded with my mother to hide the Barbie in the glovebox, out of sight.


By the end of sixth grade, I convinced myself that I was going blind (I couldn’t see in the dark), that my lung had collapsed (I realized I could breathe manually), that I was dying of cancer (I discovered a mole on my chest), and that I was passionately suicidal (I got too close to the edge of my father’s balcony). I slept with the lights on, went to the emergency room when I felt my breaths were too shallow, and spent every other night on a mattress in my mother’s room on the off chance I’d sleepwalk to the kitchen and stab myself in the heart.


Of course, none of these fears came true. My imagined due date rolled around with no contractions, I didn’t suffer from any Barbie-related withdrawals, and I learned to trust the doctors who told me I was healthy. But despite the high turnover rate of my neuroses, I lacked the essential concoction of insight and perspective to realize they would eventually fade.


For most of my life, I chalked up my intolerance for uncertainty as a symptom of being a “worrywort.” My parents seemed to tie my perpetual doom to my capacity for empathy, telling me that I “just cared too much.” My middle school therapist, an older woman who sat me down with a mound of clay and a mug of lemonade each session, labeled my disposition as “irrational.” Though I can’t quite disagree with them, my concerns were operating along an axis far more penetrating than worry alone.


By the time I was a seasoned high schooler, the themes of my fears had morphed from absurd to abhorrent. My wide-eyed childhood irrationality turned inward, shifting into existential questions aimed at navigating the liminal space between truth and delusion. I cycled through the more universal dilemmas:

Is this all a simulation? Are dreams our reality? Is everything you see, everyone you love, merely a figment of your imagination?

 Each question would surge me into obsessive contemplation, driving a wedge between the life around me and the doubt that threatened to squash it.


Sometime in my sophomore year amidst a weed-induced existential rant with my best friend, a question of my

own

 mortality crept out from the depths of my “what ifs.”

Am I immortal?

 It was a fleeting idea that turned over in my brain one too many times—causing that deep sense of doom to slither out and turn a hypothetical into an actuality.


Later that night in the safety of my bathtub, I gave myself an ultimatum: to conquer this new reality before I got out of the tub. I leaned back, avoiding the faucet, and questions and doubts and guilt over my questions and doubts seemed to cloud over the colorful splotches behind my eyelids. The waterline moved up and down my thighs and I wondered how I would cope with seeing everyone I love die over and over again. I decided that if I was right, and my life never ended, I would put myself in a sort of anesthetized state—like Woody Allen did in the movie

Sleeper

.


The next bout of fears shifted my focus from mortality to morality, casting doubt on the substance of my personhood.

Are your morals authentic or manufactured? How can you trust your ethics if they are determined by a world that is simulated, synthetic, or nonexistent? Are you a sociopath? Are you a deviant?

 The urgency to internalize the weight of these questions escalated as they …

author: Paul Messersmith-Glavin
title: A Lifelong Organizer Shares Lessons on Sustaining Activism for the Long Haul
content:
Organizer Chris Dixon discusses how we can sustain our collective efforts over years of social and political struggle.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Writer and organizer Chris Dixon has his fingers on the pulse of North American grassroots movement. Dixon has extensively and repeatedly traveled throughout North America, talking with people working for social change — engaging with activists concerning their successes and heartbreaks, their frustrations and dreams. His first book, Another Politics: Talking Across Today’s Transformative Movements, published in 2014, focused on antiauthoritarian organizers and politics across a range of movements of the 2000s and early 2010s, including migrant justice, prison abolitionism, and Occupy Wall Street. His new book, For the Long Haul: How to Stay in the Fight for a Better World, focuses on how we can sustain our collective efforts over years of social and political struggle.

Movement elders I am close to — now in their 70s — who maintain radical political commitments developed in their youth, benefitted from both the intense community that formed around movements for Black Power and liberation, the youthful counterculture and the New Left, and anti-war movements, as well as from their own inner convictions that served as an animating passion. For these elders, political engagement is a kind of vocation. Though they continue to maintain relationships with those comrades who are also still alive and committed to political struggle, those vibrant communities they once thrived in are gone. Only their specific commitment to the possibility of freedom and liberation keeps them going.

Coming of age politically in the 1990s, we also had strong bonds of friendship born through relentless organizing meetings, demonstrations, and coalition work. It seemed we could collectively change the world. Thirty years later, only a handful of us remain involved. Why? Why do people stop organizing, beyond and in addition to the realities of acquiring increasing responsibilities as we age? Why do people give up on the possibility of creating fundamental social and structural change together over the long term? How can we cultivate and sustain caring radical communities that support us all, while drawing new people in, or welcoming them back? These are some of the questions Chris Dixon sets out to answer in For the Long Haul: How to Stay in the Fight for a Better World. The interview that follows has been lightly edited for length and clarity.

Paul Messersmith-Glavin: Who should read your book?

Chris Dixon: I wrote For the Long Haul as a practical guide with two main audiences in mind. On the one hand, I wanted to warmly welcome people who have recently become involved in radical political efforts, especially those who have joined movement upsurges since 2020. I’m particularly thinking of the Movement for Black Lives and Palestine solidarity organizing, but also renewed labor militancy and collective defense of queer and trans people. A lot of people I talk to who are newer to movements — many but not all of them younger people — are hungry for conversations about how to sustain lifelong political commitments.

On the other hand, I wanted to speak lovingly to my peers — long-time activists and organizers who have been involved in movements for decades. Many of us talk informally with our friends about the challenges we face in staying actively involved on the left. We’re working a lot to pay our bills, reckoning with disabilities and chronic health conditions, and holding significant care responsibilities for kids, elders, and others in our lives. So many of us are deeply exhausted and hungry for realistic advice about how to stay steady in the fight.

I also wanted to sympathetically address people who participated in movements of the left at one time or another and then moved away from active involvement. I know many people who have followed this trajectory. Rather than being moralistic or dismissive, I wanted to remind them that they’re always welcome back. And I wanted to suggest that perhaps, together, we can build some better structures and practices for helping people stay engaged.

You have spent a tremendous amount of time travelling around the U.S. and Canada, listening to on-the-ground organizers. What have you learned?

I have learned a lot! My most intense and sustained travel was connected to the process of …

Dos décadas antes de la fundación del Estado de Israel, Camillo Berneri advirtió del peligro de un derramamiento de sangre en Palestina, ya que los sionistas querían convertirse en los nuevos amos de ese territorio. Para Berneri, el sionismo no era solo una cortina de humo para la política imperialista británica, sino también una amenaza nacionalista y hegemónica para la coexistencia pacífica entre los nuevos colonizadores y los habitantes históricos de Palestina. Lo que, en cambio, era necesario era una situación de plena tolerancia hacia los judíos en Europa, porque solo así se podría resolver verdaderamente el problema del sionismo.

Dejemos en paz el «Muro de las Lamentaciones». No es más que el fondo del cuadro. Simbólicamente se le puede considerar el centro de la tragedia, pero históricamente no lo es. Al muro de Salomón, que jurídicamente pertenece a los árabes, los judíos acudían libremente todos los viernes, desde hace diez años, para llorar la desesperación y las desgracias de su pueblo. La furia árabe nunca se ha cebado contra el elemento judío ortodoxo. Los árabes son tolerantes en materia religiosa, como buenos mahometanos. Su «fanatismo» se explica más por datos demográficos que por reminiscencias históricas y especulaciones psicológicas. La revuelta árabe ha sido, por circunstancias, antijudía; por naturaleza, simplemente xenófoba.

Tengo ante mis ojos dos entrevistas: una del doctor Weizmann, presidente de la Organización Sionista Universal, y otra de Amein Hussein, líder religioso de los árabes de Palestina. El primero afirma que es necesario que los árabes comprendan que Inglaterra no quiere modificar en absoluto su política de protección del sionismo; que es necesario facilitar la inmigración judía en la mayor medida posible. El segundo reafirma que el actual Gobierno de Palestina es contrario, tanto en su Constitución como en su política, a los árabes; exige la adopción de una forma de gobierno democrática, en la que estén representados todos los habitantes de Palestina de manera proporcional, y el abandono de la política inglesa a favor del desarrollo de un «centro nacional judío», especialmente en lo que respecta a la inmigración.

Dos posiciones claramente opuestas. Un conflicto difícilmente resoluble. ¿De qué lado está la razón? Del lado de los árabes. El sentimentalismo está fuera de lugar. Si la prensa mundial ha dado cuenta de las víctimas judías y ha descrito las horribles escenas de las masacres de colonos sionistas indefensos; si existe una justa tradición de compasión hacia los judíos víctimas de leyes absurdas e injustas y masacrados en los pogromos; si es admirable el esfuerzo sionista, todo ello se ve contrarrestado por el peso de las víctimas árabes, por el hecho de que el sionismo sirve de tapadera a la política imperialista británica y al régimen de desigualdad que impera en Palestina.

Los judíos se han declarado seguros de que en el futuro serán los hegemones en Palestina. Los árabes han visto bajar a cientos de judíos de cada barco de vapor que llegaba a Jaffa y a Haifa, han visto cómo los judíos ocupaban las zonas más propicias de su territorio, han visto cómo pasaban a manos de los judíos tierras que los agricultores árabes habían hecho fértiles, han visto cómo la mayor parte de los gastos en obras públicas …

Så kom Bresa-Litovsk-freden. Två månader förut, i december 1917, hade Trotzky tillbakavisat med en fin gest av nobel indignation den av Tyskland erbjudna freden på villkor som voro mycket fördelaktigare för Ryssland. "Vi föra intet krig, vi underskriva ingen fred!" hade han sagt, och det revolutionära Ryssland applåderade honom. "Ingen kompromiss med den tyska imperialismen, inga medgivanden" ekade det genom landet; och folket stod färdigt att försvara sin revolution ända till döds. Men nu fordrade Lenin ratificeringen av en fred som innebar det mest modlösa förräderi mot den större delen av Ryssland, Finland, Lettland, Lithauen, Vitryssland, Bessarabien - alla gingo över till den tyska inkräktaren och deras egen bourgeoisis förtryck och exploatering.

Lenins inflytande var starkt. Han segrade. Brest-Litovsk-freden ratificerades av den 4:de sovjetkongressen.

Det var Trotzky, vilken först försäkrade under avvisande av den tyska freden på de erbjudna villkoren i december 1917 att arbetarna och bönderna, inspirerade och beväpnade av revolutionen, skullem edelst guerillakrig besegra en invasionsarmé. Vänstersocialrevolutionärerna kallade nu till bonderesningar, till kamp mot tyskarna, övertygade att ingen skulle kunna besegra den revolutionära glöden hos ett folk som kämpade för bevarande av dess stora revolutions frukter! Arbetare och bönder, lyssnade till detta upprop, bildade militärdetachement och störtade till Ukrainas och Vitrysslands hjälp, tappert skridande mot de tyska inkräktarna. Trotzky befallde ryska armén att förfölja och undertrycka dessa friskaror.

Mordet på Mirbach följde härefter.

Det var det vänstersocialrevolutionära partiets protest och utmaning mot den preussiska imperialismen i Ryssland. Bolsjevikregeringen började vidta åtgärder till deras underkuvande, den hade nu en känsla av att stå i obligation till Tyskland. Dzerzhinsky, allryska utomordentliga kommissionens ledare, fordrade terroristernas utlämnande.

Det var en unik situation i revolutionsannalerna: ett revolutionärt parti med makt krävande av ett annat revolutionärt parti, med vilket det samarbetat, arrestering och bestraffning av en revolutionär för avdagatagandet av en imperialistisk regerings representant. Brest-Litovsk-freden hade ställt bolsjevikerna i den onaturliga ställningen av en gendarm för Tyskland. Vänstersocialrevolutionärerna besvarade Dzerzhinskys fordran med den senares arrestering. Denna handling och de väpnade skärmytslingarna, som följde därpå, (ehuru obetydliga i sig själva) voro helt och hållet utförda av de bolsjevikiska politikerna. De förklarade att det var ett försök av vänstersocialrevolutionära partiet att bemäktiga sig regeringstömmarna. De förklarade detta parti fågelfritt och dess utrotning började.

Denna bolsjevikiska metod och taktik var icke av tillfällig natur. Snart blev det klart att det är den kommunistiska statens ständiga politik att krossa varje slags yttring som icke var i överensstämmelse med regeringen. Efter ratificeringen av Brest-Litovsk-freden återkallade vänstersocialrevolutionärerna sina representanter i folkkommissariernas sovjet. Bolsjevikerna voro i besittning av den ensamma kontrollen över regeringen.

Under en och annan förevändning fullföljde de den mest godtyckliga och grymma undertryckning av alla de andra politiska partierna och rörelserna. Mensjevikerna och högersocialrevolutionärerna hade "likviderats" långt förut, tillsammans med den ryska bourgeoisin.

Nu var det de revolutionära elementens tur - vänstersocialrevolutionärerna, anarkisterna, de partilösa revolutionärerna.

Men dessas "likvidation" inbegrep mycket mer än undertryckandet av små politiska grupper. Dessa revolutionära element hade strängt förföljts, vänstersocialrevolutionärerna bland bönderna, anarkisterna huvudsakligen bland stadsproletariatet. Den nya bolsjeviktaktiken inneslöt …

author: Unknown
title: Эррико Малатеста - Мы и Республиканцы
content:
Автор

: Эррико Малатеста

Название

:

Мы и Республиканцы

Дата

: 25 апреля 1920

Источник

: Umanità Nova, год 1-й, №50


 Получаем и публикуем:


Рим

, 20 апреля


Объединимся и победим

!


Мы, молодые республиканцы, не можем не ликовать по поводу поистине революционной пропаганды, которую ведёт

 Umanità Nova;

но нам больно, что она ограничивается разговорами о социализме и анархии, как будто не существует другой доктрины, другой живой силы в народной среде, которое объемлет и то и другое и называется мадзинизмом, определённым Бовио как легализованная анархия. Говорю «объемлет и то и другое», потому что мы хотим республику

 не как цель, а как средство

для постепенного достижения самых высоких человеческих идеалов, следовательно социализма, следовательно анархии.


И чтобы дополнить вашу статью

 «Orizzontiamoci»

[1]


из номера от 18-го апреля, мы говорим, что земля никогда не будет принадлежать крестьянам, фабрики никогда не будут принадлежать рабочим, крупные государственные предприятия никогда не будут принадлежать народам благодаря исключительной деятельности социалистов, которые делают революцию в Парламенте, ни благодаря деятельности республиканцев, которые не устают проповедовать

 «образование!»

, ни благодаря деятельности анархистов, которые надеются на индивидуальное действие; но единственно благодаря коллективному и скоординированному действию всех этих добрых элементов, слитых воедино, которые с оружием в руках должны спуститься в народ и дать ему то правительство,

 которое Он хочет.


Кто сегодня не за это слияние, тот не за революцию.


 А. Бусси.


 _______


 У нас всегда были большие симпатии к республиканцам (не к тем, что за Короля и капиталистов, разумеется) и особенно к тем, кто обычно называет себя мадзинистами.


 Люди веры и мужества, они, как и мы, лелеют высокий идеал свободы, справедливости, обновлённого человечества и готовы, мы верим, бороться и страдать за свой идеал.


 Оставив в стороне их Бога, который нас совершенно не интересует; оставив в стороне их мистический патриотизм, который сделал их, против их собственных намерений, пособниками монархии и капиталистов

[2]

, – казалось бы, расхождения между нами и ними не непреодолимы. Мы не согласны с ними (впрочем, они и сами с собой не согласны) относительно лучшего способа решения экономического вопроса к наибольшей выгоде всех. Они индивидуалисты, мы коммунисты; но поскольку речь идёт о практических решениях проблем производства и распределения, было бы легко договориться на общей почве свободы и равенства условий.


 Но тут замешана… Республика.


 Республиканцы, которые с негодованием отвергают как не своё те буржуазные и милитаристские республики, что услаждают Европу и Америку, довольствуются словами.


 «

Мадзинизм, определённый Бовио: легализованная анархия

». Бовио был философом, и тем не менее, возможно, знал, что хотел сказать; но мы с философией мало знакомы, и нам кажется, что

закон

 означает навязывание воли одних другим, а следовательно

легализованная анархия

 – это бессмыслица.


 «

Мы хотим республику не как цель, а как средство

». Но что такое республика? И если она, согласно обычному словоупотреблению, есть Парламент (пусть даже называемый Учредительным собранием), избранный на основе всеобщего избирательного права, в котором большинство принимает закон и назначает исполнительную власть, которая в свою очередь организует силу для обеспечения соблюдения закона, – то почему то же самое средство дало бы в Италии иные результаты, чем те, что оно всегда давало во всех странах мира?


 «

Народ должен иметь то правительство, которое хочет

». Но кто такой

Народ

? Та любая фракция, которая через избирательный фильтр и парламентские интриги добивается в законодательном собрании необходимого числа голосов для принятия закона?


Воля народа

, сформулированная и применённая посредством закона, – чистая фикция.


 Сегодня народ, то есть совокупность людей, населяющих территорию, разделён на различные классы, имеющие противоположные интересы и чувства, антагонизм которых растёт по мере того, как в подчинённых классах развивается сознание несправедливости, жертвами которой они являются. И закон, несмотря на всеобщее избирательное право, всегда создаётся господствующим классом как инструмент его господства и его защиты. Упраздните правительство, провозгласите республику, созовите Учредительное собрание: поскольку сохраняется разделение на классы, привилегия одних и низшее положение других, правительство …

La propaganda no es y no puede ser más que la repetición continua, incansable, de aquellos principios que deben servirnos de guía en la conducta que debemos seguir en las varias contingencias de la vida.

Repetiremos, pues, con palabras más o menos diferentes, pero con un fondo constante, nuestro viejo programa socialista-anarquista-revolucionario.

Nosotros creemos que la mayor parte de los males que afligen a los hombres dependen de la mala organización social, y que los hombres, si quisieran y supieran cómo, podrían destruirlos.

La sociedad actual es el resultado de las luchas seculares libradas por los hombres. No comprendiendo las ventajas que podrían sacar de la cooperación y de la solidaridad, viendo en los demás hombres (excepto lo más vecinos por los vínculos de la sangre) un competidor y un enemigo, han procurado acaparar, cada uno para sí, la mayor cantidad posible de disfrutes sin preocuparse por los intereses de los demás.

Dada esta lucha, naturalmente debían salir vencedores los más fuertes o los más afortunados, y de una u otra forma, someter y oprimir a los vencidos.

Mientras el hombre no fué capaz de producir sino lo que necesitaba para su sostén, los vencedores no podían hacer otra cosa que matar al vencido y apoderarse de los alimentos por éste cosechados.

Más tarde, cuando con el descubrimiento del pastoreo y del la agricultura un hombre pudo ya producir mas de lo que necesitaba para vivir, los vencedores encontraron mas ventajoso reducir a los vencidos a esclavitud y hacerles producir para sus dueños.

Más tarde aún, los vencedores se dieron cuenta de que era más cómodo, más productivo, y más seguro explotar el trabajo ajeno con otro sistema: retener la propiedad exclusiva de la tierra y de todos los medios de trabajo, y dejar nominalmente libres a los despojados, los cuales, no teniendo ya medios con que vivir, venían obligados a recurrir a los propietarios y a trabajar para éstos en las condiciones que éstos querían.

De este modo, poquito a poco, a través de toda una red complicadísima de luchas de todo género, invasiones, guerras, rebeliones, represiones, concesiones arrancadas, asociaciones de vencidos unidos para la defensa y de vencedores unidos para la ofensa, se ha llegado al estado actual de la sociedad, en la cual unos cuantos detienen hereditariamente la tierra y toda la riqueza social, mientras la gran masa de los hombres, desheredada de todo, se ve explotada y oprimida por unos poco propietarios.

De este estado de cosas depende el estado de miseria en que generalmente se encuentran los trabajadores y por consiguiente todos los males que de la miseria derivan: ignorancia, delitos, prostitución, la abyección física causada por la desnutrición, la depresión mental, y la muerte prematura. De este modo depende la constitución de una clase especial (el gobierno), la cual, provista de medios materiales de represión, tiene la misión de legalizar y defender a los propietarios contra las reivindicaciones de los proletarios, sirviéndose, además, de esta fuerza, para crearse a sí misma ciertos privilegios y para someterse, cuando se puede, incluso hasta la misma clase propietaria. De esto depende la constitución de otra clase especial (el clero), la cual, con una serie de fábulas sobre la voluntad de Dios, sobre la vida futura, etc …

author: Unknown
title: Nils Lätt - Kommunen, den lokala samorganisationen
content:
Författare

: Nils Lätt

Titel

: Kommunen, den lokala samorganisationen

Källa

: Tidningen Brand #1 1965


 Människan i det moderna samhället är ju mer eller mindre kommunist, i så måtto att hon bor i kommuner vilkas administration hon på ena eller andra viset kan påverka, mindre i de s. k. kommunistiska länderna, och andra marxistiskt färgade samhällsskick där den politiska makten, koncentrerad i

staten

 mer och mer kringskär den personliga och kollektiva friheten och beslutanderätten. Men en allmän tendens är tydligt skönjbar också hos socialdemokraterna att mer och mer centralisera beslutanderätten, mer och mer göra alla lokala samfund och sammanslutningar fiktiva eller snarare parodiska, såsom t. ex. sker i LO där man på fullt allvar företager omröstningar i avtalsfrågor, vilkas resultat säges vara rådgivande för centralorganisationen, men som i realiteten ej tillskrives något som helst värde.


 Men fortfarande beslutar ju kommunen i vissa angelägenheter och de olika partierna väljer representanter, som har att besluta över stadens, kommunens angelägenheter. Vi anarkister och syndikalister kritiserar ju det politiska spelet runt dessa val, som liksom de statliga valen blir en kamp om makten, ofta för maktens egen skuld. Under stridens hetta i valkampanjen för de olika partierna, försvinner ofta målet kommunens administration. Människorna, för vilka ju kommunen existerar och för vars bästa man skulle kämpa, glömmes bort. Väljarna själva dras med i det spännande spelet och tänker knappast på att de dagen efter valet ej ha någon som helst möjlighet att påverka skeendet, eller ens ha någon insyn i administrationen. De konstatera helt saktmodigt att: avgifterna höjs, men spårvägen går lika fullt med förlust. Folkets representanter sitter på sina poster och man får slå sig till ro med den tanken att de gör så gott de kan.


 Men är det så säkert att de gör det, eller att de gör det som de gör, på bästa sätt???


 Vi anarkister i dett land hyllar ju

den kommunistiska anarkismen,

 i enlighet med vår uppfattning om Krapotkins och andra anarkistiska läromästares teorier.


 Vi har alltså klart förstått kommunens betydelse. Förstått att man ej må avhända kommunens innevånare rätten att besluta i egna angelägenheter. Men eftersom vi är anarkister strävar vi efter att för kommunen finna ett styrelsesätt utan diktatorisk utformning, där politisk ambition skall betyda mindre än omsorgen och vården om det allmänna, och om den gemensamma egendomen. Anarkister och syndikalister har i

federalismen

 funnit det system som hittills lämnat största garanti för en demokratisk utformning av ett styrelseskick. Korporationer och samfund besluta i egna angelägenhter under eget ansvar, för gemensamma intressen skapas centrala administrativa organ, ej utrustade med beslutande rätt, utan endast till för att övervaka fattade besluts utförande.


 SAC:s organisationsplan är ett typiskt sådant utformande, där den centrala huvudorganisationen uppbyggts av lokala samorganisationer, vilka förbehållits full beslutanderätt och handlingsfrihet i egna angelägenheter, och detta berör samtliga medlemmar oberoende av yrkestillhörighet eller sysselsättning. Professionellt är ju SAC:s medlemmar sammanslutna i organisationer på arbetsplatserna, besläktade sådana sammanförs till syndikat vilka i sin tur bilda federationer och industrisammanslutningar, som i sin tur kan samordnas internationellt.


 Alltså går vi den andra vägen ser vi att kommunen, LS är sammansatt av syndikat, som när organisationen är fullt utbyggd representera i LS med fastställt antal representanter, tillsammans med andra ej rent yrkesmässiga organisationer, som t. ex. konsumenternas, hyresgästernas osv. ALla innevånarnas intressen borde alltså vara rikligt företrädda inom kommunen direkt av de olika gruppernas medlemmar vilket system skulle eliminera risken för uppkomsten av en ny yrkespolitisk kår.


 Vilken roll spelar då denna kommun eller LS för oss syndikalister eller kommunistiska anarkister i dag???


 Den som följt med i de olika juridiska härvor, som bl. a. Vilhelm Moberg, Osvald, Kejne, Eliasson och andra försökt reda ut, måste ha märkt hur liten uppmärksamhet dessa väckt bland folkets representanter i stadsfullmäktigegrupper och riksdag, för att inte tala om regering. Är det så att de folkvalda direkt känner sig illa berörda av denna insyn i "egna" angelägenheter, eller kanske på något dunkelt sätt medansvariga??? Vi vet inte detta, bara konstaterar fakta.

author: Unknown
title: Григорий Петрович Максимов - Проблема насилия в революции
content:
Автор

: Григорий Петрович Максимов

Название

: Проблема насилия в революции

Дата

: 1927

Дополнительная информация

: Из: Голос труженика, №22, 1927


Источник террора


 Вопрос, который был подробно рассмотрен И. 3. Штейнбергом в его книге: «Нравственный лик революции», не случайно привлёк к себе огромное внимание.


 Не случайно, что этот вопрос в своё время неоднократно дебатировался в среде социалистической эмиграции. Не случайно, что этот вопрос занимает общественное внимание и теперь.


 Все это свидетельствует о чрезвычайном интересе к поставленной проблеме. Оно и понятно, разве можно пройти мимо той широкой практики насилия, проявлявшейся во время революции в самых различных формах, как в России, так и в Германии: интерес к поставленной проблеме обуславливается ещё тем обстоятельством, что насилие во всех его возможных и мыслимых формах, осуществлялось и продолжает осуществляться социалистами во имя достижения священной идеи социализма, носителями которой являются все передовые элементы современного общества.


 То разительное противоречие, которое обнаружилось во время только что минувших революций, между целью и средствами, методами осуществления, якобы вытекающими из самой цели, поставив под сомнение моральные основы социализма. Если бы не это, то, надо думать, что проблема насилия в революции не интересовала бы в такой мере, в какой она интересует сейчас все мыслящие элементы.


 Да, можно смело утверждать, что современные революции поставили под сомнение моральные устои, если не не всего социализма вообще, то его разновидности — государственного социализма. Возникает вопрос: не является ли насилие, в том числе и террор, внутренним содержанием государственного социализма? Не вытекает ли террористическая практика большевиков и немецких социал-демократов с логической неизбежностью из государственного социализма, как только он начинает осуществляться в жизни?


 И здесь честный вопрос о насилии разрастается до огромных размеров, до вопроса этики социализма, социалистической нравственности. Мы подходим здесь к той стороне социализма, на которую меньше всего обращалось внимания и котрой придавалось очень малое значение самими социалистами. Здесь кроется величайшая ошибка и величайший грех социалистов, ибо разгул террора в России и Германии (Носке-Шейдеман), есть неизбежное следствие этой печальной ошибки. И сейчас, когда вопросы насилия в революции с особой силой привлекают внимание, когда революционно-социалистическая практика наткнулась на разнообразные формы насилия и скомпрометировала на много лет идею социализма, я с сожалением констатирую, что ни автор упомянутой книги, ни его оппоненты на одном из его докладов в Берлине, в их числе и В.М. Чернов, ни Каутский, который ещё раньше поднял этот вопрос в своей книге о «Терроризме и коммунизме», не поднялись на настоящую высоту вопроса, а отделываются мелочами или просто смазывают вопрос и переносят его в плоскость отдельных частных вопросов, как террор, порицая его, но не ставя его в связь с общей системой нравственной философии социализма.


 Ведь проблема насилия в революцииесть вопрос практической нравственной философии, а если так, то вполне естественно, их нельзя рассматривать отдельно вне связи с теоретической нравственной философией. Прежде чем говорить о насилии, оправдывать его целиком или частично, или совершенно отрицать, необходимо установить на научном базисе ос новные моральные максимы, т. е. необходимо создать новую систему нравственности, той нравственности, которой проникнут социализм, но для которой он ещё не выработал системы. Потребность в выработке новой естественно-научной революционной системы нравственности, отличной от современной системы буржуазной нравственности, основанной на управлении и эксплоатации, отличной от системы Гоббса, по которой борьба всех — закон природы и где «человек человеку — волк», а также отличной от этики Канта и Нищие, между которыми бьётся современная мысль, чувствовалось давно, сожалению, очень немногими социалистами. Эта потребность чувствовалась Бакуниным, после поражения Коммуны, но болезнь, а затем смерть не позволили ему заняться специально этим вопросом. Тем не менее свою работу «Кнуто-Германская империя» он в значительной мере посвятил вопросам нравственности, о чём он сам говорит в тексте этой книги. Затем эту потребность чувствовал Кропоткин. В письме к Атабекяну (2-5—20 г.) он пишет: «Я взялся за этику, потому что считаю эту работу безусловно необходимой»… «в такой разработке, теперь, когда …

author: Chris Walker
title: Trump Bought Millions in SpaceX Bonds, Then Eased Space Travel Regulations
content:
Trump’s financial disclosures also show he bought millions in stock from Meta as the company ramps up its AI efforts.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

President Donald Trump made over 500 stock trades in the month of August, recent filings show, including millions of dollars in bonds purchased for SpaceX, just days before the administration loosened regulations that would have affected the company.

According to the most recent disclosures from Trump, the president purchased bonds from the company worth at least $1 million and up to $5 million.

Those trades involving SpaceX occurred on August 18. Two days later, on August 20, Trump issued a memorandum announcing the purported launching of “the golden age of space transportation.” Among other items, the memo seeks to loosen regulations on potential companies that venture into commercial space travel, and directs federal agencies to “incentivize co-development of space transportation infrastructure with private sector partners.”

Trump and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk have had a complicated but mostly friendly history. Musk infused hundreds of millions of dollars into the 2024 presidential election in support of Trump, and led the Trump administration’s “Department of Government Efficiency” initiative that gutted many federal agencies. The two had a brief falling out afterwards, but in recent months seem to have reconciled.

Indeed, Musk sat beside Trump at a recent White House summit on artificial intelligence (AI), and the president awarded him the National Medal of Science on Thursday.

Critics lambasted the trades and subsequent action by Trump to deregulate space travel as unscrupulous.

“There is a conflict of interest. I’m not saying he’s doing anything illegal, but this really gives the appearance of corruption,” said George W. Bush-era White House ethics lawyer Richard Painter.

“Rather than bringing down the cost of gas and groceries, President Trump is using his office to enrich himself,” Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Massachusetts) said. “That’s corruption, plain and simple.”

Trump also purchased up to $25 million in stock from Meta, Facebook’s parent company, which has been ramping up its AI efforts. During the past two months since those stock purchases, Trump has stated that he will reject any efforts to pass legislation that would regulate the AI industry, despite strong support from the public to do so, and has even gone so far as to describe those who want more restrictions or a slowdown of AI development as treasonous.

More recently, Trump has sought to rebrand AI as “super intelligence,” or “SI,” and issued a threat to anyone who continues to use the older phrasing.

“The White House considers anyone that uses the term, ‘Artificial Intelligence,’ as opposed to the highly accepted new and more accurate term, ‘Super Intelligence,’ THE ENEMY!” Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social this week.

author: CMI Argentina
title: Tras la presión popular y el temor a que caiga el DNU 70/23, la Corte mileísta rehabilita la Ley de Tierras
content:
El Tribunal suspendió los efectos de un fallo propio de una semana atrás donde eliminaba los límites legales a la extranjerización del territorio. Una reacción extraordinaria frente al repudio en las calles y un guiño a Milei, en pánico ante la posible derogación del mega decreto.


En una jugada de alto impacto político e institucional, la Corte Suprema dictó una resolución cautelar interina que reactiva las restricciones vigentes a la venta de suelo rural a capitales extranjeros.


El fallo fue dictado por los jueces Horacio Rosatti, Ricardo Lorenzetti y los conjueces Diego Barroetaveña y Juan Ignacio Pérez Curci. El juez Carlos Rosenkrantz votó en disidencia.


De esta manera, el Tribunal dio marcha atrás sobre lo resuelto apenas unos días atrás, en un trámite de urgencia que omitió los traslados procesales habituales y prescindió del paso por las instancias inferiores.


El giro rompe con la dinámica habitual de la magistratura y expone la conmoción que generó en los despachos oficiales el avance del malestar social. Entre otras movidas, la que esta semana protagonizaron las dos CTA junto a los integrantes del Centro de Ex Combatientes Islas Malvinas (Cecim) La Plata, impulsores de la cautelar que frenaba el artículo extranjerizante del DNU 70/23.


La diferencia central que argumenta ahora la Corte es el posible daño ambiental y no la afectación a la pérdida de soberanía. Dice que resulta necesario “asegurar la tutela judicial efectiva, y evitar la producción de daños irreparables”. Rosenkrantz en disidencia.


— Mariana Verón (@veronmariana)

October 9, 2026


A su vez, la reacción de los cortesanos responde a las alertas que había despertado en Casa Rosada la sesión convocada por la oposición para derogar el mega decreto en cuestión.


Con la nueva resolución, los efectos del artículo 154 quedan suspendidos de manera provisoria mientras se tramita el expediente de Árbol de Pie. El Juzgado Federal de Bariloche deberá determinar primero si los demandantes cuentan con legitimación para promover el amparo y, luego, examinar si corresponde conceder la medida cautelar solicitada.


La resolución de la Corte no constituye una sentencia definitiva sobre el fondo del asunto. La constitucionalidad del artículo 154 del DNU 70/2023 sigue pendiente de resolución, por lo que el alcance definitivo del régimen de tierras dependerá de las decisiones que se adopten durante el proceso judicial.


El desenlace dependerá de lo que resuelva el Congreso y de la continuidad del reclamo soberano en las calles. Por lo pronto, sigue en pie la convocatoria a movilizar el próximo 15 de octubre, junto a las universidades. Aún es muy pronto para saber qué hará la oposición en el Congreso: seguir danzando al ritmo del Gobierno y la Corte, o imponer su agenda y avanzar con la derogación del mega decreto fundante del mileísmo.

author: Rachel May
title: Are the feds overstepping its authority by negotiating a child welfare deal?
content:
An advocate involved in a two decade long battle over reforming the First Nations child welfare system says the federal government is overstepping its authority after signing a deal with the

Saskatoon Tribal Council, or STC

.


Cindy Blackstock, executive director of the First Nations Child and Family Caring Society, said the minister of Indigenous Services Canada is getting ahead of herself by offering the STC a deal and money for seven communities to take over their child welfare system.


“The government is behaving as if their plan has already won the day and they’re out there trying to negotiate regional deals based on their plan,” Blackstock said in an upcoming episode of Face to Face.


The plan Blackstock is referring to is one of two the Canadian Human Rights Tribunal is considering as a path to reform the on-reserve child welfare system.


The communities involved in the child welfare deal with Mandy Gull-Masty, minister of Indigenous Services Canada. Photo: Rachel May/APTN.


In 2016, the Canadian Human Rights Tribunal ruled that the federal government discriminated against First Nations children by knowingly underfunding the programs meant to help them.


It ordered Canada to end the discrimination and come up with a plan to ensure it stops.


“I’m doing this work, and I’m following the decisions that they made,” said ISC Minister Mandy Gull-Masty. “They upheld the OFA (Ontario Final Agreement). They felt this this was a good process. We are simply doing that continued work across the country.”


The OFA provides $8.5 billion until March 31 2034 to First Nations in Ontario to reform the First Nations child welfare system in 133 communities. The agreement is from a national plan that was voted down by chiefs across the country, except Ontario.


Read More: 


Two child welfare plans head to Canadian Human Rights Tribunal 


In Saskatchewan, the STC signed a $279 million deal. It gives the council’s seven members more control over developing their own child and family services system.


Gull-Masty said the approach recognizes that each First Nation has different needs.


“The best way to do that is by ensuring that the people that are taking decisions for kids know and determine who they are,” she said. “And for me, being sure that I’m able to help in this space is by giving authority, by giving resources, by giving flexibility to community to make those decisions for their children; I think this is aligned with what the vision of the CHRT is.”


At the centre of the disagreement are two competing approaches for reform. One is Canada’s proposed $35.5 billion that will provide money through to 2034. The other is the Loving Justice Plan – developed by First Nations leadership. That plan calls for a stable budget, lasting protection against discrimination, along with great accountability and transparency.


“That big number, $ 35 billion, to me, that should be in place regardless of what plan you choose because the government’s commitment should be the well being of the children; then we’re just talking about structure,” said Blackstock.


The CHRT is expected to choose a plan in the Spring of 2027.

content:
Fotoğraf: Zulfugar Karimov/Pexels

Resmi Gazete’de yayımlanan yeni yönetmeliğe göre, 15 yaşından küçükler sosyal ağları kullanamayacak.

Resmi Gazete'de yayımlanan "Sosyal Ağ Sağlayıcı Tarafından Çocuklara Özgü Ayrıştırılmış Hizmet Sunulmasına ve Yaş Doğrulamaya İlişkin Yönetmeliği" ile 15 yaşını doldurmamış kimselere sosyal medya hesabı açma, kullanma ve yönetmenin engelleneceği duyuruldu.

Mevcut hesapların, 31 Mart 2027'ye kadar doğrulanması zorunlu kılınırken 15-18 yaş arası çocuklar için hesapların varsayılan olarak gizli olacağı, mesajlaşmanın kısıtlanacağı, canlı yayın açılması ve rehber senkronizasyonunun yasaklanacağı "ayrıştırılmış hizmet" modeli uygulanacak.

Bununla birlikte ailelerin çocukların ekran süresini, harcamalarını ve hesap ayarlarını denetleyebileceği Türkçe destekli ebeveyn kontrol araçları da ebeveynlere sunulacak.

Yönetmelik, 1 Kasım 2026'da yürürlüğe girecek.

5 soruda sosyal medya yasası: 15 yaş altını neler bekliyor?

author: Jesse Staniforth
title: Sonia Caron, du PQ, va prendre les rênes de la plus grande circonscription du Québec
content:
Après 12 ans, Sonia Caron, du Parti québécois, a repris la circonscription d’Ungava, dans le Nord-du-Québec, ramenant celle-ci dans le giron du PQ lors de l’élection du 5 octobre.


Sonia Caron est née à Chibougamau, où elle réside toujours, près de la Nation crie de Mistissini. Dans une entrevue accordée à APTN Nouvelles nationales, elle a indiqué qu’elle souhaite devenir une porte-parole de l’ensemble des personnes vivant dans le Nord.


« Moi, je représente le Parti québécois, évidemment, parce que ça reflète mes valeurs », a-t-elle déclaré à APTN Nouvelles nationales, « mais mon intérêt est avant tout un intérêt pour parler du Nord à Québec et être la meilleure voie possible, justement, pour les gens avec qui je travaille. C’est important de traduire nos besoins à l’État, puis qu’on comprenne de part et d’autre avec quoi on peut avancer ensemble pour être plus efficace, puis répondre à quels besoins en priorité. »


S’étendant sur 855 164 km

2

, la circonscription québécoise d’Ungava figure parmi les plus grandes au pays. Sa superficie n’est surpassée que par celles des circonscriptions fédérales du Nunavut et des Territoires du Nord-Ouest, qui englobent chacune un territoire entier.


Ungava est plus vaste que l’ensemble de la France. Pourtant, selon Élections Québec, sa population ne compte que 45 740 personnes, dont 30 773 sont admissibles au vote. La population est dispersée aux quatre coins de cette immense circonscription, qui englobe les 14 communautés du Nunavik, où vivent quelque 13 000 Inuit, ainsi que les neuf communautés de la Nation crie d’Eeyou Istchee, qui compte environ 20 000 membres. La circonscription englobe aussi plusieurs localités non autochtones, dont Chibougamau, Lebel-sur-Quévillon, Matagami et Chapais, qui comptent ensemble quelque 14 000 personnes.


Le 5 octobre, 8 516 personnes se sont prévalus de leur droit de vote dans Ungava, pour un taux de participation de 27,61 %. Sonia Caron a obtenu le plus grand nombre de voix, soit 3 272.


Enseignante et directrice d’école ayant amorcé sa carrière à Inukjuak avant de retourner à Chibougamau pour y fonder une famille, Sonia Caron affirme vouloir mieux cerner les enjeux du Nord qui sont mal compris à Québec et qui nécessitent une représentation plus soutenue. Elle souhaite également collaborer avec les dirigeants cris et inuit afin de répondre aux besoins de leurs communautés.


« Je suis très consciente que je représente trois entités différentes sur un même territoire », a-t-elle dit. « Que ce soit pour les services aux aînés, la santé mentale, l’accès à une éducation de qualité, tout est là. Pour moi, c’est seulement de mettre tout le monde ensemble à la même table. »


Expérience et priorités


Après avoir enseigné et travaillé dans des écoles primaires et secondaires, Sonia Caron dirige un centre de formation professionnelle depuis les dix dernières années. Elle affirme également avoir siégé, au cours de la dernière décennie, à plusieurs conseils d’administration, dont ceux de l’Institut national des mines du Québec, de l’Assemblée des partenaires de la Société du Plan Nord et du Conseil régional des partenaires du marché du travail. Dans ce dernier cas, elle a notamment travaillé aux côtés de représentants des nations crie et inuit.


« J’ai touché beaucoup à la main-d’œuvre, à la santé, à l’éducation, au secteur minier, forestier, de par les formations qu’on donne à notre centre », a-t-elle dit. “Donc, je me suis dit pourquoi ne pas aller faire écouter la voix que tu portes depuis dix ans sur tous ces comités-là pour faire comprendre et connaître les réels enjeux du nord. »


Après des décennies passées dans le milieu de l’éducation, tout en collaborant avec des organismes gouvernementaux et des sociétés d’État, Sonia Caron estime avoir acquis une bonne compréhension du fonctionnement de l’appareil gouvernemental et des moyens de le rendre plus efficace.


« Mon bagage en éducation et en direction m’amène aussi à analyser toujours les causes d’une problématique », a-t-elle dit, « ou aller en profondeur pour intervenir à la source. C’est sûr que des fois, c’est plus long, mais quand on intervient sur les bons facteurs de changement, ça peut faire beaucoup de belles choses. »


Selon elle, cette expérience lui a donné les outils nécessaires pour travailler efficacement dans un territoire aussi grand qu’Ungava.


« Souvent, on est enclavé par soit l’avion, les voies maritimes ou les routes qui sont parfois hasardeuses l’hiver » …

Ankara Garı’nın önünde 2015 yılında; emek, barış ve demokrasi güçlerinin “barış ve demokrasi” talebiyle bir araya geldiği mitinge düzenlenen saldırıda 103 kişi hayatını kaybetti. Katliamın üzerinden 11 yıl geçmesine rağmen hayatını kaybedenlerin aileleri, yoldaşları, arkadaşları adalet mücadelesini sürdürüyor. İl dışında olan aileler; her davaya gelmeye, bulundukları illerde çocuklarının, yoldaşlarının mücadelesini, “barış ve demokrasi” talebini yükseltmeye, onların isimlerini yaşatmaya devam ediyor.

Katliamın 11 yılında Evrensel’e konuşan aileler her davada, her 10 Ekim’de söyledikleri gibi kamu görevlilerinin sorumluluğuna, katliama nasıl yol verildiğine dikkat çekiyor. Aileler, sorumluları ortaya çıkarmayanlara, “Mücadelemizden vazgeçmeyeceğiz” diye sesleniyor.

Katliamda hayatını kaybeden Cemal Avşar’ın eşi Gülşen Avşar, mücadeleye devam ettiğini ve ısrarla adalet talep ettiğini anlatıyor. “Çok yorulduk ama devam edeceğiz” diyen Gülşen Avşar yaşadıklarından şöyle bahsediyor: “11 yıldır mücadele ediyoruz. Onlar bizi yıldırmaya çalışıyorlar ama yılmıyoruz. Hem yollar hem mahkemeler bizi yoruyor. Her davadan döndüğümde çocuklarımın başının bükülmesi bizi yoruyor. 11 sene oldu, hiçbir şekilde sesimizi duyuramadık. O zaman kızım 11 yaşındaydı, şimdi işe başladı. Torunlarım dedelerini göremedi. Ben ağlayamadım bile. İşe gitmek zorunda kaldım. Çocuklarıma anne, baba, abi olacağım diye sağlığım gitti. Artık adalet istiyoruz.”

Şebnem Yurtman’ın annesi Şafak Yurtman da kızının mücadelesinden ne kadar gurur duyduğunu anlatarak başlıyor sözlerine. Katliamın ardından eşine karakolda, “Kızınızın oraya gittiğinden haberiniz var mıydı?” diye sorulduğunu anlatan Yurtman, “Kızım 23 yaşındaydı, izin mi alacaktı? Zaten işim olmasaydı ben de gidecektim. Beraber o alanda olacaktık. Barışı beraber talep edecektik. 11 senedir davalara gidip geliyoruz. Küçücük bir ilerleme olmaz mı? İnsan ‘adalet varmış’ demez mi? Biz diyemiyoruz. Sözüm var Şebnem’e. Ömrüm yettiği sürece mücadeleye devam edeceğim. Tüm ailelere sesleniyorum. Bu hepimizin mücadelesi” diyor. Yurtman, “Elimizden bütün renklerimizi aldılar. Ben rengarenk bir insandım. Şebnem’in sevdiği yemekler evde pişmiyor. İnternette gezinirken Şebnem’in yoldaşlarının, onun resimlerini paylaştığını görüyorum. Bazıları benim bile bilmediğim resimler. Mutlu oluyorum” diye noktalıyor sözlerini.

Korkmaz Tedik’in annesi Zöhre Tedik de o gün barış talep etmek için ailecek mitinge gittiklerini anlatıyor: “Biz ailecek gittik alana. Ben gidemeyecektim. Korkmaz, ‘Anne gelmen lazım, sen gelmezsen barış olmaz. Bak parti çağırıyor’ demişti de ikna etmişti beni. O gün hepimiz alandaydık. Bir ara Korkmaz yanımızdan ayrıldı, sonra bomba patladı. Ancak öğrendik ki bomba patladığında Korkmaz hayattaymış. Onunla ilgilenen arkadaşına, ‘Ben iyiyim, sen diğerlerine bak’ demiş. Korkmaz’ın ölümüne neden olan, bombanın ardından polis tarafından sıkılan biber gazı olmuş.”

O günden itibaren avukatlarla, Korkmaz’ın yoldaşlarıyla, katledilenlerin aileleriyle mücadeleyi sürdürdüklerine vurgu yapan Zöhre Tedik, “İçimiz kan ağlarken katillerden hesap sormak için mücadele ettik. Başta Korkmaz’ın yoldaşları, partisi, avukatlar, sendikalar birleşti. Bugüne kadar da mücadeleyi sürdürdük. Avukatlarımız bize cesaret verdi. İl il, ilçe ilçe gezip delil topladılar. Davanın heyeti 4 kere değişti, hepsine dosyayı baştan anlattılar. Biz de olduğumuz her yerde bu katliam unutulmasın diye mücadele etmeye devam ediyoruz. Dönemin başbakanının sözlerini ve sorumluluğunu, bakanlarının sözlerini ve sorumluluklarını da unutmadık, unutmayacağız. Dünya alem bilsin ki katillerden hesap soracağız. Vasiyetimdir, benden sonra da Korkmaz’ın ve diğer 102 insanın mücadelesi unutulmasın” diye konuşuyor.

Güney Doğan’ın annesi Derman Doğan da “11 yılı yaşayan bilir. 11 yıldır hem onun yokluğu hem de mahkemeler yıpratıyor bizi” diye söz ediyor mücadelesinden. Mahkemeden olumlu bir ilerleme görememenin, sürekli heyet değişmesinin, her heyete tüm dosyanın tekrar anlatılmasının yorucu olduğunu söyleyen Doğan, “Mahkeme heyetinin bize karşı tavırları, ‘Çok konuşursan dışarı atarım’ demelerine mi göğüs gerelim, acıya mı göğüs gerelim bilmiyorum” diye soruyor.

“Benim çocuğum sadece barış istediği için katledildi” diyen Doğan, “Katledilenlerin suçları barış, özgürlük, demokrasi istemekti” diye tepkisini anlatıyor. Doğan, “Bombanın ardından yaralıların üstüne zehirli gaz …

author: Daron Letts
title: Elder van project could hit the streets in 2027, premier says
content:
Five accessible elders vans that were purchased with $1 million in public money remain off the roads one year after a

pilot project

 affirmed the need for such a service.


While he wouldn’t provide a specific timeline for the vans’ rollout, Premier John Main said it’s his “desire” to see the vans back in operation in 2027 — three years after they were purchased.


“The update is, as of right now, they’re still not operating,” he said in a phone interview Friday. “But, our government does want to follow through on this.”


The project stalled in 2025, at the end of the previous government’s term, due to a lack of an operating budget.


That changed in spring 2026 when MLAs in the current legislative assembly approved $1.25 million in additional funding,

 Main said.


When the bus service was first announced, it was a partnership among Northern Future Skills Development, Arctic Training Ltd., and Caribou Cabs.


There is one van in each of five communities:

Iqaluit, Cambridge Bay, Rankin Inlet, Coral Harbour and Pangnirtung.

Northern Future Skills Development, a private company, bought them with funding it got from the GN.


Representatives of Arctic Training Ltd. and Caribou Cabs were not available to comment on this story.


Kopa Mike stands next to the elders bus operated by the Pairiniit Society at Iqaluit’s Elders’ Qammaq on Friday. (Photo by Daron Letts)


Policy is being developed behind the scenes and, once complete, the government plans to issue a call for proposals before the end of 2026, Main said.


It remains to be decided whether that call will be public or “by invitation,” he added.


Arctic Training Ltd. ran a self-funded, month-long

short-term soft launch

 of the service in Iqaluit a year ago, in October 2025. The company responded to approximately 200 service calls each weekend.


Kopa Mike, a board member with the Pairijiit Tigummiaqtikkut Iqaluit Elders Society, used the new van three times that month to travel between the Elders Qammaq, food bank, and grocery store, she said.


The new van’s ramp was a bit challenging with her bad leg, she said, but an assistant on the bus made it easy to climb until she could reach the handrails inside the bus while she boarded, she said.


“It was great having help,” she said.


The elders society itself runs three vehicles, including an elder bus. But that bus’ accessibility ramp has been broken for a long time, said fellow board member Ainiak Korgak.


”We got tired of waiting for the new bus so we forgot about it,” Mike added.


“I realize it’s been some time since these vans were originally purchased, and there is some anticipation and frustration around the fact that they’re still not operating,” Main said. “The next step is to see a policy established, which would govern that funding and see it flow across Nunavut to folks who will be running this type of service.”

author: Charlotte Morritt-Jacobs
title: Dene Nation establishes water council as leaders warn of tar sands tailings risks
content:
The Dene Nation unanimously passed a resolution to establish a Dene Water Council at its 56th national assembly, in Kátł’odeeche First Nation, Northwest Territories.


The resolution referred to water as “a sacred gift from the Creator” and called for greater Dene-led oversight of water quality, industrial activity and contamination across the North.


The conversation led by Gerry Cheezie, co-chair of Keepers of the Water and a former chief of the Tthebatthie Denesųłiné Nation, comes as Indigenous leaders raise concerns about proposed plans to treat and release oilsands tailings water into the Athabasca River, which flows north into the Mackenzie River basin.


The resolution states that Dene waters are facing increasing pressures from industrial development, resource extraction, climate change, contamination and cumulative effects.


Cheezie, who recently attended Suncor Energy Inc.’s engagement sessions on its plans to treat and release tailings, said the water issue has never been more urgent.


”We’re impacted and we don’t want to see our waters polluted,” Cheezie said.


The Dene Nation Assembly building in Kátł’odeeche First Nation, N.W.T., where delegates gathered for the 56th Dene National Assembly. Photo: Charlotte Morritt-Jacobs/APTN.


Industrial development in northern Alberta has already affected the environment and the exercise of Treaty 8 rights, which include an agreement to protect Indigenous inherent rights to fish, hunt, trap and pursue traditional ways of life.


Cheezie took issue with Alberta’s regulatory response to industrial contamination.


“They [Suncor]  were fined $50,000 by the Alberta Energy Regulators for the Carle Lake plant, in which they released millions of litres of tailings into the Atabasca and they got a slap on the wrist,” Cheezie said. “The province of Alberta’s regulations aren’t being enforced and the federal government is silent on this, so we have to rely on ourselves.”


Cheezie said oversight and advocacy groups he works with are exploring possible legal action over cumulative impacts on treaty rights and traditional ways of life.


He said the evidence, costs and next steps would need to be considered by leadership which is why he is asking the Dene Nation to join as an intervener.


“When we talk about water, it’s at the 11th hour right now,” Cheezie said. “Industry, the oil industry is trying to poison our water and we have to step up and stop it.”


Cheezie warned that the contamination threat extends far beyond any single community.


“If you live in the community of Hay River, what are you gonna do? Where are you gonna go to get your water?” he said. “Great Slave Lake will be polluted; there will be toxins, heavy metals and other all kinds of forever chemicals in the water that are all going to impact your health.”


Chief Allan Adam, on the right, of the Athabasca Chipewyan First Nation calling on chiefs across the North to speak up about the threats posed by oil-sands tailings releases.


The N.W.T. and Alberta relies strictly on a trans-boundary water agreement, which Indigenous governments are not a party to, and it’s agreement Cheezie said hasn’t helped Indigenous groups when they have tried to negotiate with oil industry and governments in the past.


“We pull out the trans-boundary agreement and say this is supposed to protect our rights in the territories, and all they [GNWT and Albertan provincial government] do is communicate with us,” he said. “They’re approving projects, approving environmental issues that could affect us without telling us.


In July, 2026, the Dene Nation and Treaty 8 First Nations in Alberta signed a memorandum of understanding to work together on protecting shared waters in the Mackenzie River basin.


“We want to work together supporting each other legally, scientifically, environmentally, to protect the water because we’re not moving anywhere,” he said.


Cheezie, who was born in Fort Chipewyan, said the resolution passed at the assembly represents a step toward protecting the water that sustains communities and traditional practices.


“We have to haul water when we’re going out on the land and that’s beyond anybody’s imagination back in 1899 that we would have to do that when we signed the treaty,” he said.


Chief Allan Adam of the Athabasca Chipewyan First Nation, a guest presenter at the assembly, also addressed delegates, delivering a passionate call to action to the large gathering about the urgency of the crisis.

author: Jesse Staniforth
title: Supreme Court decision balances Gladue factors against concern for Indigenous women
content:
The Supreme Court of Canada upheld a reduced sentence in the case of a Mi’kmaw man convicted of brutally assaulting his Mi’kmaw partner in 2021 in a decision expected to have significant effect on the way judges consider Indigenous men who commit violent crimes against Indigenous women.


In

a five-four split decision

, the court found the initial five-year sentence fell short in factoring for both the convicted man’s mental health issues and Indigenous considerations, and upheld an appeals court judgement that reduced the sentence to three years plus two years probation after release, minus time served on remand.


The case turned on two serious considerations for Indigenous people in the legal system.


One was guidance written into the criminal code following the 1999 decision in R. v. Gladue, which instructs courts to consider systemic and background factors that affect the “moral blameworthiness” of an Indigenous offender, and to consider the sentencing and sanctions appropriate to an Indigenous offender’s specific circumstances.


The second consideration was of guidance in the criminal code that resulted from the National Inquiry into Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women and Girls (MMIWG), in which a judge must prioritize objectives of “denunciation and deterrence” in sentencing someone who abused “a person who is vulnerable, including because they are an Indigenous woman or girl.”


“The legislative history of these provisions is clear that they were introduced with the goal of addressing violence against Indigenous women and girls and other vulnerable victims that has been overlooked for far too long,” writes Justice Michelle O’Bonsawin in the majority decision, which was supported by Justices Andromache Karakatsanis, Sheilah Martin, Nicholas Kasirer and Mary Moreau.


A dissenting opinion was written by Justices Malcolm Rowe and Mahmud Jamal, supported by Justice Suzanne Côté and Chief Justice Richard Wagner. It argued the original sentence should be restored, because the sentencing judge properly weighed all relevant factors, while the Court of Appeal’s reduced sentence “did not reflect denunciation, deterrence, the victim’s vulnerability, or the sentencing judge’s conclusion that the offender poses a continuing danger to society.”


Yet O’Bonsawin’s decision stresses the considerations of both Indigenous offenders and Indigenous women and girls who are victims of violence should not be seen at odds with each other.


“Viewing these provisions as conflicting misrepresents their goals,” she writes. “The sentencing judge’s task is to impose a proportionate and individualized sentence that gives due consideration to both the needs of Indigenous offenders and Indigenous victims. Reconciliation must serve as an important lodestar in applying these provisions together.”


Supreme Court Justice Michelle O’Bonsawin. Photo: Mark Blackburn/APTN.


The crime and the conviction


The case centres on Harry Arthur Cope, who pled guilty to attacking his occasional partner, a woman from Sipekne’katik First Nation, in a 2021 assault. The judgment described the attack as “horrendous” and “brutal,” in which “the victim’s head was repeatedly punched, kicked and smashed against the sidewalk, leaving her with significant injuries.”


At the time of the assault, Cope — whom the decision describes as having “severe mental health challenges” — had been off his medication for just over a year, and had instead been consuming illicit drugs.


The court ordered an Indigenous Background Report and a sentencing circle consider the case. That circle found community members felt further incarceration would not help Cope, whom they recommended receive holistic care, including in-patient treatment.


Nova Scotia Provincial Court Judge Christine Driscoll recognized that because of Cope’s “Gladue factors” (those elements in which his background as an Indigenous person affected his circumstances), as well as his mental health problems and major addictions issues, he was less morally culpable of the crime than a person that did not carry those burdens. She also acknowledged the community’s lack of recommendation of further jail time.


However, Driscoll found intimate-partner violence against an Indigenous woman was an aggravating factor, and handed down a five-year sentence.


A majority in the Court of Appeal revised that decision, arguing Driscoll failed to accurately emphasize the connections between Cope’s mental illness, drug abuse …

author: David Swanson
title: 10 Reasons for Public Executions
content:
By David Swanson, World BEYOND War, October 9, 2026


There was no public demand that led to the U.S. military announcing that it would publicly execute someone on livestreamed video (a list of advertisers, if any, during the broadcast has not been released — add your guesses below). No polling favored it. No fashion for being like Saudi Arabia was afloat. Outside of Supreme Court Justices, a return to the 18th century is generally not in vogue. So why do it? I can guess at a few contributing factors.


They can probably do it. They can’t take over countries. They can’t steal Iran’s oil. They can’t make Greenland a state. They can’t end or make anyone like their wars in Palestine or Ukraine. They can’t own Cuba. They can’t make actual humans with brains believe in the Golden Dome. They can’t stop soldiers from jumping off their ships or murdering girls near bases in Asia. The only things less popular than data centers, ICE thugs, or new nuclear waste sites, are their endless pointless wars. Trump wants to build an arch for a conquering Roman emperor because he renamed a lake or something, but he can’t even do that. This they can do. They can shoot a man with a bunch of guns and watch him die. They can declare victory. They can scream USA USA Number One Number One and justify it with having actually done a thing.


 


There was only a small step left. The murders of fishermen on boats are posted on social media. The genocide in Gaza is livestreamed. Mass shootings of the sort that this murder-spectacle claims to be addressing (themselves very disproportionately generated by the

U.S. military

) receive massive wall-to-wall media coverage beginning moments after they happen. Movies and television shows, which many often struggle to fully distinguish from reality, are saturated with murder, as well as with the glorification of revenge. Viewers have been extensively trained to cheer for good, noble, revenge murders, and to engage in them themselves in video games. In a culture (yes, they have existed) from which an individual could be traumatized by a single clip of a Hollywood movie murder, a public murder spectacle would be a catastrophe of world-shattering proportions. In a society whose largest investment is in an institution called the War Department, this step by that department is much smaller.


 


In their tiny little minds they consider this a war against an enemy, and an enemy of the very worst sort — a traitor. In a war, you kill people. You don’t kill certain people in proper ways under certain peculiar circumstances. You kill people. One member of the U.S. military recently felt compelled to confess that he had committed murder in Afghanistan. Don’t worry about it,

the Army told him

, that was the job. So they’re simply going to kill one more person.


 


Re-enactment magic is powerful voodoo for people who believe silly things like the return of Jesus as Trump or the healing powers of Robert Kennedy Jr. In England a few centuries back, people were sometimes punished at the scene of their alleged crime in the manner of their alleged crime. This set the universe aright, although any records of the universe — as opposed to some creepy sadist in a wig — voicing that opinion have been lost to time.


 


The era that Trump fans most often refer to as the time referenced in the final A of MAGA (the Great time to get back to) was an era of public lynchings. While they were not livestreamed, they were spectacles evolved from public punishments in Europe, and used to send a message to a certain group of people in the United States who needed to learn their place, as well as to train children and the public at large in the proper treatment of lesser creatures — as well as to fulfill a cycle of violence that included in most cases the violent childrearing of those doing the lynching. The Secretary of War has chosen for his victim someone who can be used to represent a religion and various cultures he despises and encourages others to.


 


A video death penalty is a Hail Mary thrown at the wish, not just of high ratings, but also of raising U.S. children in vicious violence today. It engages in the usual hypocrisy of failing miserably at discouraging murder by engaging in and celebrating murder — not just doing it with at least pretended shame, but doing it with pride. That teaches not just murder but all lesser forms of violence as well.
