author: Documentary Channel
title: Put Your Soul On Your Hand And Walk (2025)
content: Over fragile video calls, Palestinian photojournalist Fatma Hassona shares her life in Gaza with Iranian director Sepideh Farsi. They speak about religion, politics, and surviving under the ongoing violence of Israeli bombardments. A friendship grows between the women, each call a precious sign of life. Since October 7, 2023, at least 211 media workers have been killed in Gaza. Shortly before the premiere of this film, Fatma Hassona and her family are also killed in an Israeli airstrike. What remains is a testament to her resilience, her radiance, and her indispensable work in making Gaza's reality visible.

author: Darío Aranda
title: 12 de octubre: autonomías indígenas y crisis de la modernidad colonial
content:
Por Roberto Espinoza para

Debates Indígenas


Las autonomías, autogobiernos y autodeterminaciones pueden ser amazónicas, andinas, de páramos o de costas marinas. Pero en su mayoría son rurales. Eso conlleva la imagen de ser como islas que navegan en mares gigantescos de colonialidad del poder, del saber y del ser. Los peligros de naufragio aparecen cuando añadimos las intensas tormentas globales y nacionales de violencia racista y extractivista de la modernidad colonial, que fueron ocultadas por un tiempo, detrás de la aparente “democracia liberal”, y que hoy profundiza el abierto despojo territorial y arrinconamiento de derechos.


La modernidad colonial engendró y multiplicó dos grandes monstruos globales que hoy enfrentamos: la crisis climática y el autoritarismo racista

. Ambos golpean de manera particular a los pueblos originarios y a los movimientos sociales, porque afectan sus territorios, formas de vida y derechos, pero también porque encuentran en ellos

sociedades en movimiento, capaces de construir resistencias frente a estas amenazas

. La expansión de las actividades extractivas y las nuevas formas de autoritarismo no son fenómenos aislados: profundizan las condiciones de despojo y desigualdad que históricamente han afectado a estos pueblos.


Las autonomías rurales, urbanas, originarias o sociales pueden nacer y proclamarse formalmente después de una asamblea, un congreso o algún otro evento colectivo. Sin embargo, su origen suele ser mucho más profundo y preceder largamente a ese momento de proclamación. Sus motores suelen encontrarse en conflictos y luchas de gran envergadura por la defensa de los derechos, los territorios, los bienes comunes y las formas propias de vida.


En ese sentido, la autonomía no comienza con una declaración: se va construyendo en la organización cotidiana, en la capacidad de tomar decisiones colectivas y en la experiencia acumulada de enfrentar amenazas y defender derechos.


Foto: Yaymy Mamani Ccallaccassi


Motivaciones de las autonomías


La construcción de la legitimidad propia de las autonomías, en base a la paciente unificación de la heterogeneidad de organizaciones del mismo pueblo, es lo que otorga solidez y raíces estables al proceso.

El reconocimiento legal del Estado no deja de ser importante y es un derecho a arrancar, pero no es lo prioritario

 y va en segundo lugar. Desde esta perspectiva, primero es necesaria la autonomía de hecho y esto da curso a que más tarde se convierta en una autonomía de derecho. Así, nos basamos en el principio de realidad, antes de lo formal y burocrático.


El territorio es un eje central de las autonomías: es tanto el espacio físico como un sistema integral que articula vida, hábitat, cultura, espiritualidad, colectividad, sostenibilidad de los comunes, de los bienes comunes y de usos comunes que los “comunalizan” con marchas y contramarchas.


Implica pactos sociales u horizontes que cristalizan procesos y liderazgos, como cuidado profundo de las bondades de la naturaleza (madre tierra o

yakumama

) o hábitat urbano bio cultural.

El territorio no se limita a una mercancía o lucro del poder

: es un requisito para vivir en paz, mantener la armonía y alcanzar el buen vivir o vida plena.


El relevo intergeneracional exige que las juventudes conozcan y mantengan viva la memoria colectiva, fortalezcan sus vínculos con los procesos de resistencia y contribuyan a recrear nuevos espacios de autodeterminación.


Las autonomías necesitan tener sentido y ser necesarias para sus poblaciones, no solo en su dimensión política, histórica, filosófica o ideológica, sino también para garantizar una mejor calidad de vida integral, en lo cotidiano, personal, familiar y colectivo. Esto es esencial para la permanencia y la unidad de las autonomías, especialmente para manejar las divergencias, evitar la polarización y la fragmentación, que suelen estar conectadas con las disputas por espacios electorales o de poder en el Estado (dos peligros latentes que cercan y fracturan las autonomías sociales).


También

son fundamentales las resistencias históricas en defensa del territorio

 (en sus dimensiones material, cultural y espiritual) y la participación de las mujeres, con su fuerza y sus propuestas en la acción organizada. Cada generación enfrenta

el desafío de sostener la defensa autonómica sin subordinarse al Estado

.

author: Brad Reed
title: Alleged Murder by US Marine Sparks Outrage at Military Presence in Okinawa
content:
The Okinawa Council voted nearly unanimously to call for a review of its US military agreement.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

The Okinawa Prefectural Assembly on Friday adopted a resolution calling for a formal review of its Status of Forces agreement with the US military amid outrage over the alleged murder of local woman by an American Marine.

As reported by Kyodo News, the assembly passed the resolution by an overwhelming margin, with 45 members in favor and just two opposed.

According to Kyodo News, the two opponents of the resolution said that it didn’t go far enough and demanded language calling for the dismissal of the head of the US military in Okinawa.

The Status of Forces agreement, established in 1960, has been criticized for being too preferential to US service members, who are seen as being totally outside the reach of Japan’s domestic law enforcement.

Kyodo News noted that the Okinawa assembly “passed a similar protest resolution and opinion statement in 2024 when a series of sexual assaults by US servicemen in Okinawa came to light.”

Ryotaro Odo, leader of the assembly’s special committee on US military bases, said the resolution was necessary because “we are seeing the limitations of the US military’s training program and ability to maintain discipline, and have to say that it is not functioning as an organization.”

The resolution will now be delivered to the US embassy in Japan.

Authorities on Sunday arrested 20-year-old US Lance Cpl. Devin Jacob Ballard on suspicion of murdering 39-year-old Anna Yagi, whom Okinawa police say died from asphyxiation caused by pressure to her neck. In addition to facing murder accusations, Ballard also faces charges that he stole Yagi’s wallet and backpack.

The US Marine has denied all allegations.

The alleged murder sparked angry protests and led right-wing Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, who supports US military presence in Japan, to condemn what she called a “heinous crime” in a speech delivered in Japan’s parliament.

“The Japanese government has lodged a strong protest with the US side,” said Takaichi, “and has strongly demanded full cooperation with the investigation, as well as strict disciplinary action against US military personnel and thorough measures to prevent a recurrence of such incidents.”

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Trump Openly Incites Race War, Calling for “Fight” Against Somalis in Minnesota
content:
The president suggested that he would send federal agents to aid with attacks on the Somali community.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

President Donald Trump encouraged people in Minnesota to “fight” against Somali immigrants in the state on Thursday, openly inciting race war in some of his most violent rhetoric against Somalis yet.

In a post on Truth Social, Trump said that Somali immigrants are “tak[ing] over” Minnesota, invoking white supremacist rhetoric and calling on others in the state to “fight back.”

“The once Great State of Minnesota is being taken over by Somali Immigrants. There is Violence, Murder, and Mayhem all over the State. The people of Minnesota must fight back,” Trump wrote.

He attacked the state’s Democratic leaders, labeling Gov. Tim Walz as a “thief” before repeating his call for violence. The president also suggested that he would send federal agents to aid with attacks on the Somali community.

“The Somalians[sic] should not be allowed to get away with what they are doing. They view you as weak and stupid people. Fight back Minnesota, fight back!” Trump said. “If you need, the Federal Government will come to your rescue.”

The post was met with horror, with many noting that it is one of the most horrific and dangerous remarks Trump has ever made.

“President Trump is placing a target on the backs of Somali Americans. His words are not simply political rhetoric. They are a dangerous invitation to hatred and potentially violence,” said Jaylani Hussein, executive director for the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR)’s Minnesota chapter. “Minnesota has led the nation in attacks on mosques, including fire-bombings. We know firsthand what happens when hateful rhetoric turns into violence.”

Somalis in the state have already been expressing alarm over Trump’s escalating rhetoric and racist crackdowns against their community, saying that it has created an atmosphere of fear. As Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents targeted Somalis with violent raids last year, Trump repeatedly called Somalis “garbage.”

He has also targeted Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minnesota), who is Somali, with similar attacks. Earlier this year, he attacked her and Somalis at one of his rallies just hours before Omar was attacked with vinegar at a town hall by an assailant who expressed support for Trump in social media posts.

“Every Somali I know is walking through our own neighborhoods scared tonight. This is incitement, and everyone should call it that,” said Faisa Ahmed, director of public relations group Arc Initiatives and former deputy campaign manager for the 2024 Harris-Walz campaign.

The Trump administration has also sought to end temporary protected status for immigrants from Somalia, putting thousands of Somalis in the U.S. at risk of enforcement actions by the Trump administration’s expansive anti-immigration apparatus.

Minnesota state leaders also condemned Trump’s remarks.

“We’ve seen what Trump’s government coming to the ‘rescue’ looks like. It ended with two Minnesotans shot dead by federal agents, racial profiling, assaults, and the violation of our rights. Never again,” said Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison in a post on social media. Ellison said that he would “drag [Trump] back to court” if he sent federal agents to Minnesota again.

“Somali Minnesotans are our neighbors. They are part of Minnesota. And the Minnesota I know and love is so much better than this bigotry,” Ellison said.

author: Ohood Nassar
title: Destruction of Archives and Property Records Lays Ground for Land Theft in Gaza
content:
Families in Gaza fear they may lose their property rights as deeds get destroyed and buried under the rubble.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Inside a rented house in the Saraya area, west of Gaza City, 50-year-old Rami Karaja sat talking about a home he can no longer reach and documents he can no longer retrieve.

At the end of April 2025, Karaja’s home in the Shuja’iyya neighborhood was bombed. Among the many things his family lost are the property deeds to the house, which are still buried beneath the rubble.

“I cannot return to my home to retrieve the documents because the house is in an area under Israeli control,” Karaja said. “The papers proving my ownership remain beneath the rubble of the destroyed house.”

Amid widespread destruction of housing across Gaza, Karaja is not alone. According to a UN report released in February 2026, at least 92 percent of housing units in Gaza were estimated to have been destroyed or damaged between October 2023 and October 2025, while more than 90 percent of the population was displaced during the same period.

“I don’t know when I will be able to return, what the place will look like when I do, or how I will prove my ownership if I begin rebuilding my home,” Karaja said.

Karaja fears that determining the boundaries of his home and land will be difficult after both the loss of his documents and so much destruction to the property.

“If the Israeli forces leave Shuja’iyya and I return to my home and begin rebuilding, I will face a problem because I no longer have the property documents with me,” he said.

He says the destruction of so many homes has made it more difficult to determine land boundaries, and he fears this could eventually lead to disputes between families.

But his concerns go beyond the documents themselves.

Karaja’s home is located in a so-called “red zone,” which Palestinians cannot freely access. As Israel deepens and expands its control over these parts of Gaza, Palestinians like Karaja continue to be denied access to their land.

For families who have lost both their homes and property documents, the fear is not simply about losing a piece of paper. It is about losing the ability to establish a legal connection to their land at a time when they cannot even reach it.

These fears have grown as Israel has expanded the areas under its control and deepened restrictions on movement and access within Gaza.

Karaja worries that that temporary military control could become a long-term reality.

“What frightens me most is that my home could be turned into an Israeli settlement,” he said.

A 2026 Gaza Strip Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment, prepared by the World Bank, the United Nations, and the European Union, found that the destruction of land administration offices caused significant damage to property records, digital files, and surveying archives. It estimated that around 80 percent of the markers defining the boundaries of 218,000 properties had been destroyed, making it more difficult to re-establish property boundaries and verify ownership.

The assessment also found that by mid-2025, more than 65 percent of property owners had lost their ownership documents.

The assessment warned that the combination of lost official records and personal documents, together with restrictions on access to land, had significantly increased uncertainty over property rights and could complicate the return of residents and the reconstruction of homes and agricultural land.

For Karaja, then, it is not only about one house.

“I fear what could happen when the physical evidence of ownership disappears at the same time as I am prevented from accessing my land,” he said.

The widespread destruction in Gaza extends beyond the walls and roofs of people’s homes. Institutions and archives that preserve the records of the city and the memory of its residents have also suffered severe damage.

The Central Archives of Gaza City were destroyed during the war. According to a PEN America report, the archives contained around 110,000 historical documents, including maps, contracts, land ownership documents, photographs, and other materials. The report quotes Gaza City Mayor Yahya al-Sarraj: “The Central Archives building was directly hit, causing the burning of historically significant documents dating back over 150 years.”

But documents are not lost only inside …

author: Sophia Sheera
title: Lawyer Who Found Israel Is Committing Genocide Wins Nobel Peace Prize
content:
The Nobel Peace Prize has been awarded to a former UN human rights chief who led the commission that found Israel is committing genocide in Gaza. 


Navi Pillay, who was born in South Africa under apartheid, won the 2026 award in recognition of a long career defending human rights, the Nobel committee said. 


That includes her work defending Nelson Mandela and chairing the 2025 UN commission of inquiry on the occupied Palestinian territory. 


“In historic international court cases, she has shown that legal measures can help prevent acts of war and violence,” the committee said. “Her independence, expertise and steadfastness have made her one of the most respected international jurists of our time.”


The committee said it had been unable to contact Pillay, who serves as a judge at the UN’s international court of justice, before announcing her win on Friday morning. 


When colleagues at the Nuremberg Forum told the 85-year-old the news, Pillay joked: “Is it true? Being a lawyer and a judge, I still want to verify it.”


She also joked: “If you clap a little bit more, I may share this prize with Trump,” a reference to the fact last year’s winner, María Corina Machado, gave her winner’s medal to the US president. 


The Israeli foreign ministry said the choice to award the Nobel to Pillay was “a grotesque weaponisation of an award to legitimise anti-Israel hatred and prejudice”.


The 2025 UN inquiry found statements by Israeli leaders Benjamin Netanyahu, Yoav Gallant and Isaac Herzog sufficient to establish genocidal intent. The report recommended that the international criminal court consider amending arrest warrants for Israeli officials to include genocide charges.

author: Hayley Tsukayama
title: Organizing in the Town at Oakland Tech Week
content:
EFF was thrilled to join organizers, advocates, and activists in the East Bay for the second annual

Oakland Tech Week

 last week. We are grateful to our friends at

MediaJustice

 and

Upturn

 for inviting us co-present this all-day event,

“Building Beyond Big Tech: Organizing Oakland’s Future”

, on Sept. 30.  The event, hosted by the

Kapor Center

 in downtown Oakland, offered a unique chance to spend time with people across The Town and the Bay Area working to create a better future for everyone.


“We’re at this truly consequential moment,” said EFF executive director Nicole Ozer, in her speech kicking off the day’s events. “We know that in this community’s work—and communities across the country—our ability to

ensure that technology empowers

 rather than

oppresses

 is fundamental to the future of countries, our livelihoods, and, literally, our lives.”


We also participated in a panel on the state of play in California, moderated by MediaJustice executive director Steven Renderos. Director of State Affairs Hayley Tsukayama joined reporter Khari Johnson of CalMatters and Crystal Zemero of People Over Billionaires to talk about the landscape at the state level. The day also included smaller conversations focused on building better tech and fine-tuning messaging, facilitated by our colleagues at MediaJustice.


Seeing the people—our neighbors—who are fighting back against surveillance in their communities was inspiring. They’re casting doubt on the claims large technology companies make about what’s happening in their neighborhoods. They’re speaking up at council meetings and rallies. They’re seeking changes that would give their workplaces and neighborhoods a better, safer relationship with technology. It was so important to come together in solidarity to compare notes, spend time together, find opportunities to support each other, and scheme together.


We can work together to build a future that

works for everyday people

. A better world is possible—and Oakland Tech Week was a great reminder that, all around us, folks are working together to tackle huge challenges.


“There are formidable forces,” Ozer said.  “But we can pierce the other side’s narrative of inevitability with our power of indignation. The future of AI and other technology is not written and we can work together to get it right.”


Whether you’re in Oakland or Aukland, consider this a

renewed invitation to join us

.

author: Oyugi Abednego Ochillo
title: How Zambia Defeated an Election Petition Without Ever Arguing the Case
content:
Zambia’s 13 August general election was already fraught before anyone tried to challenge its result, according to an account human rights lawyer Linda Kasonde has since

published on her Substack

. The

army had been deployed to polling stations

, she writes, a role outside its constitutional mandate. The Electoral Commission suspended vote tallying for six hours over reports of attacks on polling agents, during which only police and soldiers had access to the ballots. Opposition candidate Brian Mundubile’s home was raided and

eleven of his associates were abducted

. Former Cabinet Minister

Mutotwe Kafwaya was fatally shot

 in the same raid. Authorities denied the killing for five days, until a habeas corpus application forced them to confirm it. Hakainde Hichilema was declared the winner on 18 August with around 61 percent against Mundubile’s 38 percent, though the

Christian Churches Monitoring Group’s own assessment

 of its parallel vote tabulation had projected a closer 56 percent.


It is against that backdrop that Linda Kasonde decided to petition the result. Kasonde is a human rights lawyer and former president of the Law Association of Zambia. She petitioned under Article 103(1)(b) of the Constitution, which allows any citizen to challenge an election on the ground that it was not free and fair. She had seven days from the declaration to file, under Article 101(4). She did not get seven days. On 24 August, a day before her deadline, the government shut down the courts. The closures covered the Constitutional Court, the Supreme Court, the High Court in Lusaka, and premises in Ndola, Chipata and Livingstone. The stated reason was unspecified security concerns. Police later

described the closures

as nationwide security risk assessments at government premises, without saying what threat had prompted them. The closure lasted until 27 August. In an essay she has since

published on her Substack

, Kasonde describes what she did next.


In her account, she writes that she had tried to file electronically before, under new e-filing rules introduced in May 2026, and had been told the rules were not yet operational. With the courthouses sealed, she tried again anyway, emailing her petition to the Chief Registrar’s official address. The judiciary’s website, she says she was told, had been disabled. So she sent the documents to Chief Justice Mumba Malila’s personal email instead, explaining that the shutdown had left her no other option. A day later, Kasonde recounts, the judiciary’s public relations office confirmed receipt, and the Chief Justice himself said that while the method was “highly irregular,” he would forward the documents to the Constitutional Court. Kasonde describes the relief as short-lived. A separate statement soon followed from the Chief Administrator, asserting that no petition had been received by the deadline. The Secretary to the Cabinet then announced that Hichilema’s inauguration would proceed on 1 September, citing that same claim.


Zambia Supreme Court Building in Lusaka.


This is worth pausing on, because it is not the same story as an election being rigged. The government never had to win an argument about the vote count. It only had to keep the question of whether a petition existed unresolved for as long as the Constitution’s window allowed. It then declared that no petition existed, even though its own Chief Justice had said otherwise days earlier.

Human Rights Watch called

 the closures a direct denial of access to justice. Zambia’s

Chapter One Foundation has since petitioned

 the Constitutional Court to declare the shutdown itself unlawful, a case the judiciary has yet to determine.


That distinction matters more than it might look. An election stolen at the ballot box is a familiar kind of theft, and African courts, however imperfectly, have a template for adjudicating it. They recount the votes, examine the forms and hear the witnesses. An election defended by making it unclear whether a challenge was ever properly lodged is a different kind of theft. It does not ask a judge to rule wrongly. It asks nobody to rule at all, for as long as possible, and then lets one government spokesperson’s account overwrite another’s. Zambia’s Constitution gives a losing candidate, or any citizen under the 2016 reforms that opened standing to the public, seven days to file a petition, full stop. That looks like a strength on the page. There is no room for endless litigation, and an …

author: Faisal Ali
title: How Middle Eastern powers are reshaping Somalia’s political order
content:
Flights into Mogadishu, Somalia’s capital, trace the coastline on their descent to Aden Adde International Airport, which sits beside the Indian Ocean.


In June, when Somaliland’s president, Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi, stood alongside Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu, the latter drew attention to the geography connecting them. Israel and Somaliland, Netanyahu said, sit at opposite ends of the Red Sea but share an interest in confronting “

extremism, terrorism and chaos

”.


By recognising Somaliland in late 2025, Israel became the latest Middle Eastern power to establish a significant relationship with one of Somalia’s several political centres. Somaliland declared independence in 1991 but remains unrecognised by any other state. For Israel, the relationship offers a partner on the Gulf of Aden, close to Yemen and the shipping lanes where it has confronted the Houthis. For Somaliland, it delivered something decades of engagement with other foreign partners had not: formal recognition.


Israel’s arrival comes amid a much wider expansion of Middle Eastern engagement across the Horn of Africa. Gulf states and Turkey have committed an

estimated

 $75 billion to projects across East Africa in recent years, according to the Africa Center for Strategic Studies, with the UAE alone accounting for roughly 60 per cent of the total.


The UAE has spent more than a decade cultivating commercial and security ties with Somaliland, Puntland and Jubaland, while Turkey has built its deepest relationships through Mogadishu. Egypt and Saudi Arabia have also strengthened federal ties as disputes over Ethiopia, Israel and Red Sea security intensify.


Middle Eastern money, arms and infrastructure therefore increasingly shape the resources available to different political centres, strengthening some administrations’ ability to raise revenue, secure territory, build institutions and withstand pressure from rivals. Red Sea powers have treated the Horn as part of their strategic neighbourhood for decades, but the scale of involvement expanded sharply from the 2010s.


Western governments initially saw much of this as an advantage. Judd Devermont, who served as President Joe Biden’s senior Africa official on the National Security Council, described cooperation with Middle Eastern partners as appearing to offer Washington a “

cheat code

”: additional capital, security resources and political credibility at a time when US attention was limited.


What has changed more recently is the political terrain through which those relationships operate. Formal sovereignty

remains centred

 in Mogadishu, but practical authority is distributed among several competing centres with sharply different capacities to raise revenue, provide security and negotiate with external actors.


These centres are underpinned by clan coalitions whose control of ports, customs posts, territory and security forces helps determine the reach of their authority; foreign support can strengthen those coalitions and alter the balance between them. Somali political actors are therefore also enlisting outside powers into contests and state-building projects already under way. Some centres, like Puntland and Jubaland, sustain foreign relationships with little practical involvement from the federal government.


Mogadishu nevertheless commands a distinct set of assets. It holds Somalia’s sovereign powers — including the ability to

sign and cancel international agreements

, control airspace and act as the principal conduit for diplomatic recognition and external assistance — while regional authorities may control ports, customs revenues, security forces and commercial flows on the ground.


Somali governments have

historically struggled

 to collect broad-based taxes, giving customs posts and maritime gateways an outsized role in financing the state. The federal government, for example,

collects domestic revenue equivalent

 to only about 3% of GDP, among the lowest levels in Africa. Puntland’s Bosaso, Jubaland’s Kismayo and Somaliland’s Berbera are therefore crucial revenue generators for their respective administrations.


A recurring theme in interviews with officials across Somalia’s regional administrations was that they viewed foreign engagement as a negotiated exchange, not something simply imposed on them. Foreign governments provide finance, weapons, training, infrastructure or diplomatic support; Somali authorities offer strategically located territory …

author: Chris Walker
title: Mike Johnson Suggests He’ll Quit Congress If Voters Reject GOP in Midterms
content:
The latest polls show Democrats outperforming Republicans in the midterms by around eight points.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

In a Fox News interview that aired earlier this week, Speaker of the House Mike Johnson (R-Louisiana) indicated that he might retire from the House of Representatives altogether if Republicans failed to retain control of Congress following this year’s midterm elections.

The statement is a stark departure from his previous comments this year, in which the speaker indicated little possibility of the GOP failing to defeat Democrats in this fall’s contests.

“Heaven forbid, if we lose this majority or whatever, I don’t know what my next chapter of life is,” Johnson said, adding:

If God moves on our hearts and says we should, you know, go back to my hometown of Shreveport and start a lawn business, I’ll do that with equal fervor.

In the same interview, Johnson indicated that he wouldn’t take any responsibility for his party losing to Democrats. Instead, he said he’d blame messaging issues or the media for giving voters the wrong idea about what both parties stood for.

“If we lose the House, it will be because the people were misled,” Johnson said.

Johnson’s remarks disregard issues like affordability, the war on Iran, Trump’s abuse of presidential powers, and the GOP’s support for the unfettered construction of AI data centers — all issues that are on voters’ minds this election season that Republicans have failed to adequately address.

Earlier this year, Johnson indicated that he saw no way for Republicans to lose the midterms, justifying his confidence by citing his religious beliefs.

“We’re gonna win the midterms,” Johnson said in a podcast interview this summer to a Christian nationalist host. “I’m very bullish about the outcome. We talk about it all the time, and with each passing day, I’m more confident.”

“This is a God thing,” Johnson said, claiming that the “power of prayer” would help Republicans prevail.

The American public will likely not miss Johnson very much, if he is indeed ousted from the speakership and chooses to retire. According to an Economist/YouGov poll from last month, Johnson’s favorability rating is a net -15 points.

The latest polls on congressional elections indicate that voters want a change in Washington. According to an average of polling data compiled by FiftyPlusOne, Democrats are currently favored to win the midterms, with 51.1 percent of voters backing that party’s nominee in a generic ballot question, versus just 43.4 percent supporting Republicans, as of Friday morning.

author: Unknown
title: MP Öznur Bartın: Kurds are key actors in Turkey’s democratic future
content:
As parliament begins its new legislative term, the Peace and Democratic Society Process has also entered a new political phase. The role parliament will assume in the next stage of the process, the political will demonstrated by parties and society’s participation in the process of democratic resolution are coming to the fore.


ANF spoke to Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) MP for Hakkari (Colemerg) Öznur Bartın about expectations for a democratic solution to the Kurdish question, the scope of the framework law and the steps that need to be taken.


Bartın stressed that disarmament should be regarded as the beginning of democratic transformation and underlined the importance of securing constitutional and legal guarantees for the language, identity, culture and political rights of the Kurdish people.


‘Disarmament is not the end of the process, but the beginning of democratic transformation’


Bartın said the points on which different political parties have been able to find common ground in parliament during the Peace and Democratic Society Process are important, stressing that the process must move beyond disarmament.


Bartın said a new phase had begun after nearly 50 years of armed struggle: “The main issue here is that nearly 50 years of armed struggle should not be addressed solely in terms of laying down arms. We now need to move from the abandonment of armed struggle to the question of democratic transformation. Mr. Abdullah Öcalan’s call on 27 February marked the beginning of a new phase. That call was a historic turning point, indicating that arms had fulfilled their mission and that the struggle needed to continue on a different basis.


The Kurdish movement has also fulfilled its responsibilities. The decision taken by the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK), its expression of the will to voluntarily dissolve itself, the symbolic steps taken and their public announcement were important in this respect.


Democratic transformation cannot, of course, develop under the shadow of arms. However, it would be wrong to regard disarmament as the point at which the entire issue has been resolved. This is because we are dealing with a historical question shaped by a century of policies of denial, annihilation and assimilation.


We cannot regard disarmament as the end of this struggle. It must be seen as a new beginning that will pave the way for democratic politics and a democratic society. Once arms are removed from the equation, the real questions that need to be discussed are what kind of democratic political order will be established and what legal and social guarantees will underpin this transformation.


The fact that these issues can now be discussed in parliament and that the framework law has been passed is also an important step. This has created hope in society. Of course, there are many aspects of the law that are being debated and considered inadequate. However, the fact that democratic transformation, negotiation and dialogue are now being discussed in parliament, within a system that previously relied on policies of denial, annihilation and massacres, did not come about on its own. Enormous sacrifices have been made to reach this point.”


‘The ground established in parliament is important, but not enough on its own’


Öznur Bartın said the ground established in parliament is important for creating the legal framework of the process, but stressed that the state's practices in the field of law must also change if legal regulations are to build lasting trust.


Bartın said the process could not be completed simply by passing a law and continued: “We all know very well that parliament alone is not enough. Discussing this issue in parliament, establishing a legal framework and creating legal guarantees are, of course, important safeguards. However, for these guarantees to have meaning in society, there must also be consistency between the law and its implementation.


Today, we are talking about a situation in which rulings by the Constitutional Court and the European Court of Human Rights (ECHR) are not implemented, and Turkey's commitment to international conventions to which it is a party has weakened. As long as a security-oriented approach based on violence remains evident in the field of human rights, the mere passage of a law is not enough to eliminate all concerns in society. How a legal regulation is implemented is just as important as the regulation itself.

title: HPG and YJA Star guerrillas: The international conspiracy was foiled through struggle
content:
Today marks the 28th anniversary of the beginning of the international conspiracy against Abdullah Öcalan. The process referred to as the international conspiracy, in which numerous nation-states were involved, began on October 9, 1998, when Öcalan was forced to leave Syria amid intense political and military pressure on the country. This was followed by a months-long odyssey through various countries, ending on February 15, 1999, with his abduction from the Kenyan capital Nairobi to Turkey. The Kurdish leader has been held on the prison island of Imrali ever since.


On the anniversary of the international conspiracy, guerrillas of the HPG (People’s Defense Forces) and YJA Star (Free Women’s Troops) spoke to ANF and expressed their views.


Democratic modernity against capitalist modernity


HPG guerrilla Botan Mêrdîn said: “The October 9 conspiracy began when Rêber Apo [Leader Abdullah Öcalan] was forced to leave Syria, through the cooperation of intelligence agencies led by the United States and Israel and certain Kurdish Judenrats. This was followed by the Leader’s journey to Greece, his departure from Greece for Russia, then his journey to Rome, his return to Russia, and ultimately a four-month process that ended with his captivity. From October 9, 1998, to February 15, 1999, there was a process in which the forces involved sought to carry out a conspiracy against the Leader and the Kurdish people. Rêber Apo states that the Third World War began with this plot. The aim of the forces behind the conspiracy was to intervene in the Middle East. In order to carry out this intervention, they regarded the presence of organized peoples in the region as an obstacle.”


The guerrilla fighter continued: “They saw the Leader as an obstacle to their interests and to the interventions they wanted to carry out across the entire region. They regarded Rêber Apo’s paradigm, which represents an alternative to capitalist modernity, as a major obstacle. That is why they carried out the plot, which resulted in Rêber Apo’s captivity. To this day, attempts are being made to continue the conspiracy through different methods and means. Although its methods and approaches have changed, the attempt to perpetuate it continues. However, through his stance on Imrali, the Leader thwarted these efforts. During the period of his captivity, the people and the guerrillas formed a ring of fire around the Leader under the slogan ‘You Cannot Darken Our Sun.’ The paradigm developed by Rêber Apo on Imrali defeated the forces behind the conspiracy and rendered the conspiracy they had devised ineffective.”


Botan Mêrdîn added: “In order to thwart and defeat this conspiracy and overcome the forces behind it, we as HPG guerrillas will continue our struggle on the basis of the Rêber Apo’s paradigm until he gains his physical freedom.”


 


They wanted to destroy the Freedom Movement and the Women’s Movement


YJA Star guerrilla Dicle Serbilind made the following assessment of the October 9 plot: “As fighters of the Leader, although it is difficult and painful for us in particular to assess and define October 9, we know that through the assassination attempts against the Leader in Damascus in 1998, they sought to destroy the Freedom Movement through the person of the Leader and to eliminate the Women’s Movement. But as Rêber Apo’s fighters, we will thwart this conspiracy through the stance and will that he has instilled in us. With Rêber Apo’s ideas and philosophy, we will not allow such plots to be carried out again against either Rêber Apo or the Kurdish Freedom Movement. To this day, the struggle waged by Rêber Apo has produced many heroes. It has produced many pioneering women of resistance. And day by day, this struggle is growing and finding its meaning. It is becoming the bearer of a great history. Following in its footsteps, thousands of women and men fighters are walking in the footsteps of Egîd, Zîlan and Beritan.”


Dicle Serbilind continued: “As women guerrillas, both our objective and our struggle for freedom are aimed at securing Rêber Apo’s physical freedom. For years, we have lived with the longing to see the Leader. For this reason, we pledge to continue our struggle until we see Rêber Apo achieve his physical freedom.”


The conspiracy was directed against the entire Kurdish people

title: KCK calls for the struggle for Öcalan’s freedom to be intensified in the 29th year of the conspiracy
content:
On the 28th anniversary of the beginning of the international conspiracy against Abdullah Öcalan, the Kurdistan Communities Union (KCK) commemorated the resistance against his abduction and imprisonment and called for the struggle for his freedom to be intensified. In a statement on the occasion, the Co-Presidency of the KCK Executive Council condemned the political forces involved in the international operation and paid tribute to those who lost their lives during protests under the slogan “You Cannot Darken Our Sun.” The KCK described Öcalan’s political and ideological work as a decisive factor in the development of the Kurdish freedom movement and views his freedom as a prerequisite for the success of the peace and a democratic society process.


The KCK statement on Friday reads as follows:


“We condemn in the strongest terms all political forces involved in the international conspiracy against Rêber Apo [Leader Abdullah Öcalan]. With gratitude and respect, we commemorate the martyrs of the ‘You Cannot Darken Our Sun’ resistance, who erected a barricade of fire against the conspiracy.


The international conspirators sought to eliminate Rêber Apo, who aimed to change the fate of the Middle East, whose peoples have endured a difficult fate for centuries. Rêber Apo pursued a policy aimed at resolving the Kurdish question—which had become an inextricable knot and a shackle for the states of the Middle East—on a democratic basis and in the spirit of fraternity among peoples.


This struggle led to significant developments in the states that hold Kurdistan under their rule. This alarmed the forces that had divided Kurdistan into four parts in order to maintain their dominance in the Middle East. The international powers saw the weakening of their allies by the Kurdish freedom movement led by Rêber Apo as a major threat to their hegemony and organized an unprecedented conspiracy.


An unrelenting struggle against the conspiracy


Through this conspiracy, they sought to break Rêber Apo’s influence either by physically eliminating him or by neutralizing him ideologically and politically. However, they encountered the determined resistance of our people, particularly through the actions carried out under the slogan ‘You Cannot Darken Our Sun.’ This marked the beginning of the failure of the international conspiracy.


After his physical elimination was prevented, Rêber Apo continued the struggle against the conspiracy on Imrali at the ideological and political level. Our freedom movement and our people rallied around their leader and rendered the conspiracy largely ineffective. Our movement further developed its struggle. Resistance in all four parts of Kurdistan turned the Kurds into a force that could no longer be denied. If they have today become a significant force in the Middle East, it is through the unrelenting struggle against the international conspiracy.


In his defense submission to the European Court of Human Rights, Rêber Apo stated during the early years of his imprisonment: ‘Historical conspiracies cannot stop developments; they only accelerate them.’ The development of our freedom struggle in all four parts of Kurdistan has confirmed this assessment.


Undoubtedly, Rêber Apo’s imprisonment continues. Yet he has achieved an immense ideological and theoretical development of a kind that no one in freedom has been able to accomplish, and has shown humanity the path to liberation. Through his defense writings and the Manifesto for a Democratic Society, he has dealt a fatal blow to the system of capitalist modernity, which is increasingly destroying society and humanity. The history of overcoming capitalism in human life will now be written. Democratic socialism, based on the paradigm of women’s liberation, ecology and democratic society, will bring this about.


The conspiracy was directed against all peoples of the Middle East


Rêber Apo’s Manifesto for a Democratic Society points the way not only for the Kurdish people but for all humanity in the struggle for a free and democratic life. A multifaceted question such as the Kurdish question, which has acquired an international dimension, can only be resolved through a far-reaching ideological and political perspective. The gravity of the problems facing Kurdistan and the Middle East has made Rêber Apo a leader for the liberation of all humanity. title: DEM Party and DBP condemn the international conspiracy, call for freedom for Öcalan
content:
Today marks the 28th anniversary of the beginning of the international conspiracy against Abdullah Öcalan on October 9, 1998. Forced to leave Syria amid intense political and military pressure on the country, the Kurdish leader went through a months-long odyssey through various countries before he was taken captive in the Kenyan capital Nairobi and handed over to Turkey on 15 February 1999. He has been incarcerated in İmralı Island Prison since and has not been seen his conditions improved despite the ongoing peace and democratic society process.


DBP:

Öcalan’s freedom is a historical necessity for a democratic and lasting peace


In a statement on the occasion, the Democratic Regions Party (DBP) said: “What was targeted in the person of Leader Öcalan was not only the existence of the Kurdish people and their struggle for freedom, but also the will of peoples to build an equal and free life and the democratic future of the Middle East. For this reason, October 9 must be regarded not merely as a conspiracy that took place in the past, but as an ongoing dimension of struggle whose political consequences and effects continue to this day.”


The statement continued: “The mentality that seeks to leave the Kurdish people without status for another century, neutralize Leader Öcalan’s will for a democratic solution and prevent a shared democratic future for the peoples continues to exist in different forms. In response, the Kurdish people have preserved their will for freedom, democracy and peace through the struggle they have waged against more than a century of policies of denial and annihilation. As a result of this struggle, they have today paved the way for the Peace and Democratic Society Process. Within this framework, the existence and identity of the Kurdish people must be constitutionally guaranteed, a democratic and legal solution to the Kurdish question must be secured, and conditions must be created in which Leader Öcalan can live and work freely. Because his freedom is not merely the freedom of one individual; it is one of the fundamental conditions for paving the way for a democratic solution, establishing a lasting and dignified peace, and enabling the peoples of Turkey to build an equal and free future together. For this reason, Leader Öcalan’s freedom is a historical necessity for creating all the conditions required for a democratic and lasting peace in Turkey!


Today, the task is not only that of the Kurdish people; it is to expand the common struggle of all peoples, social groups and democratic forces in Turkey that seek democracy, justice and peace. Because, the freedom of the Kurdish people cannot be separated from the freedom of the peoples of Turkey, just as a democratic solution to the Kurdish question cannot be separated from the democratization of Turkey. Expanding peace means strengthening the rule of law, justice, equality and democratic politics together. We advocate for Leader Öcalan, the architect of the Peace and Democratic Society Process and the person who continues to lead it despite severely restricted conditions, to be provided as soon as possible with conditions in which he can live and work freely. We remain determined to continue our struggle for a democratic and legal solution to the Kurdish question and for the construction of Turkey’s democratic future.”


Hatimoğulları: Öcalan must be allowed to work under conditions of freedom


The co-chairs of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party), Tülay Hatimoğulları and Tuncer Bakırhan, also issued statements marking the anniversary of the conspiracy.


Tülay Hatimoğulları stated: “The international conspiracy that began on October 9, 1998, sought to break the will of the Kurdish people through Mr. Abdullah Öcalan, fuel conflict among the peoples of Turkey and deepen chaos in the Middle East. This plan, which aimed to pit peoples against one another, was thwarted by Mr. Öcalan’s insistence on peace and a democratic solution even under the harshest conditions of isolation. The Peace and Democratic Society Process, which began with the historic February 27 call, has once again demonstrated the importance of Mr. Öcalan’s longstanding efforts for peace and his commitment to a democratic solution. It has created a significant opportunity for peoples to build an equal and free life together. For the Peace and Democratic Society Process to succeed, Mr. Öcalan must be allowed to work and communicate under conditions of freedom …

author: Unknown
title: Syriac homes in İdil demolished despite ongoing court proceedings
content:
The AKP-run municipal administration in the İdil district of Şırnak province is issuing demolition orders against homes and commercial premises belonging to members of the Syriac community. Four of the affected Syriac citizens have already initiated legal proceedings against the measures. Nevertheless, their buildings were demolished before the court could rule on their objections. Measures have also been taken against a guesthouse belonging to the Syriac Orthodox Church of the Virgin Mary. Those affected view the actions as an attempt to intimidate the Syriac community and weaken its ties to its homeland.


Demolitions despite legal objections


Lawyer Melke Karagöl, whose own family is affected by the demolition orders, criticized the municipal administration’s actions. The demolished buildings belonged to four Syriac residents and were between 20 and 25 years old. “Three days before the demolition, we filed an objection with the court. Before a decision had even been made, the houses were demolished,” Karagöl told MA. The court proceedings are still pending. However, the municipal administration created a fait accompli without waiting for the outcome.


In addition to the demolition orders, the municipal administration also sealed residential and commercial buildings belonging to Syriacs and imposed administrative fines. Karagöl is particularly critical of the measures taken against the guesthouse of the Syriac Orthodox Church of the Virgin Mary. The municipal administration has also approved its demolition. Karagöl views this as a deliberate policy targeting the Syriac community, a large proportion of whose members live in Europe. “They want Syriacs in Europe to completely lose their ties to this region. That is their goal,” the lawyer stated.


Those affected announced that they would continue to challenge the measures through legal and democratic means. “We do not accept practices aimed at pressuring and intimidating Syriac citizens. We will defend our rights through all legal and democratic means,” they stated.


DEM Party brings demolition measures before parliament


The developments have meanwhile also reached the Turkish parliament. DEM Party MPs Newroz Uysal Aslan, Mehmet Zeki Irmez, Ayşegül Doğan and George Aslan have submitted written parliamentary questions to the relevant ministries. They are seeking information on the legal basis for the sealing orders, fines and demolition orders targeting properties belonging to Syriacs. They also raised the actions of the AKP-run municipal administration, which had buildings demolished even though judicial review of the measures had not yet been completed.

title: Freedom for Öcalan Committee in Southern Kurdistan vows to continue its work without interruption
content:
The Committee for the Freedom of Abdullah Öcalan in Southern Kurdistan has called for intensified social and political efforts for the freedom of the Kurdish leader on the 28th anniversary of the international conspiracy of October 9, 1998.


In a written statement on Friday, the committee described the conspiracy as a systematic and ideological attack by hegemonic powers on the free will of society. It said the conspiracy was directed not only against a political organization, but against the vision of a democratic and self-determined society.


“As the creator of the philosophy of democratic society, Leader Öcalan, through his readings of historical truth and his dialectical insights into the crises of the contemporary world, has transformed the Imrali prison from a place of punishment into a center of thought and knowledge. The resistance of Leader Öcalan and the Freedom Movement has freed humanity from the violations of capitalist modernity and the tenets of the classical nation-state, advancing it toward a higher level of self-governance,” the statement said.


The Committee pointed out that Öcalan’s intellectual will could not be broken despite 27 years of isolation and psychological torture, while the ruling authorities have faced a multifaceted legal and moral collapse.


“As the Committee for the Freedom of Abdullah Öcalan in Southern Kurdistan, we declare on this occasion that we will continue without interruption our work and initiatives aimed at securing the physical freedom of this great thinker. We emphasize the need to thwart conspiracies and call on the Kurdish people and all those seeking freedom to unite their civil and intellectual efforts. A genuine solution is possible through the success of the peace process, the project of Democratic Confederalism and the establishment of a democratic republic. Leader Öcalan’s paradigm is a roadmap for the freedom of the Kurdish people and all peoples of the region,” the statement concluded.

title: Ayşegül Doğan calls for the peace process to be accelerated, says legal changes are needed
content:
The Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) spokesperson Ayşegül Doğan spoke about her party’s ongoing Central Executive Board (MYK) meeting in Ankara on Friday.


Speaking at a press conference at the party headquarters, Ayşegül Doğan addressed the issues on their agenda.


Doğan first referred to the 28th anniversary of the October 9 international conspiracy against Abdullah Öcalan. She said that the conspiracy was aimed particularly at pitting the Kurdish and Turkish peoples against each other, undermining domestic peace in Turkey and making peace in the Middle East impossible.


“In its 28th year, this conspiracy must come to an end, which will only be possible if we achieve lasting peace,” she underlined.


‘We are facing a systemic crisis’


Pointing to the financial scandal in the country, Ayşegül Doğan stated: “What Turkey is facing is a serious issue that requires scrutiny of public oversight and political accountability. There is an obvious systemic crisis, and the economic crisis is deepening. Hunger, poverty, unemployment and indebtedness have reached historically high levels in Turkey. On one side, there are families and children who cannot even afford a loaf of bread and are struggling for a loaf of bread and a glass of milk; on the other, there are those who continue to accumulate ever greater wealth—not simply because they are not questioned or subjected to scrutiny, but because the system itself operates this way. We will continue to pursue this issue so that the facts are brought to light. We will also continue our struggle on this matter. Although parliament has decided not to establish an inquiry commission on the issue, we will do everything we can to ensure that it is investigated and that parliament does not remain a mere spectator.”


‘The requirements of the joint report should be implemented’


Doğan called for the requirements of the joint report of the National Solidarity, Fraternity and Democracy Commission to be implemented, stating: “We would like to make a call to Speaker of Parliament Mr. Kurtulmuş: the work to establish the Monitoring Commission envisaged by law should be completed as soon as possible, using a method that will support and strengthen the process, ensure the representation of other political parties, and provide for inclusiveness and pluralism. Speaker of Parliament, Mr. Numan Kurtulmuş, should complete the necessary visits to meet with the political parties. Proposals should also be gathered during these meetings, and the procedures, principles and working guidelines should be determined. At the same time, the methodology should be shared with the public.”


‘The uncertainties must be brought to an end’


Doğan continued: “What has been so widely discussed and debated? What happened? What is happening? Has the withdrawal taken place or not? Yesterday, a statement signed by the [Kurdish] Movement Leadership addressed these questions. In addition to historic steps such as the dissolution of the organization and the destruction of weapons, it stated that, as of the framework law, it had withdrawn all of its armed forces from within Turkey’s borders and from areas outside Turkey that could be described as close to the border, and had thus fully fulfilled the requirements of ending the armed struggle against Turkey and pursuing a strategy of democratic political struggle. From this point onward, the uncertainties surrounding the implementation of the framework law must be brought to an end. In other words, when it will enter into force, how it will be implemented, how the higher board will operate, how the boards under it will function, who their members will be, and what needs to be done—all of these issues must be clarified rather than becoming bogged down in endless debate. From now on, the process must move forward rapidly.”


‘Öcalan’s participation in the process is extremely important’


Doğan pointed out that the Peace and Political Participation Coordination is extremely important because it will enable Öcalan to participate effectively in the process. She continued:


“As we stated before, this participation must be ensured as soon as possible. What is needed is not for the process to continue in a state of waiting, being delayed and becoming stagnant, but for it to gain momentum and move forward with new steps.


We also have a call for the democratic public, political parties and different sections of society. We have attached great importance to …

Es la fecha en la que se lanzó la Operación Diluvio de Al-Aqsa, liderada por las Brigadas Al-Qassam de Hamás, que combinó el lanzamiento de cohetes desde Gaza con incursiones en posiciones militares de la entidad sionista, culminando con la captura de 251 israelíes.


Se llevó a cabo en respuesta a décadas de ocupación colonial y crímenes de lesa humanidad, con el sistemático robo de tierras, detenciones, asesinatos y abusos realizados por parte del Estado de Israel.

“Desde octubre de 2023 Israel asesinó a más de 73.000 palestines, incluidas 20.000 infancias; destruyó el 97% de las escuelas; destruyó hospitales en su totalidad y los que quedaron en pie funcionan parcialmente; asesinó a más de 1.700 profesionales de la salud y a 259 periodistas”, detallaron desde el Comité Argentino de Solidaridad con el Pueblo Palestino, y reclamaron: “¡Solidaridad internacionalista! ¡Nadie es libre hasta que todes seamos libres! ¡Palestina libre del río al mar!”

author: Keelan Jacobs
title: Bill C-27 gets royal assent, giving legal force to self-government treaty
content:
Bill C-27 is legislation giving legal force to a self-government treaty with the Tłegǫ́hłı̨ Got’įnę, which received royal assent on Thursday, 20 years after negotiations began.


This legislation makes the Final Self-Government Agreement a treaty

. It recognizes the Tłegǫ́hłı̨ Got’įnę Government as the government of the Sahtu Dene and Métis of Norman Wells and affirms their inherent right of self-government.


The agreement doesn’t come into force until a date set by an Order in Council. That date has not been announced.


“At its core, this legislation recognises an enduring truth: that the Tłegǫ́hłı̨ Got’įnę have an inherent right to govern themselves, as they have since long before Canada existed,” said Crown-Indigenous Relations Minister Rebecca Alty, who is also the member of Parliament for the Northwest Territories. 


“Today, we celebrate the renewal of Canada’s relationship with the Tłegǫ́hłı̨ Got’įnę and the new opportunities that self-government will bring. I extend my heartfelt congratulations to the leadership, Elders, negotiators, and community members whose dedication and hard work over more than two decades made this milestone achievement possible.”


Sherry Hodgson, president of Tlegohli Got’ine Government Inc., called the agreement a legacy.


“This Final Self-Government Agreement is Canada’s formal recognition of the identity, culture, and inherent right to Self-Government of the Tłegǫ́hłı̨ Got’įnę,” she said. “It provides the formal basis for a new government-to-government relationship between us and the Government of Canada, and a government-to-government relation between us and the Government of the Northwest Territories,” said in a statement. 


“It is our generation’s legacy to our children and future generations,” Hodgson said. “We will do our best to use it to preserve, protect, exercise, and advance the inherent and treaty rights of the Tłegǫ́hłı̨ Got’įnę for the benefit of all our people living in Canada, here today.”


She told the community’s youth to take the agreement further. 


“Use this Self-Government Agreement, learn from the mistakes we may make and take us into the future — secure as Sahtu Dene/Metis people within the larger Canadian mosaic.”


Northwest Territories Premier R.J. Simpson said the bill matches the territory’s approach.


“Reconciliation requires action,” he said. “We welcome Canada’s decision to move forward with legislation to give legal force to the Final Self-Government Agreement for the Tłegǫ́hłı̨ Got’įnę, establishing it as a Self-Government Treaty. Collaborative governance is a cornerstone of our mandate.”


The Final Self-Government Agreement was signed on Sept. 18, 2025, by Tłegǫ́hłı̨ Got’įnę Government Inc., Canada and the Northwest Territories. 


When the agreement takes effect, the Tłegǫ́hłı̨ Got’įnę Government will be the governing body for the Sahtu Dene and Métis of Norman Wells, one of five Indigenous communities in the Sahtu Region.


The legislation gives the Tłegǫ́hłı̨ Got’įnę government authority to make laws, protect language and culture, deliver programs and services including education and health care, and elect its own leadership.


Bill C-27 also amends the Mackenzie Valley Resource Management Act and related laws to reflect the new government’s status.


Crown-Indigenous Relations says the legislation aligns with the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples and respects the rights in the 1994 Sahtu Dene and Métis Comprehensive Land Claim Agreement, which is protected by the Constitution.

.


ᒪᑐᐃᖅᑕᐅᓂᖓᓄᑦ ᖁᕕᐊᓲᑎᖃᖅᖢᑎᒃ ᑭᐱᓯᓪᓗᑎᒃ ᒪᑐᐊᕈᑎᖓᓂ ᐅᓇ ᐃᒡᓗᓕᐅᕐᕕᒃᓴᖅ ᒪᑐᐃᖅᑕᐅᓪᓚᕆᓚᐅᕐᑐᖅ ᓯᑎᐱᕆ 29-ᖑᑎᓪᓗᒍ.


ᐅᓇ $75-ᒥᓕᐊᓐᑖᓚᑐᕐᑐᖅ, ᐊᖏᓂᖃᖅᖢᓂ 64,500-ᑭᑉᐹᕆᒃᑎᓯᒪᔪᓂ ᕘᑦᓂ ᐱᓕᕆᕝᕕᒃᓴᖅ ᐱᒋᐊᕈᑎᐅᓚᐅᕐᑐᖅ 60 ᐳᓴᓐᑎᒥ ᐱᒋᐊᕈᑎᖃᖅᖢᑎᒃ ᓯᑎᐱᕆ 23-ᖑᑎᓪᓗᒍ, ᐅᖃᓚᐅᕐᑐᖅ ᓴᒃᑯᒃᑯᑦ ᐊᐅᓚᑦᑎᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᑐᑭᒧᐊᖅᑎᑦᑎᔨᖓ ᔭᐃᓴᓐ ᒋᐸᓐᔅ ᐊᐱᕐᓱᖅᑕᐅᑎᓪᓗᒍ. ᑕᖅᑭᑦ 18 ᐃᓗᐊᒍᑦ ᐅᓇ ᐃᒡᓗᓕᐅᕐᕕᒃ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖏᓐᓂᑦ ᑕᒪᒃᑮᓕᖅᑎᑦᑎᓂᐊᕐᑐᖅ ᓴᓇᕙᒡᓗᑎᒃ 40-ᓂ ᐃᓚᒌᓄᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᑲᑎᕐᖓᐅᖅᑐᓄᑦ ᐃᒡᓗᓂ ᐊᕐᕌᒍᒥ.


ᐃᓄᖕᓄᑦ ᓇᖕᒥᓂᕆᔭᐅᔪᖅ ᐃᒡᓗᓕᐅᕐᕕᒃ ᐊᕐᕕᐊᓂᒃ ᐊᐅᓚᑕᐅᔪᖅ ᐅᕘᓇ ᓴᒃᑯ ᖃᓄᐃᓕᐅᕈᑎᖏᓐᓄᑦ ᐃᒡᓗᓕᐅᕈᑎᓄᑦ, ᐱᓕᕆᖃᑎᖃᕐᓂᒃᑯᑦ ᐅᑯᓄᖓ ᓴᒃᑯ ᐃᑲᔫᑎᓕᕆᔨᓄᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᑯᐸᐃᒃᒥ ᐃᒡᓗᓕᐅᖅᑎᓄᑦ (ᐊᔾᔨᙳᐊᖅ ᐅᑯᓇᙵᑦ ᑕᓃᔅ ᑯᓱᒐᖅ/ᓴᒃᑯ ᐃᑲᔫᑎᓕᕆᔨᓄᑦ ᑯᐊᐳᕇᓴᓐᑯᓐᓂᑦ)


ᐃᒡᓗᓕᐅᕐᕕᒃ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔭᖅᑎᖃᕐᑐᖅ 15-ᓂ, 14 ᐃᓅᓪᓗᑎᒃ ᐅᖃᕐᑐᖅ ᑭᐅᕈᓕᓐ ᓅᑦ, ᐊᐅᓚᑦᑎᔨ ᐊᖓᔪᖅᑳᖅ ᐅᑯᓄᖓ ᓴᒃᑯ ᖃᓄᐃᓕᐅᕈᑎᖏᓐᓄᑦ ᐃᒡᓗᓕᐅᕈᑎᒃᑯᑦ, ᐱᓕᕆᐊᕆᔭᐅᔪᖅ ᐅᑯᓄᖓ ᓴᒃᑯ ᐃᑲᔫᑎᓕᕆᔨᓄᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᑯᐸᒃᒥᑦ ᐃᒡᓗᓕᐅᖅᑎᓄᑦ RG Solution-ᑯᓐᓄᑦ, ᐊᐅᓚᑕᐅᓪᓗᓂ ᐃᓄᖕᓄᑦ ᓇᖕᒥᓂᕆᔭᐅᔪᒧᑦ ᐱᓕᕆᕝᕕᒃᒥ. ᑖᒃᑯᓇᙵᑦ ᖁᓕᑦ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖃᖅᐸᒃᑐᑦ ᐃᒡᓗᓕᐅᕐᕕᒃᒥ ᐊᐅᓚᑦᑎᓂᒃᑰᖓᙱᖢᑎᒃ.


“ᐊᑕᐅᓯᑐᐊᕐᒥ ᐃᓅᙱᑦᑐᒥ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔭᖅᑎᖃᕐᑐᑦ, ᐅᕙᓐᓂ,” ᓅᑦ ᐅᖃᕐᑐᖅ ᐊᐱᕐᓱᖅᑕᐅᑎᓪᓗᒍ.


2028 ᐊᕐᕌᒍ ᑎᑭᑉᐸᑦ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔭᖅᑐᑦ 40-ᐅᓕᕐᓂᐊᖅᑐᑦ ᐃᓚᖃᕐᓗᑎᒃ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔮᖃᓪᓚᕆᒃᐸᒃᑐᓂᑦ, ᕿᔪᓕᕆᔨᓂᒃ, ᓱᓪᓗᓕᕆᔨᓂᒃ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐅᐊᔭᓕᕆᔨᓂᒃ, ᒋᐸᓐᔅ ᐅᖃᕐᒥᔪᖅ.


ᐱᔪᓐᓇᐅᑎᖃᓕᖅᑎᑦᑎᓂᖅ ᒪᑯᓂᖓ ᕿᔪᓕᕆᔨᓂ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖃᓪᓚᕆᒃᑐᓂᒃ ᐅᓇ ᑲᒻᐸᓂᐅᔪᖅ ᐃᒡᓗᓕᐅᕐᓂᕐᒥ ᐊᔪᕈᓐᓃᖅᓴᖅᑎᑦᑎᓂᐊᖅᑐᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐱᓕᕆᖃᑎᖃᕐᓗᑎᒃ ᓄᓇᕗᒥᑦ ᓯᓚᑦᑐᖅᓴᕐᕕᒃᒥ ᓇᓗᓇᐃᒃᑯᑎᑖᖅᑎᑕᐅᓇᓱᒡᓗᑎᒃ ᓴᓇᔨᐅᔪᑦ, ᓅᑦ ᐅᖃᕐᑐᖅ.


ᓴᒃᑯᑯᑦ ᐃᓱᒪᔪᑦ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔮᒃᓴᓂ ᑕᒪᐅᖔᕐᓯᒪᙱᑦᑐᓂ ᓴᖅᑭᑎᑦᑎᓂᐊᕋᓱᒋᓪᓗᑎᒃ ᒪᐅᓇ ᐃᖏᕐᕋᔾᔪᑎᓕᕆᓂᒃᑯᑦ, ᐋᖄᖅᑭᒃᓱᐃᕙᓪᓕᐊᓂᒃᑯᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐱᐊᓂᒃᑕᐅᑎᑦᑎᔾᔪᑎᒃᑯᑦ.


ᒫᓂ ᐊᑕᐅᓯᖅ ᐱᖓᓲᓕᖓᓪᓗᒍ ᐱᓕᕆᕝᕕᒃ, ᑖᓐᓇᓗ ᓴᓇᔭᐅᓕᓚᐅᕐᓯᒪᔪᖅ 2023-ᒥ ᐊᐅᓚᔾᔪᑎᖃᖅᖢᓂ ᒫᓂᒃ $50 ᒥᓕᐊᓐ ᑖᓚᓂ ᐅᖅᑰᑕᐅᑎᖃᑦᑎᐊᑦᑐᑦ ᓯᕐᓗᐊᖅ. ᓂᒡᓕᓇᖅᑐᓂᒃ ᐃᓂᖃᕐᕕᐅᓂᐊᖅᑐᖅ ᓯᕐᓗᐊᖅ ᓴᓂᑦᑎᐊᖓᓃᓐᓂᐊᖅᑐᖅ ᐱᐊᓂᒃᑕᐅᓂᐊᕋᓱᒋᔭᐅᔪᖅ ᓄᕕᐱᕆᐅᓕᕐᐸᑦ. ᐃᓂᖃᕐᕕᐅᑎᑕᐅᓂᐊᖅᖢᓂ ᐊᕐᕌᒍᒧᑦ ᐊᑐᖅᑕᐅᓂᐊᖅᑐᓂᒃ ᐃᒡᓗᒃᓴᕆᔭᐅᓂᐊᖅᑐᓂᒃ.


ᐅᓇ 6-ᓄᑦ ᐃᓚᒌᓄᑦ ᑲᖏᖅᖠᓂᖅᒥ ᓴᓇᔭᐅᓚᐅᕐᓯᒪᔪᖅ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᕆᔭᐅᓪᓗᓂ ᐅᑯᓄᖓ ᓴᒃᑯ ᖃᓄᐃᓕᐅᕈᑎᖏᓐᓄᑦ ᐃᒡᓗᓕᐅᕈᑎᒃᑯᑦ, ᐱᓕᕆᖃᑎᒌᖕᓂᒃᑰᖓᔪᖅ ᐅᑯᓄᖓ ᓴᒃᑯ ᐃᑲᔫᑎᓕᕆᔨᓄᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᑯᐸᐃᒃᒥ ᐃᒡᓗᓕᐅᖅᑎᓄᑦ RG Solution. (ᐊᔾᔨᙳᐊᖅ ᐅᑯᓇᙵᑦ ᑕᓃᔅ ᑯᓱᒐᖅ/ᓴᒃᑯ ᐃᑲᔫᑎᓕᕆᔨᓄᑦ ᑯᐊᐳᕇᓴᓐᑯᓐᓂᑦ)


ᓴᒃᑯ ᐃᑲᔫᑎᒃᓴᓕᕆᔨᒃᑯᑦ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᖃᖅᑎᑦᑎᓯᒪᔪᑦ ᐃᒡᓗᓕᐅᕐᕕᒃᒥ ᐊᑐᖅᖢᑎᒃ ᐃᓄᖕᓅᖓᔪᓄᑦ ᐱᖁᑎᓄᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐱᓕᕆᖃᑎᒌᖕᓂᒃᑯᑦ ᐃᓄᐃᑦ ᑲᑐᔾᔨᖃᑎᒌᖏᓐᓂᒃ, ᑲᓇᑕᒥ ᐅᑭᐅᕐᑕᖅᑐᕐᒥ ᐱᕙᓪᓕᐊᔪᓕᕆᔨᒃᑯᓐᓂ, ᐃᓛᒌᓄᑦ ᐱᕙᓪᓕᐊᔪᓕᕆᔨᓄᑦ, ᑲᓇᑕᒥ ᐃᒡᓗᓕᕆᔨᕐᔪᐊᓄᑦ, ᑲᓇᑕᒥ ᖃᐅᔨᓴᖅᑐᓕᕆᔨᒃᑯᑦ ᑲᑎᒪᔨᖏᓐᓄᑦ ᑲᓇᑕᒥ ᐊᒻᒪ ᓄᓇᕗᒥᑦ ᒐᕙᒪᒃᑯᓐᓄᑦ.


ᐃᒡᓗᓕᐅᕐᕕᐅᔪᖅ ᓴᖅᑭᑎᑦᑎᕙᓪᓕᐊᓚᐅᕐᑐᖅ ᐃᓚᒋᔭᐅᓂᐊᖅᑐᓂ ᑕᖅᑭᐅᓵᖅᑐᒥ 9-ᓂ ᐱᖓᓱᓂ ᐃᒡᓗᕈᓯᖃᖅᑐᓂ ᐃᒡᓗᒃᓴᓂᒃ, ᑖᒃᑯᐊᓗ ᐋᖅᑭᒃᑕᐅᓯᒪᓪᓗᑎᒃ ᓄᓇᓕᖕᓄᑦ ᐃᓕᐅᖃᖅᑕᐅᓂᐊᕐᓗᑎᒃ ᐅᐱᕐᖔᙳᖅᐸᑦ, ᓅᑦ ᐅᖃᕐᑐᖅ. ᑲᒻᐸᓂᒃᑯᑦ ᐸᕐᓇᒃᐸᓪᓕᐊᔪᑦ ᒪᕐᕈᐃᓂ 12-ᓂ ᑲᑎᕐᖓᐅᖅᑐᓂᒃ ᐃᒡᓗᓕᐅᕐᓂᐊᕐᓗᑎᒃ ᑲᖏᖅᖠᓂᖅᒥᓐ.


ᓯᕗᓂᐊᒍᑦ ᐃᒡᓗᓕᐅᕐᑕᐅᔪᑦ ᐱᐊᓂᒃᑕᐅᓚᐅᖅᑎᓐᓇᒋᑦ ᑯᐸᐃᒃᒥ ᐃᒡᓗᓕᐅᕐᕕᒃᓴᓂᑦ, ᑲᒻᐸᓂᒃᑯᑦ ᐋᖅᑭᒃᓯᓚᐅᕐᑐᑦ ᒪᕐᕈᐃᓂ ᑕᓪᓕᒪᐅᓕᖓᔪᓂᒃ ᐃᒡᓗᒃᓴᓂᒃ ᐊᕐᕕᐊᓂᑦ, ᒪᕐᕈᐃᓄᑦ ᐃᓚᒌᓄᑦ ᐃᒡᓗᒃᓴᓂ ᓴᓪᓕᓂᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᑎᓴᒪᓂᒃ ᖁᓕᕇᓕᖕᓂ ᐃᒡᓗᒃᓴᓂᒃ, 6-ᓄᑦ ᐃᓚᒌᓄᑦ ᐃᒡᓗᒃᓴᒥᑦ ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᒪᕐᕈᐃᓕᖓᔪᒥᑦ ᑲᖏᖅᖠᓂᖅᒥᓐ.


ᐃᒡᓗᐃᑦ ᐋᖅᑭᒃᑕᐅᓯᒪᔪᑦ ᐅᑭᐅᕐᑕᖅᑐᕐᒥ ᐃᓅᓯᕐᒧᑦ, ᐃᒻᒥᒃᑳᖓᔪᓂᒃ ᐃᓯᕐᕕᖃᐅᖅᖢᑎᒃ ᐃᓚᒌᓅᖓᔪᓄᑦ ᐃᒡᓗᓂ ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᑐᕐᓲᖃᖅᖢᑎᒃ ᓯᕗᓂᐊᓂ ᐊᒻᒪ ᑐᓄᖏᓐᓂ ᐊᑕᐅᓯᐅᓈᕐᓯᒪᔪᓂᒃ ᐃᒡᓗᒃᓴᓂᒃ, ᓅᑦ ᐅᖃᕐᑐᖅ.


ᐊᓂᐊᕐᕕᖃᑦᑎᐊᖕᓂᖏᓐᓄᑦ ᐅᖁᔭᔾᔮᖏᑦᑐᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᖃᓄᐃᓕᒍᑎᖃᙱᓐᓂᕐᓴᐅᓗᑎᒃ, ᐅᖃᕐᑐᖅ.


ᒪᑐᐃᖅᑕᐅᑎᓪᓗᒍ ᖁᕕᐊᓲᑎᖃᕐᓂᖅ ᐅᐸᒃᑕᐅᓚᐅᕐᑐᖅ ᐅᑯᓇᙵᑦ ᑭᕙᓪᓕᖅᒥᑦ ᐃᓄᐃᑦ ᑲᑐᔾᔨᖃᑎᒌᑦ ᐊᖓᔪᖅᑳᖓᓄ ᑯᓄ ᑕᑦᑎᐃᓂᕐᒧᑦ, ᓄᓇᕗᒥᑦ ᑐᙵᕕᒃᑯᑦ ᐊᖓᔪᖅᑳᖓᓄᑦ ᒍᓘᕆᐊ ᐅᓗᕐᓯᒧᑦ, ᔮᓐ ᒪᐃᓐᒧᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᒪᓕᒐᓕᐅᖅᑎ ᓘᕆ ᐃᓪᓚᐅᕐᒧᑦ.

author: Unknown
title: Группа антифа и либертариев провела в Швейцарии акцию «Михаил Бакунин — иностранный агент»
content:
«В точке встречи разных идей и воль Рождаются жизнь и борьба. Здесь у камня увиделись мы с тобой, Убивши в себе раба…»

Чтением этого стихотворения, найденного на могиле великого революционера Михаила Бакунина в Берне, завершился перформанс либертарных активистов Швейцарии «Бакунин — иностранный агент».

Памятный монумент покрыли алым стягом с портретом философа и надписью на русском и немецком языках «Бакунин — иностранный агент». Так антифа и либертарии Швейцарии выразили солидарность с «Автономным действием» и другими иностранными агентами.

«Сегодня Бакунина, Кропоткина, Волина, Аршинова, Махно и других борцов за свободу и справедливость, в России точно объявили бы иноагентами. Или — членами нежелательных организаций, террористами и экстремистами», — сказал прибывший из Восточной Европы товарищ Таган. — здесь, в месте памяти о прекрасном человеке, мы заявляем о поддержке политзаключенных и изгнанников». Велась видеосъемка. Ждем её размещения.

author: Sophia Sheera
title: ICE Shoots Man in Front of His 5-Year-Old Then Removes Him From Hospital
content:
An ICE agent shot a man in New York in front of his five-year-old child yesterday before taking him from hospital in an unmarked vehicle, sparking renewed anger at the agency as it “terrorises” US communities.


Agents – some wearing construction vests and face masks and at least one carrying a long gun – surrounded the car of a 28-year-old Dominican national in the Bronx on Thursday, police and eyewitnesses said. 


At least one ICE agent shot seven rounds at the man, identified as Oscar Belgal, as his child sat in the car’s back seat. Belgal was wounded below his left ear and taken to hospital by city police. The child was physically unharmed and relatives have been taking care of him. 


Hours after the shooting, ICE agents removed the man from hospital.

Footage

from Freedomnews TV showed several unmarked ICE vehicles speeding away from the hospital as protesters lined the side of the road. 


Hundreds of New Yorkers including elected officials protested at the hospital treating Belgal, calling for the abolition of ICE. The protests later spread to nearby streets. Congressional candidate Darializa Avila Chevalier was

pushed to the ground

by police officers. 


“I will not stand by while ICE agents terrorise our communities,” mayor

Zohran Mamdani wrote on X

 on Thursday, adding that he had spent two hours on the phone to president Donald Trump trying to secure Belgal’s release but was unable to convince him. 


“Today’s shooting is only further devastating confirmation of what we have long known – which is that ICE operates with impunity,” he added at a press conference. “They sow chaos and terror across our country, that they have killed far more of our neighbours than they could ever have claimed to save.” 


The Department of Homeland Security claimed on X that officers targeted a “criminal illegal alien” associated with the Trinitarios gang who had been previously arrested for incidents involving assault, robbery and drug possession. ICE has

previously faced criticism

 for falsely accusing immigrants of gang membership after they were shot by officers. 


Last night’s shooting comes as

ICE arrests hit record levels

, the Guardian reports. Immigration agents have shot

at least 21 people

 since Trump returned to office in January 2025. 


ICE leaders instructed agents to

increase arrests by 1,000 per day

 earlier this week, CNN was told, despite growing unease among even Republicans over Trump’s immigration crackdown.

author: Marina Amaral
title: Centro esquerda e extrema direita: a diferença essencial que a imprensa não fez
content:
Quer receber os textos desta coluna em primeira mão no seu e-mail? Assine a Newsletter da Pública, enviada sempre às sextas-feiras, 8h. Para receber as próximas edições,

inscreva-se aqui

.


Imagine por um minuto que em vez de um candidato de extrema direita houvesse um candidato da esquerda radical em disputa com qualquer outro moderado. Como seria a cobertura das

eleições

? Será que se buscaria um falso equilíbrio entre as duas forças como acontece desde que os Bolsonaro passaram a disputar a presidência do Brasil?


A resposta é óbvia e a pergunta uma provocação para pensar no embuste que é a imparcialidade da imprensa desde a ascensão da extrema direita pós-redemocratização. Em especial nessas eleições, quando a aliança entre os Bolsonaro e a extrema direita dos Estados Unidos já interfere na nossa soberania, inclusive nas próprias eleições.


Nem assim a imprensa cumpriu o papel de informar com rigor quais são os projetos políticos em disputa no país.

Com o argumento da “polarização”, apresentou, e continua a apresentar, a centro-esquerda de Lula como pólo inverso e, portanto, equivalente à extrema direita de Flávio Bolsonaro – um erro, também jornalístico, que enviesa toda a cobertura da campanha.


A esquerda caminhou para o centro enquanto a direita se deslocou para a ponta extrema, esse é o fato oculto sob a suposta “polarização” dos eleitores.

 A terceira via, tão desejada pela imprensa, está na chapa Lula-Alckmin como sabemos desde 2022. Em termos simples, à moda das redes, Lula não é comunista, mas Flávio é fascista, e a imprensa poderia ter deixado essa diferença clara para a população.


Tendo como escudo a alegada isenção e a falsa equiparação como método, a imprensa contornou o tema mais importante das eleições nacionais, as primeiras depois de uma tentativa de golpe de Estado, quando enfim o país conseguiu condenar presidente e generais que conspiraram contra a nossa suada democracia. E que agora, tem a soberania ameaçada pelos Estados Unidos de Donald Trump e

Marco Rubio

.


Não estou cobrando de jornais e emissoras de rádio e TV, de propriedade de famílias ricas, que sejam sequer progressistas, como são, aliás, a esmagadora maioria dos jornalistas que para eles trabalham, mas que

pelo menos honrem o lugar que ocupam entre as instituições democráticas brasileiras

.

Assim como não existe democracia sem imprensa livre, não existe imprensa livre sem democracia.


Nem o risco à liberdade de imprensa e de expressão, que deveria ser valor inegociável de jornais, emissoras de TV e rádio, fez com que expusessem claramente a possibilidade real, e já ensaiada, de Flávio Bolsonaro rasgar a Constituição.


O monitoramento e a investigação de questões cruciais dessas eleições, como o lobby dos Bolsonaro no governo Trump, a farsa do Dark Horse, a predominância dos aliados políticos de Flávio no Caso Master e em outros casos envolvendo o crime organizado, a interferência dos Estados Unidos e das Big Techs ficou a cargo de veículos menores, feitos por jornalistas, que podem exercer a profissão de forma totalmente independente.


A imprensa também se esquivou de alertar os cidadãos sobre o que a eleição de Flávio Bolsonaro tiraria dos brasileiros e que afeta todos nós (excluindo

o 1% mais rico que ganha 31,6 vezes mais que a metade mais pobre da população

). Os usuários do SUS, os médicos, professores, dentistas, e outros profissionais da saúde e educação, assim como as famílias que utilizam os equipamentos públicos não foram alertados do risco que correm os sistemas públicos de educação e saúde – mesmo com muitos exemplos a retirar da pandemia da Covid, incluindo a contribuição desastrosa dos hospitais federais do Rio, gerenciados por indicados pelo próprio Flávio Bolsonaro no governo do pai.


Enquanto cobrava dos candidatos e eleitores o debate sobre “propostas”, e noticiava escândalos com base em vazamentos seletivos, permitiu a omissão de Flávio não apenas em relação às explicações devidas no caso Vorcaro, mas em se posicionar claramente sobre temas que afetam diretamente os direitos individuais e coletivos, como a demarcação de terras indígenas e quilombolas, ou as políticas para a promoção de igualdade de gêneros e de proteção aos direitos das pessoas LGBTQIA+ – inexistente em seu programa de governo e ainda mais relevantes pelo sofrimento imposto às pessoas trans pelo governo Donald Trump, inspiração confessa dos Bolsonaro. Sem falar nos jornalistas, cientistas, artistas e professores …

author: Jaharra Anglin Stubbs
title: Mail-In Ballots are Safe, For Now
content:
As early voting gets underway in many states, voters can continue to rely on existing mail-in voting procedures for the 2026 midterm elections. On September 14, the US Supreme Court declined to allow the Trump administration to implement new restrictions that would have given the USPS a greater role in determining which voters could receive mail-in ballots. The decision left a lower court order blocking the restrictions in place, allowing states to continue using their existing systems for the November election.

The ruling followed Trump’s Executive Order 14399, issued in March 2026, which took effect in August 2026. The Executive Order required states to adopt a “uniform envelope style” and to submit lists of eligible voters to an online portal. It gave the USPS the authority to refuse to deliver ballots to noncompliant states. In its appeal to the Supreme Court, the Trump administration argued that additional measures like this were needed to preserve election integrity, but that claim was disputed.

Concerns also emerged about whether the new system could function reliably before the midterm elections. A whistleblower report revealed that ballots may never be sent because of systemic and programmatic flaws. Implementing a new federal system shortly before an election could create additional obstacles for state and local election officials, potentially leaving voters uncertain about whether their ballots would reach them in time. Despite knowing about these flaws, the Trump administration remained ready to disenfranchise voters further.

The proposed restrictions posed particular challenges for states that rely heavily on mail-in voting, including California, Colorado, Hawaii, Nevada, Oregon, Utah, Vermont, and Washington. Many voters in these states regularly receive and return ballots by mail, making established mail-voting systems central to election administration. Requiring these states to adopt new procedures shortly before Election Day could have complicated ballot distribution and created uncertainty for election officials and voters alike.

Before the Supreme Court issued its emergency docket ruling, lower courts had blocked the new USPS requirements after states and voting rights groups challenged. The Supreme Court’s decision did not resolve every legal question surrounding the administration’s plans. Instead, it left the lower court’s order in place for the upcoming election, with the justices concluding that the government was unlikely to succeed in its challenge. The ruling allows states to proceed with their existing mail-in voting procedures while the broader legal dispute continues.

Although the Supreme Court decision preserves existing mail-in voting procedures, the legal fight will likely continue over the USPS’s potential role in future federal elections.

For now, eligible voters can continue to use the mail-in voting options available in their states. Voters should check their state and local election officials’ websites for ballot request deadlines, return deadlines, and instructions for confirming that their ballots have been received. With Election Day approaching, understanding the rules in your state can help you make a plan to cast your ballot. For more information, visit vote411.org/feminist.
