title: Mark A. Sullivan - An Anarchist View of the Land Problem
content:
Author

: Mark A. Sullivan

Title

: An Anarchist View of the Land Problem

Date

: 1984–85

Notes

: Originally published in the

The Storm!

 (Issue 14/15 – 1984/’85)

Source

: Retrieved 10/08/2026 from

cooperative-individualism.org


 The land problem is one of apparent scarcity: The supply of land appears to be insufficient to meet the demand. Many individuals who seek access to land — whether in rural or urban areas — find land values (rents and prices) too high. This apparent scarcity is an illusion — an illusion created and perpetuated by the state.


 The state creates the illusion of land-scarcity by: (1) TAKING land away from some people (like Native Americans, small-scale farmers, and low-income inner-city dwellers); (2) creating and protecting TITLES TO ABSENTEE-OWNERSHIP over land, which it grants to non-using individuals and legal (i.e., fictitious) “persons” or corporate “entities”; and (3) levying compulsory tribute or TAXES upon the use of the land. All these methods tend to transfer control of land away from those without sufficient money (i.e., power) to hold on to it. To these, then, we may add (4) the monopolization of money, the means of credit and exchange: the current legal-tender/banking scam.


 If you do not have enough money to buy land (for a house, business, etc.) you must either borrow some at exorbitant rates of interest, or pay for the mere USE Of land — i.e., RENT. Usually the poor, who cannot get credit approval from the banks or afford high interest rates, pay rent all their lives only to be thrown out of their homes at the whim of landlords and the so-called “market” — with the state, of course, upholding the landlords by force if necessary. The killing of Eleanor Bumpers clearly illustrates the function of “police protection” in a confrontation between landlord and tenant.


 Titles to absentee-landownership allow for the non-using title-owner to collect monopoly rents from the non-owning users. (A building-owner who does not own the land must collect enough in building-rent to pay the land-rent — thus acting as a “middleman” in the process.) Absentee-owners can also speculate and hold their land out of use while they wait for someone to come along willing and able to pay a monopoly rent for use, or a monopoly price for title.


 Taxation and monopoly interest rates penalize those who would put their land to more efficient use. Thus they prevent land from being used to accommodate larger numbers of people. This can be seen in cities with slums and acute housing shortages. In both urban and rural area poorer “marginal” land is thus forced out of use, raising monopoly rents and prices on other land, encouraging land speculation, raising the costs (thus prices) of commodities, and disemploying workers and lowering wages. Kent, interest, and taxation are Monopoly tributes paid by the user of land to non-users who have legal claims upon a percentage of the wealth produced by the user.


 The title of the absentee-landowner is a LICENSE to collect tribute as a sub-monopoly granted by the supreme monopoly of tribute over the land, the government, or more exactly: the state. And the state is nothing but a group of people who have got away with CLAIMING a “right” or mandate from “the people” to exercise force over everyone within certain geographic boundaries. The sub-monopoly which the state grants to absentee-landowners (and similar privileges to others) is protected or paid for out of the taxes collected from land-users (i.e., workers or producers). Thus folks are paying the state to protect their-own exploiters! Naturally, in the irony of the problem lies its ultimate solution.


 One false solution — because only a half solution — to the land problem is proposed by many “free market” libertarians who advocate abolishing taxation while leaving monopoly titles to absentee-landownership intact. Some even suggest these titles should be made virtually absolute. They regard the state as interfering with land titles — not creating them. Of course, one may ask how the state is to protect these titles, if taxation is abolished — or even greatly reduced? The great amount of taxes needed to fund “welfare” benefits are spent to protect absentee-landownership and other privileges. “Welfare” is but a way to take care of the dispossessed — as compensation and to quell dissatisfaction which could otherwise lead to violence, expropriation, even revolution.


 Other market libertarians do …

title: Ankara Tabip Odası'ndan çağrı: Onur Kurullarının disiplin yetkisi için yasal boşluk giderilmeli
content:
Ankara Tabip Odası Yönetim Kurulu ve Onur Kurulu, TTB ve tabip odalarının disiplin yetkilerinin askıya alınması ve gerekli yasal düzenlemenin yapılmamasına ilişkin basın toplantısı düzenledi.

ATO Genel Sekreteri Dr. Zafer Çelik, etik ihlal iddialarının tabip odalarının yönetim kurullarınca soruşturulduğunu ve Onur Kurullarında karara bağlandığını hatırlatarak, Anayasa Mahkemesinin iptal kararından bu yana geçen 18 ayda yasal boşluğun giderilmediğini söyledi.

Basın açıklamasını okuyan Dr. Fuat Kalyoncu, 65 tabip odasında sonuçlandırılmayı bekleyen binlerce soruşturma dosyası bulunduğunu belirterek, “Sadece Ankara Tabip Odası’nda 16 Eylül 2026 itibarıyla sonuçlanmamış 414 dosya mevcuttur” dedi.

Kalyoncu, dosyaların hasta ve hasta yakınlarının yanı sıra Sağlık Bakanlığı, il sağlık müdürlükleri ve Sosyal Güvenlik Kurumu gibi kurumlardan gelen şikâyetler üzerine açıldığını söyledi.

Yasal düzenlemenin yapılmamasının, etik kurallara aykırı davrandığı öne sürülen hekimlerin yaptırımsız kalmasına yol açabildiğini belirten Kalyoncu, aynı zamanda haklarında şikâyet bulunan hekimlerin kendilerini savunup aklanma imkanının da ortadan kalktığını ifade etti.

Kalyoncu, hekimlik mesleğinin özdenetiminin tabip odalarının sorumluluğunda olduğunu belirterek, idari veya siyasi kurumların denetim mekanizmalarının meslek örgütlerinin bağımsız özdenetiminin yerini tutamayacağını söyledi.

Disiplin mekanizmasındaki boşluğun yalnızca hekimleri değil, sağlık hizmetinin niteliğini ve toplumun sağlık hizmetlerine erişimini de etkilediğini belirten Kalyoncu, meslek etiğine uygunluğun nitelikli sağlık hizmetinin bir parçası olduğunu vurguladı.

ATO Hukuk Bürosundan Avukat Tonguç Cankurt, Anayasa Mahkemesi kararından önce verilen bazı disiplin cezalarının da yasal boşluktan etkilendiğini belirtti.

Cankurt, “Kesinleşmiş idari mahkeme kararları dışındaki soruşturma dosyalarının konusu ne olursa olsun ciddi bir cezasızlık riskiyle karşı karşıya olduğunu görüyoruz” dedi.

Cankurt, tabip odalarına gelen dosyalarda etik dışı reklam, abartılı sosyal medya paylaşımları, yetkisiz tıbbi işlemler, tıbbi hata ve ihmal, yayın etiği ihlalleri ile cinsel saldırı ve şiddet iddialarının yer aldığını söyledi.

ATO Onur Kurulu Üyesi Dr. Mine Önal, Onur Kurullarının yalnızca ceza veren yapılar olmadığını, haklarında şikâyet bulunan hekimlerin savunma yapabilmesi ve gerektiğinde aklanabilmesi açısından da önemli olduğunu ifade etti.

ATO Onur Kurulu Üyesi Dr. Ömer Cengiz de meslek örgütlerinin özdenetiminin hekimlerin yanı sıra hastaların ve toplumun korunması açısından gerekli olduğunu söyledi.

Toplantının kapanışında konuşan Dr. Zafer Çelik, “Meslek örgütlerinin güçlü olması, halk sağlığının da güçlü olması gerektiği sonucunu doğurur” dedi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: KON-MED calls for demonstrations in five German cities against the international conspiracy
content:
The Confederation of Kurdish Communities in Germany (KON-MED) has called for demonstrations and rallies in Düsseldorf, Berlin, Hamburg, Frankfurt and Bremen on Saturday, October 10. The occasion is the 28th anniversary of the beginning of the international conspiracy against Abdullah Öcalan on October 9, 1998. The umbrella organization is demanding freedom for the Kurdish leader imprisoned in Turkey and a democratic solution to the Kurdish question.


In a statement on Thursday, KON-MED described October 9, 1998, as the beginning of a new and decisive phase in the international conspiracy against the leader of the Kurdish freedom movement. On that date, Öcalan was forced to leave Syria. After a months-long odyssey through various countries, he was arrested in Kenya on February 15, 1999, and forcibly transferred to Turkey.


“These events made it clear that the Kurdish question does not concern Turkey alone, but that international powers are also directly involved,” the statement said. Even 28 years later, the developments of that period have lost none of their political significance, according to the Kurdish umbrella organization.


Referring to the current peace and democratic society process, KON-MED emphasized that peace must not be reduced to the silencing of weapons. “Peace means that the Kurdish people can freely participate in determining their own future. This requires genuine dialogue and serious negotiations. Öcalan’s freedom is key to a democratic solution.”


“The Kurdish people’s demand for freedom and a democratic life cannot be postponed,” the umbrella organization stated. Through the actions on October 10, Kurdish communities and their supporters in Germany aim to commemorate the events of 1998 and bring the democratic resolution of the Kurdish question into public debate.


KON-MED calls on the Kurdish population, as well as everyone committed to democracy, human rights and peace, to take part in the events in the five cities.

title: “80 Lakh Voters On the Line”: After Gyanesh, Opposition Turns the Heat on Delhi CEO Ashok Kumar Amid Mass Deletions in State
content:
Hundreds protested outside the Kashmere Gate office of the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer Ashok Kumar on Monday demanding immediate rollback of SIR in the state amid 47 lakh deletions and 33 lakh notices issued for alleged ‘discrepancies’, with the INDIA block taking the lead. A report by

 Mouli Sharma

.


 


New Delhi, 7 October 2026:

Hundreds of people took to the streets for a short notice protest call outside the Kashmere Gate office of Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) Ashok Kumar on Lothiyan Road amidst ongoing SIR processes, which have seen massive voter deletion from the state’s draft rolls as well as the issuances of ‘notices’ to many more. 


 


Police barricaded the roads, causing hours long congestion and traffic diversions between the hours of 12 and 4PM, following which a delegation of INDIA block representatives was permitted to have a private audience with Kumar during which they submitted a joint memorandum addressed to the President of India, Droupadi Murmu, through CEO Kumar.


 


“47,56,722 (32.78%) of Delhi’s voters have been removed from the rolls under SIR and 33,12,919 (34%) (sic) individuals have been issued notices. Deletions of this drastic a scale raise grave questions about citizens’ voting rights as well as the transparency of the electoral process,” the representation by the INDI alliance said, whose signatories included the state representatives of the INC, RJD, CPI, CPI(M), CPI(ML), RSP, AIFB, and TMC (MAMTA). Press were denied entry and efforts to contact the CEO have so far yielded no response.


 


Besides the INDIA block, though, large numbers of protesters from student and workers’ organisations, including the AICCTU, RWPI, Disha Students’ Organisation, and even the Aam Aadmi Party joined the protest in solidarity with the demands for an immediate rollback of SIR. Dozens of locals also joined the protest, expressing that recent revelations about the ECI’s functioning as well as the accusations against CEC Gyanesh Kumar had led them to lose faith in the electoral machinery. 


 


“The student character of the protests in Jantar Mantar might lead people to believe that this is solely a youth issue,” said Shweta Raj of the CPI(ML). “The Kashmere Gate protest clearly shows that this is not the case. People as old as 60-70 years old were there on the ground, women had travelled in large numbers from Shastri Park, because at the end of the day this is a universal issue. Day in and day out we get calls from people all over the city who have been pushed to the point of desperation trying to fulfill the bureaucratese of SIR who are still falling short, whose names are still being deleted.”


 


She also highlighted that the process of SIR, which severely disadvantages those without

permanent residential

 addresses in their current states of residence, has followed a pattern of recurring displacement drives across the city, effectively earmarking those affected for immediate loss of their voting rights. 


 


“The largest number of people affected were from

bastis

 that had been demolished without any rehabilitation of the residents. There is no roadmap for a person like that to get back on the rolls; the whole thing is systematised,” she said. 


 


The demands: rollback, resign, and EVM ban


 


The delegation submitted three demands to the CEO in writing: first, the immediate rollback of SIR in Delhi, along with the readmittance of all the deleted voters (barring the dead) back into the rolls and an indefinite stay on ‘processes’ such as responding to issued notices of ‘logical discrepancies’ in voters’ identities; second, an immediate resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar; and third, perhaps most longstanding within India’s electoral debate: a ban on EVMs and conduct of future all elections through ballots, in an effort to regenerate people’s trust in the electoral machinery. 


 


In 2010, engineer Hari Prasad had demonstrated in an infamous live broadcast on national TV how India’s Electronic Voting Machines could be hacked to favour a preselected candidate. Prasad was arrested for his ‘demonstration’ at the time, under the then ruling UPA government. Ironically, it was the BJP led opposition at the time who was most vocal about the demand for a return to traditional ballot-paper voting. In fact, Prasad’s demonstration had followed a similar row between opposition and Election Commission in 2009, when L. K. Advani had demanded the reintroduction of ballots, following which …

title: Demiryol-İş seçimlerinde AKP-MHP dizaynı
content:
Bugünlerde ve önümüzdeki aylarda kamu iş kolunda Türk-İş’e bağlı Demiryol-İş Sendikası seçimlerinin nasıl bir siyaset denkleminde yapıldığını sizlerle paylaşmak istedim. Delege ve şube kongrelerinin, genel kurulların ve merkez yöneticilerinin nasıl seçildiğine ilişkin bir değerlendirme kaleme aldım. Eskişehir’deki demir yolu fabrikası TÜRASAŞ’ta 13 yıldır çalışan bir işçiyim. Bu yazıda, kendi sendikamın nasıl bir süreç işlettiğini de aktarmak istiyorum.

Bildiğiniz üzere Demiryol-İş’e üye olmak, işe girdiğimiz andan itibaren zorunlu. Başka bir sendika seçeneğimiz yok; çünkü Demiryol-İş, iktidar ve kamu işvereninin iş birliğiyle bu iş kolunda yaklaşık 60 yıldır tek sendika olarak varlığını sürdürüyor. Sendikanın şu anki üye sayısı 31 bin civarında. Özelleştirmelere karşı dişe dokunur bir hamle yapmayan sendika bürokrasisi, çözümü masa başı uzlaşmalarda arıyor. Öyle bir anlayış yerleşmiş ki yöneticilere, temsilcilere ve hatta işçilere mücadele yerine umutsuzluk hakim olmuş durumda. Örneğin şube yönetimine ve temsilcilere, geçen sözleşme döneminde yaptığımız eylemlerin göstermelik değil sonuç alıcı olması gerektiğini söylediğimde bana; “15 bin işçiyle mücadele mi edeceksin? Onlar eskide kaldı, artık işleri masada çözüyoruz” yanıtını vermişlerdi. Şube kongreleri ve seçimlerinde de bu anlayış ve koltuklarını korumaya çalışan bürokratik bir tarz korunmaya çalışılıyor.

İstanbul Şubesi, seçimlerini temmuz 2026’da gerçekleştirdi. Mevcut başkan, yönetim kadrosunda oyuncu değişikliği yaparak yeniden seçildi. Delege seçimlerini tamamlayan Eskişehir Şubemizin genel kurulu ise 13 Ekim’de yapılacak. Delege seçimlerinde ağırlıklı olarak Cumhur İttifakı sempatizanları yer aldı. Geçmişte Ülkü Ocakları başkanlığı yapmış olan mevcut şube başkanı, ikinci dönemi için adaylığa hazırlanırken kendisine yakın işçileri delege olarak belirledi.

Diğer şubelerde seçim çalışmaları şöyle:

Sakarya, Ergün Atalay’ın memleketi olduğu için şubede onun işaret ettiği isim genel merkez tarafından aday gösterilecektir. Ancak Sakarya şubesinde, geçtiğimiz toplu iş sözleşmesi döneminde Ergün Başkanı istifaya davet eden işçiler bir şekilde tehdit edilmişti. Sonrasında ise Sakarya Şube başkanı genel merkez tarafından ifadeye çağrılmıştı. Seçim sürecinin bu yaşananlar göz önünde bulundurularak yürütüleceğini duymaktayım. Sakarya Şubesinde muhalif işçiler de var fakat şu an güçlerini toparlayabilmiş değiller. Sahada daha çok genel merkezin desteklediği isimler öne çıkıyor.

Ankara’da iki şubemiz bulunuyor; bu şubelerden birinde sadece Ankaray’da çalışan işçiler yer alıyor. Diğer şubeye ise fabrikamızın ve demir yollarının işçileri üye. Ankara şubelerine doğrudan AKP müdahalesi gerçekleştiğini rahatlıkla söyleyebilirim. Çünkü burası başkent... “Başkentte muhalefet mi olur?” denilerek geçtiğimiz dönem şube seçimine bizzat genel merkez tarafından operasyon yapıldı. Delegelere para dağıtıldığı iddia edildi, çeşitli entrikalarla korku iklimi yaratıldı. Önümüzdeki dönemde de benzer yöntemlere başvuracaklarını öngörmek için kahin olmaya gerek yok.

Afyon Şubesinde mevcut başkana muhalif olarak iki farklı isim adaylığını açıkladı. Üye sayısı bakımından çoğunlukta olan 15 yıllık makinist işçiler şube yönetimini devralmak istiyor. Sahada, bu makinist adaylardan hangisi genel merkezin desteğini arkasına alırsa seçimi onun kazanacağı konuşuluyor.

Konya Şubesindeki mevcut yönetim ise göreve gelirken genel merkezin 30 yıllık şube başkanını devirdiği ve genel merkeze muhalif durduğu için koltuğa oturduğu günden beri genel merkez toplantılarına dahi davet edilmiyor. Oysa Konya Şube başkanı da seçilmeden önce her işçinin iradesini ve sözünü yansıtacağını vadederek göreve gelmişti. Ancak seçildikten sonra ne yazık ki bu şubede de işlerin değiştiğini söyleyebilirim.

Kamu işçileri sendikalarının genel kurullarında siyasi partiler mutlaka gündeme gelebilir. Ancak sendika içindeki güç ilişkilerini yalnızca AKP-CHP (Şimdi Yeni Parti) veya iktidar

-muhalefet eksenine yerleştirmek, sendikalar ve iş yerlerinde farklı görüşlerden işçilerin olabileceğini göz ardı etmek olacaktır. Seçim, daha geniş bir güç mücadelesinin son aşamasıdır. Kamu iş kolundaki Demiryol-İş Sendikasının genel kurulları genellikle yalnızca "Hangi aday kazanacak?" sorusu üzerinden okunmaktadır. author: Unknown
title: Davanın avukatlarından Erkan Ünüvar: “10 Ekim’in gerçek failleri ortaya çıkarılmadan sahici bir barıştan söz edilemez”
content:
Fotoğraf: Kübra Kırımlı/Evrensel

Kübra Kırımlı [email protected]

Ankara — 103 yurttaşın yaşamını yitirdiği 10 Ekim Ankara Gar Katliamı üzerinden 11 yıl geçti. Yıllardır sorumlular hesap versin diye durmaksızın hukuk mücadelesi veren dava avukatlarından Erkan Ünüvar ile konuştuk. Yargının gerçekleri ortaya çıkarmak bir yana dursun önlerine duvar ördüğünden söz eden Av. Ünüvar, “10 Ekim Ankara Katliamının gerçek failler ortaya çıkarılmadan sahici bir barış ortamından söz edilemez.” dedi

Avukat Ünüvar dünden bugüne davada yaşananları kısaca anlattı: “Katliamdan 1 yıl sonra 36 sanık hakkında iddianame düzenlendi. 19 sanıktan 9’una 101 kez ağırlaştırılmış müebbet cezası ve insan öldürmeye teşebbüsten binlerce yıl ceza verildi; kalan 1 sanık hakkında katliamdan sorumlu olması nedeniyle suç duyurusunda bulunuldu. Diğer sanıklara ise örgüt üyeliğinden 7,5 ila 12 yıl arasından değişen çeşitli cezalar verildi. Yargıtay bu sanıklar hakkındaki kararlardan bir kısmını bozdu; yeniden yargılama yapıldı ve mahkumiyet kararları kesinleşti. Sanıklardan Erman Ekici hakkında, insanlığa karşı suçtan iddianame düzenlemesine rağmen, 2019 yılında bu suçtan beraat kararı verildi. Ekici diğer sanıklarla benzer katliamdan ve anayasal düzeni yıkmaya teşebbüs suçundan mahkumiyet kararı aldı.

Fotoğraf: erkan Ünüvar (Kişisel arşiv)

Fotoğraf: erkan Ünüvar (Kişisel arşiv)

Bugüne gelecek olursak yargılama firari sanıklara yönelik devam ediyor. Suriye’deki son gelişmeler sonucunda firari sanıklardan Ömer Deniz Dündar Suriye’de HTŞ tarafından tutulduğu cezaevinden, IŞİD mensuplarıyla birlikte Türkiye’ye getirildi. Ve geçen celselerde tutuklanarak sorgusu yapıldı. Suriye ve Irak’taki kamplarda 10 Ekim ve diğer katliamların faili olan, dosyamız açısından kritik öneme sahip bazı firari sanıkların da Türkiye’ye getirildiği haberleri basında yer aldı. Ancak henüz mahkemeye ulaşan somut bilgi yok. Kamu görevlilerinin sorumluluğuna dair edindiğimiz yeni belgeler üzerine çalışıyoruz.”

Diğer katliam davalarından davanın başından itibaren nasıl seyredeceğini tahmin ettiklerini, “belli sayıda IŞİD’liye en ağır cezaların verileceği, bu yolla diğer sorumlukların üstünün örtüleceğini biliyorduk” sözleriyle tamamlayan Ünüvar, “Bu katliamın adli bir vaka olmadığını, katliamın arka planında Türkiye’de ve Ortadoğu’da yaşanan gelişmeler ve katliamlardan beslenen siyasi hesapların bulunduğunu savunduk. Tüm sorumluların insanlığa karşı suçtan yargılanması gerektiğini savunduk.” dedi.

Kamu görevlilerinin sorumluluğuna ilişkin de çalıştıklarını “Ankara Emniyet Müdürlüğü görevlileri” hakkında suç duyurusunda bulunduklarını anlatan Ünüvar, “Katliamdan 10 gün önce bomba malzemesi aldığı anlaşılan ve ihbar edilen katliam failleri hakkında gerekli işlemleri yapmayan ve yakalamayan başta dönemin Gaziantep Valisi Ali Yerlikaya ve diğer Emniyet görevlileri hakkında suç duyurusunda bulunduk. Ancak şu ana kadar katliamla ilgili yargılanan hiçbir kamu görevlisi bulunmamaktadır” dedi.

Katliamın yaşandığı günden bugüne hem bölgesel hem de Türkiye’nin iç siyasetinde yaşanan gelişmelerin dava sürecine etkisine dair sorduğumuz Ünüvar, “Geride bıraktığımız 11 yılda önemli gelişmeler yaşandı. Dönemin başbakanı Ahmet Davutoğlu’nun ‘konuşursam yer yerinden oynar’ imalı sözlerini hatırlayın. Sadece Davutoğlu değil; Ümit Özdağ ve Kemal Kılıçdaroğlu’nun da benzer açıklamaları olmuştu. Israrlarımıza rağmen mahkemede dinlenmediler. Yargı bile bizim zorladığımız yerde gelip önümüze duvar örüyor!

Diğer gelişmelere bakacak olursak; Suriye’de HTŞ’nin hakimiyeti ele geçirmesi ile birlikte IŞİD etkisinin azalacağı genel olarak kabul edilse bile bu IŞİD tehlikesinin biteceği anlamına gelmiyor. Zaman zaman HTŞ ve SDG arasında çatışmalar yaşandığı dönemde SDG’nin elindeki kampların ve Suriye’deki cezaevlerinin kontrolsüz biçimde boşaltılması ciddi bir şekilde IŞİD militanlarının rahat hareket etmesine zemin oldu. Şu anda kaç IŞİD’linin Irak’a sevk edildiği, kaçının serbest kaldığı, kaçının belki de HTŞ saflarına katılarak kendini gizlediği bilinmiyor. Bu belirsizlik ve kontrolsüzlük önümüzdeki süreçte IŞİD tehlikesinin devam edeceğini düşündürmektedir. Firari sanıklardan Ömer Deniz Dündar Türkiye’ye getirildi. Fakat özellikle geçtiğimiz yıllarda Irak ve Suriye’de kamplarda olduğuna dair dosyamıza bilgiler gelen İlhami Balı, Savaş Yıldız vs. gibi önemli firari sanıkların akıbetleri hakkında şu anda sağlıklı bilgi alınamıyor. Firari sanıklar Savaş Yıldız ile İlyas Aydın, SDG’nin elindeyken …

author: Unknown
title: Harb-İş Kayseri’de ‘atanmış başkan’ tartışması: İşçiler kendi başkanını seçmek istiyor
content:
Kayseri’de yaklaşık 2 bin üyesi bulunan Türk Harb-İş Sendikası Kayseri Şubesinde 2027 yılında yapılması planlanan genel kurul öncesi tartışmalar başladı. Genel kurul sürecinin demokratik ve şeffaf yürütülmesini isteyen bir grup sendika üyesi işçi, şube yönetiminin şimdiden delege ve temsilci belirlemeye çalıştığını, işçilerin siyasi görüşlerine göre değerlendirildiğini belirterek tepki gösterdi. İşçiler, “İşçiler kendi istediğini delege, kendi istediklerini başkan seçmelidir” dedi.

10 yıllık bir işçi, sendikadaki mevcut sürece ilişkin şunları söyledi: “Sendikamızda demokrasinin kırıntılarını yok etmeye çalışıyorlar. Şimdiden kimler delege olacak, kimler temsilci olacak şube yönetimi belirlemeye çalışıyor. Sendika dediğin her işçinin sözünün dinlendiği bir kurum olmalıdır. Tüm üyeler seçim sürecine dahil edilmelidir. Ama bazı iş yerlerinde sendikanın ekabir takımı diye geçinen işçiler bu aralar iş yerlerinde boy göstermeye başladılar. Herkesi siyasi görüşü doğrultusunda değerlendiriyorlar.”

7 yıllık bir işçi ise sendikadaki anlayışın ülke yönetimindeki anlayışa benzetildiğini belirterek şöyle konuştu: “7 yıllık bir işçiyim. Ülke yönetimi nasılsa sendika yönetimini de öyle dizayn etmeye çalışıyorlar. Tek adamcı bir sendikal anlayışı benimsemeye çalışan Kayseri Şube tabanda işçinin sesine kulak vermiyor. Bu anlayış bizim sendikamızda olmaması gereken bir anlayıştır. Çünkü Türk-İş içerisinde demokrasinin kırıntılarının kaldığı nadir bir sendikadır. İşçiler kendi istediğini delege, kendi istediklerini başkan seçmelidir.”

13 yıllık bir işçi de Harb-İş üyesi işçilerin mücadeleci kimliğine dikkat çekerek şunları söyledi: “13 yıllık bir işçiyim. Harb-İş üyesi işçiler mücadelenin öncüleridir. Ama bizim şubemiz bizim mücadeleci kimliğimiz yerine uzlaşmacı, bürokratik bir anlayışı hakim kılmaya çalışıyor. Ben sizin aracılığınızla işçi arkadaşlara çağrı yapmak istiyorum. Mücadeleci işçiler sakın ola korkmayın. Bizim alın terimiz de mücadelemiz de kutsaldır. Kayseri Şubenin ayak oyunlarına gelmeyelim, birbirimize kenetlenelim. Genel merkezin ayak oyunlarına gelmeyelim.”

Bir başka işçi ise genel kurul sürecinin tüm üyelerin katılımıyla ve şeffaf biçimde yürütülmesi gerektiğini belirterek şube yönetimine şöyle seslendi: “Şubemizin genel kurul sürecinin demokratik bir şekilde işlemesini talep ediyorum. Tüm şeffaflığıyla ve tüm üyelerin katıldığı süreç işletmek zorundasınız. Çünkü bu sendika tarihine ihanet ediyorsunuz. Sizden önceki başkanı bunları yaptığı için eleştirdiniz, bunları yapmayacağız diyerek aday olup seçildiniz. Şimdi de siz aynısını yapıyorsunuz.”

Harb-İş Genel Başkan Yardımcısı Hasan Karaca’yı da konuya ilişkin bilgi almak ve sendikanın yaklaşımını öğrenmek amacıyla aradık. Karaca, görüş vermeyeceğini belirterek telefonu kapattı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Trump, Facing Sinking Approval on Earth, Sets Sights on Colonizing the Moon
content:
The president said that the US will soon “establish a permanent” base on the moon, then gave Elon Musk a medal.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

This week, President Donald Trump — facing increasingly worse approval ratings on issues ranging from the Iran war to immigration — is touting a U.S. program to colonize the moon.

“Under NASA’s Artemis program, American astronauts will soon return to establish a permanent American presence on the moon,” Trump said, in remarks unveiling a supposed “New Golden Age” of science initiatives on Thursday.

“And then, we will go to Mars,” Trump added.

The remarks were meant to unveil the administration’s initiative to funnel $6 billion into artificial intelligence companies, including NVIDIA, Anthropic and Google, and OpenAI, as well as investments in AI infrastructure in partnership with universities across 10 states, a White House press release said. The release also touted that Trump has “replaced DEI with merit across the Federal R&D enterprise,” and said that the administration is “bringing back national missions.” It does not mention the Artemis program.

White House Office of Science and Technology Policy Director Michael Kratsios characterized the announcement as “the most transformative day for the American scientific enterprise since the reshaping of the Federal research ecosystem following World War II,” perhaps ignoring the tens of billions of dollars of scientific grants that the administration has sought to cut under sweeping initiatives by Elon Musk last year.

The White House’s X account also touted the program on Thursday.

Shortly after bragging about Artemis, Trump gave Musk the National Medal of Science, calling him “one of the greatest technology founders to ever live.”

Musk’s SpaceX is a major recipient of government funding, often partnering with NASA, including in its Artemis missions. It raked in billions of dollars worth of contracts as Musk slashed government programs and research, often illegally, under his “Department of Government Efficiency” program.

Trump praised Musk for four minutes straight, before moving on to grant awards to Google co-founder Sergey Brin, NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang, and Advanced Micro Devices CEO Lisa Su. The four tech leaders were also all invited to a White House dinner with Chinese President Xi Jinping last week.

Later in the press conference, Trump was also given an award — his uncle’s National Medal of Science.

Tech billionaires have played a major role in shaping Trump’s space exploration policies. Space exploration requires massive taxpayer investment in tech companies like SpaceX and Jeff Bezos’s Blue Origin — while also fueling the U.S.’s battle for dominance with China in the 21st century space race.

In the past decades, Musk in particular has repeatedly touted that his company is set to colonize Mars. More recently, he has scaled that back to colonizing the moon, saying earlier this year that SpaceX is focused on “building a self-growing city on the Moon” and that that could be achieved in less than a decade — a claim he made about Mars 10 years ago.

NASA’s Artemis was first established by Trump during his first term in 2017, with the ultimate goal of establishing a base on the Moon. NASA has announced plans to build a moon base near the moon’s south pole.

Trump has bragged about the program several times. In a post on Truth Social last month, he posted a picture of the moon with text over it that said “the moon is ours,” with an American flag.

The Artemis program had already spent nearly $100 billion by 2024, and has been criticized as wasteful — especially amid an affordability and energy crisis here on Earth, caused in large part by Trump policies slashing welfare and spurring war.

The White House was mocked for the plan on social media, with users pointing out that the administration couldn’t even successfully line the Reflecting Pool, and that it has made other sky-high promises that it hasn’t kept.

author: Nahuel Lag
title: Mucha tierra en muy pocas manos: un plan para favorecer a las grandes empresas globales
content:
Por Nahuel Lag 


La decisión del gobierno de Javier Milei de buscar estrategias jurídicas —DNU 70/2023, Ley de Inviolabilidad de la Propiedad Privada— para derogar la Ley de Tierras y la decisión de la Corte Suprema de validar la derogación sin revisar su constitucionalidad, no son un fenómeno aislado. Carlos Duarte, relator por América Latina del Grupo de Trabajo de la Declaración de las Naciones Unidas sobre los Derechos de los Campesinos (Undrop, por sus siglas en inglés), lo identifica dentro de una “arquitectura jurídica transnacional que se difunde por mimetismo legislativo y presión multilateral” en el informe

“Contrarreformas agrarias: anatomía de un despojo en progreso”

. 


El trabajo da un a

nálisis minucioso, con particular foco en América Latina, en el que establece cuatro lógicas contemporáneas de despojo

 que se repiten en todos los continentes: ingeniería legal,

financiarización, acaparamiento verde y el rol del Estado como promotor corporativo

. El objetivo: avanzar sobre las tierras campesinas, indígenas y de pequeños productores para trastocar el derecho de acceso a la tierra y ponerla al servicio de los intereses corporativos.  


El informe, publicado este año, continúa actualizándose de manera vertiginosa en los últimos meses ante cada nuevo paso de los sectores políticas de la derecha regional: el

debate del capítulo de tierras en la Argentina

, el

decreto de “fortalecimiento del agronegocio” en la Honduras

 del presidente Nasry Asfura y

la Colombia del flamante mandatario Abelardo de la Espriella

, cuya primera acción fue prohibir la palabra “campesino” en documentos oficiales.    


“

Con la llegada de gobiernos de ultra derecha hay un proceso muy agresivo

 de intentar romper todas las salvaguardas sobre la propiedad de la tierra y reinterpretar los marcos regulatorios para generar procesos de concentración”, sentencia Duarte en diálogo con Tierra Viva y contrapone que el problema tampoco logró pasar de

tímidos reformismos durante los gobiernos progresistas

 por la imposibilidad de romper con las élites terratenientes.  


Foto: Luciana Fernández


Seguir concentrando lo ya concentrado


América Latina, advierte Duarte, es el laboratorio primordial de estas estrategias que tienen como objetivo pasar de “la tierra como base material de proyectos de vida” a “su consolidación definitiva como un simple activo financiero líquido” y como consecuencia la

“concentración acelerada, desplazamiento de los sujetos vulnerables y ruptura del relevo generacional campesino”

.


Al contextualizar esta arquitectura jurídica global, el profesor e investigador del Instituto de Estudios Interculturales Javeriana de Cali (Colombia) contrapone llamamientos a la redistribución de la tierra como la

Declaración de Derechos Campesinos

, en 2018, y los acuerdos alcanzados en la última

Conferencia Internacional sobre Reforma Agraria y Desarrollo Rural

 (Ciradr+20) con un mundo en regresión normativa y en proceso de concentración. El dato más reciente del informe “La situación de la tenencia de la tierra y la gobernanza” —publicado por la FAO, la Coalición Internacional por la Tierra y el Cirad— ubicó la distribución de la tierra entre países en un 0,95 en el coeficiente de Gini, siendo 1 el mayor nivel de concentración. 


Tres datos permiten realizar un repaso rápido de cómo esa situación se refleja en la Argentina. Según el informe

"Los señores de la tierra"

 —FIAN Internacional y Focus on the Global South, 2025—,

diez terratenientes transnacionales controlan 40 millones de hectáreas y tres de ellos operan en Argentina: Arauco, Benetton y Cresud

. Según datos del Registro de Tierras —creado por la Ley en disputa—, el

Observatorio de Tierras

 señaló que Argentina el cinco por ciento de la tierra está en manos extranjeros y en 36 municipios con recursos estratégicos superan hasta el 50 por ciento. Según el

Censo Nacional Agropecuario 2018

,

el 55 por ciento de las chacras solo tiene el dos por ciento de la tierra y el uno por ciento de las grandes explotaciones agropecuarias controla el 36 por ciento de la tierra

. 


La ingeniería legal para los negocios corporativos con la tierra 


El trabajo de “Contrarreformas agrarias” del relator de la Undrop toma dimensión para entender qué lugar ocupa la Argentina en un proceso de orden mundial. author: Chris Walker
title: FBI Adds Torture Charges Against Maduro as US Faces Questions Over Its Abuses
content:
New torture charges against Maduro come as the US faces scrutiny over its treatment of migrants.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

FBI Director Kash Patel announced additional charges against ousted Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores, alleging that both have committed crimes relating to torture.

Patel announced the new charges in a post on X on Thursday. The two were already indicted on separate charges relating to drug trafficking and firearms shortly after the U.S. invasion of Venezuela that resulted in their capture earlier this year.

Both Maduro and Flores are now facing an additional count of Conspiracy to Commit Torture, Patel said. Flores is also charged with one more count of narcoterrorism.

“They will now answer for their crimes,” Patel promised.

The 30-page indictment alleges that Maduro and Flores tortured opposition party members and dissenters to his presidency from around 1999 through 2025, including some U.S. citizens. The couple have not yet entered a plea on the new charges, but pleaded “not guilty” to the original ones.

“President Maduro ⁠denies the charges in the new indictment and looks forward to his day in court,” Barry Pollack, Maduro’s lawyer, said in a statement.

Aspects of the charges against Maduro and Flores may prove difficult for the Department of Justice (DOJ) to prosecute. The “narcoterrorism” statute has rarely been used at trial, and has only resulted in four trial convictions since it was enacted in 2006. Even then, two of those four convictions were later overturned due to concerns about witness statements.

Much of the evidence against Maduro relies on witness statements from less-than-reputable sources, The Washington Sun reported after his capture.

The January invasion resulted in over 100 people killed, including civilians, with at least one United Nations expert decrying it as a likely violation of international law and the sovereignty of Venezuela. After Maduro’s removal, the U.S. began seizing Venezuela’s oil reserves, and this past summer, a “deal” between the countries was brokered, which includes the U.S. taking control of 65 billion barrels of Venezuela’s oil reserves, and 100-year leases to 17 oil fields.

Trump reportedly sought advice on his decision to invade Venezuela and capture Maduro, in part, from the AI chatbot Grok.

The charges against Maduro come as the Trump administration has also been accused of employing torture techniques.

For example, as part of the administration’s mass deportation campaign, the White House is sending refugees and other immigrants to countries known for torturing incarcerated people, including to El Salvador, where immigrants have been incarcerated at the notorious CECOT prison, which critics contend is in violation of U.S. and international law.

Within the U.S., the administration has tortured immigrants in detention facilities across the country, such as at the now-closed “Alligator Alcatraz,” where incarcerated people were subjected to a device known as “the box” — a 2×2 foot cage-like structure that was used to punish people.

The U.S. has also sent immigrants (some of whom were legally permitted to live in the country) to Guantánamo Bay Naval Base in Cuba, where individuals have been subjected to horrendous, unsanitary conditions and kept in isolated confinement for up to 23 hours per day.

author: Daron Letts
title: Crosswalk crash stalls Iqaluit traffic
content:
A downed crosswalk pole on Niaqungusiariaq Rd., across from Iqaluit’s Qikiqtani General Hospital clinic entrance, slowed traffic for 90 minutes, following a two-car collision at around noon on Thursday.


“Everyone was checked at the scene, and one person went to the hospital on their own afterwards for further assessment,” said city spokesperson Geoff Byrne in an email.


The city warned drivers of the traffic disruption in a public service announcement issued shortly after 12 p.m.


Two RCMP vehicles blocked Niaqungusiariaq Rd. about two hundred metres past the Sailijaaqvik boarding home at the southeast corner of the intersection. An RCMP truck also blocked Queen Elizabeth Way about 100 metres from the entrance to Astro Hill.


Traffic was backed up on Niaqungusiariaq Road all the way up to Joamie School for approximately 90 minutes while city workers removed the pole, broken in two places, with heavy equipment. The crew also filled-in the hole left behind.


The intersection is the site of Iqaluit’s first controlled

crosswalk

, which was installed in fall 2024.

author: CMI Argentina
title: La oposición en Diputados convocó a excombatientes para darles voz por el proyecto del gobierno sobre Malvinas
content:
Después de que el gobierno enviara a la secretaria legal y técnica a defender el proyecto de Ley de Defensa de Soberanía Nacional, el peronismo convocó a organizaciones de ex combatientes. La sesión del 15 de octubre por la Ley de Tierras y las maniobras oficialistas.


Por Verónica Benaim @VeBenaim


 


La agenda Malvinas copó toda la semana legislativa en la Cámara de Diputados de la Nación. El día

después de la presentación de María Ibarzabal Murphy

, funcionaria clave del gobierno de Javier Milei, el peronismo abrió este jueves la Comisión de Asuntos Cooperativos, Mutuales y ONG para darle voz a representantes de organizaciones de excombatientes de Malvinas en el marco del debate sobre el proyecto de ley de Defensa de la Soberanía Nacional.


Mientras el oficialismo prepara una estrategia para desactivar la sesión convocada por la oposición para la semana que viene, que tiene como fin principal voltear el DNU 70/23 que deroga la ley de venta de tierras rurales a extranjeros, el diputado de Unión por la Patria, Aldo Leiva, convocó a un batallón de representantes de asociaciones civiles nucleadas en la Mesa de Coincidencia Malvinas (MECOMA). Y es que, tras el fallo de la Corte Suprema, el peronismo buscar sumar rechazos a la decisión judicial por facilitar la extranjerización de tierras nacionales.


Del encuentro, que tuvo una fuerte presencia de dirigentes y expertos de Malvinas de la provincia de Buenos Aires -sobre todo de la ciudad de La Plata- participó el diputado Máximo Kirchner que no forma parte de la comisión y que suele participar de las actividades cotidianas del parlamento.


Los que estuvieron ausentes fueron los diputados del bloque de La Libertad Avanza que, según pudo saber Tiempo, tomaron la reunión como una forma de “oportunismo político” por parte de los opositores. Es más, enviaron una carta, en donde expresaron su rechazo al encuentro bajo el argumento de que “se propuso un temario que no se condice con la comisión. Se desvirtúa el objeto de una comisión permanente de esta Cámara”.


Durante el encuentro,

Tiempo

For most of human history, you could say “I am going to take Gilgamesj / Odysseus / King Arthur / Laosheng* /etc” and give him a completely new story, maybe in a completely different setting" and it would be considered just as valuable as a work of fiction with ‘original’ characters. That wasn’t 'fan’ fiction, that was just fiction.

The idea of the individual genius that has to build a completely new setting with new characters and a new plot from scratch is a very recent invention and a very European invention and it has greatly reduced the spectrum of what can be considered 'real’ art.

(*ok, a character archetype isn’t exactly the same as a character, but it’s another example where taking cues from a pre-established story telling tradition is appreciated and encouraged)

The very idea of “intellectual property” is and always has been antithetical to the way we communicate and share knowledge. No one can own a character or a setting or an idea, and we all know that. Copyright laws don’t exist to protect you or your unique ideas, they exist to enforce the existing power structure.

Because you really. do not. need to. do this. alone! And not just writing either. Painting, pottery, sculpture, everything. Art can be collaborative and it will usually be better art and more fun to make.

I am asking genuinely and without ulterior motive. This is not a trap, and any informed answer will be welcomed:

Does the use of the word 'novel’ (which simply means “new,” of course) to describe a particular format of written fiction - does that have anything to do with the advent of the expectation of originality described above?


I’m not an etymologist so I had to look this up and it looks like the word 'novel’ for a story is very old, 500-ish years, and from what I can find it does come from the word for news and used to mean something like 'a short story’.

But the idea that such a story should be

entirely

 original in all aspects (characters, plot, dialogue, etc) and could not borrow anything substantial from previous stories, is much more recent.

Though copyright law is probably the biggest culprit, literacy probably does have something to do with this too. When most people could not read, most stories were read aloud or performed as plays. Familiar characters or familiar plots are useful in such a setting because you can skip some of the set up and get right to the storytelling.

Shakespeare plays are obvious examples. They’re full of historical characters and often used a familiar plot from an existing play that Shakespear did not invent. The fun for the audience was often not in a completely new story, but in Shakespeares’ twist on a familiar character and/or the plot. (This is also how good fan fiction works.)

It’s worth noting that our current cultural idea of a 'new’ story is genre specific and has culturally accepted exceptions. Putting familiar characters in movies and TV series is considered more socially acceptable, especially if they’ve been recycled before. If you choose a public-domain character like Sherlock Holmes, you can put him in new adventures and make a successful TV show out of it without being side lined as 'fan fiction’.

title: Activists Abused By Israel Return to New Freedom Flotilla Mission
content:
By Elizabeth Murray,

Washington Report on Middle East Affairs

, October 8, 2026


A NEW FREEDOM FLOTILLA

, led by the aptly named

Tenacity

, set sail from Bristol, UK in September and headed for Gaza in yet another attempt to break Israel’s siege and blockade of Gaza.


A significant percentage of the ship’s passengers and crew—whose countries of origin include Denmark, Norway, Spain, Ireland, France, the United Kingdom, the United States and Palestine (currently residing in Sweden)—have been kidnapped, detained and tortured by Israeli soldiers on previous Gaza-bound solidarity missions. Nevertheless, they are determined to challenge Gaza’s isolation.


Captain Tomás Alberto Moraté Serna, who hails from Spain, is the captain of the

Tenacity

. He was kidnapped, brutalized, tortured and deported by Israel in April 2026. He explained that he is back for the same reasons he joined the Gaza mission in the first place: “I am not happy with what I see in the world, and I need to do my part” to transform it.


Serna is primarily an environmental activist, but he is keenly aware that environmental and climate concerns overlap with ending wars. Knowing that Israel is daily murdering Palestinian men, women and children amid governments’ silence and/or complicity impels him to sail with the Freedom Flotilla once again. The flotilla’s slogan is “When governments fail, we sail.”


Colm Byrne, First Mate aboard the

Tenacity

, experienced violence at the hands of Israeli soldiers on a previous mission. He sails again “because there’s still kids being slaughtered and degraded,” he said. “And there’s no sign of it ending. This should not be happening in 2026.” Asked what he would say to the Palestinian people, Byrne, who hails from Ireland, stated: “I’d apologize for the Western world’s lack of response. I would let them know that the majority of the people of the world are on their side. We [the Gaza-bound Freedom Flotilla Coalition] represent the people.”


Another crew member who experienced Israel’s violent seizure of Gaza-bound boats in April 2026 said he has received several written death threats from Israel in the mail warning him that his life will be in danger if he is again apprehended by Israel on the high seas. For him, sailing again is an act of resistance against Israel’s crimes against humanity.


MY ROAD TO

TENACITY


For me personally, sitting at home during a genocide is not an option.


In the 1980s I was stationed in Amman, Jordan for two years, working as an editor for the U.S. government’s media translation office—then known as the Foreign Broadcast Information Service and later the Open Source Center.


As part of my duties, I would travel periodically to the U.S. Consulate in East Jerusalem (a diplomatic outpost which no longer exists) to collect the local Arabic language newspapers for translation. The trip usually entailed spending one or two nights in East Jerusalem.


It was during the time of the first Intifada, and most Palestinian businesses shuttered their doors at 1 p.m. in a nonviolent protest against the Israeli occupation. An eerie silence often pervaded those afternoons, when the streets were deserted.


In the early evenings I would often see armed Israeli soldiers chasing Palestinian children down the ancient cobblestone streets as clouds of tear gas hung in the air. I saw Israeli soldiers yanking a shopkeeper from behind his store counter and hauling him away in an armored vehicle. An Israeli policeman riding a very large horse once drew dangerously close to me as I walked in the park; he menaced other pedestrians in a similar fashion; and from my hotel window one morning, I awoke to the sight of a blackened Palestinian car in flames. (Israeli and Palestinian vehicles can be identified by their color-coded license plates.)


I visited several Palestinian families in their homes and learned about the Israeli poisoning of local water wells, the denial of housing permits and other cruelties designed to make life unbearable for Palestinians and encourage them to leave.


From that time, Palestine began to occupy a place in my heart.


My time among the Palestinians helped me to become more aware of the pro-Israel biases in the U.S. media and the militaristic mindset that prevailed among the government and think tank communities in Washington, DC. author: Mike Ludwig
title: Border Patrol Unleashes Violence on Protesters Over Trump’s Border Wall
content:
Activists say federal agents dragged protesters across a barbed wire and used “extreme pain compliance” tactics.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Since construction began on President Donald Trump’s border wall in haste on October 5, federal agents have clashed with land defenders and arrested roughly two dozen activists who camped out on private land to protest the destruction of fragile desert ecosystems on both sides of the imaginary line that separates Mexico from the tiny town of Lochiel, Arizona.

The protest received media attention after Border Patrol agents extracted and arrested a tree sitter and cut down the “Grandmother Tree,” an ancient cottonwood in a grove of several trees that stood in the way of contractors building the border wall. Estimated to be around 200 years old — older than the current border — the grove’s branches reached from the United States to Mexico, a symbol of international solidarity for the protesters.

The felling of the Grandmother Tree may have also symbolized the Trump administration’s disregard for nature and public opinion, but it did not mark the end of the protests, as construction continues. Video captured by journalist Max Granger shows land defenders climbing into a tree on the Mexican side Tuesday morning and setting up another tree-sit style blockade in a renewed attempt to halt construction. Clashes with Border Patrol continued throughout that day, with activists accusing federal agents of dragging protesters across a barbed wire fence during a chaotic confrontation that was caught on video.

On Wednesday afternoon, a protester locked themselves to moving construction machinery, according to a statement from activists. Border Patrol agents attempted to remove the protester with “extreme pain compliance” and pepper sprayed the surrounding crowd, the activists said. Protester continued to lock themselves down after construction came to a halt and construction crews left, the activists noted. “We do not intend to back down,” said Adriana, a Tierra Libre activist identified only by first name, in a statement on Wednesday. “Our resolve only grows with their violence.”

Jason, an activist from the Tierra Libre protest camp in Lochiel who declined to use his last name due to concerns over state repression, said roughly two dozen people have been arrested. Some received citations on the spot, and others were taken into custody and released onto the streets of Nogales or Tucson hours later, he noted.

Among the police presence is an elite unit known as the Border Patrol Tactical Unit (BORTAC). BORTAC was also deployed to Operation Metro Surge, the now-defunct federal invasion of Minnesota’s Twin Cities launched in December 2025 as part of the Trump administration’s violent immigration crackdown.

Activists say the tactics that the unit are using now in Arizona are similar to the ones deployed in Minnesota. “BORTAC was kind of one of the units famous for their brutality in Operation Metro Surge,” Jason said. “We are seeing a lot of the same tactics on the ground that they started to use during Metro Surge and some of these other large mobilizations against various cities like Chicago and Los Angeles.”

“A lesson from past attempts at a fascistic regime is that, if they are able to [abuse] one population of people that is easy to ‘other,’ what they are doing to that population will always expand out to other populations,” said Jason. “It’s all the more reason to take what they are doing to immigrants seriously, and what they are doing in Lochiel seriously.”

In their statement on Wednesday, protesters said Border Patrol and BORTAC have “beaten, detained, arrested, and maced activists engaged in morning prayer,” and “kidnapped” fellow protesters who faced further abuse while in custody for about 24 hours. Jason said arrestees were released at random public places such as a fast-food restaurant, mirroring stories about people swept up in Trump’s immigration crackdown.

Jessica Turner, a spokesperson for Customs and Border Patrol, said Border Patrol conducted an “enforcement operation” in Lochiel to protect personnel and the federally managed area around the border line. While most activity remained peaceful, Turner said agents took appropriate action in response to “alleged violations” and an “alleged assault on a federal officer.”

Sure. Fanfic in general sucks ass though

write better books and your medium won’t be seen as shit


I think you’re probably just being rude and annoying on purpose but on the small chance that you generally don’t know this: you’ve got the chicken and the egg backwards.

Most fan fiction spaces are very welcoming to new inexperienced writers. So it is where a lot of people learn to write. Of course there’s going to be a lot of work that isn’t great yet in a place where a lot of people are still learning and where their imperfections are allowed to exist without shame or mockery.

A lot of fan fiction writers with real talent eventually move away from fan fiction because writing fully 'original’ works is the only thing that gets them money and status. As a result there’s a constant talent drain on the community.

Books are curated. There are a LOT of shitty books out there that you’ve never read because libraries and bookshops already filtered them out so they never reached you. There are A LOT A LOT of terrible drafts of books that you’ve never read because publishes already filtered them out.

Result: because fan fiction spaces are uncurated or much less curated, you need to put more effort into finding the good works and you will encounter more bad works in your search for good works.

If fan fiction was not curtailed by copyright and more respected as a medium, then high quality works would be printed by publishers, sold by book stores and reviewed by newspapers and you could easily read only high quality works and never encounter a bad piece of fan fiction.

Shakespeare wrote fully new plays about familiar historical characters (tons of British kings, Antony and Cleopatra, Julius Caesar, etc) and borrowed characters from other works of fiction, such as Romeo and Juliet. In other plays he invented new characters but put them in a familiar plot from an existing play. The fun for the audience was in his twist on a familiar character and/or plot. This is how good fan fiction works.

author: Jillian C. York
title: When No ID Means No Internet: Age Verification and the Right to Access Information
content:
This post was co-authored by

Sheila B. Lalwani

, a doctorate student and recent 

COMPASS Fellow

 hosted by EFF.


Age verification proposals are

often presented

 as a simple tradeoff: sacrifice a little privacy to better safeguard children online. But that framing overlooks a more fundamental question. What happens to people who cannot verify their age at all? This is particularly a problem when users are required to prove their age with identity documents.


Age-related restrictions are developing quickly around the world. While they differ radically across jurisdictions, in the past year, we’ve witnessed a sharp uptick toward mandatory age assurance for social media access but also for other high-risk digital services.


For example:


In late 2025,

 Australia

became the first country

 to implement a minimum age requirement for prohibiting children under age 16 from creating or holding social media accounts. 


India

passed the

Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act

 that includes mandatory verifiable parental consent and has undertaken ongoing discussions for social media restriction.


The United Kingdom

passed the

Online Safety Act


requiring age verification

 across a swath of services hosting content considered harmful to users under 18. More than half the states across the

U.S.


have enacted age verification laws

. 


An

EU Commission

’s expert

report

 recommends a ban on social media access for users under 13. It also recommends mandatory age verification for platforms to ensure that users are ‘age appropriate.’ 


The Access Problem 


Age verification laws that

are predicated on the necessity of

 users possessing a current passport, driver’s license, credit card, or similar documents proving their identity exclude critical sections of populations.  And this problem is global in nature:

Millions of people lack government-issued identification

 or encounter regular challenges to obtaining or updating it. 


Roughly

15 million adult U.S. citizens

 lack a driver’s license, and a further

2.6 million lack any government photo ID

; leaving large groups blocked from online content or services. The UK has a similar predicament: proof-of-age checks are often reliant on passports, driver’s licenses, or other recognized alternatives, which can pose unique challenges to people without these documents.


Much of the advocacy around age verification discusses the

privacy harms

 of age verification. Yet these measures also threaten something more fundamental: equal access to information and the ability to exercise the right to freedom of expression. 


Unfortunately, age verification systems foster unequal access to information and provide an asymmetric solution to find essential information, build community, and weigh in on public discourse. As governments and companies increasingly require users to prove their age before accessing online services, these individuals risk being excluded from large parts of the internet altogether. 


Effects on Global Majority Countries 


Age verification laws reshape who can speak, who can access information, and who gets excluded from the digital public sphere. In other words, age verification is not a neutral safety measure: it presents a structural barrier to disproportionately exclude certain groups—particularly those in the global majority—and alters the architecture of global online expression. Some of these groups are already marginalized offline, and age verification extends that exclusion into digital spaces.


For instance,

850 million people globally do not have ID

. Most of these individuals exist in primarily low and middle income countries in Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia. The World Bank

points out

 that many are members of marginalized groups and more than half of those lacking access to identity documentation also have children whose births have not been registered. Women are particularly vulnerable and are 8% less likely than men to have an ID. Other vulnerable groups, such as adults in low income countries, are less likely to have an ID when they fall below 25 years, as are those with a primary school education or less or those in rural areas. 


A

policy paper

 from EDRi points out that age verification laws provide quick tech solutions but overlook longstanding structural challenges and undermine the universality of the internet. The analysis finds that age verification laws have serious human rights implications and …

author: Daron Letts
title: Nunavut Sport and Recreation awards gala honours leaders, volunteers
content:
Leadership and volunteerism were recognized during the Nunavut Sport and Recreation awards gala at Iqaluit’s Aqsarniit hotel on Saturday.


The Recreation and Parks Association of Nunavut co-hosted the event in partnership with the NU Sport Federation and the territorial government’s sport and recreation division.


Novoalia Carriere of Kinngait earned the Calm Air Youth Leader of the Year award for his work as a summer camp supervisor and now as head of the hamlet’s after-school program.


“Sport is important for young people because it promotes healthy physical growth, builds mental resilience, and teaches essential life and social skills,” said Carriere over Facebook Thursday.


The 18-year-old athlete cares for up to 40 children aged five through 12 from 4 p.m. to 6 p.m. weekdays at the youth centre.


With the music of Black Eyed Peas and other pop artists filling the background at low volume, Carriere tries to create an atmosphere that’s distinct from school and home.


He cycles through creative indoor activities to foster social connection without any concern for “competition or adult expectations.”


“When activities feel less like school and more like an unfolding adventure, kids naturally stay hooked,” he said.


The non-profit association also honoured the Kinngait Youth Group with its Volunteers of the Year award.


“Volunteers really are the heart of their communities,” said association executive director Aaron Robinson in a phone interview Thursday.


Made up of 10 youths aged 13 to 19, the group offers a safe, welcoming space for younger children, he said.


In February, the teens served more than 200 residents at a Valentine’s Day breakfast, Robinson said.


“These youth have led with heart, teamwork and pride, and it’s still going,” he said. “They are inspiring others, building community and showing us what volunteerism and leadership truly looks like.”


City of Iqaluit recreation director Breton McNeil received the Recreation Leader of the Year award.


During the gala, the NU Sport Federation inducted former NHL player Jordin Tootoo and the late Arctic sports athlete and organizer Attima Hadlari into its newly established Nunavut Sports and Recreation

Hall of Fame

.


The federation and the Government of Nunavut also handed out awards to athletes, officials, and administrators from throughout the territory.


The audience included more than 100 recreation professionals who participated in the association’s weekend summit.


Organizations that included Nunavut Basketball, Volleyball Nunavut, Nunavut Soccer, Nunavut Table Tennis, Cambridge Bay Wrestling and Nunavut Badminton hosted coaching sessions in Iqaluit school gyms on Saturday and Sunday.

author: Amy Goodman
title: Throughout US War on Afghanistan, “We Could Clearly See Failure Was Coming”
content:
The “war on terror” is still ongoing in Afghanistan despite US withdrawal, journalist Emran Feroz says.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

This week marks 25 years since the U.S.-led invasion of Afghanistan, the beginning of what would become the longest war in U.S. history. After installing a pro-Western government in Kabul in December 2001, U.S. and other NATO troops would remain in the country for the next two decades battling a stubborn insurgency — until a chaotic U.S. withdrawal in August 2021 that saw the Taliban return to power.

“During the 20 years of America’s longest war in Afghanistan, we could clearly see that failure was coming,” says journalist Emran Feroz, just back from a month of reporting in Afghanistan. He says the relative economic and political gains under the Western-backed government were undercut by widespread corruption and violence, particularly in rural Afghanistan. “You had torture prisons next to Burger King and KFC and Starbucks.”

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

AMY GOODMAN: This is Democracy Now!, democracynow.org. I’m Amy Goodman, with Nermeen Shaikh.

NERMEEN SHAIKH: This week marks 25 years since the U.S.-led invasion of Afghanistan, the beginning of what would become the longest war in U.S. history. Less than a month after the September 11th World Trade Center attacks, the United States launched airstrikes against Afghanistan. The Taliban government was ousted within months, but the U.S.-led war and occupation would continue for nearly two decades, during which more than 100,000 Afghan civilians were killed, according to the U.N. More than 2,300 U.S. service members died. The U.S. spent trillions of dollars on the war and efforts to build an Afghan government and military, that ultimately collapsed with stunning speed in August 2021.

Today, Afghanistan is facing a deepening humanitarian crisis. Women and girls have been shut out of higher education and face sweeping restrictions on their work, movement and participation in public life.

AMY GOODMAN: Our next guest, Austrian Afghan journalist Emran Feroz, is just back from a month reporting in Afghanistan. His new piece for Truthout is headlined “The War on Afghanistan Was Launched 25 Years Ago. It Still Hasn’t Ended.” He’s joining us from Stuttgart, Germany.

Emran, welcome back to Democracy Now! Why don’t you lay out what you found, as you’ve just returned from Afghanistan? The U.S. bombed Afghanistan when the Taliban were in power, and the Taliban are back a quarter of a century later.

EMRAN FEROZ: Hi. Thanks for having me.

So, yes, I spent almost a whole month in Afghanistan, and the thing is that, as I wrote in this piece, I believe the “war on terror” is not over, especially because since the U.S. withdrawal, a lot of airstrikes are still taking place, especially in the last weeks and months. And all these airstrikes are being conducted by the Pakistani military regime, which kind of took over America’s role and is now using the same “war on terror” arguments that we heard for 20 years, again to hit Afghan civilians. And the recent strike just took place a few days ago in the south of the country, close to the Pakistani border. And again, most of the victims were civilians, especially children.

NERMEEN SHAIKH: So, Emran, if you could say — you know, a lot of people were surprised by the fact that the Taliban came back to power so quickly. Who was supporting the Taliban in all those years?

EMRAN FEROZ: I mean, during the 20 years of America’s longest war in Afghanistan, we could clearly see that failure was coming. The Afghan regime in Kabul, the pro-Western Afghan regime in Kabul, was highly corrupt and was engaging in a war that seemed to be endless because too many people were profiting from it. And this war actually made a lot of people angry and, you know, left them frustrating, and a lot of these people, actually, especially in Afghanistan rural sites, started to support the Taliban again.

But I also want to highlight that a lot of the places that I visited during the last weeks, for example, Bagram Air Base, close to Kabul, were in fact breeding grounds for America’s enemies, because you had this huge prison complex in the middle of the country, which became kind of a Little America. author: David Swanson
title: The Combination of Nuclear Energy and War Threatens Us All
content:
By David Swanson, World BEYOND War, October 8, 2026


The latest news is of war fighting around the nuclear facilities in Zaporizhzhya, Ukraine. This is in a part of the world that can already boast in Chernobyl one of the four big nuclear power disasters. When Russia first invaded, unarmed civilians protected the dangerous site in Zaporizhzhya, but as soon as armed troops took over, the shooting started, and it’s worsened since, with taboos being tossed aside in succession as if the continued existence of humanity is grounds for not only keeping nuclear weapons and power plants around but also for upping the risks just a little.


The largest nuclear power plant in Europe, with six 1,000 MW reactors and decades’ worth of nuclear waste, is now in a battlefield. Already in this war (find a summary in

No to Nuclear

 by Linda Pentz Gunter) the site has lost power, caught on fire, almost been shelled, had its water supply drained, and been attacked by drones. Even with the reactors shut down, a loss of power could still lead to a meltdown.


Meanwhile in Iran and Israel we have seen

intentional attacks

 on nuclear sites, with Trump famously — if unconvincingly — claiming to have obliterated Iran’s nuclear facilities. The International Campaign to Abolish Nuclear Weapons says “A direct hit on a nuclear facility would not cause a nuclear weapon-style explosion. The central risk is a radiological release – radioactive material spreading into the environment, potentially causing long-term contamination. The exact consequences depends on what part of a site is struck and what radioactive materials are present. But the IAEA’s general warning is clear: a conflict that brings missiles, bombs and drones into the surroundings of nuclear infrastructure carries dangers that can quickly extend beyond the battlefield and the

ICRC points out the obvious risks

, as a result of military activities in and around nuclear sites, and explains why nuclear power plants and other installations containing dangerous forces have specific protections under international humanitarian law. But as the conflict between US-Israeli-forces and Iran intensifies, The World Health Organization (WHO) has begun preparing for the

‘worst-case scenario’

 of a nuclear catastrophe.”

lists

a new one

The tower is largely gone. Debris flew for great distances — many times the distance of 270 meters to a nuclear reactor (white in the background in the photo

here

Any use of force whatsoever on any target at all is excessive when attacking someone’s country with violence, but it’s likely that much less force than two massive missiles could have sufficed for the crime of depriving people of electricity and communications. It’s also possible that something could have gone slightly wrong, resulting in a need to evacuate millions of men, women, children, and infants. Visiting this location was part of the fourth day of a peace delegation to Venezuela (

While the excuse for threatening and attacking Iran has often included false claims of a nuclear weapons program, the fact is that a nuclear power program is a major step toward a nuclear weapons program. Gunter argues in her book that President Eisenhower replaced a project under President Truman on pursuing solar and wind energy with pursuing nuclear power, despite the risks, costs, poor performance, and ineliminable deadly waste — as a means of giving a positive spin to nuclear programs known for mass murder. For decades the tight connection between nuclear power and weaponry was carefully if implausibly denied.
