There are many people who don’t share this sentiment, but I have an appreciation for when a fanfic is so separated from canon that it could’ve easily been its own original novel, and yet the author was only ever going to put that much energy into it if their favourite characters got to be there

I think there’s a difference between “the author stripped the media of everything it had to replace it with something easy” and “the author thought up a concept they really really like and are bestowing it upon the character like a medal”

For most of human history, you could say “I am going to take Gilgamesj / Odysseus / King Arthur / Laosheng* /etc” and give him a completely new story, maybe in a completely different setting" and it would be considered just as valuable as a work of fiction with ‘original’ characters. That wasn’t 'fan’ fiction, that was just fiction.

The idea of the individual genius that has to build a completely new setting with new characters and a new plot from scratch is a very recent invention and a very European invention and it has greatly reduced the spectrum of what can be considered 'real’ art.

(*ok, a character archetype isn’t exactly the same as a character, but it’s another example where taking cues from a pre-established story telling tradition is appreciated and encouraged)

The very idea of “intellectual property” is and always has been antithetical to the way we communicate and share knowledge. No one can own a character or a setting or an idea, and we all know that. Copyright laws don’t exist to protect you or your unique ideas, they exist to enforce the existing power structure.


YES! And so is the idea of the individual genius.

Every time I see a post on here about how difficult it is to write and how it’s hard to write dialogue when you only want to do world building or it’s hard to write world building when you only want to do dialogue or it’s hard to see where the story should go next I want to shake people and go IMAGINE IF YOU DID NOT NEED TO DO THIS ALONE.

Because you really. do not. need to. do this. alone! And not just writing either. Painting, pottery, sculpture, everything. Art can be collaborative and it will usually be better art and more fun to make.

author: Marcelle Edenlord
title: Ovarian Cancer Awareness Month Has Ended, ​​But the Need for Research Remains
content:
September marked Ovarian Cancer Awareness Month, but the need for greater research, better treatment, and improved early detection does not end when the month does. Ovarian cancer is expected to cause nearly 14,000 deaths in the US this year. Despite the burden of the disease, detecting ovarian cancer early remains a significant challenge.

Ovarian cancer is actually the deadliest cancer among women and the number one cause of gynecologic cancer deaths. Additionally, only 15% of patients are diagnosed in early stages. Meaning the vast majority of individuals are diagnosed in advanced stages, their survival rate of 30.8%. This tragic reality is largely due to a lack of early detection testing.

Other cancers, such as breast cancer, have preventive measures, such as mammograms routinely recommended; so what’s preventing ovarian cancer from having similar life-saving services?

Breast cancer is the most funded women’s health condition, surpassing ovarian cancer funding levels by billions. Over a span of 25 years, the federal government funded prostate cancer 5.5 times more than ovarian cancer, allocating $276.5 million to the ovarian and $1.53 billion to the prostate.

Given this, you may assume prostate cancer has more detrimental effects than ovarian cancer. However, ovarian cancer actually has under half of prostate cancer’s survival rate. Additionally, when comparing funding levels between the two cancers, relative to the amount of life lost due to each, prostate cancer was funded 19 times more than ovarian cancer over seven years. This significant absence of funding makes it difficult to attract young researchers to pursue new initiatives, let alone sustain ongoing research.

Unfortunately, this phenomenon does not exist in a vacuum. Despite women making up over half of the US population, women’s health as a whole is disproportionately underfunded.

Between 2013 and 2023, the National Institutes of Health’s budget increased by 58.7%; however, within the same period, the Women’s Health Research Agencies’ budget decreased from 9.7% to 7.9%. Additionally, out of the US’s $2.9 trillion budget, a measly 6% is spent on conditions affecting women. Internationally, we see the same trends, as women spend 25% more of their lives in poor health or with disabilities when compared to men. This reality has caused women to lose 75 million years of life globally.

Outside of preserving millions of years of life, supporting women’s health would significantly add to the economy. Domestically, a $350 million investment in women’s health would add $14 billion to the economy. Additionally, globally addressing women’s poorer health outcomes would add a minimum of $1 trillion to the global economy by 2040.

Women’s lives deserve to be valued. The absence of funding for ovarian cancer is just one example of the neglect women experience due to a globally broken system. Ovarian Cancer Awareness Month is over, but the international neglect of women’s health is not. Women’s health should not be limited to a month on the calendar. Research, treatment, and prevention efforts must continue throughout the year.

author: Sharon Zhang
title: US Embassy Aide Suppressed Report on Israeli Killings of Americans in West Bank
content:
David Milstein, top aide to Ambassador Mike Huckabee, has wielded enormous power in US-Israel policy decisions.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

A Senate request for information on the Israeli killings of Americans in the occupied West Bank was recently blocked by a top aide to U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee, David Milstein — a pro-Israel extremist who has quietly taken over a huge breadth of U.S. policy decisions on the genocidal state.

In March, a group of more than 30 senators, led by Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Maryland), requested that Huckabee and the State Department release information about nine Palestinian Americans killed by Israeli forces and settlers in the West Bank since January 2022.

According to bombshell reporting by The New York Times, who interviewed 15 officials in the embassy and in Washington, Milstein in response “suppressed a detailed report that the embassy staff had written, effectively stonewalling lawmakers’ efforts to gain information” on the killings. In that report, diplomats found that U.S. officials had made little progress in the investigations of the Americans’ deaths, and had closed some cases. They further found that nobody had been charged.

Milstein blocked that report from being sent back to Congress, arguing that the embassy should instead say that Israel was handling the investigations well.

The State Department responded to Van Hollen on May 4, saying that the embassy was focused on security cooperation with Israel in the U.S.’s war on Iran, despite the ongoing ceasefire at the time, and that the U.S. was working with Israel on investigations into the killings. Last month, Van Hollen forced a vote on the killings, but that vote failed 47 to 51, with Sen. John Fetterman (D-Pennsylvania) voting with Republicans to block it.

“The American people deserve answers about what’s happening in the West Bank, especially when it comes to the killing of American citizens,” Van Hollen said in a statement to Truthout. “It’s unacceptable that Amb. Huckabee’s point person is participating in a cover-up and blocking access to essential information about these killings.”

“Both Republicans and Democrats alike should be outraged about the obstruction of information to Congress, and I will be demanding answers here,” the senator went on.

The suppression of that report was just one of many actions that Milstein has taken in recent months to tilt U.S. policy toward Israel and shield it from accountability, the report finds — wielding a strange amount of power within the embassy for someone with his rank, and even ruffling feathers among openly pro-Israel officials for his efforts to back its government.

Milstein, who has been in his role since April 2025, has “repeatedly suppressed or significantly revised embassy reporting on Israeli activities to present the Netanyahu government in a favorable light,” the sources said. He frequently goes to “unusual lengths to frame Israel in a positive light,” officials said, and “has blocked reporting from being sent, rewritten cables to deliver a different — sometimes opposite — message from the original, and delayed approving drafts until the topic was no longer relevant.”

He has insisted that all reports from the section of the embassy that handles Palestinian affairs go through him, which had a major chilling effect on the flow of such reports, going “from several a week to a few a month, as some staffers refrained from writing reports for fear that Mr. Milstein would block or rewrite them.”

Among the other reports he’s suppressed is one on the massive surge of settler violence in the occupied West Bank this spring, during which Israelis rampaged across Palestinian communities on a daily basis, leaving death and destruction in their wake.

In that report, the embassy reportedly suggested that the Israeli government was not taking sufficient action to stop settler violence. The Israeli government fully backs Israeli settlers and is known to be providing them with the weapons they use to siege Palestinian villages and homes.

Milstein, who is known by officials for intervening in efforts to prevent the expansion of illegal settlements in the West Bank, blocked the report from being sent. author: Sofia Little
title: The Cornell 57: How Educational Institutions Fail Women
content:
Note: This article contains discussions of rape and sexual assault. If you or someone you have experienced sexual violence, help is available 24/7. Contact the National Sexual Assault Hotline or call 1-800-656-4673.

On the night of October 19, 2024, a 20-year old Cornell University undergraduate student, identified as Jane Doe in court filings and media reports, went to the Chi Phi Fraternity house believing she was going to meet a friend. In a civil lawsuit filed in September 2026, Doe alleges that she was drugged and sexually assaulted by seven men over the course of several hours.

These are who the media have coined the ‘Cornell 7’: Matthew Ingalls, Jonathan Newell, Winston Lee, Gillio Lopes, Diego Sarabia, Scott Norris, and Scott Kretzschmar. The men have been accused of sexually assaulting Jane Doe, but they have not been criminally charged in connection with the allegations.

According to screenshots and video of the Snapchat group chat, named “Chi Phi Actives, obtained by CBS News, Newell described Jane Doe as ‘free p*ssy,’ while Ingalls wrote, ‘you can walk in and whip it out.’ Later, another fraternity brother asked whether the “shop” was still open, when referring to Jane Doe, and received an affirmative response.

The group chat reportedly included roughly 50 other members. No messages in the screenshots obtained by CBS show anyone in the group chat intervening, normalizing the behavior. The group chat raises broader questions about the conduct of the 50 men who received messages about Jane Doe that night—not just the seven men named as defendants.

Jane Doe reported the incident to the Cornell Police Department on November 8th, 2024. Cornell subsequently suspended the Xi chapter of the Chi Phi fraternity, and the seven defendants while internal university investigations ensued.

Jane Doe’s attorney, Thomas Giuffra, has said that investigators from the Tompkins County District Attorney’s Office had little contact with her and that she was not interviewed by investigators trained to work with rape survivors. Ultimately, the case was closed due to ‘insufficient evidence,’ without a single criminal charge being filed.

Instead, as Giuffra told CBS News, of the seven men that were accused, only two were expelled, while others received lesser sanctions including suspensions, workshops, or essays.

These allegations of sexual violence and institutional failures are not simply a result of 7 men, or even 57 men. This is a result of an established system of power designed to prioritize the wants and needs of men at the expense of women’s livelihood.

This phenomenon has been described as institutional betrayal. In her book, On the Wrong Side: How Universities Protect Perpetrators and Betray Survivors of Sexual Violence, researcher Nicole Bedera examines how institutions can create additional harm when they fail to respond appropriately to sexual violence. Researchers have similarly documented the psychological consequences of institutional betrayal among survivors of sexual violence.

The Cornell case is not the first time a university’s response to sexual assault has faced national scrutiny.

In 2014, student Emma Sulkowicz from Columbia University carried a mattress around campus to protest the university’s handling of her allegation of sexual assault and in 2015, Chanel Miller was sexually assaulted on Stanford’s campus, with her assaulter only serving three months in prison before being released for good behavior. Over a decade later, little has changed.

Universities have a responsibility to investigate allegations of sexual violence and provide survivors with meaningful avenues for reporting and support. When institutions fail to do so, survivors can be left navigating both the consequences of the assault and the consequences of the institution’s response.

The Cornell case has brought those questions back into public view. On September 14, 2026, Jane Doe filed a 101-page civil lawsuit against Cornell University, the Chi Phi fraternity organization, and the seven defendants. The lawsuit accuses Cornell of failing to adequately protect her and of mishandling its response to the allegations. The defendants have the opportunity to respond to the allegations in court.

The lawsuit and public outrage has prompted District Attorney Matthew van Houten to reopen the case. But it should not take this much pressure to secure justice. Accountability must extend beyond the individual perpetrators to the system and …

author: Chris Walker
title: Trump Approves WI Disaster Aid, Credits GOP Candidate Rather Than Actual Governor
content:
Trump’s announcement ignored the current Wisconsin governor, who had applied for aid back in August.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

President Donald Trump announced disaster aid for the state of Wisconsin on Wednesday in a decidedly partisan manner, crediting a Republican candidate in the state’s gubernatorial race rather than Wisconsin’s current Democratic governor, who originally made the request for aid.

“I just spoke with Tom Tiffany, who has my Complete and Total Endorsement to be the next Governor of the Great State of Wisconsin,” Trump wrote in a Truth Social post. “I told Tom that I will be approving 17.9 Million Dollars for the Severe Storms and Tornadoes that Wisconsin has experienced.”

“18 Million Dollars should help, A LOT,” Trump added. “See you soon, Wisconsin.”

The request was formally made by Gov. Tony Evers (D-Wisconsin) in August, after an EF-3 tornado and its accompanying storms destroyed homes and other structures in Menasha and additional parts of the Fox Valley area of the state in late July. The amount Trump approved is about $4 million less than what the state had requested, and the delay in approval has forced several communities’ residents to launch fundraising drives on their own.

Tiffany, who is a Republican member of the House of Representatives (and is running for governor against Democratic candidate and Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley), thanked Trump for the funds.

“Today, President Trump called to let me know that roughly $18 million in aid for Wisconsin has been approved,” Tiffany said in a statement. “I appreciate the administration responding to Wisconsin’s needs.”

Evers took on a different tone, noting the delay in funding and that the president mentioned a political endorsement as part of his announcement.

“Clearly, President Trump and Congressman Tiffany are continuing to play politics with emergency aid that’s meant to help communities recover in the wake of disasters like tornadoes and floods,” Evers said. “That’s Complete and Total Bullshit.”

Using the announcement of disaster aid funding for political purposes isn’t new to Trump — earlier this year, he made dozens of social media posts following disasters that acknowledged Republican lawmakers or candidates while largely ignoring Democrats who made requests for funds.

The Trump administration’s decisions on how to distribute aid for natural disasters frequently appear to be politically motivated.

An Urban Institute analysis in July examining Trump’s second term found that over 84 percent of aid requests from states that voted for him in the 2024 presidential race received approval, whereas only 41 percent of aid requests from states that voted for Democratic candidate Kamala Harris were approved. Additionally, aid appears to be expedited for red states, as funding is typically sent twice as fast to those places as it is to blue states.

As Trump cracks down on political speech, independent media is increasingly necessary.

author: Nehaa Bimal
title: Nanuq is king of Arctic-inspired chess set
content:
A men’s group in Cambridge Bay has helped create a Nunavut-inspired chess set that features polar bears, grizzlies, snowy owls, rabbits and muskoxen.


Clifford Nzombato plays an Arctic-inspired Snakes and Ladders game he helped create at the National Arts Centre in Ottawa. The board features northern wildlife. Players who land on an animal’s mouth slide down to its tail. (Photo by Nehaa Bimal)


Hunter Nathan Kaoslead has led the Cambridge Bay men’s group for two years. He said the idea emerged last year as the men played chess, Snakes and Ladders and cards at their weekly game nights.


“As we were playing, we said to each other, ‘Wouldn’t it be awesome if these were Arctic animal pieces?'” Kaoslead said.


Kaoslead first drew the animals on a napkin, then figured out how they could replace traditional chess pieces. He also consulted elders on names and characteristics.


The resulting Isumaniq Chess includes a polar bear, or nanuq in Inuinnaqtun, as the king; a grizzly bear, or akhak, as the queen; a snowy owl, or okpik, as the bishop; a rabbit, or okalik, as the knight; and a muskox, or umingmak, as the rook.


An inuksuk represents the pawns.


“Most of our communities have lost our language, so it was very important to get it in the game, for educational purposes for all ages,” Kaoslead said.


The squares include the English and Inuktitut names of each Nunavut community.

The reverse side of the board features

Arctic Bite

, an Arctic-themed Snakes and Ladders game. 


“One game simply wasn’t enough,” Kaoslead said.


Kaoslead developed the game with Clifford Nzombato, through their company, KT Game Centre.


Nzombato came to Nunavut in 2009 and has worked as a social worker in Iqaluit, Rankin Inlet and Pond Inlet. Last year he moved to Cambridge Bay, where he also runs Arctic Air Cabs in the community.


He said in an interview that he had picked up the first shipment of the finished game while down south in late September.


“When I went to the warehouse to pick it up, I nearly fainted,” he said. “I mean, it’s come to life.”


The first production run is 2,500 games, which are available to purchase online for $120 each. 


The game sets are manufactured in China and Nigeria because the company could not find an affordable Canadian producer, said Nzombato, who is funding the venture himself.


He is now seeking partnerships from the territorial and federal governments, as well as Canadian gaming developers to develop an online version.  


Kaoslead said that he and Nzombato plan to start with plastic game pieces and, once those sell, invest in limited-edition pieces made by Inuit carvers.


Nzombato also wants to bring Inuit game designers into KT Game Centre, including youth.


Proceeds will support programming for the men’s group, through which members gather for cooking, games, cultural activities and time on the land, Kaoslead said.


Around 200 games have been shipped to Cambridge Bay, and he said the group is looking forward to seeing the final product.


“I can see these games coming into the men’s group as a reason to spend time together,” he said.

title: Milano viale Monza. 50 anni di vita della sede
content:
Domenica 27 settembre ci siamo ritrovati in sede per ricordare i suoi primi 50 anni di vita.


Numerose le presenze, significativa la mostra di locandine e foto d’epoca, nutrito il programma. Dopo un intervento introduttivo che ha illustrato il senso della giornata – non un retorico ricordo del passato, ma uno sprone a guardare avanti e a misurarsi con gli ostacoli e le problematiche del presente – sono intervenuti Federica Ermacora, Lorenzo Pezzica e Alberto ‘Abo’ Di Monte.


Federica Ermacora ha presentato, insieme a Selva Varengo, il suo ultimo lavoro,

Contro-immaginari. Municipalismo libertario e femminismo comunitario

, edito da Quaderni di Paola, incentrato sul superamento dello Stato/nazione e sulle possibili alternative fondate sull’autogestione e sulla partecipazione attiva. Un intervento sostanzioso che ha preso in esame il comunalismo, il municipalismo libertario e l’esperienza della Comunità di comunità che tesse i territori in reti orizzontali e femministe suggerendo proposte concrete per scardinare le logiche di dominio e ripensare la giustizia sociale ed ecologica.


Dopo una breve pausa ha preso la parola Lorenzo Pezzica che ha parlato di un fatto che non è avvenuto, ma che avrebbe dovuto tenersi: le Olimpiadi Popolari di Barcellona del 19 luglio del 1936. Un evento poco conosciuto, sul quale esistono ancora pochi studi, organizzato in alternativa alle Olimpiadi di Berlino, vetrina del nazismo, e che vide l’arrivo nella città catalana di migliaia di atleti da tutto il mondo. Gli stessi atleti che, proprio il giorno dell’inaugurazione dei giochi, furono sorpresi dal golpe militare e dall’insurrezione popolare. Molti di loro scesero nelle strade al fianco del proletariato in armi, imbracciarono i fucili sulle barricate e alcuni entrarono nella Colonna Durruti. Un’occasione interessante di riflessione, quella sviluppata da Pezzica, anche sul ruolo degli storici nello studiare e nel tramandare gli avvenimenti.


Ha concluso gli interventi Alberto ‘Abo’ Di Monte che, con un ampio intervento, ha illustrato il lascito dell’Olimpiade

Impopolare

 di Milano sia dal punto di vista economico, sia da quello ecologico e sociale, ricordando anche i morti sul lavoro nei cantieri. Sebbene manchino ancora dati certi, quello che appare evidente è l’incremento indefinito dei costi, che vanno a gravare sul pubblico, e l’incertezza sulla conclusione di opere ancora in fase di progettazione; il tutto in un quadro di gestione del territorio milanese che ha mostrato tutta la sua valenza speculativa, a scapito delle infrastrutture sociali (chiusura di spazi, liquidazione di occupazioni storiche, chiusura di molte librerie indipendenti, ecc.).


Dopo la squisita cena, organizzata da Antonio, e le due torte preparate da Rosaria – una per il 50° della sede e l’altra per il compleanno di Alessio – ha preso il via il concerto di Alessio Lega. Partendo dai canti dei Moti di Lunigiana, Alessio ha percorso il lungo filo dell’emigrazione italiana fino all’America degli IWW (Industrial Workers of the World) e ai canti di Joe Hill: un concerto che, nello stile di Alessio, fatto di parole, musica e canzoni, ci ha accompagnato lungo una storia ricca di lotte, sofferenze, vittorie e sconfitte, sempre con il pugno alzato e mai in ginocchio. Una bellissima conclusione per una giornata ricca di presenze, di stimoli, di suggestioni e, soprattutto, di relazioni.


——————————————


Descrivere cos’è la sede della Federazione Anarchica Milanese e dell’Ateneo Libertario in viale Monza 255 significa, in qualche modo, parlare di una parte sostanziosa dell’anarchismo milanese dell’ultimo mezzo secolo.


Per farla breve – ma non tanto – la vita della nostra sede, e quindi della nostra attività attuale (e, si spera, futura) prende respiro da quel gruppo che affonda le proprie radici nei primi anni Settanta, con la costituzione di “Lotta Anarchica”, aderente alla Federazione Anarchica Italiana. Era il 1971 e il collettivo era inizialmente composto da compagne e compagni provenienti dal Gruppo Libertario del Politecnico e dal Movimento Anarcocomunista di Lambrate, che si ritrovavano inizialmente nella mitica Aula F della facoltà di Architettura. Costituito il gruppo, la sua sede divenne prima il Circolo Pinelli di Via Scaldasole, poi uno scantinato in via Mamiani a Crescenzago. Quando, nel 1974, al gruppo venne affidata dal congresso della FAI la redazione di Umanità Nova, esso si trasferì nei locali di via Fratelli Bozzi 29 a San Siro. Alla fine …

author: Katja Diehl
title: Zu Gast bei Phoenix: Tankrabatt, Deutschlandticket - stuck on repeat :)
content:
Nicht nur mit Journalist*innen spreche ich gerade über drei Dinge:


„Auf dem Land geht es nicht anders.“


Ich höre diesen Satz ständig und nehme ihn ernst. Mobilität ist eine tiefe Routine. Wir ändern sie meist nur, wenn sich unser Leben ändert, beispielsweise wenn ein Kind kommt oder ein Umzug ansteht. Aber ich wünsche mir, dass der Mann auf dem Land nicht nur sagt: „Es geht nicht anders“, sondern auch: „Ich will, dass es anders geht.“ Diesen Anspruch darf er an die Politik stellen.


Die Autoindustrie und die Arbeitsplätze.


Ja, an ihr hängen viele Jobs. Routiniert und ohne Steuerungseffekte fließen viel politisches Engagement und Geld in diese Branche, die dennoch seit Jahren nicht aus ihrer "Krise" kommt. Angela Merkel hat uns eine Million E-Autos bis 2020 versprochen. Das hat nicht geklappt. Wie auch, wenn man keine klaren Rahmenbedingungen setzt, immer „technologieoffen” bleibt und weiterhin Milliarden in die Subventionierung fossiler Autos steckt? Warum sollte dann irgendjemand sein Mobilitätsverhalten ändern?


Der Verkehr bleibt das Sorgenkind beim Klima.


Die Emissionen im Verkehr steigen, weil immer zu viele Neuwagen (DIENSTWAGEN!) mit Verbrennungsmotor verkauft und subventioniert werden.


Worüber würde ich eigentlich gern sprechen?


‼️ Zum Beispiel darüber, dass diejenigen, die emissionsarm unterwegs sind, endlich auch mal einen Rabatt bekommen. Ticketrabatt statt Tankrabatt.


‼️ Über eine Mobilitätsgarantie für jedes Dorf.


‼️ Über Busfahrer:innen und Lokführer:innen, deren Jobs genauso zählen wie die am Autoband.


‼️ Über Bahnhöfe, an denen sich Frauen nachts sicher fühlen.


‼️ Über Barrierefreiheit, die kein Nice-to-have ist.


‼️ Über Straßenraum, der Kindern gehört und nicht parkenden Autos.


‼️ Und darüber, dass Mobilität Daseinsvorsorge ist und kein Luxusgut.


Ich habe nicht vor, in vier Jahren wieder über den Tankrabatt zu reden. Lasst uns die Gespräche führen, die uns weiterbringen! Ich bin bereit. Wer ist dabei?

author: Julia Conley
title: Judge Orders Trump Admin to Return Phoenix Man Deported to Equatorial Guinea
content:
Ahmed Soliman has been detained since he was sent there in April under Trump’s third-country deportation policy.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

A lawyer for Ahmed Soliman, a 31-year-old Phoenix man who has been arbitrarily detained in Equatorial Guinea since April, when US immigration agents forced him onto a plane under the Trump administration’s third-country deportation policy, expressed cautious optimism and relief on Wednesday after a federal judge ruled that the Department of Homeland Security must return Soliman to the United States.

“We all frankly broke into tears of relief, and hope” when the ruling in the US District Court of Arizona was handed down, Dana Camilleri, a senior attorney at Green Evans-Schroeder, told the Arizona Daily Star.

District Judge John C. Hinderaker, who was appointed by President Donald Trump, ordered DHS to “take all reasonable steps within their control” to facilitate Soliman’s return to the US.

Soliman’s removal to Equatorial Guinea violated his due process rights under the Fifth Amendment of the US Constitution, said Hinderaker, who said the man has faced “irreparable harm” after being “unlawfully” deported.

As Common Dreams reported last month, human rights advocates have warned that Soliman has been placed at risk of being tortured in Equatorial Guinea, where he and dozens of other people deported by the Trump administration have been held at a decommissioned hotel in Malabo.

None of the prisoners have any ties to Equatorial Guinea, which Trump paid $7.5 million in one of several secretive deals, in exchange for taking deportees whom the US is barred from sending to their home countries due to their credible fear of persecution.

Last month, Soliman was targeted for arrest in Equatorial Guinea after he spoke out about the abuse that he and others have faced at the hotel.

He has since been held “incommunicado” at a jail, despite the fact that he has not been charged with a crime.

Soliman’s family in Arizona “have been left waiting, without any assurance that he is safe — or even still alive,” Jesse Evans-Schroeder, another lawyer representing him, told the Star.

A video that was shared with the press last month showed armed guards pointing a gun at Soliman and another man in the hotel lobby. According to Amnesty International, after the video was shared, Soliman was taken to an overcrowded jail where he has been denied food and access to counsel.

“The unrebutted record shows that, since his removal, [Soliman] has been confined under armed guard, assaulted, held at gunpoint, and, most recently, arrested, hooded, beaten, and held incommunicado, reportedly without food or water,” Hinderaker wrote in his order.

Since Amnesty, United Nations rights experts, and US Rep. Adelita Grijalva (D-Ariz.) have raised alarm about Soliman’s case, DHS has been dismissive of his ordeal, sneering in one social media post that a New York Times article on the case was a “poor excuse for a sob story” and that he and another detainee, Samson Birhane, “are CRIMINAL ILLEGAL ALIENS with rap sheets a mile long.”

Soliman arrived in the US when he was 4, after his family fled Egypt, where they had faced persecution due to their political activities.

He lost his immigration status after being convicted of driving under the influence in 2021. Soliman has said in media interviews that he developed substance abuse problems as he came to terms with his identity as a gay man, having grown up in a conservative household.

He served two-and-a-half years in prison after the car accident that led to his conviction. While serving his sentence, Soliman “rehabilitated himself, confronting the ‘self-hatred’ he said led to his addiction,” the Star reported.

US Immigration and Customs Enforcement ordered his deportation in October 2025. His attorneys had won protections against his deportation to Egypt, based on his LGBTQ+ identity and his family’s history there.

But under the Trump administration’s third-country deportation policy and deals with dozens of governments that the White House has spent $40 million brokering, about 25,000 people have been sent to countries where they have no ties. From there, many have been sent on to their home countries, while others have been detained and faced ill treatment.

title: La fine del genocidio è la fine del sionismo
content:
Riportiamo l’intervento introduttivo del convegno svoltosi mercoledì 7 ottobre presso l’Università di Torino, organizzato dal coordinamento Torino per Gaza, dal titolo “La fine del genocidio è la fine del sionismo”. In questa introduzione vengono toccati molti nodi politici fondamentali che aiutano a capire quanto sia mistificato il dibattito attorno alla resistenza palestinese da gran parte dei media main stream.


L’evento è stato partecipato da più di 300 persone che hanno ascoltato gli ospiti invitati in presenza e in collegamento. Alla fine del convegno si è dato vita ad un corteo attorno al polo unversitario del campus Einaudi letteralmente circondato dalle forze dell’ordine. Infatti sono state schierate una ventina di camionette, un idrante e centinaia di poliziotti in assetto antisommossa e in borghese. La governance universitaria si è piegata a questa ennesima militarizzazione del dissenso, i cui effetti ricadono su chiunque viva lo spazio universitario. In un momento in cui vengono approvati decreti che vogliono bollare come antisemita ogni voce in disaccordo con le politiche genocide di Israele crediamo sia ancora più importante dare spazio alle ragioni che animano la solidarietà al popolo palestinese e alla sua resistenza. Buona lettura!


Buonasera a tutti e tutte,


Vogliamo ringraziarvi moltissimo per essere qui oggi con noi e, soprattutto, per essere qui ad ascoltare i nostri ospiti. Con noi oggi abbiamo Adel, della rete Samidoun, è una rete internazionale di organizzatori e attivisti impegnati a promuovere la solidarietà con i prigionieri palestinesi nella loro lotta per la libertà. Atef, studente palestinese, e Miriam Abu Daqqa, attivista femminista palestinese e dirigente del Fronte Popolare per la Liberazione della Palestina (FPLP). 


Prima di dare la parola a loro, vorremmo spendere due parole sull’importanza di essere qui oggi e sull’importanza di un dibattito di questo tipo all’interno dell’università. 


Questo in cui ci troviamo è un luogo di sapere, di pensiero critico ma il sistema di guerra e di israelizzazione delle società sta rendendo le università un veicolo propagandistico a favore del genocidio. Le futili polemiche giornalistiche, non possono nei fatti impedirci di far emergere un’analisi completa che permette di leggere eventi come il 7 ottobre nella loro storicità ma soprattutto di assumere lo sguardo dell’oppresso e un approccio decoloniale per comprendere gli sconvolgimenti del presente.


Il sapere viene utilizzato per  mantenere una precisa torre d’avorio: quella del potere. 


Il sistema della formazione dentro cui veniamo educati, sin dai primi anni di scuola, ci insegna unicamente ad acconsentire, a stare zitti, a non interrogarci, ma soltanto a integrarci ad un sistema di sopraffazione e violenza.


Basti pensare che, ad esempio, in cinque anni di scuola superiore, nessun programma affronta davvero il colonialismo. Nessuno affronta la storia della schiavitù, della segregazione dell’Africa e della sua spartizione secondo gli sporchi interessi europei. 


a Nessuno viene insegnato che, tuttora, per avere un’Europa ricca e benestante (sempre per pochi) è necessaria una periferia, uno scarto, un luogo di lavoro, di sfruttamento e di povertà. E questo luogo viene rappresentato dai Paesi del Sud globale.


A Nessuno viene insegnato che gli Stati Uniti d’America hanno macellato e distrutto interi territori del Medio Oriente per il puro controllo delle risorse e del petrolio.


in virtù di questo appare chiaro che raccontare la verità è un compito sempre più nobile e sempre più difficile, soprattutto quando le aule vengono negate, i microfoni vengono spenti, e le voci vengono silenziate.


Il 7 ottobre 2023, il muro che ha confinato la popolazione di Gaza per oltre vent’anni si è aperto per la prima volta. È bene sottolineare come il 7 ottobre non sia stato l’inizio del genocidio, bensì l’inasprimento e l’innalzamento di uno sterminio che era già in corso a “bassa intensità”, da quasi ottant’anni. Non possiamo non leggere questa data come un evento che si inscrive all’interno di precise coordinate storiche, dentro un processo coloniale feroce e dentro un regime di apartheid. La strumentalizzazione di questa data è direttamente imputabile alla volontà di continuare questo genocidio, che ormai non riguarda più soltanto la Palestina, ma tutto il Medio Oriente.

author: Unknown
title: Ilya Kharkow - Spotlight on Ilya Kharkow
content:
Author

: Ilya Kharkow

Title

: Spotlight on Ilya Kharkow

Subtitle

: Anarchism, Ukraine, and war in the new book THE MINING BOYS

Date

: 08/10/2026

Source

: https://www.radonjournal.com/interviews/ilya-kharkow-mining-boys


Ilya Kharkow is a writer from Ukraine who refused to fight. After nine months of trying to escape the country, he finally crossed the border. That experience became The Mining Boys, a novel about war and the cost of staying alive. His work explores masculinity, queer identity, and life in wartime Europe.


 More of his work can be found at ikharkow.com


1. Why do you write books that some people probably shouldn’t read?


 Because not every book wants to be liked.


 You know, I’m a gay guy from a homophobic country. A bookworm from a mining town. A pacifist at a time when everyone demands that I die for a country.


 I simply describe my life in Ukraine and in exile. People do the hard work of finding it offensive. That makes it even more fun.


2. What’s the biggest misconception about your work?


 At first glance, my work looks like it’s about war. It isn’t. It’s about what war does to intimacy. I’m interested in people, not governments.


 My short story “Hotel,” for example, is about guys trying to go on sex dates while hiding from forced mobilization.


3. Do you keep a journal / notes?


 Some people pray when they’re afraid. I take notes. That’s probably the biggest difference between me and healthy people.


4. Bataille, Mishima, and Palahniuk all influenced your writing. What’s one book by each that you’d recommend?


 I’d recommend throwing all your books away and going outside. Don’t even read me. To hell with literature. Grab your friend and go swim in the nearest lake. Eat something greasy. Food poisoning is an underrated teacher. Then come back to Bataille, Mishima, and Palahniuk.


5. Who are some contemporary writers (besides Palahniuk) you’re excited about, and why?


 Over the past month, four different people recommended that I read Denis Cooper.


 Then, a few nights ago, I couldn’t sleep. In moments like that, I usually choose between masturbation and self-improvement. That night, I chose self-improvement and decided to Google Denis Cooper.


 Damn... the more I read about his books, the more I thought: I wish I’d written that. And that. And that.


 Then I realized why I’d never heard of him. He’d barely been translated into Russian. His subjects, his tone of voice, the intention behind his writing – they all felt strangely close to me. Suddenly it hit me that my own books will probably never be published in Russian for the same reason.


 So there really are nights when masturbation is the better choice.


6. What projects are you working on right now that we can look forward to?


 I just finished the second volume of Holes in the Shape of Humans and returned toThe Mining Boys.


 There’s still one publisher considering the novel. I sincerely hope they reject it this autumn. When they do, I’ll make it available on my website.


 The best thing about having no publisher is having no limits. I have no contracts, no sponsors, no permanent address, and no country whose censorship I need to worry about. My only responsibility is my own conscience. And I intend to use that freedom to prove that a world without violence is possible. If that made you smile, let me remind you that in wartime, being a pacifist can be dangerous as hell.


7. What was the reader reaction to the first volume?


 I thought I knew what my work was worth. My readers disagreed.


 Only two people paid the asking price. Everyone else paid more. One reader paid $50 for a $10 book. Readers like that make it possible for me to continue after years of writing into the void.


 What stayed with me wasn’t the money. It was realizing that somewhere in the world, a complete stranger believed in my work that much.


 But what stays with me even longer are the emails and comments I receive from readers. Recently, someone from the US left a long comment on my Buy Me a Coffee page about his father, who refused to fight against Hitler. One day, I’m certain it will become one of my short stories.


8. Have you ever regretted publishing something?


 Who cares? Once a text is published, it’s already too late. Literature is a severe form of alcoholism. I only pretend to have control over it.


9. Do you listen to music while you write?


 Sometimes.


 I never get tired of literature. I get tired of myself. After …

title: Συγκέντρωση αλληλεγγύης στους/τις 3 διωκόμενους/ες για την υπόθεση της 01/07 της Θεσσαλονίκης, Παρασκευή 9/10, 09.30, στα Δικαστήρια
content:
Κάλεσμα από την

Ανοιχτή συνέλευση αλληλεγγύης στα 3 προφυλακισμένα συντροφια για την υπόθεση της 01/07 στη Θεσσαλονίκη:


Στις 10/7, 2 συντρόφια και ένα ακόμα άτομο συλλαμβάνονται από την «αντι»τρομοκρατική, ενώ η τελευταία συνδέει τις συλλήψεις με πρόσφατο εμπρησμό. Παράλληλα πραγματοποιούνται, μετά από 16 χρόνια, συλλήψεις για την υπόθεση της Marfin. Επιπλέον την Πέμπτη 16/07 συλλαμβάνεται ένας ακόμα σύντροφος με τα κανάλια να τον συνδέουν με την υπόθεση της 01/07 της Θεσσαλονίκης και την αντιτρομοκρατική να εισβάλλει σπίτι του, πραγματοποιόντας έρευνα. Τα τρία συντρόφια προφυλακίζονται με τα μίντια να επιτίθενται στον αναρχικό χώρο και τη δικογραφία να παραμένει ανοικτή.


Δύναμη ως την λευτεριά στα συντρόφια μας, που είναι στα χέρια του κράτους.


Αγώνας, αυτοοργάνωση, αλληλεγγύη


Συγκέντρωση αλληλεγγύης στον προφυλακισμένο σύντροφο


Τα ξημερώματα της 1ης Ιούλη πραγματοποιείται τριπλή εμπρηστική επίθεση σε σπίτια πολιτευτών της ΝΔ στη Θεσσαλονίκη. Η μία απο αυτές οδήγησε στον, υπό αδιευκρίνιστες μέχρι στιγμής συνθήκες, θάνατο της Βάγιας Νέστορα, μητέρας της πολιτεύτριας με τη ΝΔ, Αφροδίτης Νέστορα. Η κυβέρνηση και τα μίντια, ως είθισται, άδραξαν την ευκαιρία εργαλειοποίησης του εν λόγω θανάτου πραγματώνοντας το προεκλογικό τους σόου. Ως συνήθως, στο στόχαστρο των ερευνών, βρέθηκε για άλλη μία φορά ο α/α χώρος, με τα μίντια να συντηρούν το αφήγημα της κυβέρνησης, παρουσιάζοντας τον αντιεξουσιαστικό χώρο ως τη μήτρα παραγωγής υπόπτων, προδικάζοντας την υπόθεση πρωτού αυτή φτάσει στα χέρια της αστικής δικαιοσύνης.


Εννιά ημέρες μετά, η αντιτρομοκρατική προχωράει στη σύλληψη του συντρόφου Χάρη Σ., της συντρόφισσας Γεωργίας Β. κι ενός ακόμα ατόμου, ενώ στις 16/7 συλλαμβάνεται και οδηγείται στη ΓΑΔΘ ο σύντροφος Αίμονας Τ., με μοναδικό στοιχείο ενοχής την ψευδομαρτυρία του τρίτου συλληφθέντα. Ελλείψει στοιχείων, παρά την άρνηση όλων των κατηγοριών και ενώ δεν δόθηκε το περιθώριο εξέτασης μαρτύρων υπεράσπισης από την ανακρίτρια, αποφασίζεται η προφυλάκιση των δύο συντρόφων και της συντρόφισσας, οι οποίοι οδηγούνται στις φυλακές Λάρισας, Δράμας και Κορυδαλλού. προκειμένου να ολοκληρωθεί το αναγκαίο αφήγημα κράτους-μίντια, περί της ύπαρξης τουλάχιστον τριών δραστών και να αποκατασταθεί η “κοινωνική ειρήνη”. Παράλληλα, τα ειδησιογραφικά ασκώντας άριστα την ποταπή δουλειά τους διαρρέουν φωτογραφίες της συντρόφισσας και του συντρόφου από τυχαίες κάμερες της πόλης, ποινικοποιώντας για ακόμα μία φορά τις συντροφικές και φιλικές σχέσεις εντός του χώρου. Φυσικά, ο πολιτικός χρόνος στον οποίο συμβαίνουν τα παραπάνω δεν είναι τυχαίος. Είναι εμφανές πως το ελληνικό κράτος έχει εισέλθει σε καθεστώς πολεμικής προετοιμασίας και επομένως σε καθεστώς θωράκισης απέναντι σε εσωτερικούς εχθρούς. Εχθροί οι οποίοι κατασκευάζονται και παρουσιάζονται με μαεστρία από τον κρατικό μηχανισμό, με στόχο τον αποπροσανατολισμό του δημόσιου διαλόγου από τους υπαίτιους της εκμετάλλευσης και εξαθλίωσης των ζωών μας.


Δεν μας εκπλήσσει η χυδαία στάση μπάτσων, δημοσιογράφων και δικαστών απέναντί μας, αλλά ούτε και η αναξιοπρεπής μεταχείρηση και ο ευτελισμός του θανάτου ενός ατόμου της “δικής τους πλευράς”, με τα στελέχη της ΝΔ να παίζουν ένα ντροπιαστικό και συνάμα θλιβερό θέατρο στα κανάλια, προκειμένου να ασκήσουν συναισθηματικές πιέσεις στο κοινωνικό σύνολο. Οι τακτικές αυτές στοχεύουν διαχρονικά στην αποδυνάμωση και διάσπαση του α/α χώρου μέσα από ψεύδη και βρώμικα πολιτικά παιχνίδια.


Απέναντι σε όλη τη λασπολογία, τη χυδαιότητα και τη στοχοποίηση του αντιεξουαστικού κινήματος απαντάμε πως όχι μόνο τρόμο δεν αισθανόμαστε, αλλά τώρα, πολύ περισσότερο από ποτέ, μπροστά στην ολομέτωπη επίθεση που συλλογικά δεχόμαστε, δεν σκύβουμε το κεφάλι. Όσο προσπαθείτε να καταστήσετε κανονικότητα την υποτίμηση της ανθρώπινης ζωής, τόσο οι αγώνες μας θα μπαίνουν ανάχωμα στα σχέδιά σας. Στεκόμαστε πλάι στα συντρόφια μας με υπερηφάνεια, υψώνοντας τις φωνές μας ωστέ να μην σας αφήσουμε να ξεχάσετε πως οι δολοφόνοι είστε εσείς.

title: Hüseyin Olan: AKP uses all state resources for its own interests in Bitlis
content:
A long-running road problem in Aladana village in the Hizan district of Bitlis (Bedlîs) has pushed residents to the point of revolt.


Road repair work carried out by teams from the Bitlis Special Provincial Administration on the Horozdere Group Road has raised many questions after Aladana, a village largely inhabited by Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) voters, was left without asphalt.


DEM Party MP for Bitlis Hüseyin Olan spoke to ANF about the extent of the Justice and Development Party’s (AKP) partisanship in Bitlis and across Kurdistan. Olan said, “The AKP has now become a party-state. It uses all the resources of the state for its own interests and discriminates in the provision of services between those who vote for it and those who do not.”


‘AKP invests in villages where it receives the most votes in Bitlis’


The failure to asphalt the road to Aladana village, where most residents are the DEM Party voters, has sparked strong reactions during repair work on the Horozdere Group Road launched by the Special Provincial Administration in the Hizan district of Bitlis. While teams from the Bitlis Special Provincial Administration laid asphalt on the Horozdere Group Road, the entrance road to nearby Aladana was left unpaved, raising questions over the decision.


Aladana residents are being deprived of services they should receive in return for the taxes they pay. After rainfall, vehicles are often unable to reach the village, forcing residents to walk four kilometres to get home.


Heavy snowfall in winter brings life virtually to a standstill. Children cannot attend school, people who fall ill wait for hours for help to reach hospital, and villagers are effectively confined to their homes.


DEM Party MP for Bitlis Hüseyin Olan, who has repeatedly brought the conditions faced by Aladana residents to the attention of parliament, said the situation was entirely politically motivated.


Olan said the road problem in Aladana falls under the responsibility of the Bitlis Special Provincial Administration and pointed to services being distributed according to political preferences.


Olan said the AKP holds the majority in the Special Provincial Administration. He said, “The AKP administration in the Special Provincial Administration acts as it pleases, directing these investments to villages that are close to it and where it receives the most votes. We have raised this issue many times, but they continue their partisan approach.”


‘They arrested one of our council members and secured the majority’


Olan said the political balance resulting from the Provincial General Council elections also affects the distribution of services. He said the 12-12 balance between the DEM Party and the AKP in the Provincial General Council was disrupted ahead of the council presidency and commission elections on 1 April when a DEM Party member was arrested on the pretext of “Rojava protests.”


Olan said this enabled the AKP to take control of both the presidency and all commissions. He continued: “In the Provincial General Council elections, we as the DEM Party had 12 members, while the AKP had 11. The AKP brought in a member from the New Welfare Party (YRP), creating a 12-12 balance. But in January, using the Rojava protests as a pretext, they detained and arrested one of our council members. Our colleague was later released, but the court subsequently issued another arrest warrant against him. In the renewed elections in April, the AKP had 12 members while we were left with 11, and as a result they took both the presidency and the commissions. After the AKP achieved this result, our council member was released. We see the same partisanship in the KÖYDES elections. KÖYDES, which has a separate budget, is essentially the body responsible for providing services to villages. In KÖYDES elections, members of the KÖYDES Commission are selected from village heads and council members. To put it plainly, in every election the village heads tend to side with the government. This weakens our position because decisions there are also made according to who holds the majority, and services are directed to the places they choose.”


‘Bitlis governor’s response amounts to an admission: Those who hold the honey lick their fingers’

title: KJK: We should demand Öcalan’s freedom louder
content:
The Kurdistan Women’s Communities (KJK) Coordination issued a statement on the anniversary of the 9 October Conspiracy, saying: "9 October 1998 marked one of the major turning points in the history of the Kurdish genocide. The global and regional alliance of international and regional powers that paved the way for the Kurdish genocide has gone down in history as one of the dirtiest and most dangerous alliances and conspiracies in the history of the Middle East and the world. Abdullah Öcalan, who was captured as the conspiracy unfolded, has been held under unprecedented conditions on Imrali Island for 28 years and has mounted an unparalleled resistance against these conditions and his captivity. We first salute Öcalan for this resistance, which enlightens us, strengthens us and guides us, and we renew our pledge and determination to bring the struggle for freedom and democracy to success along Öcalan’s path."


The KJK added: "Beginning on 9 October itself, thousands of our martyrs formed a circle of fire and blood around Öcalan in an effort to thwart this conspiracy. Throughout almost every day of this 28-year conspiracy, martyrs have been lost in all areas of our struggle. Each of our martyrs is a symbol and a great value of the struggle against this conspiracy. Every martyr whom we commemorate with respect and gratitude has illuminated our path and left us the values of humanity for which they sacrificed themselves. As those who remain, it is now our turn to carry this great and sacred legacy towards construction, liberation and success. Successfully fulfilling this great task is our pledge to Öcalan and our martyrs and reflects our determination. The path to success begins, above all, with Öcalan’s physical freedom. Without forgetting this reality for even a moment, thwarting the 9 October conspiracy and transforming the circle of fire that our martyrs formed around Öcalan into a circle of freedom stand before us as a duty to humanity. Both the process of democratic integration and the long-term struggle for democratic socialism depend on this in order to gain momentum."


The whole world is in a ring of fire


The statement continued: "As the international conspiracy enters its 28th year, not only the Middle East but the entire world is engulfed in a ring of fire. At precisely such a time, reassessing and analysing the conspiracy and taking action is no longer an issue solely for the Kurds and forces engaged in revolutionary struggle. The political and social earthquake caused by the international conspiracy launched 28 years ago against Abdullah Öcalan, the leading figure of Democratic Modernity, no longer affects only the Kurds, but the entire Middle East and the world. As capitalist modernity sought to redesign the world beginning in the 1990s, following the collapse of real socialism, it also sought to erase everything associated with socialism from humanity’s collective memory.


The system of capitalist modernity, seeing Öcalan’s historic role and influence and regarding him as a dangerous obstacle to its interests, developed the international conspiracy against him. In this sense, the purpose and consequences of the 9 October international conspiracy are becoming clearer with each passing day. The 9 October conspiracy was not confined to a particular period or place. It became permanent and has continued as a destructive mentality and method directed against all peoples and women. Looking at developments over just the past five years, from Latin America to the Middle East, makes the gravity of the situation clearer. Global capital seeks to ensure its own continuity by keeping forces it cannot bring under its control trapped in a spiral of war through conspiracies. Öcalan, in response, has acted with historical and strategic foresight. Above all, he has stressed the need to defend social existence under threat of destruction, demonstrating that liberation cannot be achieved by any one entity alone. He conceptualised this reality as democratic integration, further strengthening relations among peoples and social forces. Drawing on his historical experience, he reformulated communalism in the form of Democratic Modernity and presented democratic integration as its political formula. By countering each emerging conspiracy with a new strategy for a solution, Öcalan has sought to break not only the established patterns of the capitalist system but also those of the social forces struggling against capitalism …

title: Kurdish Movement: There are no longer any obstacles for delaying steps regarding Öcalan’s freedom
content:
In a statement about the peace and democratic society process, the leadership of the Kurdish freedom movement announced further steps by its armed forces. According to the statement, the forces that had remained in Turkey until now have also been fully withdrawn in recent days. At the same time, four war tunnels and positions in Metîna, west of Zap, have been evacuated.


The Movement Leadership stated that this completes the implementation of the consequences arising from the decision to end the armed struggle against Turkey. Responsibility now lies with the political leadership in Ankara. In particular, there is no justification for any further delay regarding Abdullah Öcalan’s freedom, free working and communication conditions for the Kurdish leader, and further legislative measures, it underlined.


In its statement, the Movement Leadership also reviewed the course of the peace process to date, criticized the form of the framework law adopted in August, and called on social and democratic forces in Turkey to actively engage in the process.


The statement on Thursday reads as follows:


From the end of the armed struggle to a political solution


“Two years have passed since Rêber Apo [Leader Abdullah Öcalan] responded to Devlet Bahçeli on October 23, 2024, stating that he had the power to place the conflict on a political and legal footing. Over these two years, Rêber Apo has made tremendous efforts and brought the process to its current stage. Following Rêber Apo’s call of February 27, 2025, our movement declared a ceasefire. At its 12th Congress, held from May 5 to 7, it dissolved the PKK and ended the armed struggle against Turkey. At the same congress, it was also decided that Rêber Apo should lead the peace and democratic society process in all its dimensions. This once again reaffirmed the commitment to a democratic and political solution to the Kurdish question that Rêber Apo had already expressed in 1993.


On July 11, 2025, KCK Executive Council co-chair Besê Hozat, together with 30 comrades, burned their weapons as a symbol of their determination to end the armed struggle against Turkey. This made our strategic transformation concretely visible. Following our decision to end the armed struggle, the guerrilla forces that had been gradually withdrawn from Turkey were also presented to the public on October 26, 2025, together with our comrade Sabri Ok, a member of the KCK Executive Council. They declared their determination to end the armed struggle and continue the struggle through democratic and political means.


Rêber Apo and our freedom movement have stated unequivocally in numerous declarations that they have chosen to pursue a solution to the Kurdish question on the basis of democratization. The Kurdish people, as well as public opinion in Turkey and around the world, welcomed and supported this position adopted by our movement. They emphasized that the stance taken by Rêber Apo and the PKK will usher in a new phase for Turkey and the Middle East. For two years, there have been no armed clashes in Turkey, and not a single young Turkish or Kurdish person has lost their life in such clashes. This alone demonstrates the value of the peace and democratic society process.


Democratic integration as the basis for a solution


Not only Kurds, but everyone in Turkey who seeks democratization is convinced that all sections of society in Turkey will benefit if this process achieves its intended goal. They have experienced firsthand that the Kurdish question, unresolved for a hundred years, lies at the root of all problems. Tens of thousands of people on both sides have lost their lives. Trillions of dollars have been spent on the war. The Kurdish question has been a vulnerability for the Turkish state not only in domestic politics but also in foreign policy. The most serious consequence, however, is the alienation that has emerged between the Kurdish and Turkish peoples, despite having lived alongside one another as neighbors for nearly a thousand years. An alienation and antagonism have developed between the Kurds and the Turkish state on a scale unseen at any point in centuries.


The peace and democratic society process aims to end this antagonism and armed conflict and, through democratic integration, overcome the multifaceted alienation between Turkey and the Kurds. title: Berlin Twinning Association visits partner city Dêrik
content:
A delegation from the Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg–Dêrik Twinning Association has been visiting its partner city of Dêrik in Rojava since September 28. During meetings with the city’s new leadership and visits to schools, healthcare facilities and water projects, the focus has been both on political and administrative changes and on continuing the long-standing partnership.


At the beginning of the visit, the delegation met Dêrik’s new mayor, Mihemed, and her deputy, Carlos Kori. The discussions focused on the current integration process in Syria, changes to municipal structures and future cooperation with Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg. During an official reception, the delegation also met Şero Şero, who holds an important regional role as district governor.


“Reliable relationships at the municipal level are particularly important at a time when political and administrative structures are undergoing fundamental change,” said Janosch Tries, a board member of the Twinning Association.


Featured image © Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg–Dêrik Twinning Association e.V.


Economic crisis weighs on daily life


The political changes are unfolding against the backdrop of an ongoing severe economic crisis. Sharp increases in fuel prices are driving up the cost of daily life. Numerous public-sector employees, including doctors at state hospitals, are still waiting to receive their salaries. At the same time, many internally displaced people continue to live in camps in the greater Dêrik area. Healthcare is also shaped by the long-term consequences of the war that has continued since 2011. Thousands of doctors have left Syria, and access to medical care remains limited, particularly in rural areas.


Mobile clinic serves 19 villages


The Berlin delegation accompanied several visits by the Mobile Clinic, which has been operating with support from the Twinning Association since 2020. Established jointly with the Foundation of Free Women in Syria (SJAS), the project is aimed particularly at women and children in remote communities, where the nearest healthcare facility is often far away. The Mobile Clinic visits 19 villages in the surrounding area of Dêrik every month. Last year, more than 1,000 women received medical care through the project. In addition to examinations and treatment, its services include first-aid courses and medical information sessions.


Schools face switch to Arabic


The political changes are currently particularly evident in the education sector. The delegation visited four schools that had been renovated with support from the Twinning Association and its partner organizations. In recent weeks, Kurdish students and families in various parts of Rojava have protested against restrictions on Kurdish-language education. “Our language is Kurdish—and we have a right to it,” was one of their central demands.


Teachers at the schools visited by the delegation also reported sudden changes. Instructions from Damascus require most teaching to be switched to Arabic. For many children, this poses a significant challenge, as they have grown up speaking Kurdish in their daily lives. “This abrupt transition is extremely difficult for the children. But what are we supposed to do? If we don’t follow the Arabic curricula, they won’t receive a school-leaving certificate,” one teacher said.


According to teachers, there have also been changes to religious education. Whereas lessons previously covered different religions and shared ethical values, the new curricula have a markedly more conservative Islamic orientation.


Further water projects planned


Another focus of the visit is water supply. During a meeting with the responsible water authority, the delegation discussed the continuation of joint projects. These efforts build on the solar-powered well completed in the Şehîd Xebat neighborhood in 2024. The facility supplies around 5,000 people with drinking water. The talks are intended to identify areas in which cooperation on water supply can be continued and expanded through additional projects.

author: Chris Walker
title: Trump Admits He Wants to Privatize Social Security
content:
“I wanted to do it so badly,” Trump said of his desire to privatize Social Security in his first year in office.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

In remarks to reporters at the White House on Wednesday, President Donald Trump admitted that he wanted to push for privatizing Social Security in his first term in office, contradicting campaign promises he made in 2016 and earlier that he wouldn’t touch the popular social safety net program.

“I wanted to ride with Social Security being fully invested in the stock market, in the first month of my first year, so 2016,” Trump said, errantly conflating the year he was elected to the year he was inaugurated.

Trump complained that he wasn’t able to do so due to “tremendous criticism from the Democrats and some Republicans.”

Trump: I wanted to ride with Social Security being fully invested in the stock market. But I was met with opposition from Democrats and Republicans. pic.twitter.com/wv15WCI7Ze

Trump then reiterated his desire to privatize the program. “I wanted to do it so badly,” he said.

Trump described so-called “Trump Accounts,” investment accounts for children in the U.S., as “a version” of what Social Security privatization could look like — confirming observers’ fears that the accounts were a means to eventually overhaul the program.

At many points during his 2016 presidential campaign — and in the years prior to announcing a run — Trump denounced the idea of cutting Social Security as a way to reduce costs for the program, using his stance to differentiate himself from GOP rivals. But budget proposals he has sent to Congress as president have included deep cuts to Social Security.

A 2025 analysis published by Edward Lane, a professor at the Levy Economics Institute of Bard College, argued against the idea of privatization, noting that the privatization of similar retirement and social safety net programs around the world has failed.

“It is financially impossible to replace the scope of current Social Security benefits in the private market without a substantial increase in cost,” Lane noted, adding that there is also an increased financial risk in tying Social Security to the markets, as privatization “would subject retirement savings to stock market volatility, potentially leaving retirees with significantly reduced benefits during economic downturns.”

“The bottom line is that privatizing Social Security programs has not worked elsewhere, as benefits for many groups have been curtailed where it has been implemented. There is no reason to expect a different result in the U.S.,” Lane explained.

Social Security remains extremely popular among most Americans. An AARP poll published in August found that 95 percent of respondents view the program as important. Furthermore, 91 percent of Americans want Congress to enact legislation to protect Social Security so that it remains available to future generations, the survey found.

author: Shireen Akram-Boshar
title: As French Police Teargas Students, Trump Blames Protests on “Mass Migration”
content:
Over 200 students have been injured as police fired teargas and used batons against the youth protestors.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

On Tuesday, Trump took to his social media platform, Truth Social, to smear the student mobilizations spreading across France as caused by “out of control mass migration” and “Islam wanting to take over.”

Other right-wing politicians and commentators echoed these spurious claims.

“This will come to America if the Democrats take power again,” claimed right-wing commentator Dave Rubin on X.

Their comments came as France’s weeks-long student movement transformed into a nationwide revolt on Tuesday, with organizers and trade unions estimating some 450,000 people protesting in 40 cities across the country.

The movement began on September 21, with high school students organizing demonstrations against poor school conditions, a neglected public education system, and dilapidated buildings. The protests began in the suburbs of Paris and quickly spread, with students blockading their schools to force them to shut.

Since the movement’s start, French police have arrested some 6,000 students — a majority of them minors. Over 200 students have been injured, as police have fired teargas and used batons against the youth protestors.

On Tuesday, France’s General Confederation of Labor (CGT) — one of the country’s largest and most powerful trade unions, representing teachers and civil servants, among other workers — joined the nationwide protests.

One of the participants in Tuesday’s demonstration, a teacher named Manel ben Boubaker, told Truthout that the mobilization was “a massive success.”

“What struck me most is that it really shows the emergence of a new generation of young people in France who are refusing the world as it has been built for them — the way the education system is organized, neoliberal policies, racism, the way our society is structured,” she said.

Manel added that 90 percent of universities in France were blockaded and shut down on Tuesday, largely by left-wing university student unions acting in solidarity with the high school protestors.

Contrary to the claims of Trump and right-wing commentators in the U.S. and internationally, Manel asserted that the student movement “is extremely organized and serious. The students have clear demands and clear slogans. They know exactly what they are fighting for.”

Manel outlined the students’ demands: more resources for public education; renovation of school buildings; free school meals; and more teachers, nurses, psychologists and social workers in their schools.

The student movement is also demanding the abolition of the university selection process and the Parcoursup platform introduced by French President Emmanuel Macron — which has restricted access to higher education, as previously high school graduates who passed their exit exam could enroll automatically in local public universities.

Manel explained that the high school student protests originated in Seine-Saint-Denis, a working-class neighborhood, in a high school largely attended by students of color. Manel works in this neighborhood.

The students, she said, “are making connections very explicitly” between the negligence at their schools, Palestinian liberation, and racism and Islamophobia.

“There are slogans about racist violence in schools, about the banning of abayas and the wearing of the hijab — in other words, about Islamophobia. We also see many Palestinian flags and Congolese flags,” she said.

“These students are part of a generation that is becoming politically conscious around questions of genocide and mass violence around the world. They are deeply outraged by what they are witnessing.”

But they are also building on a long tradition of mass protest and revolt in France, including by students and youth, dating back to May 1968, when student protests against grievances at French universities eventually grew into a general strike that paralyzed the national economy. Student movements in France have become commonplace — though today’s are being described as the most powerful student-led movement since May 1968.

“The students are mobilizing around issues that I have also fought over for many years,” Manel explained. “I personally took part in major education struggles in 2018, 2019 and 2020, as well as in the 2024 emergency plan mobilization in Seine-Saint-Denis. We went …

title: It's DAF Day! Wait...What's a DAF?
content:

If you have a DAF, consider supporting EFF today.


Decisions about your privacy, encryption, artificial intelligence, online speech, and digital security will determine whether technology empowers people or concentrates power in the hands of a few. A grant from your DAF to EFF supports our mission to ensure that technology remains a force for freedom, innovation, and human rights.  

 

 


If you’ve never heard of a DAF, just think of it as a

bank account for your giving with some special benefits.

 


Grants from DAFs allow you to:

 


Simplify your taxes

Receive immediate tax benefits

 of multi-year gifts

Defend encryption, privacy, and security

author: Giovanna DeStefanis
title: New Poll Finds Voters Concerned about Rights and Democracy Ahead of 2026 Midterms
content:
A new national poll from The Leadership Conference on Civil and Human Rights finds that voters are increasingly concerned about threats to their rights, democracy, and the 2026 elections. The 2026 Civil Rights Monitor found that 82% of voters are concerned that rights and freedoms are being taken away or rolled back, the highest level recorded in the five-year history of the poll.

The poll, conducted by Brilliant Corners Research, surveyed 1,000 likely voters by phone between August 23 and September 6. It found that concerns about democracy are also at a series high, with 76% of voters saying they believe democracy is under a major threat. At the same time, voters report high motivation to participate in the upcoming midterm elections, with 84% saying they plan to definitely vote in November.

Protecting the freedom to vote was rated as the top civil rights priority, receiving the highest importance rating among white, Black, Hispanic, and Asian American voters as well as among Democrats and Republicans. Overall, 14% of voters identified voting rights as their top issue, tying it with border security and ranking ahead of abortion rights, which 10% selected.

The findings come as voters express potential concerns surrounding potential interference with the midterm elections. Seventy seven percent said they are concerned that political leaders could pressure election officials to change election outcomes, while 65% are concerned the federal government could attempt to stop elections by declaring a state of emergency.

Voters also expressed concerns relating to Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). In fact, 62% are concerned that ICE could appear at polling places to intimidate or interfere with voters. Opposition to ICE is particularly strong when voters are asked about the budget increase from $10 billion to $85 billion by cutting programs such as Medicare and SNAP. In fact, 71% oppose using those programs to fund the increase, including 61% who strongly oppose it.

Black voters reported particularly high levels of concern with 83% said they are very concerned about their rights being taken away. Black voters were also the group most likely to say race relations are getting worse, and 81% said their heritage, traditions, and cultural identity are under attack in the United States.

Despite widespread concerns about the state of race relations, the poll found broad agreement on the value of a diverse society. Ninety-two percent of voters said that diversity makes the country stronger, including most Republican voters.

As the 2026 midterms approach, the poll indicates that protecting voting rights remains a priority for voters across racial and partisan lines. Students have an important role to play in making sure those rights are protected. Make sure you are registered to vote at your current address and have a voting plan! Find more information at vote411.org/feminist.

author: CMI Argentina
title: Informe reveló el alto nivel de endeudamiento y atraso en los pagos en barrios populares
content:
De acuerdo a un relevamiento realizado por el Centro para la Integración Socio Urbana (CISUR) casi ocho de cada diez hogares de los barrios populares están endeudados y casi la mitad de esas familias tomó deuda para comprar alimentos.


Escuchar el reporte de Gabriel Robledo desde Radio Futura de La Plata


El informe se realizó sobre unos 420 hogares de 119 barrios populares en 15 provincias y  muestra que tres de cada diez hogares endeudados están en mora, con más de 90 días de atraso.


Fernanda García Monticelli, directora del CISUR, dijo que casi la mitad de las deudas de las familias son para comprar alimentos, “las familias están en una situación muy complicada, tienen muchos trabajos, trabajan en general más de 45 horas semanales, solamente el 15% de los encuestados tiene trabajo registrado”.


El relevamiento muestra además que la deuda promedio por hogar supera los 2 millones de pesos, mientras que el ingreso promedio ronda el millón de pesos. Es decir que las familias acumulan deudas que superan ampliamente lo que ganan en un mes.


Fernanda García Monticelli explicó que las deudas tienen tasas de intereses muy altas y las familias no llegan a pagar. “Esta situación genera mucha angustia, fue una realidad muy difícil porque muchas cuestiones de salud mental, las familias se levantan a la mañana y no saben cómo van a terminar el día y cómo van a hacer para afrontar estas deudas que se van multiplicando día a día”, relató Monticelli.


Según el relevamiento, las aplicaciones y billeteras virtuales son la principal fuente de endeudamiento. También aparecen los prestamistas del barrio y el fiado en comercios.


La directora del Centro de Integración Socio Urbana adelantó que estos datos fueron enviados a los legisladores para que lo tengan en cuenta en el debate sobre el endeudamiento de las familias que se discute en el Congreso la semana que viene.
