author: ABC-Belarus
title: The reality of released Belarusian anarchist prisoners: Why our support doesn’t stop at prison doorstep
content:
In the last two years, quite a few of our comrades left prison: some after completing their sentences, others were released as a result of pardons negotiated between the dictator and US diplomats in exchange of easing sanctions. We are preparing a longer analysis on this kind of trading and how it enables dictatorship, but today, we wanted to focus on what awaits released political prisoners on the outside and why they need even more support than before.

As a reminder, all imprisoned anarchists are put on a list of extremists and some additionally end up on the terrorist list. What is means is that once they are released in Belarus, they can’t open a bank account, can’t register a phone number, can’t register as self-employed. Of course, most employers would refuse hiring them as they can’t even transfer salary to the ex-prisoner, saying nothing of them being scared of engaging with an “extremist”. People on the extremist list can’t engage in publishing activity or teaching. Combined, this effectively pushes the released to the grey economy zone and makes them dependent on external support.

Moreover, every released person usually falls under police supervision for a period of up to 2 years. This means they have to check-in with local police weekly, be at home at specified hours, ask for permission to leave town and can’t leave the country. Most ex-prisoners feel like they were just moved to a prison with a milder security and prefer to move abroad illegally, meaning they then have a criminal case opened in Belarus resulting from violation of the supervision.

In the last two years, about 850 prisoners have been released on pardon, many of them were expelled from Belarus right from prison and ended up in Lithuania, Poland and Ukraine. These people don’t have their passports, so they need to ask for international protection or a similar humanitarian status. While they are waiting for decision, they can’t work, travel but need to be able to pay the rent and support themselves. The majority of ex-prisoners don’t speak the language of the host country or English, which limits their employment opportunities. Many experience depression and anxiety over losing access to homeland and family, the need to start from scratch in an unfamiliar place, and PTSD resulting from years of isolation. According to our in-depth interviews with released comrades, it takes over a year to regain the agency and become more independent in a new country.

There are multiple organisations and projects that try to meet the most urgent needs of the expelled prisoners. We at ABC Belarus also assign a part of our budget to the immediate or ongoing support of the ex-prisoners. Your donations are greatly appreciated and can be made at abc-belarus.org/donate

author: Trojka
title: Relacja z demonstracji w Toruniu – Nasze ulice, wasze granice!
content:
W sobotę, 3 października, wspólnie wyszliśmy i wyszłyśmy na ulice Torunia aby zademonstrować swój sprzeciw wobec rosnących nastrojów ksenofobicznych i rasistowskich.


Demonstracja odbyła się dzięki zaangażowaniu

Toruńska Grupa Anarchistyczna

 w ramach ogólnopolskiej kampanii Nasze ulice – Wasze granice organizowanej przez

161 Crew

 i

Federacja Anarchistyczna


Start spod pomnika Mikołaja Kopernika próbowała zakłócić grupa “białych obrońców Europy” , którzy czekali na nas z banerem Defend Europe. Podjęli próbę zorganizowania kontry, która gdyby nie interwencja policji, skończyłaby się dla nich utratą baneru i resztek godności.


Garstka przestraszonych chłopaczków, wspierana przez kilku napinaczy jest dowodem na to, że hasła “White power” są cały czas obecne w publicznej przestrzeni.


I, mimo że wykrzykuje je banda sfrustrowanych neonazistów, to nie możemy zapominać, że są oni użytecznym narzędziem w ręku władzy, antagonizującym społeczeństwo. Społeczeństwo, które ma uwierzyć w to, iż osoby z doświadczeniem migracji są realnym zagrożeniem dla naszej pracy, dla marnej polityki socjalnej, zaś każda osoba w drodze stanowi bezpośrednie ryzyko dla naszego życia i bezpieczeństwa.


Skrajna prawica buduje swój kapitał polityczny na strachu i ten strach chciały narzucić nam osoby “kontrmanifestujące”. Oczywiście bezskutecznie – ponieważ demonstracja ruszyła i nie daliśmy się zablokować!


Idąc ulicami Torunia, w obecności Samba Rythms of Resistance, kierowaliśmy do mieszkańców i mieszkanek przekaz “Mamy tylko siebie, tu nie ważne są korzenie” “Bez granic, bez nacji, stop deportacji” “Solidarność naszą bronią” “Otwarte serca, otwarte granice”.


Jako ruch anarchistyczny sprzeciwiamy się dzieleniu ludzi na równych i równiejszych, sprzeciwiamy się tworzeniu gett dla osób innego pochodzenia, sprzeciwiamy się ograniczaniu swobody przemieszczania się i dostępu do rynku pracy, sprzeciwiamy się traktowaniu osób migrujących jako tanią siłę roboczą, która zdana jest na łaskę barbarzyńskich agencji pracy!


Demonstracja zakończyła się w Forcie Jakuba gdzie odbył się koncert zaangażowanego HH:


Profesor Ulicy, NMCP, Erick Havok oraz punkowa załoga z Torunia z trąbką – 8Kaw.


Zarówno sobotnia demonstracja jak i cała Kampania są dowodem na to, że nasza siła tkwi we wspólnocie, kulturze oporu i pomocy wzajemnej. Pokazaliśmy i pokazałyśmy, że na próby siania nienawiści odpowiadamy jeszcze donośniejszym głosem sprzeciwu.


Nasze ulice pozostaną wolne od ksenofobii, dopóki będziemy tworzyć je razem!


Do zobaczenia na kolejnych akcjach.


Nasze ulice – wasze granice!

author: bert
title: Konto bleibt: Rote Hilfe gewinnt Hauptsacheverfahren
content:
Konto bleibt: Rote Hilfe gewinnt Hauptsacheverfahren


Die Rote Hilfe

e. V.

 hat heute auch das Hauptsacheverfahren gegen die Sparkasse Göttingen gewonnen. Das Landgericht Göttingen hat entschieden, dass die Kündigung des Kontos der bundesweiten linken Solidaritätsorganisation vom 9. Dezember 2025 keinen Bestand hat.

Bereits im Eilverfahren war die Sparkasse gescheitert. Darin 

verpflichtete zunächst das Landgericht die Sparkasse das Konto weiterzuführen

. Im Anschluss stellte das Oberlandesgericht Braunschweig fest, dass eine öffentlich-rechtliche Sparkasse ein Konto nicht ohne sachlichen Grund kündigen darf. Die von der Sparkasse vorgebrachten Gründe, dass ein erhöhter Prüfaufwand bestehe und ein Reputationsschaden bei Führung des Kontos des antifaschistischen Vereins bestehe, überzeugten das Gericht nicht.

Ein zusätzliches Risiko durch die

US

-Listung der sogenannten „Antifa Ost“ als Terrororganisation  konnte die Sparkasse nicht plausibel machen. Das

OLG

 stellte zudem klar, dass die Rote Hilfe nicht eine Organisation „Antifa Ost“ finanziert, sondern gemäß ihrer Satzung Beschuldigte und Angeklagte in den entsprechenden Verfahren unterstützt. Die

US

-Einstufung selbst entfaltet keine unmittelbare rechtliche Wirkung in Deutschland. Dieser Beurteilung des

OLG

 schloss sich das Landgericht heute »vollumfänglich« an.

Damit hat die Rote Hilfe nach den Erfolgen im Eilverfahren nun auch in der Hauptsache Recht bekommen.

Für die Rote Hilfe geht es über den eigenen Fall hinaus auch um die Frage, wie weit politische Entscheidungen und Sanktionslisten aus Drittstaaten auf zivilgesellschaftliche Strukturen in Deutschland durchschlagen können.

Hartmut Brückner vom Bundesvorstand der Roten Hilfe

e. V.

, erklärt: „Das ist ein wichtiger Erfolg für die Rote Hilfe und für alle, die sich gegen politisch motiviertes Debanking wehren. Einer Organisation die finanzielle Infrastruktur zu entziehen kann ihre Arbeit faktisch lahmlegen. Genau deshalb war es notwendig, diese Kündigung nicht einfach hinzunehmen.«

Brückner weiter: „Besonders problematisch bleibt, dass politische Entscheidungen und Sanktionslisten aus den

USA

 überhaupt solchen Druck auf zivilgesellschaftliche Strukturen in Deutschland entfalten können. Solidaritätsarbeit für Beschuldigte und Angeklagte ist keine verdächtige oder illegale Tätigkeit. Das Recht auf Verteidigung und ein faires Verfahren muss auch und gerade dann gelten, wenn Verfahren politisch aufgeladen sind.“

Die Rote Hilfe dankt der Gesellschaft für Freiheitsrechte, den beteiligten Anwält*innen, dem Netzwerk Debanking Stoppen und allen Menschen, die den Verein seit Bekanntwerden der Kontokündigung solidarisch unterstützt haben.


bert


8.10.2026 - 11:50


Pressemitteilung


Rote Hilfe gewinnt auch Hauptsacheverfahren gegen Sparkasse Göttingen. Das Landgericht Göttingen hat die Kündigung des Kontos für unwirksam erklärt. Ein wichtiger Erfolg gegen politisch motiviertes Debanking und für die Solidaritätsarbeit der Roten Hilfe.

author: Fozzie
title: Answers to review questions, Chaps 19-20.
content:
From Harry Cleaver's study guide to Marx's Capital volume 1.

3. The wage hides exploitation by making it appear that all labor is paid for, by obscuring the fact that the wage buys only what is necessary to reproduce labor power. Time wages do this through their form, e.g. an hourly wage: you work an hour you get paid for an hour, you work another hour and you get paid more, the more you work, the more you get paid. Similarly, piece wages also do this through their form: in as much as you get paid by the piece, the more pieces you produced (the more you work) the more you get paid. In both cases the real link between how much you work and how much you get paid hides the existence of surplus labor. It also hides the relationship between the wage and the reproduction of labor power. Focusing on the time or piece rate obscures the aggregate relationship which demands that these rates and the amount of work time available be such that total wages can in fact buy enough goods to reproduce the worker. The fact that some workers are not reproduced but live and die in poverty below subsistence wages, while others receive very high wages, far beyond anything one would want to call subsistence, also obscures the average class-wide situation.

6. Grades = IOU’s on future wages? The degree to which this is the case depends on the empirical relationship between the grade hierarchy and the wage hierarchy. While there is certainly no strict correspondence between the two, high grades do not guarantee high paying jobs, it is generally true that higher grades allow you to progress to higher levels of the schooling system and to acquire higher level degrees. And, there is a fair correlation between the level of degree acquired and the level of wages associated with jobs open to those with various educational degrees, e.g. Ph.D’s on the average earn much more than those with only a high school diploma. At a theoretical level, grades measure not only the acquisition of knowledge (often quickly lost) but the amount of work and self-discipline demonstrated by the student and reflected on tests, papers, etc. Moreover, obtaining higher degrees require more self-discipline and less teacher/professor-imposed discipline and thus demonstrates the suitability of the students for more "responsible" professional positions where most supervision is internalized and outside supervision is relatively indirect. Credit? Perhaps if later wages are considered payment for previous work done producing labor power. On the other hand, perhaps not, perhaps the work is never compensated for. Hide exploitation? Certainly in the short run when work is being done (producing labor power) and no real money is paid as wages. However, exploitation is analyzed by Marx in terms of the extraction of surplus value which is not the case here, immediately, but at best only later when the school work results in higher productivity and higher s/v. Then, the question is whether the forthcoming wage compensates for the earlier unpaid work? If not, then exploitation for sure.

2. If intensity of labor rises while time wages rates remain constant then the real wage, measured in terms of the value of commodities obtainable with the wage remains constant, but measured in relationship to the expenditure of energy the real wage clearly falls because more work is being done for the same money.

4. Time wage rates hide exploitation by making it appear that all labor is paid for, by obscuring the fact that the wage buys only what is necessary to reproduce labor power. Time wages do this through their form, e.g. an hourly wage: you work an hour you get paid for an hour, you work another hour and you get paid more, the more you work, the more you get paid. The real link between how long you work and how much you get paid hides the existence of surplus labor. It also hides the relationship between the wage and the reproduction of labor power. (basically the same answer as that to question 3, chap 19.

8. Wages as expression of working class power or weakness? When wages were at or close to biological subsistence they might well be seen as a measure of weakness. Workers were unable to force capital to pay them enough to live decently. But as long as, and everywhere that, wages are well above subsistence they measure the ability of workers to force capital to develop and to share in the fruits of that development. Moreover, wages provide the material foundation of much of workers ability …

author: Fozzie
title: Chapter 22: National Differences in Wages
content:
Harry Cleaver's study guide to chapter 22 of Marx's Capital volume 22.

Each country has a certain average intensity of labor.

Each country has a certain average productivity

The development of capitalism brings increases in productivity and in the intensity of labor, above average development means above average levels of these characteristics.

Suppose we have the same kind of commodity being produced during the same working time in different countries. Given the above we should expect:

Case Study #1: Spinning Industry in England and Continental Europe

Marx notes that in the spinning industry productivity, wages and the organic composition of capital (c/v)are all lower on the continent while hours of work are longer. His two main cases are Germany and Russia.

With respect to the organic composition of capital he gives data for the ratio spindles/worker (the technical composition of capital) in several countries. When speaking of Russia he notes that despite "over-work" (long hours) and "shameful under-payment of the workers" (low wages), Russian manufacturing "vegetates" due to protectionism.

Case Study #2: Railroad Construction in Eastern Europe and Asia

Marx is refering here to English business investment abroad.

English firms use both English and foreign labor, so:

Marx ends with critiques of H. Carey:

Marx's discussion of this subject is more of a cursory indication of what things should be taken into account than a systematic treatment. He starts off with a list of seven factors, but in his ensuing discussion he really only deals with two issues: variations in intensity and in productivity across countries. It's good that he does what he does, but it's unfortunate that he doesn't do more, because this subject has long been an extremely important one.

As recent work by historians Peter Linebaugh and Marcus Rediker has begun to document, along with the tendency of British capital to follow the Dutch lead in developing trade and foreign investment as international extensions of domestic operations went the internationalization of their labor force. "British" capital did not merely employ workers in England, Scotland, Wales and Ireland, but shipped them abroad and put them to work in colonies, hired polyglot crews from all nations to man their commerical and war fleets, entered the slave trade to redistribute African workers internationally and enslaved workers in every colonial area they could manage. In short, throughout virtually its entire history capitalism has been international, it has imposed work on people over as much of the world as it could conquer and has reorganized both itself and those workers in ways designed to maximize its profit and control.

With the extensive development of multinational corporations and rapid rebound of international trade in the post-WWII period such international organization and reorganization became evermore essential. The more capitalists came to operate production at a multinational level and the more international trade developed to redistribute that production globally, the more important this subject has become.

By the end of the 20th Century, capitalist attacks on higher paid workers in "developed countries" by shifting production overseas to lower paid labor pools and their drive for so-called "free trade" to facilitate the re-import of production that has been shifted abroad made consideration of international wage differentials of growing importance. The current growing use of offshore "outsourcing" of particular business operations has become a hot political topic as the slow growth of jobs during the recovery from the 2000-2001 recession has made any and all replacement of American jobs anathma to American workers and political fodder for Democratic politicians.

Therefore, we can see that Marx's interest in "national differences in wages" is not merely a casual interest in making international comparisons or constructing some United Nations-like index of development or standards of living, but in drawing attention to the unevenness of capitalist development and how that unevenness is the result of different circumstances.

Some of those circumstances, as his original list makes clear, may have to do with "natural" factors, e.g., the cost of reproducing labor in northern countries may be higher than that in the tropics because winters mean greater housing costs. But most of the factors involved are historically determined, and as we have seen …

author: infolibre
title: Συγκέντρωση αλληλεγγύης στους εξεγερμένους μαθητές στη Γαλλία, Πέμπτη 8/10, στις 19.00, στα Προπύλαια
content:
Συσπείρωση Αναρχικών


Συγκέντρωση αλληλεγγύης στους εξεγερμένους μαθητές στη Γαλλία


ΣΥΓΚΕΝΤΡΩΣΗ ΣΤΑ ΠΡΟΠΥΛΑΙΑ ΠΕΜΠΤΗ 8 ΟΚΤΩΒΡΙΟΥ 2026, στις 19.00. – ΑΛΛΗΛΕΓΓΥΗ ΣΤΟΥΣ ΕΞΕΓΕΡΜΕΝΟΥΣ ΜΑΘΗΤΕΣ ΣΤΗ ΓΑΛΛΙΑ


Η εξέγερση των μαθητών με αφορμή διάφορα εκπαιδευτικά αιτήματα σε δεκάδες πόλεις της Γαλλίας και ενώ 500 Γυμνάσια και Λύκεια παραμένουν κατειλημμένα, αντιμετωπίζεται από το γαλλικό κράτος με άγρια καταστολή, εκατοντάδες τραυματίες και τουλάχιστον 5.000 συλλήψεις, κυρίως ανήλικων διαδηλωτών.


Οι εξεγερμένοι μαθητές στήνουν οδοφράγματα, πυρπολούν σχολεία, αυτοκίνητα, επιτίθενται σε αστυνομικά τμήματα και συγκρούονται με τις δυνάμεις καταστολής δίχως να υποχωρούν.


Τα παιδιά της «κρίσης» κραυγάζουν για το παρόν και το μέλλον και πυροδοτούν μια ακόμη κοινωνική εξέγερση, όπως έγινε στον ελλαδικό χώρο το 2008, δίχως να έχουν ψευδαισθήσεις για όσα υπόσχονται οι εξουσιαστές, χωρίς να έχουν αυταπάτες για τους λόγους για τους οποίους τα πράγματα θα χειροτερέψουν.


Η «κρίση» χρέους, οι «απαραίτητες» μεταρρυθμίσεις, η προετοιμασία των ευρωπαϊκών κοινωνιών για πόλεμο, η έκρηξη του πληθωρισμού, η ενεργειακή ή πολιτική «κρίση» σημαίνουν ένα και μόνο πράγμα για τους καταπιεσμένους και εκμεταλλευόμενους: οι ζωές μας δεν έχουν την παραμικρή αξία για τους δυνάστες μας.


Να σπάσουμε τις αλυσίδες της παραίτησης,


του φόβου και της ανάθεσης.


Να πιστέψουμε, ότι το μόνο αδύνατον,


είναι να ζούμε με σκυμμένο το κεφάλι.


Η καταστολή δεν θα κάμψει τους αγώνες μας


Το τελευταίο διάστημα, στη Γαλλία έχει πυροδοτηθεί ένα εκτεταμένο κύμα κοινωνικών και μαθητικών κινητοποιήσεων. Μαθητές και μαθήτριες σε ολόκληρη τη χώρα προχωρούν σε καταλήψεις, αποκλεισμούς σχολείων, διαδηλώσεις και συγκρούσεις με τα όργανα καταστολής, διεκδικώντας αξιοπρεπείς συνθήκες εκπαίδευσης και εναντιώνονται στην ολοένα εντεινόμενη υποβάθμιση της δημόσιας παιδείας. Οι κινητοποιήσεις αυτές δεν αποτελούν ένα μεμονωμένο ξέσπασμα δυσαρέσκειας, αλλά αναδεικνύουν τις βαθύτερες αντιφάσεις ενός εκπαιδευτικού συστήματος που αντιμετωπίζει τις ανάγκες των μαθητών ως κόστος και τις κοινωνικές διεκδικήσεις ως απειλή προς καταστολή.


Υπερπλήρη τμήματα, χρόνια υποστελέχωση, ελλείψεις σε εκπαιδευτικούς, σχολικούς νοσηλευτές και προσωπικό υποστήριξης, ανεπαρκείς υποδομές και εξαντλητικά ωράρια συνθέτουν την καθημερινότητα χιλιάδων μαθητών. Πρόκειται για συνθήκες που δεν είναι καθόλου άγνωστες και στην ελληνική εκπαιδευτική πραγματικότητα. Η υποχρηματοδότηση, η απαξίωση των δημόσιων σχολείων και η μετακύλιση των ευθυνών στις ίδιες τις σχολικές κοινότητες αποτελούν όψεις μιας ευρύτερης πολιτικής που υποτάσσει την εκπαίδευση σε δημοσιονομικούς περιορισμούς, αποκλείοντας σταδιακά όλο και περισσότερα κομμάτια της κοινωνίας από την ισότιμη πρόσβαση στη γνώση.


Την ίδια στιγμή, απέναντι στις μαθητικές διεκδικήσεις, το γαλλικό κράτος επιστρατεύει την αστυνομική καταστολή, τις συλλήψεις και τη βία, επιχειρώντας να επιβάλει την πειθάρχηση και να ανακόψει την εξάπλωση των κινητοποιήσεων. Περισσότερες από 5.000 συλλήψεις έχουν καταγραφεί από την έναρξη των κινητοποιήσεων, ενώ σύμφωνα με τις γαλλικές αρχές πάνω από 170 μαθητές έχουν τραυματιστεί.


Ωστόσο η κρατική καταστολή


στις 5 Οκτωβρίου, πήρε μια ιδιαίτερα σοβαρή διάσταση. Στη Λανς, ένας 15χρονος μαθητής τραυματίστηκε σοβαρά κατά τη διάρκεια κινητοποίησης έξω από σχολείο, χάνοντας το χέρι του μετά την έκρηξη αστυνομικής χειροβομβίδας.


Η αντιμετώπιση των μαθητών ως απειλή, αντί ως υποκειμένων που διεκδικούν τα δικαιώματά τους, αποκαλύπτει τον τρόπο με τον οποίο η κρατική εξουσία αντιμετωπίζει κάθε συλλογική αμφισβήτηση της κυρίαρχης πολιτικής. Όταν οι διεκδικήσεις δεν χωρούν στα θεσμικά όρια που τίθενται από τα πάνω, η καταστολή επιστρατεύεται για να επιβάλει τη σιωπή και την επιστροφή στην κανονικότητα.


Ωστόσο, η κανονικότητα που υπερασπίζεται το κράτος είναι η ίδια που γεννά τις ελλείψεις, την ανασφάλεια και την υποβάθμιση της καθημερινότητάς μας. Είναι η κανονικότητα που απαιτεί από τους μαθητές να αποδέχονται παθητικά τις αποφάσεις που καθορίζουν τη ζωή τους, να προσαρμόζονται σε ένα σχολείο που αδυνατεί να καλύψει τις ανάγκες τους και να αντιμετωπίζουν ως αυτονόητη την αστυνομική παρουσία όταν επιλέγουν να αντισταθούν. Απέναντι σε αυτή τη συνθήκη, οι μαθητικοί αγώνες αναδεικνύουν τη δυνατότητα συλλογικής οργάνωσης, αυτοοργάνωσης και διεκδίκησης από τα κάτω, έξω από τη λογική της ανάθεσης και της παθητικής αναμονής λύσεων από τους εκάστοτε διαχειριστές της εξουσίας.


Για εμάς, η αλληλεγγύη στους αγωνιζόμενους μαθητές και …

author: Redazione_web
title: Istigazione alla cura. La medicina sotto l’attacco razzista del governo
content:
Con questo articolo le Collettive Brigate Basaglia mostrano la totale solidarietà a colleghi, colleghe e altre persone indagate per aver fatto quello che dovrebbe essere il gesto più semplice e naturale della medicina: guardare una persona prima ancora del suo documento, ascoltare una sofferenza prima ancora della sua posizione amministrativa, riconoscere un essere umano prima ancora di una categoria giuridica. Già, proprio così:

la Procura di Ravenna ha indagato di recente oltre 20 professionisti sanitari in tutta Italia (circa 23-24 medici) con l’accusa di aver emesso

falsi certificati di non idoneità

 per impedire il trattenimento di migranti irregolari nei

CPR

(Centro di Permanenza per il Rimpatrio)

.


Forse mancava solo questo. Dopo il reato di solidarietà, dopo il reato di soccorso in mare, o a chi attraversa un confine senza il permesso o senza un conto in banca abbastanza consistente, arriva finalmente il nuovo grande pericolo per l’ordine pubblico italiano: l’istigazione alla cura!


Perché se il personale medico osa fare quello per cui dovrebbe esistere la medicina — guardare una persona, ascoltare la sua sofferenza, valutare la sua vulnerabilità — allora forse, qualcosa nella macchina istituzionale “democratica” si è inceppato..


Ma forse la questione più profonda non riguarda soltanto i CPR, il personale medico o un singolo procedimento giudiziario. La questione riguarda un problema ancora più grande, l’esistenza stessa di strutture amministrative o detentive costruite attorno all’assurda idea che alcuni esseri umani possano trovarsi fuori posto (soprattutto se poveri).


Ma fuori posto rispetto a cosa? Rispetto a una linea tracciata su una mappa da quattro burocrati. Rispetto a un confine deciso nella storia. Rispetto a un documento che stabilisce chi può muoversi liberamente (soprattutto se pieno di soldi) e chi invece deve dimostrare continuamente di avere il diritto di stare da qualche parte. La guerra ai migranti poveri agita dai governi ad ogni latitudine è realtà anche per la “democrazia europea”, non un errore di percorso!


Il problema non è soltanto il modo disumano con cui questi lager, definiti strutture “amministrative”, vengono gestiti e su cui abbiamo già detto abbastanza. Il problema è proprio il principio stesso secondo cui un essere umano possa diventare irregolare, invisibile, sospeso, semplicemente perché nato dall’altra parte di una frontiera, o perché “povero”, o perché non bianco abbastanza, o non cristiano abbastanza.


Prima ancora dei CPR esiste questa maledetta dottrina: quella secondo cui il mondo sia diviso in territori appartenenti a Stati-nazione e che dentro questi territori alcune persone siano considerate legittime e altre temporaneamente tollerate, controllabili, espellibili.


È proprio dentro questa logica disumana che nasce la contraddizione più profonda, dove la medicina viene chiamata a certificare non la salute, ma la capacità di una persona di sopportare una condizione che può danneggiare la salute. Infatti, come viene affermato ampiamente anche dalla rete “Mai più lager- NO ai CPR”, di cui fanno parte alcuni dei medici accusati, è riconosciuta ormai la patogenicità, ovvero la capacità di questi centri di detenzione, di creare malattie e danni. La sola permanenza in un CPR, a causa delle condizioni profondamente dannose documentate e testimoniate, può portare infatti a gravi compromissioni della salute. Ciò è tristemente ironico, se si pensa che per definizione legislativa, in questi centri “lo straniero deve essere trattenuto con modalità tali da assicurare la necessaria assistenza ed il pieno rispetto della sua dignità”.


Ormai non è più sufficiente che una persona venga privata della libertà dentro un CPR. Non è più sufficiente che il suo corpo venga inserito dentro un dispositivo amministrativo costruito per rendere possibile l’espulsione. Ora quel corpo deve anche essere dichiarato compatibile con quella condizione assurda e disumana, la repressione chiama dunque la medicina ad essere collaborazionista di tutto ciò.


E qui emerge il paradosso. La medicina dovrebbe porsi una semplicissima domanda clinica: di cosa ha bisogno questa persona per stare meglio?


E invece non basta! In questi contesti la stessa medicina è chiamata anche a porsi ulteriori domande, domande di natura politica: questa persona può essere ficcata dentro l’ingranaggio disumano che lo Stato centrale ha deciso per lei senza che crei troppi problemi?; la possiamo rendere …

author: Marina Amaral
title: O saldo do 1º turno para a Amazônia
content:
Já temos os resultados do primeiro turno das eleições, e com um Senado dominado pela extrema direita e um STF fragilizado, as perspectivas pro meio ambiente não são boas. Isabel Seta, Marina Amaral e Ricardo Terto analisam o cenário pós primeiro turno, com foco nos impactos para a Amazônia, para os povos indígenas e para o clima – o que impacta a todos.


O episódio traz a dimensão geopolítica, em que os Estados Unidos se tornaram uma ameaça a nossa democracia, o crescimento de Flávio Bolsonaro justamente no arco do desmatamento, e também os senadores e governadores eleitos na região. Ouça agora.


E MAIS:


Uma Trombeta negacionista. E no quadro “Se é pra falar de economia…”, Clara Marinho mostra que nem sempre os indicadores econômicos se refletem no resultado das eleições.

author: Unknown
title: 12 prisoners begin hunger strike at Bukan prison
content:
The Kurdistan Human Rights Network reported that at least 12 Kurdish prisoners being held at Bukan Prison for political and religious reasons began a hunger strike on October 5 to protest pressure exerted by Iranian regime forces in prisons.


The prisoners announced in a letter to Bukan Prison authorities on 5 October that they had begun a hunger strike. They are reportedly protesting restrictions on their access to leave permits and the open-prison placement program, as well as restrictions imposed on them under prison conditions.


The prisoners whose names have been identified as participating in the hunger strike are: Ardalan Mineh, Behrouz Barakhas, Esmail Atash-Mard, Kaveh Rahimi, Hamed Maroufi, Ali Mohammadi, Mahmoud Jafari, Ali Faroughi, Arsalan Minaei, Aziz Banehei, Ghader Salimi, and Mullah Davoud.


It was reported that on the second day of the hunger strike, the 12 prisoners were transferred to the quarantine section on the orders of the director of Bukan Prison. Their phone calls and family visits are reportedly still being restricted.


A Kurd detained


Meanwhile, Faramarz Seîdî, from the city of Dehgolan in Kurdistan Province, was detained by forces from the Ministry of Intelligence using violence and taken to a detention facility operated by the ministry. It was reported that Ministry of Intelligence forces arrested Seîdî on 6 October on Esteghlal Street in Dehgolan, without a court order.

author: Unknown
title: Women murdered in Amed: A common story of violence, complaints, and failed protection
content:
In the first eight months of 2026, 197 women were killed by men in Kurdistan and Turkey. The same period also saw suspicious deaths of women and cases in which women were driven to suicide.


In Diyarbakır (Amed), one woman has died under suspicious circumstances since June, while the body of another woman who disappeared years ago was also found. Four women were also killed by men during this period.


Similar circumstances emerged behind the suspicious deaths and femicides in the city, while the families of the women killed shared a common demand: penalties must be sufficiently deterrent.


Four women killed


Interviews with the families of the women killed during this period revealed that the women had been subjected to systematic violence and were not adequately protected despite reporting the abuse to the police.


Sultan Karadağ was killed on 10 August. Sultan Kara was killed on 26 August by Ersan Akdemir, whom she wanted to divorce. Mizgin Kılıç was killed on 18 September by her former husband, and Ayfer Çakmak was killed on 27 September by her husband Orhan Çakmak, after reportedly enduring systematic violence for years.


The names and number of the women killed are more than mere statistics. Although their stories differed, they shared a common experience: they were subjected to violence, and their requests for protection went unanswered.


Mizgin Kılıç and Sultan Kara wanted to build new lives despite the violence they had endured, but they were not protected despite filing complaints. According to information provided by her relatives, Gülistan Karadağ was killed by people who had subjected her to violence and were reportedly using drugs.


Ayfer Çakmak was shot dead by her husband Orhan Çakmak, who had reportedly prevented her from even leaving the house for years. Following the killing, Çakmak claimed that her death was a suicide, saying, “The gun suddenly went off.”


Gülistan was targeted with violence and drugs


The family of Gülistan Karadağ said their daughter had been subjected to violence and threats for a long time and demanded that those responsible be held accountable. The family said: “Gülistan suffered violence and had been beaten again before she died. Who is bringing in these drugs, and how are they getting here? She constantly wanted a new beginning, a life of her own. But they never allowed her to have one. She was constantly beaten and threatened. Whoever did this must be held accountable. Our only demand is justice. We want nothing else.”


Sultan was not protected despite requesting a restraining order


The family of Sultan Kara, who was killed in front of her three-year-old daughter, said numerous complaints had previously been filed against the perpetrator. The family said Sultan had endured threats and violence for a long time: “The state is doing nothing. We lost our sister. Sultan had been married for four years. Every morning, my sister would say, ‘He is going to kill me.’ Twice, he beat her almost to death. He threatened and assaulted her. Even when Sultan was pregnant, he grabbed her by the throat and tried to kill her. His family threatened her to prevent her from filing a complaint.


Sultan had requested a restraining order when she filed for divorce. Following the decision to divorce, the perpetrator threatened both my older sister and Sultan with death. My sister is dead, while that man is walking around freely. Women are being killed and no one is taking it seriously. I want justice. Enough is enough.”


Sultan’s family said she had been subjected to violence not only by the man she wanted to divorce but also by his mother: “Sultan suffered violence both from him and from his mother. When she went to file a complaint, they sent her away, saying, ‘They are not the kind of people who would kill someone.’ Our only demand is that he receive the harshest possible sentence.”


The electronic tag was removed after the divorce


Mizgin Kılıç, who was killed by Ömer Kırıcı a year after divorcing him, had also endured violence and threats for a long time. According to her family, Mizgin left the house several times because of the violence but was forced to return after “family elders” intervened.


Ömer Kırıcı reportedly continued to stalk and threaten Mizgin even after their divorce. Mizgin was shot dead, and Kırıcı died by suicide following the killing.

author: Unknown
title: KDP seeks permission from Turkey to use roads in its own territory
content:
Organizers of the Berwarî Bala Festival in Amêdiyê, linked to the KDP, and the KDP’s 18th Branch obtained permission from the Turkish state to use the roads for the event.


A source who spoke to Rojnews about the issue said that although the decision provides some relief to citizens and festival participants, it has also raised serious concerns and questions among local residents. The source said: “This is a public and tourist road within the Kurdistan Region. However, it has become an occupied and military road. Citizens have to obtain permission from the Turkish state to travel on this road in their own territory, and their passage is subject to conditions. This permission has been granted for only three days for the festival.”


According to information obtained, the road normally used to reach these areas is 35 kilometers long. However, for the past three days, people coming from outside the city who need to travel to Kanîmasî have been forced to use a route more than 80 kilometers long that is designated for local residents and villages. This situation places a significant burden on tourists and the local population.

author: Fozzie
title: Chapter 23: Simple Reproduction
content:
Harry Cleaver's study guide to Marx's Capital volume one, chapter 23.

Production must be continuous, i.e., repeat itself, as such it is also reproduction. In capitalism reproduction is also reproduction of value advanced as capital, i.e., "self-valorizing value." (p. 711)

Reproduction requires all of the elements of production be replaced, i.e., the means of production and labor power.

Reproduction of means of production = replacement of used up raw materials and worn-out machinery, buildings, etc.(MP) (p. 711)

Reproduction of labor power = reproduction of workers and their labor power requires production of necessary means of subsistence (MS). (p. 712)

Both MP and MS are produced by workers.

the means of subsistence required for reproduction of labor power (p. 712),

variable capital (under capitalism); rare, 1/4 world's workers) (p. 714, footnote 4),

product of peasants own land/labor (under feudalism) (p. 713).

... is the "mere continuity of the production process" (p. 715)

... "converts all capital into accumulated capital" (p. 715)

=alienation of workers' labor, sold by them to capitalist (p. 716)

=alienation of workers' product, owned by capitalist, an "alien power that dominates and exploits him." (p. 716)

Worker's consumption is of two kinds:

Productive consumption of MP during work - allows capital to live

Individual consumption of MS outside work - allows worker to live

Abusive consumption: where individual consumption is merely the means to "keep his [the worker's] labor-power in motion, just as coal and water are supplied to the steam-engine." (p. 717)

At the aggregate level of the classes:

Investment of variable capital = "reconversion of the means of subsistence . . . into fresh labor power which capital is then able to exploit."

As such, "individual consumption" . . . remains an aspect of of the production and reproduction of capital."

But, "the capitalist may safely leave this [individual consumption] to the worker's drives for self-preservation and propagation." (p. 718)

With some exceptions, e.g., South American mine owners who force their workers to eat beans to increase their strength and work. (p. 718, footnote 9)

Workers' consumption above what is needed for reproduction of labor power is unproductive consumption - from capitalist point of view.

Reproduction of workers is also "transmission and accumulation of skills from one generation to another." (p. 719)

Marx gives a series of quotes from a spokesperson for English cotton textile industry who objects to any government subsidy to worker emmigration during cotton famine and high unemployment caused by American Civil War.

workers are machines that should be kept on hand and in order

if they left, it would take a generation to replace them with a new batch of skilled workers

therefore the cotton industry and other, related industries would suffer

therefore the workers should be kept via forced public works (pp. 720-22)

The Times newspaper editorial also worried:

that "human machinery will rust under inaction"

that "human machinery will, as we have just seen, get the steam up of its own accord, and burst or run amuck in our great towns" (p. 722)

Marx concludes his example by noting Parliament passed an Act "empowering the municipal corportations to keep the workers in a state of semi-starvation, i.e., to exploit them without paying the normal wages." (p. 723)

As Marx pointed out in a two-page introduction to this section of Capital, pp. 709-710, his analysis in this and the subsequent two chapters is based on a number of simplifying assumptions. The most important one in this chapter, and the one that differentiates this chapter and its discussion of simple reproduction from the discussion of expanded reproduction in the next two chapters, is that capitalists consume all of the value that their operations generate over and above that which is necessary to replace the used up means of production, e.g., raw materials, tools, and to replace their living workers. In other words this chapter deals with how production is also reproduction of all of the elements of the capitalist organization of production in abstraction from investment that generates growth, i.e., accumulation.

This said, most of what Marx writes in this chapter should already be familiar from the study of preceeding ones, especially chapter 6 that deals explicitly with the reproduction of labor power, and indeed he often refers back to previous …

author: Joseph Lee
title: From the farm to your door: How our global food system exploits workers
content:
Like many big cities, New York teems with delivery workers who bring takeout, groceries, and any number of other things to anyone with a cellphone. They work at all hours and in all conditions, often without job security, health insurance, or even

access to safe restrooms

. They are often hit by cars, assaulted, or robbed. Many of them are Indigenous people from Guatemala and Mexico who left home to escape violence and the impacts of climate change.


The worst impacts of that global crisis

add to the risks

 those

workers face

.


“When the city is hit with with massive snowstorms, floodings, or the recent smoke fires, many deliveristas are the ones who are on the front lines doing this work and responding to the climate crisis in order to take care of New Yorkers,” said Ligia Guallpa, who is Kichwa and the co-founder and executive director of the Worker’s Justice Project and Los Deliveristas Unidos. The organization organizes app-based delivery workers and advocates on their behalf. “But the reality is that often they cannot even take care of themselves.”


A report released Monday says that exploitation is deeply embedded in the global food system, leaving many of the 1.4 billion people who produce, process, distribute, and deliver food poorly paid,

inadequately protected

, and vulnerable to abuse. Climate change and a global affordability crisis are intensifying those pressures, according to the International Panel of Experts on Sustainable Food Systems, or IPES-Food, an international food policy research organization.


Although the document does not specifically focus on Indigenous peoples, it finds that many of the forces driving that exploitation have roots in the colonialism, land dispossession, forced labor, and racialized labor systems that have long harmed Indigenous communities worldwide. 


“Here we are in the United States, a country that’s founded on stealing land and the import of enslaved people to be able to make agriculture and agricultural labor possible and cheap,” said Raj Patel, an IPES-Food expert and a professor at the University of Texas at Austin. “And the legacy of that is still with us.”


The report notes that Indigenous peoples remain

particularly vulnerable to displacement

, and pressures from industrial agriculture and climate change that can undermine traditional livelihoods. For people who have been

forced off their land

 and are disconnected from those livelihoods, exploitative, low-paying work is often the only option. 


“If you put yourself in a situation of a woman who needs to feed her children, they can go to any extreme,” said Teresa Chemosop, who is Ogiek from Mount Elgon, Kenya, and the coordinator for the East Africa Indigenous Women-Led Assembly, which advocates for Indigenous women across the region. 


Read Next


The people who feed America are going hungry


Ayurella Horn-Muller


Chemosop said that Indigenous workers face severe discrimination and abuse, such as being compared to baboons and not being given utensils to eat with while working. That’s on top of low wages and long, difficult hours. 


Indigenous and intergenerational

agricultural knowledge

 is routinely minimized or dismissed as “unskilled,” the report notes, obscuring valuable expertise and helping to justify lower wages. That knowledge, which often goes back millenia, includes skills like cultivating plant medicines and drought-resistant crops. The authors call for formally recognizing that expertise alongside broader efforts to strengthen worker rights and protections.


The people who keep the global food system running do far more than grow and harvest food. They distribute it to markets and restaurants, deliver it to homes and offices, and provide care work like cooking and feeding families, often in seasonal or subcontracted jobs. Between 60 and 80 percent of food workers are informally employed — a higher share than in any other industry — and they earn about half as much as those with conventional employment. About 30 percent of food system workers, or more than 400 million people,

earn less than a living wage

.


An estimated 2.1 million people in agriculture work under forced-labor conditions, the report estimates. Migrants, who account for about a quarter of all farmworkers worldwide, are three times as likely to experience such conditions and are more likely than their peers to die on the job.


Despite their importance in feeding the world, these workers do not receive …

author: Dominic Gutoman
title: Badoy red tags UP Rural High School teacher, community
content:
A teacher and the community of UP Rural High School are the recent targets of red-tagging by former National Task Force to End Local Communist Armed Conflict (NTF-ELCAC) spokesperson Lorraine Badoy.

On October 6, Badoy red-tagged UP Rural High School teacher Trist’n Buenaflor. Before this, Badoy, in a series of Facebook posts, also red-tagged faculty members and students of the UP Rural High School after the UP Day Remembrance of Martial Law.

The UP Rural High School released a statement on October 1, condemning the red-tagging by Badoy and a military agent named “Emjay Chico.”

“We believe in developing learners who can think critically and engage with the complex problems confronting Philippine society and affecting their basic rights to education, decent life, and human dignity,” the statement reads. “It is deeply concerning that a legitimate educational activity and those who participated in it have been subjected to red-tagging.”

The University asserts the right to academic freedom: fostering discourse that is open, informed, and grounded in evidence.

For his part, Buenaflor has stood his ground.

“All I can say is that I love teaching, and I deeply value my university. I am not afraid,” Buenaflor told Bulatlat in an interview. “I will continue my studies and continue teaching and serving society. I will keep moving forward.”

The Supreme Court of the Philippines already ruled that red-tagging, vilification, labeling, and guilt by association threaten a person’s right to life, liberty, and security.

Read: SC rules: Red-tagging is threat to life, liberty

Buenaflor is a children’s book author, teacher, Christian activist, and unionist. He was the founding chair of UP Baguio Bahaghari until he graduated in 2019.

After this, he became the deputy spokesperson of the Student Christian Movement in the Philippines in 2020.

These affiliations are branded by Badoy as “fronts” of the Communist Party of the Philippines. Buenaflor is also part of Kinaiya, a collective of LGBT writers, essaysists, poets, book authors all over the Philippines.

“Red-tagging is a threat to our freedom of expression and our right to participate in social issues,” Kinaiya pointed out in a statement. “This has no space in a democratic society. Participating in the issues that affect us should not be a reason to threaten everyone’s lives, including our teachers and students.”

As of this writing, Badoy and another former NTF-ELCAC spokesperson Eric Jeffrey Celiz continue with a series of red-tagging posts. They used a Bulatlat feature article as justification for their terrorist-tagging. The article cited by Celiz and Badoy is a feature story about Buenaflor’s queer children stories.

Read: Rainbow realities: A queer author writes radical stories for children

Bahaghari, the organization that Badoy accused of being tied with the Communist Party of the Philippines, released a statement standing in solidarity with Buenaflor.

“Bahaghari is at the forefront of advancing the rights and welfare of the LGBTQIA+ community, as well as fighting discrimination and oppression. While Trist’n and other human rights defenders devote their efforts to defending the rights of the people, red-taggers such as Lorraine Badoy have instead chosen to subject them to dangerous allegations,” Bahaghari said.

More UP Rural High School teachers, organizations, and alliances also joined the call to end the red-tagging of their school and its community.

“Widespread and baseless red-tagging is undoubtedly a mechanism of violence, fascism, and oppression against our freedom and democracy. Guns, intimidation, and militarization are not the path to genuine and lasting peace,” the UPHRS Student Council, student publication, and academic organizations said in a joint statement.

“What the people need is to address the root causes of poverty through adequate funding for education and other social services, genuine land reform for farmers, and fair wages and job security for workers,” the groups added. (RTS, RVO)

title: Li Maltepeyê avahiyeke 7 qatî hilweşiya: Xebatên rizgarkirina kesên di bin kavilan de mane berdewam dikin
content:
Sê qatên destpêkê ên avahiya 7 qatî ya li Kolana Dogu ya li Taxa Cevizliyê ya navçeya Maltepeyê, derdora saet di 05.40an de ji ber sedemeke ku hîn nehatiye diyarkirin hilweşiya. Ji bo cihê bûyerê gelek tîm hatin sewqkirin.


Dema di 3 qatên avahiyê de hilweşîn pêk hat, kesên di qatên jorîn de mabûn bi midaxeleya tîmên lêgerîn û rizgarkirinê hatin rizgarkirin. Li qatên jêrîn xebatên lêgerîn û rizgarkirinê berdewam dikin. Ji beşa ku hilweşiyaye 2 kes derdora saet di 8.00an de hatin derxistin.


Daxuyaniya Walîtiyê


Walîtiya Stenbolê daxuyanî daye û weha gotiye: “Di saet 05.40ê roja Pêncşema 08.10.2026an de li Maltepeyê sê qatên destpêkê ên avahiya 7 qatî hilweşiya ye ku li Kolana Dogu ya Taxa Cevizliyê ye. Ji bo cihê bûyerê tîmên AFAD, agirkujî, tenduristî û ewlehiyê hatine sewqkirin.”


Daxuyaniya Dozgeriyê


Li gorî agahiyên ku ji çavkaniyên Wezareta Karên Navxweyî hatine wergirtin, ger hebe ji bo tespîtkirina wan xemsarî, qusûr û berpirsiyariya peywirdarên dewletê di pêvajoyên plansazî, çêkirin û nûjenkirina avahiya hilweşiyayî ya li Maltepeya Stenbolê de, 2 mufetişên mûlkî hatine peywirdarkirin.


Wezîr Çiftçi daxuyanî da


Wezîrê Karên Navxweyî Mustafa Çiftçi ku li ser hesabê xwe yê medyaya civakî daxuyaniyek da û diyar kir ku ew xebatên lêgerîn û rizgarkirinê berdewam dikin.Çiftçi weha got: 


“Heta niha ji bin kavilan 5 welatiyên me bi saxî hatin derxistin û ji bo nexweşxaneyan hatin şandin. Her weha 10 welatiyên me yên di qatên jorîn ên avahiyê de ne bi awayekî ewle ew jî hatin derxistin. Bi 4 welatiyên me re ku tê nirxandin di bin kavilan de ne pêwendî hat danîn. Tê nirxandin ku dê bi tevahî 7 welatî di bin kavilan de bin. Ji bo ku bûyer bi hemû aliyên xwe ve bê ronîkirin, 2 mifetişên mûlkî yên ku me peywirdarkirine dest bi xebatan kirine. Ez ji welatiyên xwe yên birîndar re şîfaya lezgîn dixwazim û ji welatiyên me yên Maltepeyî re daxwaza derbasbûnê dikim.”

author: EDRi
title: The Cloud and AI Development Act (CADA) represents everything that’s wrong with Europe’s approach to digital sovereignty
content:
The EU’s Tech Sovereignty Package is supposed to jump-start Europe’s “sovereign AI” ambitions. But due to fundamental misunderstandings about the technology behind ‘AI’ and the blind trust in Big Tech’s AI doomer and boomer narratives, it is more likely to instead hurt digital rights and the environment instead, and waste valuable public resources that should have been invested in actually increasing Europe’s digital resilience. The Cloud and AI Development (CADA) Act, a part of the Tech Sovereignty Package, adds up to an aggressive policy push to impose “European AI”.

Published on 3 June, the European Commission’s Tech Sovereignty Package—comprising the Chips Act 2.0, the Cloud and AI Development Act (CADA), the EU Open Source Strategy, and a Strategic Roadmap for Energy Digitalisation—is portrayed as a significant shift in the EU’s digital governance strategy. It signals that the EU is no longer content to rely on regulatory frameworks like the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), Digital Services Act (DSA), Digital Markets Act (DMA) and the Artificial Intelligence (AI) Act. The EU now seeks to artificially inflate both the supply of and demand for AI data centres, as well as to expand the material infrastructures underpinning them.

Yet, as the rhetoric of “strategic autonomy” echoes through the policymaking corridors of Brussels, the Package is fractured by internal contradictions. It conflates the fraught competitiveness agenda with the goal of genuine digital self-determination, mistakes building AI data centres on EU soil for structural tech independence, and engages in what can only be described as “sovereignty-washing”—repackaging the deregulation of fundamental rights and environmental protection as an industrial win. This aggressive industrial policy also embraces the EU’s securitisation and militarisation agenda, as Europe’s loss of competitiveness is perceived as a security threat.

The Commission’s AI policy is almost entirely based on the highly speculative assumption that ‘AI’ is the inevitable future of tech and everybody needs it now or they will lose out on global markets. It claims—without evidence—that “the Union’s limited data centre capacity poses a significant threat to its ability to benefit from the digital transformation” towards AI.

The CADA proposal specifically aims at “regaining and retaining control over data and cloud computing services” and “expanding domestic computational capacity” in order to push for broad AI adoption.

In order to achieve that, the Regulation proposes the massive funding of “research and innovation” projects through public funds and private investment. These projects—called “Cloud and AI Leadership Initiatives”—are supposed to develop, test and deploy “advanced AI technologies,” including autonomous cars, drones and robots (“physical AI”) and AI models for specific industrial sectors (“industrial AI”), notably in healthcare, defence, and in the public sector. CADA is thus supposed to provide the material conditions to implement the EU’s Apply AI strategy principle of “AI first,” forcing the use of more ‘AI’ on public administrations across the continent.

Moreover, CADA would require Member States to establish national “experience and acceleration centres for AI” meant to secure the widespread adoption of AI in private and public sectors. EU countries are also expected to adopt national strategies, mandating the application of the “AI first” principle by all private and public organisations.

On the infrastructure side, Member States would be required to designate so-called “Data Centres Acceleration Zones” on their territory, in which permit-granting procedures are sped up, energy supply is guaranteed, and environmental assessments are fast-tracked, an approach that can put some Member States in a tight spot and risks increasing popular discontent with such imposed infrastructural build-out in their communities.

The inherent flaw of the EU’s “digital sovereignty” policy, illustrated by CADA, is to focus its effort on territorial control over data, infrastructure, and supply chains, instead of the ability to control vendor dependencies and the technology itself. “Building tech in Europe” becomes a goal in itself, one that shifts public resources and attention towards an unproven technology that is currently developed in wildly overvalued markets full of highly indebted companies that may fail at any moment. But it buries a much more important question …

author: EDRi
title: No human required: Austria’s plan for AI-only government decisions
content:
A sweeping change to Austria's administrative law would let authorities issue binding decisions using AI systems with no human ever reviewing the outcome. EDRi member epicenter.works has sent an open letter to parliament, and is looking for input from readers elsewhere in Europe about how other countries are handling, or planning to handle, the same issue.

By epicenter.works (guest author) · October 8, 2026

Austria is about to find out what happens when a member state lets large language models write legally binding government decisions, with no human required to review them.

This autumn, the Constitutional Affairs Committee of Austria’s parliament will debate a sweeping change to the country’s General Administrative Procedure Act (AVG). The AVG is the default procedural code for essentially all administrative proceedings in Austria, covering everything from social assistance and building permits to business licensing and public subsidies. A single change to the general code can therefore affect how decisions get made across almost the entire administration, not just in one sector. According to the draft law, authorities would for the first time be allowed to issue fully automated administrative decisions: legally binding rulings with direct effect on a person’s rights, comparable to what other jurisdictions might call an administrative act or order, without a human ever reviewing the specific outcome before it goes out.

Ahead of this autumn’s debate, epicenter.works has written to the Constitutional Affairs Committee, sending an open letter laying out exactly why fully automated decisions with no human review are incompatible with fundamental rights.

Let’s be precise about what’s actually being automated, because the draft treats generative AI the same way previous automation laws treated simple rule-based software.

Classic automated administrative systems are deterministic: same input, same output, traceable logic. A system built on a large language model works fundamentally differently in three ways that each map directly onto a legal guarantee:

Hallucination. LLMs generate outputs that sound plausible but can be flatly wrong or entirely invented. Even specialised legal AI systems show hallucination rates of roughly 17 to 33%, and errors are often impossible for the affected person to spot. Hallucinated facts underpinning a binding decision affect the right to a fair trial under Article 6 of the European Convention on Human Rights: a person can’t meaningfully exercise that right when the decision against them is built on evidence that doesn’t exist.

Black box. How the system arrived at a given output is structurally not fully explainable. This is not simply “not yet documented” but not explainable even in principle with current models. That sits uneasily with a basic rule-of-law demand: that the exercise of state power be transparent and reviewable, not just efficient.

Bias. Systematic distortions like race, income level, migration status etc. are baked into how these models are trained and can’t be engineered away by picking a “better” vendor. Left unchecked, this risks group-based unequal treatment that no one notices, because the system doesn’t expose it, touching the principle of non-discrimination, which both EU law and the Austrian constitution guarantee explicitly.

These aren’t implementation flaws. They’re inherent to how current LLMs work, and every legal objection below follows directly from this technical reality.

Weeks before this autumn’s parliamentary debate, Austria’s own state-run AI assistant “ida” supplied a preview of the problem: it falsely described a sitting vice-chancellor as a former government member and invented a government minister who doesn’t exist.

A more serious example came out of the UK in July 2026. An Upper Tribunal judge found that the Home Office had refused an asylum claim, from a woman who had fled forced child marriage and severe violence, by citing a policy document that, on inspection, appears never to have existed. The judge noted the refusal letter bore the hallmarks of AI-generated content, and suggested the reference was likely an AI hallucination, warning that this would represent an extremely serious failing on the department’s part if confirmed.

Read together, these two cases show an escalation from a chatbot inventing a minister’s name in Austria to a fabricated document underpinning an actual refusal of protection in the UK, in exactly the kind of …

author: EDRi
title: D3 brings class actions on addictive design against Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube
content:
The Portuguese digital rights organisation and EDRi member D3 announces that it has brought four class actions lawsuits against Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube over the use of addictive design practices. The cases challenge design practices that can encourage compulsive use of online platforms and seek to hold platforms accountable for the way their services affect users. Similar initiatives might come up in other EU Member States as part of a broader European response.

By D3 – Defesa dos Direitos Digitais & NOVA School of Law (guest author) · October 8, 2026

In April and May 2026, D3 brought four cases before the Portuguese civil courts against Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube. The proceedings took the form of a “popular action”, that is, a specific legal mechanism for collective redress provided for in the Portuguese Constitution in which D3 acts as a collective representative of the rights of people in Portugal.

The cases concern the business models of major platforms and the incentives created by the attention economy. D3 argues that the platforms’ business models should not depend on design mechanisms that undermine users’ ability to exercise control over their own use of digital services.

The purpose of the actions is to seek greater accountability from platforms and to ensure that users can have a safer experience online.

The actions were brought by a team of lawyers led by Miguel Miranda and Efigénia Marabuto Tavares, from Andersen Tax & Legal Iberia. Academic experts Fabrizio Esposito and Cecília Isola, from NOVA School of Law, also supported the cases.

Online platforms have access to large amounts of information about users’ behaviour and interactions. Such concentration of information gives a small number of companies significant power to shape how people interact with their services.

The actions focus on design practices commonly described as dark patterns, including infinite scrolling, automatic playback, persistent notifications, personalised recommendation systems and gamification. Together, these features act as a powerful force that makes people spend more time on platforms and interact with them more frequently.

The case argues that such practices draw on knowledge of human behaviour and psychology, combined with information about users’ preferences, vulnerabilities and interests. The resulting systems can make it more difficult for users to stop using a service voluntarily and can reduce the scope for independent decision-making.

Research across fields including medicine, psychology, sociology and technology has examined the relationship between digital design and compulsive patterns of use. The issue has also received attention from the European Parliament and the European Commission, as well as in legal proceedings in the United States and by EDRi member Bits of Freedom in the Netherlands.

One of the groups of people most vulnerable to deceptive and manipulative design of platforms are young people. So far, the EU’s response to calls for protecting them has unfortunately been limited to age gates and restrictions, putting the responsibility on the individual rather than the platforms.

D3 argues that restricting access to social media for people under 16 should not be treated as a substitute for addressing potentially harmful design practices. Social media platforms have become important means of communication and interaction, making it necessary to address the design of these services rather than simply excluding particular groups from them.

As D3 president Ricardo Lafuente explains, platforms can provide a healthier online environment if effective rules are properly enforced and responsibility is placed on platforms that fail to comply with them.

The Portuguese cases contribute to a growing European debate about platform design, user autonomy and platform accountability. D3’s approach focuses on the responsibilities of platforms and the conditions under which digital services are designed and operated.

With similar initiatives potentially being prepared in other EU Member States, cooperation between digital rights organisations and legal initiatives could help develop a coordinated European response to addictive design.

The objective is not to prevent people from using social media, rather to support an online environment in which users retain meaningful control over their digital experiences.

People should not have to choose between access to essential online …

author: Franck Dick Rosete
title: Bukidnon Lumad’s fight for ancestral land remains uncertain
content:
Representatives of the Gulinsao and Maranding clans join a dialogue held at Provincial Tulugan Hall, Malaybalay City, Bukidnon, on September 7, 2026. Photo from Bukidnon Provincial IPMR Datu Makayuba Renato Sumbongan’s Facebook page

CAGAYAN DE ORO — After the fifth dialogue aiming to settle the land dispute between Indigenous peoples and a government agency in Barangay Dalwangan, Malaybalay City, Bukidnon, Lumad are still deprived of their ancestral land.

“They should return the land they borrowed,” Datu Aldren Gulinsao told Bulatlat in the vernacular following the dialogue last month.

Since 2017, the Gulinsao clan belonging to the Talaandig tribe has been reclaiming over 600 hectares of ancestral land, while their relative, the Maranding clan, has been claiming over 400 hectares. These form part of the more than 1,000 hectares of land under the title they obtained during the Philippine Commonwealth owned by their ancestor Maximo Gulinsao.

The Department of Agrarian Reform (DAR), on the other hand, said the subject land has been a titled property of the Department of Agriculture (DA) since the 1930s.

To assert their rights, in February, a few members of the Gulinsao clan forcibly entered the land, which resulted in the arrest of three individuals.

CONTEXT: Uncertainty forces Lumad to enter disputed ancestral land in Bukidnon

In a dialogue launched in December 2021, lawyer Heinz Villanueva, then legal officer of the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples (NCIP), told the Lumad claimants that they needed to file a case to cancel DA’s title before they could proceed in filing an ancestral domain claim.

Gulinsao opposed the suggestion, saying that DA possessed the same title that they have. During the September 7, 2026 dialogue, he asked the DA representative if they have a Deed of Sale. The representative could not provide a definite answer as it still needed to be checked.

The Lumad leader said they are in the process of completing their certificate of ancestral domain claim (CADC) before the NCIP.

The concerned Lumad clans, however, were told that they could be beneficiaries of the government’s agrarian reform program after 358 hectares of the subject land—also within the claim of the Gulinsao clan—has been subject to Executive Order No. 75-2019, an order directing all government agencies to identify state-owned lands suitable for agriculture for distribution to qualified agrarian reform beneficiaries.

Datu Ornan Lesion, a representative of the Maranding clan, said in the September 7, 2026, dialogue that there were more than 200 of them who wanted to become beneficiaries. The Gulinsao clan has almost the same number of members. Both clans welcomed the offer because of their eagerness to have a land to till. But this also remains a challenge.

Gulinsao said they already made repeated requests to the municipal and provincial agrarian reform offices, but they were told to also submit a request to the DA, which allegedly did not respond despite follow-ups.

Marvin Calleja, DAR Malaybalay representative, said that Task Force Dalwangan was already created in 2023, but the status of the 358 hectares of land remains pending. He said he would forward the dialogue discussion to their provincial office to clarify the matter.

“With our process now, we have lost hope on our government agencies,” Gulinsao said in the vernacular when asked for their future plans.

He said there are clan members currently living in Barangay Dalwangan, but outside their ancestral land. Other members are living in the neighboring town of Impasug-ong. He said they want to resolve the matter through a sala, a Lumad customary practice of settling disputes, as their final resort.

The month of October serves as the Indigenous Peoples’ Month. (RVO)

Disclosure: All of the dialogue discussions cited in this article were based on the minutes of meetings obtained by the Gulinsao clan from the Office of the City and Provincial Indigenous Peoples Mandatory Representatives and forwarded to Bulatlat.
